It may use a queued/buffered pre-stop frame or the latest successful media-engine repeat cache to close only already-accrued ticks; post-stop source frames are discarded. Any packet beyond the stop target, missing accrued tick, or >1.01-tick PTS gap is a validation failure.
```md
- WGC CFR visual source selection is bounded to about `250 ms` or `32` frames behind live, whichever is tighter. Stale buffered WGC history is dropped before selection.
- The live visual-debt bound is not a pre-live startup-reservoir bound. If an armed smoothness target exceeds the live window, pre-live WGC/DXGI pruning must preserve the retained-cap-bounded post-barrier history until the startup frame/contract is selected; otherwise the default 300 ms target can never outlive the 250 ms live window and every run falls into partial-span fallback. Once output is live, ordinary and encoder-limited pruning resume unchanged. This exception neither moves the immutable CFR grid nor changes the audio anchor.
- WGC/DXGI frame PTS and audio samples follow the immutable CFR endpoint. Source-frame selection targets the output slot's grid QPC and is never independently clamped toward current wall time or raised to the oldest retained frame; wall-clock frame age cannot prove content sync when the encoder grid is behind. Obsolete source history may be pruned, and overdue time is preferentially repaid with bounded cached/held repeats that do not postpone the next normal wake. Without active render-domain delay, a buffered screen frame more than three output ticks newer than the effective selection target is skipped/held.
- WGC automatic render-domain sync chooses the first audio anchor from the accepted startup video's raw QPC plus the resolved render-loopback delay. Any selected startup smoothness extra delay advances only the live playout QPC in the same immutable contract. The startup schedule offset between the audio anchor and encoder live-start QPC is diagnostic only; it must not be subtracted from steady-state WGC selection targets. Steady-state selection applies the contract's requested content delay, otherwise WGC can build a larger delay reserve through repeated frames and create visible judder while A/V sync appears fixed. The selected extra smoothness delay is not a live audio retiming loop; source deficits after startup are represented as CFR repeats.
- WGC retained copy-pool slots are single-owner resources. A slot with an outstanding WGC lease must not be overwritten while it is queued, buffered, cached as the last frame, selected for startup, or inside the media-engine copy. Exhausted copy pools must drop the incoming WGC frame with `wgc_pool_saturated_safe_drop` instead of reusing old/leased content. Pool generations must make stale releases harmless after a pool recreate.
- WGC copy-pool pressure trim may discard newest surplus buffered frames only down to the active delay target. It is a lease/free-slot protection mechanism, not an audio sync mechanism and not permission to shrink the smoothness reservoir below the requested target.
- WGC active-delay hard-safe is not the same as quality-safe. In healthy/recoverable/post-stall windows, a frame must be soft-safe (within the 5-7 ms target in both predicted and raw timestamp domains) to be preferred over a sync-protected repeat. The 10 ms hard cap exists to prevent invalid output, not to define the normal perceived-sync target.
- WGC encoder-limited mode is allowed only when the WGC source is healthy enough and encoder/mux capacity is the limiting factor. In that mode, visual debt is bounded to about `50 ms` or `3` target frames, stale buffered source frames are dropped aggressively, selected source timestamps must not move backward relative to the last emitted WGC source timestamp, and equal-source repeats under encoder pressure are explicit holds rather than stale-fresh-stale backtracking. Audio/sample accounting does not change.
- Source-starved WGC episodes must not be reclassified as encoder-limited smoothness. Missing source frames are source evidence; healthy source input plus encoder/mux pressure plus near-live source drops is encoder-limited evidence.
- WGC startup must not accept the first stale post-barrier frame if fresher WGC frames are already queued or buffered. With no active render-domain delay, the startup handoff drains pending WGC material and selects the freshest valid post-barrier frame before the shared A/V anchor is published.
- With active render-domain delay, WGC startup should use the available post-barrier reserve when it is sufficient: select the candidate closest to `latestCandidateSelectionQpc - requestedDelayQpc`, keep newer candidates buffered for the first live ticks, and wait briefly before live output for reservoir low-water when needed. If the wait budget expires or the candidate span is insufficient, fall back to the safest valid frame and log whether this was source startup underfeed, partial-span timeout, or another reserve failure; do not invent delay or feed startup schedule offset back into steady-state selection. During live active-delay selection, strict residual tolerance is tighter than generic CFR future-frame tolerance; a bounded relaxed selection is allowed only when it stays inside the hard residual limit and its target-distance/repeat-cluster cost is lower than extending a repeat. Rejections above the hard sync limit and repeat-cluster pressure must be counted in the WGC summary so future logs can distinguish source limitation from CE policy damage.
- After WGC active-delay selection, any later low-source clamp or reserve-preservation fallback must re-check the final frame against the same hard residual cap in both predicted and raw timestamp domains. If that final check fails, CE should repeat/classify rather than encoding the too-new frame, and the analyzer should report `wgc_active_delay_post_selection_reject` or `wgc_timestamp_domain_mismatch` as strict evidence.
- WGC source-limited repeats are acceptable only near the computed lower bound. Source-starved sync-delay holds can count as lower-bound repeats, but healthy-source or CE-policy repeats above the lower-bound thresholds should surface as `wgc_cfr_smoothness_not_maximal` instead of being hidden under source starvation.
- WGC smoothness FLOOR (`wgc_smoothness_floor_ms`, WGC-only) may engage the active-delay smoothness machinery even with no audio-latency content delay (video-only capture / low-confidence loopback probe), so WGC is not left on maximally-jitter-exposed near-live selection. The floor is **sync-neutral by construction** and this property is an invariant: the audio anchor delay stays `= avContentDelayQpc` (true latency `L`; the mediaengine derives the anchor from `GetWgcStartupAudioAnchorQpc(firstVideoQpc, renderDelayQpc=L)` and the smoothness/floor extra `S` is used only for logging). The floor `S` is realized purely as the selected startup video frame being `S` older with a correspondingly later live-start (`liveStart ≈ startupVideoQpc + (L+S)`, absorbed by `scheduleOffset`), so for every PTS tick the selected video content time equals the audio real-sound time independent of `S`. The floor is resolved once at the startup barrier (auto: from measured WGC delivery jitter; or explicit ms) and HELD FIXED for the session — it must never retime the media/audio anchor live, which is what would reintroduce the realized-delay-collapse / ghost-image-judder family. Floor delay flows only into the VIDEO effective delay (`getWgcEffectiveContentDelayQpc`) and reservoir sizing; CFR PTS grid, audio sample data, track lengths, stop/endpoint, and mux are unchanged. `wgc_smoothness_floor_ms=0` reproduces prior behavior bit-for-bit, and the floor is a no-op in the healthy with-audio path (the audio-latency reservoir target already dominates). Regression-locked by `CapturePipelinePolicyTest.WgcSmoothnessFloorIsSyncNeutralAcrossDelays` (the sync-neutrality property), `WgcSmoothnessFloorDerivationIsClampedAndMonotonic`, and `WgcSmoothnessDelayDesiredArmsForFloorWithoutAudioLatency`.

## Diagnostics

Use these signals together:

- `TimerRebase` / duplicate timer-rebase counts: nonzero values indicate live CFR rescheduling pressure. They must not represent discarded timeline debt in CFR captures.
- `CFR stop drain ... path=inject|WGC`: shows whether stop-time outstanding CFR ticks were closed.
- `[EncoderThread] CFR stop drain skipped before first live video frame`: the recording stopped before any video frame committed the output timeline. There is no CFR prefix to close; the encoder worker disarms the drain and proceeds to reserved-output cleanup instead of polling an already-shut-down empty queue.
- `[A/V START] Audio source reset ... timelineValid=...`: non-app sources should become valid at the shared anchor; app audio stays optional only until first packet evidence. If an app source saw sync-pending packets, subsequent bootstrap should wait rather than encode a leading silent head.
- `[PullAudio] Track ... bootstrap complete ... forced=0 trimmed=0`: any `forced=1` or nonzero `trimmed` indicates the old content-shortening startup path.
- `[PullAudio] Timeline source gap silence ... idle=<ms>`: a started source exhausted the ingestion reservoir and is intentionally contributing silence instead of blocking the exported track. `idle` is the time since that source last placed a real packet; a large value means a genuinely sparse source, while a small value with real packets, QPC overlap, or `Late source cursor advance` right after is consumer-overrun starvation evidence to inspect.
- `[PullAudio] Late live source hold ...`: the source was short but still delivering, so the pull was held and the reservoir deepened instead of exporting silence that would have destroyed the late audio. Informational recovery, not a fault.
- `[PullAudio] Ingest reservoir deepened|relaxed ... worstHeadroom=<ms> atCap=<0|1>`: adaptive pull-lookahead changes. `worstHeadroom` below zero means the consumer had already overrun the capture edge. `atCap=1` sustained is a real capacity problem; the reservoir cannot grow further and silence plus the last-resort re-anchor become reachable.
- `[AudioLoop] WARNING: source ingest starvation ...`: real captured audio is being discarded as timeline overlap because the exported cursor ran past the live capture edge. Strict; the recording is losing content even if every duration matches.
- `[AudioLoop] WARNING: unrecoverable ingest starvation - re-anchoring ...`: last-resort placement re-anchor after the reservoir saturated. Always a bug signature to investigate.
- `[STOP AUDIO INGEST] Source N: starve=... resync=.../... reservoirPeakMs=...`: per-source destroyed-sample total, last-resort re-anchor accounting, and the session's peak extra lookahead. `starve=0 resync=0/0` is required for a clean recording; a nonzero `reservoirPeakMs` alone is healthy adaptation.
- `[PullAudio] WARNING: Source underrun ... forceDrain=0`: live source underrun and strict audio evidence. The same line with `forceDrain=1` is stop-tail padding evidence; it is diagnostic only when decoded strict markers, inter-track spread, CE zero residuals, and final packet/post-mux durations are clean.
- `[AudioLoop] Late source cursor advance ...`: late source data is being stitched against the already-advanced source/track cursor rather than delaying the exported track.
- `[AudioLoop] Late app source live join ...`: a process-loopback source first became active after recording start and stale first-packet backlog was suppressed so the source joins the current track cursor.
- `[STOP AUDIO] Source ... qjoin=... qjoinKeep=... process=...`: late app-source join accounting, including how much stale queued gap was suppressed and how much fade cushion was preserved.
- `[STOP AUDIO TRACK] Track ... encoded=... expected=... realMixed=... fullSilence=... partialSilence=...`: per-exported-stream cursor and real/silence accounting.
- `[A/V SYNC SUMMARY] Track ... audio_vs_encoded_us=... audio_vs_target_us=... residual_samples=... target_samples=... cursor_samples=...`: live sample accounting. For strict CFR diagnosis, `residual_samples=0` is the hard requirement after startup; `audio_vs_encoded_us` is diagnostic because encoded packet duration can lag live scheduled duration under CFR.
- `[A/V ZERO DRIFT WARNING]`: settled CFR track cursor and CFR target sample disagree. Treat as a strict failure even when final packet/container durations still match.
- `[STOP AUDIO DETAIL] Source ... ratePpm=... compDelta=... sat=...`: source-clock compensation state at stop. For healthy CFR recordings this should stay effectively zero; saturated `ratePpm` with clean source clocks usually means compensation is chasing buffer level instead of real drift.
- `[StopAudio] forceDrain ... iterations=...`: stop-time force drain may run multiple bounded chunks. Warnings `forceDrain made no progress` or `forceDrain incomplete` are strict follow-up evidence for track-cursor failures.
- `[StopAudio] Source ... diff=+0 (+0.0 ms)`: sample-count equality to the selected final video timeline.
- `[VideoEncoder] Final packet timeline`: actual last written packet end per stream and packet-level delta. Audio pass/fail endpoints exclude terminal `AV_PKT_DATA_SKIP_SAMPLES` discard while retaining `rawAudioMaxEnd` for packet-topology diagnosis.
- `[VideoEncoder] Final metadata durations`: in-memory stream metadata sampled only after `av_write_trailer`; the log reports available/declared stream counts. Missing `AVStream::duration` fields are informational because some muxers do not populate them even after trailer. Packet timelines plus the bounded post-mux packet probe remain authoritative, and only complete metadata is compared against tolerance.
- `[VideoEncoder] mux_closed ...`: trailer/file close and muxer cleanup completed; later probe problems should not imply the muxer is still owned.
- `[VideoEncoder] post_mux_probe_start/complete/timeout/cancelled ...`: reopened-file stream duration/end check after trailer write; this is the external duration authority when it completes, and a timeout is a bounded validation failure/diagnostic rather than a shutdown hang.
- `[VideoEncoder] Post-mux duration probe`: reopened-file stream duration/end check after trailer write. Audio endpoints are decoded endpoints: Matroska packet coverage is reduced by codec-declared initial padding and terminal packet discard padding. Raw endpoints and padding evidence remain logged; an incomplete bounded tail scan cannot silently excuse a mismatch.
- `[VideoEncoder] Post-mux audio codec-padding applied`: informational proof that raw AAC/Opus packet coverage was translated to the externally decoded endpoint using explicit codec metadata.
- `[VideoEncoder] Post-mux audio duration rounding evidence`: reopened-file audio duration differs from the target only within the one-sample / one-timebase-tick rounding tolerance. This is informational; larger mismatches still log `WARNING: Post-mux audio duration mismatch`.
- `[VideoEncoder] Stop: WARNING writer_finalize_slow phase=...`: phase-aware stop diagnostic emitted once when trailer/final probe/cleanup is slow. It is diagnostic evidence, not by itself mux corruption.
- `[VideoEncoder] Stop: ERROR writer_finalize_timeout ...`: strict mux ownership failure unless the same session later has exact final packet/container/post-mux evidence and no sync-finalize fallback. The async writer still owns the FFmpeg context, so CE must not run a synchronous trailer write on the same context. Old logs that combine `Writer thread did not finish ... detaching` with `Sync Stop: Finalizing file...` indicate the double-finalize crash family.
- `[AudioEncoder] Using codec: requested=... resolved=... channels=... mask=...`: codec alias, resolved encoder, and track layout policy.
- `[AudioEncoder] Silence queue ...`, `Clamping final packet duration ...`, and `Added packet end-skip side data ...`: encoded silence and AAC/Opus padded-tail handling.
- `[AudioEncoder] Opus requires 48000 Hz ...`: expected adjustment when Opus was configured with another sample rate.
- `[Cadence Health]` inject fields plus `[Inject CFR QUALITY SUMMARY]`: `InjectCatch=fresh/repeat`, `TickUnique`, `TickDup`, `Shortfall`, `AgeAvg/AgeMax`, `TargetSelect`, `Superseded`, `TargetHold`, `HoldWithCandidate`, `BufferCapTrim`, and `TargetResidualMax` distinguish honest source-limited repeats from selector or buffer-policy churn. `InjectAgeTrim` is a legacy pre-target-playout metric and should remain zero in new sessions.
- `[Inject CFR] Recovery entered/progress/completed` and `[Inject CFR SUMMARY]`: start/best/current debt, episode duration, `Recovery=active/episodes`, `FreshCatchup`, `RepeatCatchup`, `StaleTrim`, duplicate reasons, pure encode time, normalized per-output service time, raw full-cycle time, and source FPS show whether debt converged, was paused for genuine encoder/mux pressure, or was caused by source/game FPS below target or fence deferral. A recovery that remains active long enough to emit the five-second warning is classified as `inject_cfr_recovery_stalled` by `tools/analysis/analyze_capture_av.py`; old summaries remain accepted.
- `FPS Limiter: Local timer stats ... phaseSkipped=N` reports whole capture-grid slots skipped after late Presents. `[CFR PhaseLock] path=screen_grab|inject` reports scheduler-path acquisition, stable rephase, or variable-source release; `[CFR PHASE LOCK SUMMARY] Backend=dxgi_dup|wgc|inject` records the actual final backend, offset, and transition counts. Legacy hard-coded phase-lock `backend=wgc` labels are not valid ordered backend-transition evidence. These are selection-phase diagnostics, not audio/CFR-grid corrections.
- Session present-gap triage uses the `source_frame_index` live span when available, excluding pre-live initialization and post-stop frozen metrics. Inject target-policy churn requires repeated hold-with-candidate/superseded pairs in consecutive per-window source-rate-matched, non-overloaded windows; a session-wide minimum distorted by one real hitch is not a valid stability test, and honest varying/under-target resampling is not classified as a policy fault.
- `[Cadence Health]` WGC fields: `WgcSelBias`, `Shortfall`, `LeadExcess`, `Oldest`, `BufNow`, `LiveClamp`, and `AgeMax` expose visual debt, selected-content drift, and live-window source-selection clamping. Large values are a content-sync bug even when stream durations match.
- `[EncoderThread] CFR Catchup applied using fresh frame`: legacy current-frame/old-PTS WGC catch-up and always a strict failure. Safe current recovery instead logs `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR grid-matched recovery frame` and requires a monotonic historical frame matched to that exact old selection target plus encoder-service/reservoir headroom.
- `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR repeat catch-up armed`: rate-limited proof that shortfall recovery will emit two to four packet-backed CFR slots on the immutable grid. `ticksThisLoop>1` is intentional under debt; an extra slot uses safe grid-matched history when available and otherwise holds the prior frame. It must not move the next normal wake deadline.
- `[WGC CFR] Uniform playout grid-debt sync hold`: every retained frame is substantially newer than the immutable audio-aligned content target. The old wall-age anti-freeze floor is gone; held-repeat catch-up must advance the grid until safe history becomes selectable. `GridDebtSyncHolds` and `GridDebtLeadMax` report the total and worst target/history gap.
- `[WGC CFR] Overload repeat pacer entered|exited` and `[WGC CFR OVERLOAD PACER]`: WGC/DXGI-only evidence that measured fresh/repeat service invoked the sustainable or degraded liveness policy. Logs include entry/exit reason, service EMAs/sample counts, effective budget, fresh fraction, decisions/emitted repeats, maximum paced repeat run, and explicit unchanged CFR/audio invariants. Paced repeats are separated from genuine no-source repeats.
- `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR slot repeat: buffered frame is too new for scheduled slot`: expected only for short gaps or while WGC is honestly building/holding the requested render-domain delay. Frequent events while `Shortfall` is near/above the live-window limit mean source selection may still be pinned too far behind live and should be investigated with `LiveClamp`, `WgcSelBias`, `BufNow`, reservoir low-water ticks, and the sync-delay hold attribution.
- `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR visual timeline debt drop`: WGC visual debt exceeded the live window. It logs current and maximum excess ticks as a warning to inspect, not permission to shorten audio or move future frames into old slots.
- `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR live scheduler rebase`: legacy output-grid skipping. Current `GetWgcLiveSchedulerRebaseTicksThisLoopForMode` returns zero because advancing coverage without a packet punches CFR PTS holes; any occurrence in a current build is a regression.
- `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR stale visual debt drop`: buffered WGC frames older than the live-debt window were dropped instead of being encoded as delayed visual history.
- `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR encoder-limited source drop`: legacy output-slot coalescing coupled to scheduler rebase. It must remain absent now that every CFR tick requires a packet; ordinary stale source-snapshot pruning is reported separately and does not consume the output grid.
- `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR slot repeat: buffered frame is too new for scheduled slot`: WGC intentionally repeated the prior frame instead of selecting future visual content for the delayed source-selection target. New builds log `allowedLead`, `avDelay`, `syncDelay`, `syncSourceLimited`, `lowSource`, `sourceStarved`, `encoderLimited`, recent input/delivery FPS, and `noFresh` so a real-game repeat can be attributed to sync-delay reserve pressure, true source starvation, or capacity recovery without sacrificing A/V sync. If a bounded relaxed selection is less damaging than repeating and stays under the hard residual limit, WGC may select it instead; current policy also requires rolling residual avg/p95/late-max headroom so sync improvement cannot accumulate visible judder or audio-late residual. The uniform WGC playout path now uses the same repeat-rescue scoring before holding (`[WGC CFR] Uniform playout rescued repeat with sync-safe frame`) and classifies holds with no soft-safe candidate as sync-protected/source-limited lower-bound repeats rather than healthy-source policy repeats. The summary records these as `delayResidualRelaxedSelections` or `delayRepeatRescue`, plus hard/soft-safe candidate and `delaySyncProtectedRepeats` counters.
- `[WGC CFR CADENCE EVENT]`: compact per-window WGC pressure line. `mode=encoder_limited` means healthy-source encoder pressure; `mode=source_starved` means missing source frames; `phaseError*`, `encoderDropWindow`, `tooNewRepeat`, `staleDrop`, `syncDelaySourceHold`, `syncDelayPolicyHold`, `bufNow`, `oldest`, `sustain`, and `overload` explain the smoothness failure shape.
- `[WGC CFR SMOOTHNESS SUMMARY]` plus split `BUFFER` / `DELAY` / `REPEAT` / `VERDICT`: final WGC smoothness rollup. Key fields are `encoderLimitedDrops`, `phaseErrorMax`, `shortfallMax`, `staleDebtDrops`, `liveRebase`, `tooNewRepeats`, `syncDelayHolds`, `syncDelaySourceLimitedHolds`, `syncDelayPolicyHolds`, `tooNewLeadMax`, `avDelay`, `startupDelay`, `scheduleOffset`, `effectiveDelay`, `startupReserveFrames`, `startupReserveSpan`, `startupDelayTarget`, `startupReserveSelected`, `startupReserveReason`, `smoothTargetDelay`, `smoothActualDelay`, `smoothDelayDeficit`, `startupDelayDeficit`, `delayReservoirLowWaterFrames`, `delayReservoirTargetFrames`, `delayReservoirLowWaterTicks`, `realizedDelayAvg/Min/Max`, `delayResidualAvg`, `delayResidualMax`, `delayResidualP95`, late/early residual maxima, relaxed/repeat-rescue reason counters, relaxed/repeat-rescue rejection counters, repeat-cluster pressure, hard/soft-safe repeat counters, sync-protected repeats, and source-recovery counters; high values with exact audio durations are visual cadence/content-sync evidence, not audio drift. Source-limited sync-delay holds are minor reserve-pressure evidence only when requested/startup/effective delay match and residual stays bounded; policy holds, requested/startup/effective mismatch, residual beyond the strict target, or small-but-visible policy-added repeat rates are strict A/V/smoothness evidence. A large `scheduleOffset` with many holds is especially suspicious; it should remain diagnostic and not become another WGC selection delay.
- `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR stop drain using held pre-stop frame`: stale-build/failure signature for WGC exact-stop work. New WGC captures should not use generic stop drain.
- `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR stop drain discarded frozen-tail debt`: superseded older policy. Treat this as a stale-build warning if it appears in new strict validation.
- `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR post-stop frame drop`: a WGC frame timestamped after the stop QPC was discarded and must not extend the recording. Discarding such callbacks is endpoint protection, not itself a strict failure.
- `tools/analysis/analyze_capture_av.py` log gates include `wgc_stop_drain_aborted`, `wgc_fresh_catchup`, `wgc_too_new_slot_repeat`, `wgc_stale_visual_debt_drop`, `wgc_stale_fresh_catchup_blocked`, `wgc_visual_timeline_debt_drop`, `wgc_live_scheduler_rebase`, `wgc_stop_hold_repeats`, `wgc_drain_duplicate_summary`, `wgc_stop_frozen_tail_drop`, `wgc_post_stop_frame_drop`, `audio_extreme_drift`, `late_app_source_backlog`, `started_app_source_underrun`, `post_mux_probe_hang`, `post_mux_probe_timeout`, `ce_process_crash`, and the cadence/reservoir/residual/source-recovery metrics. Live or unclassified legacy extreme drift remains strict. A new `[PullAudio] Stop force-drain backlog ... forceDrain=1` line is `audio_stop_force_drain_backlog` context because it describes retained post-target input that final endpoint clamping excludes; older source-qualified drift warnings are downgraded only when the preceding per-source `[AppDrain]` state proves `forceDrain=1`. `[PullAudio] Source primed` now includes `app=0|1`; old logs use `[STOP AUDIO] ... process=-|name` so a late microphone prime is not mislabeled as an unjoined app backlog, while ambiguous legacy prime-only evidence remains strict. `--strict-sync-events` still sets zero thresholds for live audio trim/drop/underrun/extreme-drift events plus genuine late app-source backlog, WGC fresh catch-up, WGC stop-drain abort, WGC held stop repeats, and nonzero WGC drain duplicate summaries.
- `dx12_av_sync_test.exe` app logs: `AVSYNC START`, `AVSYNC EVENT`, `AVSYNC FRAME`, `AVSYNC AUDIO_BUFFER`, `AVSYNC WARNING`, and `AVSYNC SUMMARY`. These logs are diagnostic evidence for the app's QPC anchors, event schedule, audio buffer health, frame marker cadence, underruns/timeouts, and final summaries.
- `[WGC CFR ATTRIBUTION]`: compact source-starvation attribution line emitted for logged WGC source-starved episodes. It includes `fault_hint`, QPC range, duration/output/duplicate counts, `minIn`, `minDel`, `freshMiss`, callback gap, encoder EMA, mux backpressure, overload flags, copy health, and fence health.
- `perf_metrics_*.csv`: appended `qpc_delta_us` column gives per-Present QPC gaps without breaking existing readers. A large QPC delta with small `total_us`, small `capture_us`, and no overload flags points toward source Present gaps rather than CE backpressure.
- `tools/analysis/analyze_av_sync_stimulus.py`: strict content checks distinguish `corrupted_video_frame`, `visual_judder`, `planned_source_stall`, `unplanned_repeat_cluster`, `video_content_drift`, `missing_marker`, `audio_marker_missing`, `audio_video_event_offset`, `audio_video_offset_slope`, `inter_track_spread`, `decode_error`, and `ce_strict_log_event`. It auto-scales video decode when marker tiles would be too small, decodes both slow and fast motion lanes when present, uses a short-window Goertzel refinement around coarse audio transitions, reports per-track offset slope and matched-offset span, fails on `[A/V ZERO DRIFT WARNING]`, and treats mixed/microphone streams as non-strict ordinals when they are diagnostic rather than deterministic evidence. Source-local strict-track stop padding remains visible, but it is diagnostic when decoded strict markers/spread and CE zero-residual evidence are clean; actual missing content should still fail through marker, offset, spread, underrun/trim, or zero-drift checks.
- `tools/analysis/analyze_capture_av.py --session-dir <logs>`: real-session stutter triage for sessions where no synthetic manifest exists. It parses media/hook logs, `perf_metrics_*.csv`, crash/dump evidence, and manifests, then emits source, CE capacity, audio, visual, and shutdown verdicts. Ordered runtime `Backend:`/`backend=` telemetry is authoritative over the configured manifest: one backend retains `wgc_*` or `dxgi_dup_*`, while an observed DXGI→WGC fallback reports `screen_capture_backend=dxgi_dup_to_wgc`, preserves `screen_capture_backend_history`, adds `screen_capture_backend_transition` context, and uses neutral `screen_capture_*` diagnostics. A DXGI→WGC transition can leave a bounded aggregate lower-bound accounting gap because the producer/accounting domain reset; up to 10% (with a five-tick accounting floor for short runs) is source-limited context only when the final packet timeline is exact, source starvation is proven, encoder/mux/pool are clean, policy-added repeats/clusters/holds, soft-safe candidates, post-selection rejects, mixed policy, and incomplete-evidence counters are all zero, and the runtime verdict says `smoothnessNotMaximal=0`. The same evidence without the actual transition remains strict. Perf CSV `capture_phase=2` remains the authoritative live-Present window. Use the analyzer to separate expected source/loading stalls and backend transitions from encoder/mux pressure, avoidable repeat policy, content-delay faults, audio damage, or shutdown/probe failure before changing CFR policy.
- The same triage mode also reports `multi_app_audio_track_stall` when stop summaries show multi-source tracks ending far before the expected video/audio endpoint, and treats `writer_finalize_timeout` as encoder/mux backpressure evidence. This keeps duplicate app-audio routing regressions distinct from normal source starvation.
- `tools/analysis/run_av_sync_matrix.py`: writes one scenario config at a time, restores `installed/captureengine/config.ini`, kills stale `dx12_av_sync_test.exe` instances, runs CE with `--auto-record ... --launch ...`, stores artifacts under `installed/captureengine/avsync_runs/<timestamp>/`, and emits `matrix_report.json` plus per-scenario reports linking the capture, logs, manifests, and analyzer/triage output. Bare execution is the fast WGC/inject ALAC/AAC 60/120 zero-drift gate; optional passes cover all audio codecs, late app-source joins, stress, sync smoothness, full matrix, and long soak. The adaptive 4K120 high-entropy `--wgc-overload-gate` tries p5/p6/p7 and requires actual encoder pressure, overload flags, encoder-limited cadence, and material shortfall. A current healthy overload result keeps packet/audio integrity and grid-relative residuals bounded while representing missing capacity with repeats; legacy encoder-limited output-slot drops are not required. Source FPS, encoder settings, fullscreen/tearing behavior, strict versus opportunistic tracks, artifact snapshots, and external-system-audio policy remain scenario-configurable.

Important interpretation: a `Final packet timeline` delta near zero proves file-tail alignment, but it does not prove content-level sync if earlier CFR timer debt was discarded, a WGC old slot selected future visual content, a source-start bootstrap trimmed content, or a track marker ends earlier than its peers. When investigating subjective late-video/audio-lag reports, inspect `TimerRebase`, live `Shortfall`, `CatchUp`, WGC `WgcSelBias`/`LeadExcess`, stop-drain logs, per-track bootstrap/trim/underrun logs, and waveform-tail marker spread. When investigating judder with clean A/V duration, inspect WGC/inject selected-frame age, unique-versus-duplicate ticks, fresh/repeat catch-up, and stale trims.

## Validation Notes

- `installed/captureengine/logs/audiodeath`, recording `r0001` (`capture_20260724T215403653Z_p15720_s2.mkv`, build `0.1.5180`, DXGI Duplication into 120 fps CFR, AV1 NVENC with lookahead/B-frames/multipass, deliberate encoder overload) is the reference case for consumer-overrun starvation. Every structural check passed: all three AAC tracks and video ended at exactly `11,888,000` samples / `247.666667 s`, `maxPacketDelta=0`, CFR coverage `29720/29720 missing=0`, `residual_samples=0`, `ratePpm=+0.00`, zero underruns/overruns/trims, and a clean post-mux probe. Audio was nevertheless almost entirely silent after about 40 s: `[STOP AUDIO TRACK]` showed `realMixed=3056000/1863200/3104000` against `fullSilence=8832000/10024800/8784000`, and `[STOP AUDIO DETAIL] overlap=` reached 9.36M-10.15M samples per source. `[AppDiag] place` pins the mechanism exactly — healthy until 23:50:23 (`placed == writeCursor`, `writeMinusEncoded≈2079`, `ringAvail≈2079`, `overlapTotal=161`), then from 23:50:33 onward permanently `pendingWriteSamples=0 ringAvail=0 writeMinusEncoded=0` with `overlapTotal` growing by exactly 480,000 samples per 10 s, i.e. 100% of the real audio discarded. `[AppDiag] consume` shows the trigger was a single ~67 ms over-consumption (`rb` 3349 -> 149 in one second at 23:50:24); after that `placed` stayed 2700-3500 samples (57-73 ms) behind the pinned write cursor forever. All five live sources (system loopback, microphone, and both Fortnite process-loopback routes) latched within two seconds of each other, so this is a consumer-side failure, not a producer one. No `[WARNING]`/`[ERROR]` line existed anywhere in the 3.8 MB media log, and `tools/analysis/analyze_capture_av.py` reported `audio=0` faults, which is why the class was invisible.
- The 2026-07-25 fix makes the reservoir adaptive and adds the missing evidence. Re-triage of that same session now reports `audio_ingest_starvation` and `ce_audio_timeline_fault` with `destroyed=48376521 samples (1007844.2 ms) sources=5` through the legacy `[STOP AUDIO DETAIL] overlap=` fallback, so pre-fix logs can no longer pass triage. Fresh runtime validation on a real overloaded capture is still required; the fix is proven at policy and log-evidence level only.
- `installed/captureengine/logs/fortiaudiodesync`, recording `r0008` / `capture_20260723T001702274Z_p11948_s2.mkv`, proved that exact endpoints do not protect content sync under sustained encoder overload: the old run reached `ShortfallMax=6558.3ms`, `TimelineDebtDrop=784`, repeatedly drove app routes to the `0.5%` drain cap, and accumulated roughly 292k samples of live audio backlog, yet final video and all three audio packet endpoints still matched exactly. The 2026-07-24 fix uses bounded held-repeat catch-up without a second wake-deadline advance, keeps source selection on the CFR output grid, and suppresses app-only backlog compensation during timeline recovery. Non-overload desktop→game sessions `20260724_185313` and `20260724_185601` then revalidated the diagnostic boundary: both had exact exported A/V, zero encoder/mux/audio/visual faults, real DXGI→WGC fallback, and expected game-launch/source-loading stalls; the latter's stop-only backlog is context. Build `0.1.5171` validated the scheduler/audio fix; build `0.1.5172` plus the exact-build gate passed product/package/PE verification, all 1,836 native tests, and all six Python tool self-tests.
- `installed/captureengine/logs/20260717_005930` (Fortnite DX12 borderless DirectFlip/VRR, 4K 10-bit 120 CFR inject, variable source FPS) had exact structural A/V output despite one brief overload: 14,693 contiguous video packets, every AAC track decoding to 5,877,200 samples / `122.4416667 s`, one-microsecond container rounding only, and no capture/mixer/resampler/worker loss marker. Its cadence telemetry nevertheless falsified the prior inject recovery claim: debt plateaued around 35-37 ticks, recovery emitted only repeats (`FreshCatchup=0`), and unique output remained around 60-76 frames/s while source and encode throughput could support more. The two root causes were raw two-output cycle duration feeding the slow-service gate and the extra catch-up output advancing the normal wake deadline. Build `0.1.5022` now normalizes service per output and separates the immutable output-QPC grid from backend wake cadence; final metadata `0.1.5023` passed all 1,649 native tests and all Python tool self-tests. Fresh equivalent runtime validation remains required because the original recording predates the fix.
- `installed/captureengine/logs/20260513_133907` showed packet-level and metadata duration alignment (`maxPacketDelta=1 us`, metadata `maxDelta=0 us`) but subjective end-of-video audio lag. The likely root cause was inject CFR timer debt deletion: the run ended with `TimerRebase=64`, so about 64 scheduled CFR ticks could be removed from the visual content timeline while audio stayed continuous.

- 2026-06-14 constant audio-late A/V offset investigation (from `installed/captureengine/logs/fortniteaudiodelayed`, WGC+ALAC, Fortnite): the recording was packet/zero-drift perfect (`maxPacketDelta=0`, `residual_samples=0`, `ratePpm=+0.00`) yet audio played slightly late. The pre-existing stimulus harness could NOT catch it because `tools/analysis/run_av_sync_matrix.py` applied a hidden method-aware "audio lead" (56 ms WGC / 45-50 ms inject) that deliberately cancels exactly this offset before the analyzer measures it. Added `--raw-offset-gate` (forces `--app-audio-lead-ms 0`) which measures the true offset, plus `--audio-capture-latency-ms` to write `[AudioSync] audio_capture_latency_ms` into the scenario config for validation, and device-period/buffer fields on the `[AudioCapture] Started` log. Measured offsets on the dev box at 120 fps (after the crackle fix below made the oracle reliable): WGC system loopback (192 kHz) ~72 ms, WGC app/process loopback (48 kHz) ~46 ms, inject ~39-47 ms; stable to ±1-2 ms. The offset is per-source (the 192 kHz system endpoint has ~26 ms more latency than 48 kHz process loopback).
- 2026-06-14 stimulus crackle fix (prerequisite for a reliable measurement oracle): `dx12_av_sync_test.exe` had developed audible crackling. Not a render underrun (`AVSYNC AUDIO_BUFFER ... underruns=0`) and not a schedule phase break (the tone is integer-cycles-per-1 s-segment, so segment boundaries are zero crossings). Root cause was `AudioRenderer::FillAudio` re-deriving `baseOffsetSeconds` from the audio device clock on EVERY buffer fill (`audioClockScheduling=1`), injecting a sub-ms phase jump each ~10 ms engine period. Fix (`testapp/dx12_av_sync_audio.h`): establish the stimulus-time phase anchor ONCE (from the audio clock / QPC) then advance the waveform phase monotonically by `sampleCursor_`. Verified: decoded audio went from continuous clicks to a single benign startup tick at ~0.15 s (before the 2 s analysis window); the analyzer's system-track per-event offset span collapsed from ~92 ms to ~8 ms and run-to-run offset variance from ±30 ms to ±1-2 ms. Regression test `AvSyncStimulusTest.AudioWaveformIsPhaseContinuousAcrossSegmentBoundaries`.
- 2026-06-16 offset fix IMPLEMENTED (commit f4651e1): delay VIDEO content by the configured loopback latency, leaving audio byte-exact (the constraints: you cannot advance live audio — earlier samples do not exist, so the pipeline pads silence and the encoded-cursor re-pins, absorbing it; delaying video is the only content-correct direction; audio latency is roughly per-source but on the same render endpoint the WGC system/app difference is within the ±half-frame measurement floor once the crackle is fixed, so a single delay = max source latency aligns all sources to ~0). Implementation:
  - WGC: `ce::capture_policy::GetWgcSelectionTargetQpc(..., extraSelectionDelayQpc)` — the configured delay IS the selection lag (it replaces the dormant `kWgcSelectionDelayTicks` one-tick delay when set). `ShouldApplyWgcSelectionDelay(..., contentDelayActive)` returns true for live recording when a content delay is configured, so the bias applies continuously and the bounded "too new for slot" hold self-builds/holds the delay buffer. The healthy path therefore keeps the full delay without help from a live-floor clamp; current `ClampWgcSelectionTargetToLiveQpc` deliberately leaves the output-grid target unchanged even under shortfall.
  - Inject (`bufferedInjectFrames`, pops oldest above a reserve): `minBufferedInjectFrames += ceil(L / frameInterval)`, with `maxBufferedInjectFrames` and `maxInjectLiveAgeQpc` widened so the retained frames are not trimmed; the oldest popped frame is then ~L old. Frame-quantized (whole frames) vs WGC's QPC-precise delay.
  - Config: per-source `capture_latency_ms` (falls back to `[AudioSync] audio_capture_latency_ms`); media_main computes `avContentDelayQpc` / `injectContentDelayFrames` from `max` enabled-source `captureLatencyMs`. 0 = no-op (default → zero behavior change; fast quick gate passes unchanged).
  - Validation (120 fps oracle, lead 0, latency 46): WGC + inject × ALAC/AAC/Opus offsets ~0 (from ~46 ms), cadence clean, all tracks `diff=+0`, `maxPacketDelta=0`, zero-drift; inter-track spread in the pre-existing 0–6 ms band. Measurement floor is ±half a video frame (±8.3 ms at 120 fps) because video content is frame-discrete; use the raw-offset gate at 120 fps with long runs and the mean as the oracle.
  - Diagnostics: `[EncoderThread] A/V content delay armed: ... method=wgc-selection-bias|inject-buffer-reserve injectDelayFrames=...` and `[A/V START] Audio source reset ... captureLatencyMs=` per source.

## UPDATE 2026-06-17 — per-device-domain latency model + render→loopback auto-detect (fixes the per-source regression)

The 2026-06-16 fix delayed video by `max(per-source captureLatencyMs)` and equalized faster sources up to it. Modeling latency PER-SOURCE was wrong and regressed real use (session `20260617_010909`, Fortnite/WGC): the user set `[Audio] capture_latency_ms=46` but `[General]=0`, so app process-loopback inherited 0 while system loopback got 46; equalization then delayed the game's app-loopback by 46 ms even though it shares the SAME render endpoint. Latency is a per-DEVICE-DOMAIN property:

- **Domain 1 = default render endpoint:** system loopback (`[SystemAudio]`/`[SystemAudio.N]`) + ALL `[AppAudio.N]` process-loopback → ONE value (`[AudioSync] audio_capture_latency_ms`). They all capture the same endpoint.
- **Domain 2 = each mic/input:** its own value (`[General] mic_capture_latency_ms` or per-mic `capture_latency_ms`). Mics no longer inherit the render-endpoint value (`common/config.cpp` mic fallback fixed). This is the regression fix.

**Auto-detection (no hardcoded device value — works automatically on any system):** `mediaengine/audio_latency_probe.{h,cpp}` renders a brief near-inaudible Hann marker to the default render endpoint and detects it in a loopback capture; latency = loopback marker-CENTER QPC − render-start marker-center QPC. It takes 5 independent shots and aggregates with `MedianWithConsistency` (≥3 within 8 ms) so a noisy reading cannot over/under-correct; no consensus → ok=false → NO correction applied and `[AVSyncAuto] confidence=low` is logged (graceful, never a guessed value). The resolved value is cached only in process memory, keyed by endpoint format and period metadata; CE must not create or update `audio_latency_cache.ini`, and legacy files are best-effort deleted at startup. The tradeoff is one near-inaudible probe per fresh CE process instead of persistent endpoint data on disk. The marker is low amplitude (`0.015`) and sample rates below 44.1 kHz are rejected as likely audible. `[AudioSync] audio_latency_autodetect` defaults true; the fresh profile explicitly uses `audio_capture_latency_ms=0`, meaning auto, while a manual value greater than zero disables the probe. `captureengine/media_main.cpp` measures once before `MediaEngine_Init` (not while recording) and re-applies the resolved value to render-domain sources on every config (re)load via the mediaengine export `MediaEngine_MeasureRenderEndpointLatency`. Do not ship a device-specific nonzero latency.

**No visible product calibration:** the old WGC/window-flash calibration code (`av_sync_calibrator.*`, `audio_av_calibration`) was removed on 2026-06-18. The DX12 A/V stimulus app and matrix harness remain test/validation tools only; normal product startup must not spawn windows or flash video to calibrate.

**Delay-only reconciliation:** `ApplyCaptureLatencyCompensation` (`audio_time_utils.h`) no longer advances live audio at the packet-placement sites in `audio_capture.cpp`/`app_audio_capture.cpp` (advancing is absorbed by the CFR pipeline and double-counts with the video delay on devices that report a nonzero `GetStreamLatency`). ALL latency flows through the video content delay + equalization. `streamLatency`, device period, packet duration, buffer depth, WASAPI QPC, and device position stay telemetry/passive model inputs. `[AVSyncApply]` shows WGC `wgc-selection-bias` or inject `inject-buffer-reserve` with reserve frames and residual estimate; `[AVSyncAuto] stop_summary` records final confidence/reason. The A/V harness writes `audio_latency_autodetect=false` so its explicit latency stays authoritative.

## Open Questions / Stale-Risk

- Normal local A/V iteration should start with the fast zero-drift quick gate, then the codec-finalization pass or targeted stress only when the touched code warrants it. Full matrix validation should remain part of release-level or high-risk A/V changes even though `20260612_200944` was green: run AAC, ALAC, FLAC, Opus, PCM at 60/120 fps across WGC and inject, plus focused stress runs for low source FPS, GPU load, and heavier 120 fps captures. Synthetic MKV analysis is final evidence; app logs and scenario-local CE log snapshots are mandatory diagnostics for every run.
- Fresh WGC and inject codec-matrix recordings should first be checked with `tools/analysis/run_av_sync_matrix.py` for content-level sync/smoothness, then with `tools/analysis/analyze_capture_av.py --full-scan --decode-check --waveform-tail-scan --strict-sync-events --max-audio-spread-ms 0 --max-video-audio-delta-ms 0 --max-audio-tail-marker-spread-ms 0 --max-log-event audio_extreme_drift=0 --max-cadence-metric wgc_sel_bias_abs_us=20000 --max-cadence-metric wgc_lead_excess_ms=250 --max-cadence-metric wgc_oldest_ms=250 --max-cadence-metric wgc_buffered_frames=32 --max-cadence-metric wgc_live_rebase_max_ticks=1 --max-cadence-metric wgc_phase_error_us=50000` for packet/log-level invariants. `wgc_visual_timeline_debt_drop`, `wgc_stale_visual_debt_drop`, `wgc_live_scheduler_rebase`, `wgc_encoder_limited_source_drop`, `wgc_post_stop_frame_drop`, and brief `wgc_shortfall_ms` excursions are warnings to inspect for visual smoothness impact; `wgc_stop_hold_repeats` and `wgc_drain_duplicate_summary` should be zero for WGC.
- If future diagnostics show equal packet durations but subjective drift, inspect whether the visual content timeline skipped CFR repeats, whether raw WGC timestamps exceed the predicted residual model, and whether decoded stimulus content agrees before changing audio correction policy.
- `tools/analysis/run_av_sync_matrix.py --sync-smoothness-gate --keep-going` is still the content-level gate for WGC active-delay/smoothness work. After the 2026-06-20 follow-up, the last known failing representative (`inject_aac_120fps_active_delay_encoder_pressure`) passed when rerun by itself at `installed/captureengine/avsync_runs/20260620_043138`: preflight-derived latency, zero corrupt/repeated marker frames, strict system/app offsets within target, inter-track spread `2.649 ms`, app-source `pad=0`, `ringUnderruns=0`, and exact track lengths. The full six-scenario gate was intentionally not rerun in that continuation to avoid duplicating the earlier multi-hour run; treat the targeted run as closure for the suspended final failing case, not release-level proof for every scenario.
- If future diagnostics show clean A/V packet duration but visible judder, compare `AgeAvg/AgeMax`, `InjectCatch`, `TargetHold/HoldWithCandidate`, `Superseded`, `BufferCapTrim`, `TargetResidualMax`, `TickUnique/TickDup`, and source FPS before changing encoder quality or audio policy.
- Fresh WGC/DXGI 4K120 overload validation should confirm that the overload pacer enters from measured pressure or existing shortfall, keeps `MaxRepeatRun` bounded, survives near-interval repeat-cost fluctuations, exits only after eight recovered decisions, and does not increase packet gaps, audio residuals, source-starvation attribution, or final endpoint spread. Repeat service above the frame interval remains fundamentally unsustainable, but degraded pacing should still preserve sparse fresh-frame liveness rather than adding an unbounded static run.
```

```md
# Code Style

Last cross-checked: 2026-07-28

Primary sources:
- `AGENTS.md`
- `tools/config/.clang-format`
- `tools/config/.flake8`
- `tools/config/pyrightconfig.json`
- `common/raii_helpers.h`
- representative headers such as `common/shared_defs.h`, `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h`, and `hook/wrappers/custom_hook.h`

## Scope
This page records the style rules that are either tool-backed or strongly reflected in the current tree. Local file conventions still win if a touched subsystem clearly uses a different established pattern.

## Tool-Backed Rules

### C++
- `tools/config/.clang-format` is based on Google style, but it is descriptive guidance for existing files rather than permission to rewrite them wholesale.
- Column limit is 120.
- Indent width is 4 spaces and tabs are disabled.
- Brace style is attached / K&R.
- Pointer and reference alignment is on the left.
- Include blocks are preserved.
- Include sorting is case-sensitive.
- `Standard: c++20`.

### Python
- `black` is run with `--line-length 120`.
- `flake8` max line length is 120.
- `flake8` ignores `E203`.
- `pyright` uses `typeCheckingMode: basic`.
- `pyright` targets Python 3.10 on Windows.
- `pyright` has `analyzeUnannotatedFunctions: true`.

### Bounded source fragments

- The governed source ceiling is 800 lines; the working target is ~750. Splits must follow semantic boundaries
  (one entity/module per file), never line-count cuts; `_part_NNN` fragments are retired.
- C++ modules are split into semantic `.cpp` units plus a generated `<module>_internal.h` that holds the hoisted
  includes, class forward declarations, prototypes of non-static functions, and shared file-scope state. Shared
  variables are renamed with a `<module>_` prefix (string/comment aware); shared static functions become `inline`
  at global scope (preserving overload resolution). Grouping JSONs under `build/refactor/` can also mark function
  chunks `destatic` (turning file-static functions into unique non-static units with header prototypes) and
  `hoist_regions` (hoisting `#if`-regions that hoisted classes depend on). See `tools/refactor/source_splitter.py`.
- Multi-unit test apps (e.g. `dx12_fg_switch_test`, `vulkan_fg_switch_test`) compile one object per unit and link
  them together via the per-source object paths in `tools/build/build_testapps.py`.
- A file that is genuinely one cohesive unit may exceed the ceiling and be registered in
  `tools/file_size_baseline.json` as deliberate debt; keep such entries rare.
- Python compatibility facades execute ordered fragments in one module-global namespace. This preserves direct scripts,
  `import build`, monkeypatching, constants, and CLI behavior. exec-facade unit files (the `<tool>_*.py` families, `build_*.py`, `source_splitter_*.py`) are excluded from standalone flake8/
  pyright discovery because their names/imports intentionally come from neighboring fragments; source reassembly tests,
  `compileall`, facade execution, and the full verification gate cover the logical program.
- Before accepting a split, compare logical source reassembly, inspect symbol/state ownership, run focused tests, and use
  `--verify` for build, parser/configuration, media/capture, audio, graphics, or FG changes. The clang-tidy ratchet
  must stay at zero warnings; NOLINT comments must stay attached to their statements.

## Common Tree Conventions
- Headers generally use `#pragma once`.
- Standard and platform headers use angle brackets. Project headers use quotes.
- Types and most C++ functions and methods are usually `PascalCase`.
- Local variables and parameters are usually `camelCase`.
- Python functions and variables are usually `snake_case`.
- Globals often use a `g_` prefix.
- Many constants use `kName`. ABI and shared constants also use all-caps names such as `SHARED_MEMORY_VERSION`.
- Fixed-width integers are common in shared-memory, hook, and ABI-sensitive code.
- `enum class` is common when introducing new enums.
- Match the touched file's local naming and member-style convention instead of renaming neighbors.

## Existing Helper Patterns
- Common RAII helpers already live in `common/raii_helpers.h`: `HandleGuard`, `MappingGuard`, `VirtualAllocGuard`, `ComGuard`, and `ScopeGuard`.
- Hooking code is not one-size-fits-all in this tree. Current subsystems use wrapper hooks plus typed hook helpers such as `HookSystem::TypedHook` and `CustomHook::TypedHook`. Match the local subsystem pattern instead of forcing a global hook abstraction rewrite.

## Practical Notes
- Do not run `clang-format.exe -i`, `python build.py --format`, or another whole-file automatic formatter on existing source unless explicitly requested. The current tree contains legacy formatting and mixed stored line endings; an in-place whole-file pass can create large unrelated diffs even when the intended edit is narrow.
- Preserve the touched file's existing formatting and line endings. Inspect `git diff --check` and the semantic `git diff` before building.
- Perform the required full build once after the final code change set, not after every intermediate edit. Stage only task-owned paths; use `git add -A` only when every worktree change has been verified task-owned and safe.
- Scope dump analysis, LSP cleanup, and wiki edits to the task/touched area. Update the wiki only for durable future-useful knowledge, and keep diagnostic logging high-signal and rate-limited.
- Formatter configuration values are high confidence as style guidance, but automatic whole-file conformance is intentionally not assumed.
- Naming and local-pattern guidance is medium confidence and should be re-checked against the files you touch.
- If formatter output, local file style, and this page disagree, preserve the local subsystem's established pattern unless the user explicitly requested a formatting migration.

### Current clang-tidy debt and triage

As of 2026-08-06 the clang-tidy baseline is **zero warnings** across 552 translation
units. Remaining analyzer findings are either fixed at the root or carry a targeted
`NOLINT` comment with a concrete rationale; checks are never disabled globally. See
`known-debt.md` for the category-by-category disposition.

`run_tests()` captures the executable's stdout/stderr and, on failure, writes `unit_tests_failure.log` into the verification bundle while logging the diagnostic tail. This is required because an exit code without the failing GoogleTest name is not actionable.
```

```md
# Configuration

Last cross-checked: 2026-08-09

Primary sources:
- `captureengine/config.ini.template`
- `captureengine/captureengine.rc`
- `common/config_resource.h`
- `common/config.{h,cpp}`
- `common/monitor_selection.{h,cpp}`
- `common/screen_grab_privacy.{h,cpp}`
- `captureengine/media_main.cpp`
- `captureengine/screen_grab_privacy_runtime.{h,cpp}`
- `tests/config_template.rc`
- `tests/test_config.cpp`
- `tests/test_config_override.cpp`
- `tests/test_monitor_selection.cpp`
- `testapp/run_tests.py`

## Summary

`captureengine/config.ini.template` is the only authored first-run configuration. The CaptureEngine executable embeds its exact UTF-8 bytes as `RCDATA`; `CreateDefaultConfig` writes that resource only when `config.ini` is absent. The unit-test executable embeds the same resource and proves the generated file is byte-for-byte identical to the source template. The integration-test harness also reads the same template when it must create a temporary config.

An existing `config.ini` is never merged or replaced automatically. Active values in the template define the fresh-user profile. Parser fallbacks for keys missing from an older file are compatibility behavior and can intentionally differ from that explicit fresh profile; changing the template therefore does not silently migrate existing installations.

## First-run creation invariants

- Product and tests compile the same `captureengine/config.ini.template` into their executable resource tables under `IDR_DEFAULT_CONFIG`.
- Creation uses `CREATE_NEW`, so simultaneous processes cannot overwrite a file another process just created.
- A partial/failed write is removed. A missing resource fails safely and leaves ordinary parser fallbacks available; it does not synthesize a second hardcoded template.
- Any new or renamed documented option belongs in the template plus focused semantic tests. Do not reintroduce a raw config string in `common/config.cpp`.
- Options deliberately kept out of the user-facing profile, including compatibility-only VFR paths, remain parser-supported only when there is a specific reason.

## Current section layout and compatibility

- Fresh configs group capture selection in `[Capture]`, ordinary WGC behavior in `[WGC]`, file locations/container in `[Output]`, scaling in `[VideoScaling]`, DLSS overrides in `[DLSS]`, audio timing in `[AudioSync]`, logging in `[Logging]`, and troubleshooting switches in `[Diagnostics]`.
- `[DesktopOverlay]` is the canonical name for the non-injected screen-corner window. `[Overlay]` remains the injected overlay. Any `[DesktopOverlay]` setting can be qualified inside a process-backed application profile, for example `DesktopOverlay.mode=1`.
- `[Audio]` contains shared encoding defaults. `[SystemAudio]` and `[SystemAudio.N]` describe render-output sources; `[Microphone]` / `[Microphone.N]` describe inputs. New per-application audio belongs in the application's `[Profile.*]` section beside its video/injection route and setting overrides. `[AppAudio.N]` remains readable for existing configs.
- Existing locations remain aliases: `[General]`, `[Scaling]`, `[Screenshot]`, `[pseudo-overlay]`, `[Audio]` source keys, `[Audio.N]`, DLSS keys in `[Graphics]`, and `copy_queue_priority` in `[Performance]`. The new location wins when both are present, including an intentionally empty canonical value.
- Canonical profiles are named `[Profile.<label>]` sections with no fixed numeric limit; `[Profile.1]` remains valid. `process` is the executable selector and always matches the complete executable name, case-insensitively. `window_title` can refine the chosen window or stand alone for WGC/DXGI routing. `window_match=exact|contains|contains_or_class` controls only the title match; the last form also checks the window class. Injection and app audio require a process name.
- `video_capture=inherit|inject|wgc|dxgi_dup|none` chooses the application's video source and determines normal DLL behavior. `inject` implies full injection for video, the injected overlay, and graphics overrides; it needs no second setting. WGC, DXGI Duplication, and `none` do not normally inject. `inherit` follows `[Capture] capture_method`; global `auto` normally resolves to injected capture. The older `global` and `default` values remain aliases for `inherit`.
- `dll_injection` is optional and only overrides that normal relationship. `always` also injects for WGC, DXGI Duplication, or a profile with no video so the injected overlay and graphics overrides remain available. `never` blocks injection; if the resolved video source is inject, the profile fails closed to no video route. `when_needed` remains accepted as an explicit spelling of the default source-driven behavior, but fresh examples omit it. A new profile that omits `video_capture` contributes no video target even with `dll_injection=always`; this keeps overlay-only profiles independent from video routing.
- The older `injection_mode=capture|overlay|none` and `injection=normal|inject|overlay|none` spellings remain compatibility inputs with their exact historical behavior. `dll_injection` wins when both schemas are present. Legacy injection settings can still imply the inherited video route when `video_capture` is absent; legacy `[App.*]` sections still imply capture injection.
- Fresh configs no longer contain `[Injection] whitelist`, `overlay_whitelist`, or `wgc_window_detection`. The loader still reads them for compatibility and converts profile routes into the same internal runtime lists. A canonical profile removes legacy entries for the same process/window before its route is added, including a `none` route. Overlapping profiles are diagnosed and the later profile wins; a canonical profile wins over an overlapping legacy `[App.*]` section.
- The profile reference explains the source-driven default before the optional DLL override. Three commented examples cover DXGI Duplication plus DesktopOverlay/app audio with an optional `never` safety lock, injected video without a redundant DLL setting, and DXGI Duplication with `always` for the injected overlay/graphics overrides. They use distinct executable names and do not create active default profiles.

## Important user-facing semantics

- `capture_method` selects the global video acquisition policy, not whether a process is injected. A profile can therefore request WGC/DXGI video with `dll_injection=always` for the injected overlay and graphics overrides; hook-side video publication stays disabled while the screen-grab backend is active.
- `[Capture] monitor=auto|primary|window|cursor|id:<stable-id>` selects the physical display for monitor-scope WGC/DXGI capture. `auto` resolves the known target window first, then an eligible foreground window, then the Windows primary display. `window` requires a matched target window; `cursor` is resolved once when recording starts. `CaptureEngine.exe --list-monitors` prints copyable DisplayConfig-backed IDs. A profile may use bare `monitor=` or `Capture.monitor=`. Explicit selectors fail closed if unavailable and never redirect capture to another display; DXGI may still fall back to WGC for the same resolved monitor. One recording has one monitor source; arbitrary multi-monitor compositing is not implemented.
- `[Capture] black_when_no_fullscreen_focus=false` is an opt-in, best-effort WGC/DXGI privacy mask and supports `Capture.black_when_no_fullscreen_focus=true` in a profile. Window capture reveals only when that exact root window is foreground and fullscreen-like; monitor capture reveals only when the foreground fullscreen-like window occupies the selected monitor. Missing, changing, or ambiguous state produces opaque black, including cursor and overlays. Audio capture, timestamps, CFR/VFR scheduling, synchronization, and finalization continue. Windows can briefly misreport focus or bounds, so this is not a guaranteed privacy/redaction boundary and can mask or reveal incorrectly. The check uses documented passive window-state APIs and does not inspect or interact with the captured process. For anti-cheat-sensitive use, the profile must still select WGC/DXGI and set `dll_injection=never`; the mask itself does not make an injected profile safe or claim universal anti-cheat approval.
- Use qualified keys such as `Video.encoder` or `Graphics.vsync_mode` in `[Profile.*]`. Profile-local app audio uses the unambiguous `audio_enabled`, `audio_track`, `audio_codec`, `audio_bitrate`, `audio_sample_rate`, `audio_bit_depth`, `audio_downmix`, and `audio_capture_latency_ms` keys. Named profiles and their app-audio sources are not capped at eight. A numeric profile with `audio_enabled` still shadows the same-numbered legacy `[AppAudio.N]`; bare override keys remain compatible but can be ambiguous because several sections use names such as `enabled`, `bitrate`, or `track`.
- Process-backed profiles can override every `[DesktopOverlay]` setting with qualified keys. While idle, the controller-side overlay follows the foreground profile. Once a video/audio recording starts it pins that profile so Alt+Tab does not change the indicator's mode, position, or appearance midway through the session; an actual injected-video source PID supersedes the provisional foreground selection.
- `[DesktopOverlay] show_encoder_overload_warnings=true` is the fresh-template and parser default. It covers sustained encoder/mux pressure, immutable-CFR recovery debt, and a latched video-degraded result; it never changes or downgrades encoder settings. Existing configs that explicitly set `false` remain authoritative.
- Every process-backed application profile with a video route is automatically a `NOT RECORDING` warning target. `[DesktopOverlay] process_list` is now a global compatibility fallback for older configs and extra unprofiled processes; it is not needed beside a video profile. Profiles with `video_capture=none` do not become warning targets merely because they configure app audio.
- Logical audio track IDs are `1..255`. A source can fan out to several IDs, duplicate IDs within one list are discarded, and different sources sharing an ID are mixed. Capturing one application through both system loopback and profile/legacy app audio on the same track can duplicate the signal and produce comb filtering.
- `sample_rate=default` means 48000 Hz; Opus always uses 48000 Hz. `bit_depth=default` means 24-bit for ALAC, FLAC, and PCM, while AAC and Opus ignore it. `downmix=false` preserves the main source layout and `true` converts the track to stereo.
- Video `color_space=auto` follows the captured source contract. Explicit `bt709` defines an SDR file and tone-maps HDR/scRGB or packed PQ input before BT.709 encoding; it never only relabels HDR pixels. Explicit `bt2020` preserves an HDR source as BT.2020/PQ but selects SDR BT.2020 transfer characteristics for an SDR source rather than falsely tagging those pixels as PQ. Fresh configs use `bit_depth=auto`, which selects 10-bit for HDR and 8-bit for ordinary SDR; old files are not auto-migrated. HDR output requires HEVC or AV1 through NVENC/AMF/QSV, while H.264 HDR and Media Foundation HDR fail closed. `[Video] hdr_nominal_peak_nits=1000` is the configurable 100-10000-nit mastering/content-light compatibility ceiling. It is intentionally nominal because composed screen capture has no measured mastering/MaxCLL/MaxFALL data.
- `[Screenshot] color_space=auto|bt709` is independent of the video setting. `auto` preserves HDR as 10-bit BT.2020/PQ AVIF and saves SDR as PNG; `bt709` tone-maps any HDR source to an ordinary BT.709/sRGB PNG. Missing or invalid values fall back to `auto`. The option is present in the first-run template, but existing configs are intentionally not auto-merged; add the section explicitly when migrating an installed config.
- NVENC `lookahead` is deliberately not Boolean: it accepts `off`, `auto`, or a depth from `1` through `31`. `spatial_aq` and `temporal_aq` are independent Booleans, and `aq_strength` applies only to spatial AQ (`0` asks NVENC to choose, otherwise `1..15`).
- NVENC `split_encode=0..4` controls native single-session split-frame encoding for HEVC and AV1. `0` explicitly disables it and is the fresh/default policy; `1` forces splitting when multiple engines exist and lets the driver choose the strip count; `2..4` request that many physical encoder strips when available. H.264 accepts only `0`. The former `auto`, `disabled`, and `forced` spellings remain compatibility inputs for existing configs, where `auto` retains NVIDIA's preset/tuning/resolution policy. Splitting favors throughput over a small amount of compression efficiency; it is not multiple independent recordings or GOP concatenation.
- NVIDIA Smooth Motion compatibility is detected and applied automatically. There is no user-facing compatibility switch; failures must be fixed in the detection/compatibility code.
- `[DLSS] force_ray_reconstruction=on` is an opt-in injected x64 UE5 override. It persistently selects the existing
  NVIDIA plugin's `r.NGX.DLSS.DenoiserMode=1` read without changing Engine.ini; legacy `[Graphics]` and qualified
  `DLSS.force_ray_reconstruction` profile input remain supported. It cannot add an absent RR integration or render
  inputs and does not falsify runtime capability/support results.
- `msaa_samples`, `sgssaa`, and `disable_auto_mip_bias` remain parser/runtime-compatible graphics overrides but are intentionally absent from the fresh template. They are specialized legacy controls rather than useful defaults.
- Default-render system loopback and process loopback share one render latency domain. Per-source latency differences within that domain recreate an A/V mismatch. Microphones use the separate input latency domain. Fresh configs disable microphone capture for privacy/predictability.
- Empty video and screenshot output directories both resolve to the `captures` directory beside the executable. The two paths are independent when customized. `crash_dump_dir` accepts only a safe relative subfolder beneath `logs`; absolute and parent-traversal paths are ignored.
- An empty optional hotkey disables it. `start_stop` is the exception and falls back to F9 so recording cannot be left without a toggle.
- Choosing `video_capture=inject` or `dll_injection=always` can trigger anti-cheat protection. Do not use either for multiplayer/anti-cheat software unless injection is known to be permitted; `never` remains available as an explicit safety lock.
- Desktop-overlay mode 2 is warning-only. With the shipped mode 2 profile there is no steady recording dot.
- `[Overlay] copy_queue_priority` controls the injected D3D12 overlay's DIRECT queue priority, not a copy queue. The key name is retained for compatibility.

## Validation boundary

- User-facing booleans accept `true/false`, `1/0`, `yes/no`, and `on/off`; malformed values use the documented fallback and emit a rate-limited warning.
- `force_ray_reconstruction` defaults off, is live-reloadable, and is published through an existing shared-config
  alignment gap; static offset/size assertions keep the shared-memory ABI unchanged.
- Audio track lists accept unique IDs from `1` through `255`; invalid entries are ignored and an entirely invalid list uses its section default.
- Overlay padding, font size, corner radius, alpha, outline thickness, and text-update interval have finite documented bounds. Pseudo-overlay geometry/mode/grace values also fall back rather than being silently clamped to a different edge value.
- Overlay colors are exactly six hexadecimal RGB digits with an optional leading `#`; malformed strings use the documented palette fallback.

## Diagnostics / stale-risk

- Windows INI lookup is case-insensitive. The manual compatibility parser also accepts either case for `[Injection]`, `[DesktopOverlay]`, and legacy `[pseudo-overlay]`; multiline key spellings and semicolon comments should still follow the old syntax when maintaining an existing file.
- Resource parity is proven in the native config suite. Any new build path that links `common/config.cpp` and can create a config must also provide the resource or explicitly establish that creation is not its responsibility.
- Config annotations are a broad surface and can drift as behavior changes. When changing capture, audio, graphics, overlay, output, or performance behavior, check this page and the authoritative template rather than updating parser comments alone.
- Title-only profiles can route WGC/DXGI video, but arbitrary per-app setting overrides (including `DesktopOverlay.*`) require `process`, matching the general profile override contract.

## Verification

- The focused config/profile/pseudo-overlay/injected-overlay gate covers generated-template parity, the fullscreen-focus blackout default/global/profile parsing and warning annotation, source-driven WGC/DXGI behavior, injection overrides, safe invalid-value fallback, compatibility-key precedence, overlay-only profiles, legacy behavior, and all three commented examples. Focused config plus encoder-option coverage additionally passes the NVENC split-encode parser/default and planning matrix.
- Clean product build `0.1.5105` passed x64/x86 hooks, MediaEngine/CaptureEngine, 149 unit-test objects, 30 test apps, both Vulkan layers, packaging, import closure, PE mitigations, effective CFG, architecture, and PDB checks.
- The exact `0.1.5105` no-build gate passed the complete native suite and all six Python tool self-tests.
```
