It preserves the fresh post-FSR Streamline `scQueue`, clears the unsafe `GetState`-only suppressions on the explicit `SetOptions(ON)` edge, keeps startup Presents on the normal route with `callbackOnNormal=1`, later reaches ECL expiry activation, and eventually still confirms rendering. The problem is that the same live comeback gets restarted before first confirmation: after `DX12: FG transition cooldown complete — preserving half-armed synthetic PostSL startup state until confirmed render`, GTA immediately logs `DX12: Scene transition detected (gap=46254ms) during FG — overlay cooldown 30 frames`, routing diagnostics later show `postSLCallback=1 postSLActive=0`, and the same session does a second `DX12: PostSL REACTIVATED (epoch=2 ...)` before the first visible `Post-SL overlay SUBMIT #1`. Talos on its matching post-FSR DLSS comeback path reaches `postsl-activation-complete`, `PostSL REACTIVATED (epoch=1 ...)`, and the first `Post-SL overlay SUBMIT` without that extra restart.
- The current tree now extends the generic cooldown preservation rule to already active half-armed PostSL startup too. `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` adds `ShouldPreserveActivePostSLDuringFGCooldown(...)`, and `hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp` now uses it in both the outer late-ON preservation seam and the inner ProcessFrame FG cooldown countdown. The generic rule is: once a post-FSR DLSS comeback has already promoted PostSL into the active-but-unconfirmed startup state, later generic FG cooldown bookkeeping must keep that same path alive until first confirmation instead of dropping it back to inactive. Otherwise CE can restart the same live comeback into a second reactivation epoch and unnecessarily lengthen the invisible-overlay window even though queue ownership, startup routing, and explicit activation provenance were already correct.
- Current DX12 overlay policy code treats a runtime-owned swapchain alone as insufficient proof of FSR FG. That matters because GTA can keep a runtime-owned swapchain during non-FSR windows, and misclassifying that state can break post-FSR or post-DLSS recovery.
- GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260417_024338` on build `0.1.2367` showed that mixed-runtime startup handoffs can also hide the visible overlay without any FG activation or device loss if the post-startup resume gate stays too tied to the exact swapchain HWND. In that session CE rendered normally first, then a later authoritative runtime-owned Streamline no-FG handoff re-armed startup compatibility, the queue topology settled, and CE logged `Resuming DX12 overlay after startup overlay windows settled`. But instead of progressing into the old GTA resource-prime / first-draw-probe sequence, it stayed in `Keeping overlay rendering deferred after startup-overlay resume ... (remaining=0ms)` forever.
- GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260420_225446_gtanocrash_startedwithnofgoverlaydoesnotshow` on build `0.1.2495` refined that same startup-resume seam further. The earlier same-process-foreground acceptance was directionally right, but the no-FG session still proved the countdown could fail to start at all: CE only evaluated a usable same-process foreground window after `elapsedSinceResumeReady >= settleMs`, yet `elapsedSinceResumeReady` itself only grows after a stable foreground candidate has already been chosen. When the exact swapchain HWND was no longer foreground and the same-process foreground window was the only viable resume candidate, the timer kept resetting and the session latched forever on `remaining=0ms`. The current tree now resolves the candidate first, then runs the countdown against either the exact swapchain HWND or the usable same-process foreground window. New logs now show both failure and success sides of that boundary: `Startup-overlay resume still waiting for a usable foreground window ...` when no viable candidate exists yet, and `Startup-overlay resume tracking usable same-process foreground window ...` when CE intentionally starts the countdown on a different same-process foreground window instead of the old swapchain HWND.
- Current DX12 overlay policy comments repeatedly preserve queue and recovery choices specifically to avoid Talos device-removed paths and stale-overlay teardown behavior during mixed FSR and DLSS transitions.
- Effective FSR runtime mode is now also used as the guard for SL routing suppression. That prevents a stale SL hook from re-activating Present routing after FSR takeover.
- Runtime-owned native FSR FG must not use the old separate injected DX12 `FG overlay SUBMIT` path on the FFX-owned queue. That path was the one observed freezing in GTA V Enhanced.
- Native FSR FG now has a runtime-cooperative path: CE chains FFX's own `presentCallback` from `ffxConfigure()` and renders the overlay on the FFX-supplied command list / output surface instead of issuing a separate injected queue submission.
- The FFX callback bridge preserves the runtime's own default composition callback when the game does not provide one, then renders CE's overlay on top of the callback's output surface.
- The callback-side runtime-owned FSR setup path now also treats stored swapchain pointers as weak evidence only. Talos `installed/captureengine/logs/20260421_182513_taloscrash_dlssfgtofsrfgcrash` on build `0.1.2510` showed the crash boundary precisely after native-FSR `configure-on`, callback composition-contract logging, and callback-backend `InitDX12`, but before the usual later `initialized overlay adapter` / callback-render lines. The healthy Talos comparison `installed/captureengine/logs/20260421_165756_talosnocrash_multipleswitching` reaches that same boundary and immediately continues. The current tree now captures trusted callback HDR/color-space state from the live `ffxConfigure(... swapChain=...)` pointer while the runtime is still explicitly handing CE a current swapchain object, and the later callback thread consumes only that cached trusted state instead of probing DXGI output state through raw non-AddRef'd swapchain globals after takeover.
- The FFX callback path must also classify HDR the same way the normal DX12 overlay path does. `DXGI_FORMAT_R10G10B10A2_UNORM` is ambiguous: it can be HDR10/PQ or plain 10-bit SDR. Talos `installed/captureengine/logs/20260419_221615` on build `0.1.2464` showed why this matters. The normal Talos overlay path on the same `fmt=24` target stayed visually correct, but the native-FSR callback path looked dim because it had been treating `R10G10B10A2_UNORM` as automatically HDR and therefore PQ-encoding overlay colors even when the output color space was still SDR. The current tree now shares the same rule in both paths: FP16 is always HDR, 10-bit UNORM probes the real DXGI output color space, and only true HDR/PQ color spaces enable HDR overlay rendering there.
- If neither an explicit game callback nor the runtime's default composition callback is available, the bridge now does exactly one fallback `currentBackBuffer -> outputSwapChainBuffer` copy before overlay rendering. It must not also repeat that copy inside the render helper. GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260417_020859` on build `0.1.2363` exposed that code/wiki drift directly: every `ffxConfigure` logged `originalPresent=0000000000000000`, the callback path still rendered repeatedly on the runtime-owned FSR swapchain, and the dump again showed the AMD FSR presenter/interpolation threads blocked in `amd_fidelityfx_dx12!ffxQuery` immediately afterward.
- The native-FSR callback bridge now also logs two callback-side diagnostics that matter for future visual investigations: `DX12: FFX present callback HDR check ... colorSpace=... isHDR=...` shows the callback-side HDR decision boundary, and `DX12: FFX present callback composition contract ... premulAlpha=%d` shows whether the FFX callback attached the premultiplied-alpha extension for UI composition on that path.
- The generic invariant for runtime-owned callback setup is now: callback threads may consume cached trusted swapchain/HDR facts captured earlier from a live swapchain, but they must not depend on weak raw COM pointer lifetime for late callback-side classification. Runtime-owned native-FSR callback rendering can legitimately outlive the last normal tracked swapchain object.
- GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260420_021433_gtacrash_dlssfgtofsrfg` on build `0.1.2472` refined the remaining `DLSS_FG -> FSR_FG` freeze family further. The decisive difference from Talos is not that GTA fails to reach the callback path at all. GTA still reaches authoritative FFX takeover on `queue=000002600B5AA0F0`, spends hundreds of `enabled=0` callbacks on the no-runtime-composition fallback-copy path (`originalPresent=resolvedPresent=null`), then reaches live native-FSR enable at `frameID=621-623`, initializes the callback backend on `fmt=87`, and successfully renders several callback frames (`DX12: FFX present callback rendered overlay on runtime-owned FSR path` for generated and non-generated frames). The later dump again shows the `AMD FSR Interpolation Thread` and `AMD FSR Presenter Thread` blocked in `amd_fidelityfx_dx12!ffxQuery`.
- The surviving mismatch is queue-authority drift at the create-swapchain seam before that callback run. In the GTA session, the later FFX-owned queue `000002600B5AA0F0` was first captured on a path that still also carried stale Streamline runtime evidence, so CE treated it as an authoritative Streamline runtime queue and hooked its `ExecuteCommandLists` vtable (`Hooking authoritative Streamline runtime queue vtable 000002600B5AA0F0`) before authoritative FFX takeover finished. Talos's no-crash rerun captures its FFX-owned queue `000001EB5995C4C0` directly onto the generic FFX/native-FSR path instead and logs `Skipping vtable hook for FG runtime queue ... — preserving FSR timing`. Because the queue-vtable detour is exactly the timing-sensitive overhead the code comments already call out as able to stall native FSR inside `ffxQuery`, stale Streamline provenance was still enough to reintroduce the old native-FSR deadlock family on GTA even though the callback backend itself was otherwise correct.
- The current tree now lets current FFX ownership win over stale Streamline provenance on the same non-origGame queue. `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` adds `ShouldTreatSwapchainQueueAsAuthoritativeFFXRuntime(...)`, and `hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp` now computes FFX and Streamline queue authority separately inside `CaptureSwapchainQueueFromCreateDevice(...)`. If FFX already owns the queue, CE no longer promotes that queue into the Streamline startup-handoff family, no longer arms the Streamline startup window from that queue capture, and `ShouldHookSwapchainQueueVTableForFrameGenerationRuntime(...)` now forces `false` for FFX-owned runtime queues even when stale Streamline authority is also present. New logs now distinguish the generic FSR skip from the mixed-authority case: `Authoritative FFX ownership overrides stale Streamline runtime queue authority ...` plus `Skipping vtable hook for FFX-owned runtime queue ... despite stale Streamline provenance ...`.
- GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260420_121020_gtacrash_dlssfgtofsrfgcrash` on build `0.1.2482` narrowed the remaining `DLSS_FG -> FSR_FG` crash family one step further after that queue-authority fix. GTA no longer reopens the old stale-Streamline queue-hook path: it now logs the mixed-authority override, skips queue-vtable hooking on the FFX-owned queue, reaches authoritative FFX takeover, spends hundreds of `enabled=0` callbacks on the fallback-copy path with `originalPresent=resolvedPresent=null`, then enables native FSR at `frameID=667-669` and successfully renders several runtime-owned callback frames (`frameId=668-674`). - The surviving mismatch was Present-routing ownership during that native-FSR runtime-owned window. GTA still correctly logs `SL routing DISABLED ...` at authoritative FFX takeover, but later in the same runtime-owned teardown window it logs `SL routing ACTIVE ... SL FG chain will execute` again even though native FSR still owns the swapchain and is only publishing explicit `enabled=0` teardown callbacks. CE only force-disables Streamline routing again once native FSR is already actively rendering callback frames. Talos on the same build does not show that mid-window Streamline Present-routing re-activation on its FSR path.
- The current tree now makes the native-FSR Present-routing guard follow ownership of the Present path, not just the later `runtime=FSR_FG` label. `hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp` exports `HookHasRuntimeOwnedNativeFGPresentPath()`, which stays true while the swapchain is runtime-owned and either authoritative native FSR is active or CE is still inside the explicit `ffxConfigure(frameGenerationEnabled=0)` teardown window. `hook/common/dxgi_shared.h` now adds `ShouldKeepSLPresentRoutingDisabledForNativeFG(...)`, and `hook/common/dxgi_shared.cpp` now uses that stronger predicate in all four relevant seams: re-enabling Streamline Present routing from `DetectSLPresentHook()`, the top-level `Present` routing latch, the `Present1` routing latch, and the runtime force-disable logs. The generic invariant is that once native/runtime-owned FSR owns presentation, Streamline's Present-hook chain must stay detached until that ownership really ends; a temporary `Off` configure edge during runtime-owned teardown is not sufficient proof that it is safe to re-attach Streamline routing.
- GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260420_171341_gtacrash_fsrfgcrashonsuspend` on build `0.1.2489` exposed a different native-FSR suspend/resume seam after those queue-ownership and Present-routing fixes. GTA's initial FSR run is healthy on the same `originalPresent=resolvedPresent=null` fallback-copy callback path, but after the temporary menu suspension at `17:15:20` the session logs a second `DX12: FFX present callback initialized overlay adapter for runtime-owned FSR ...` right before the freeze, and the dump again shows the `AMD FSR Interpolation Thread`, `AMD FSR Presenter Thread`, and another GTA worker thread blocked in `amd_fidelityfx_dx12!ffxQuery`. - The current tree now treats that backend churn as another generic native-FSR ownership invariant: normal pre-SL overlay cleanup must not tear down the dedicated runtime-owned FFX callback backend while the runtime-owned native-FG Present path still owns presentation. `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` adds `ShouldPreserveFFXPresentCallbackBackendDuringNormalOverlayCleanup(...)`, `hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp` now lets `CleanupOverlay(...)` optionally keep `g_FFXPresentOverlayAdapter` / `g_FFXPresentRtvHeap` alive, and the ProcessFrame stale-normal-overlay cleanup path now uses that preserve mode while `HookHasRuntimeOwnedNativeFGPresentPath()` remains true. New logs now distinguish warm-backend reuse from cold init (`preserving native FSR present-callback overlay backend during normal overlay cleanup ...` and `Reusing FFX present callback overlay adapter ...`), so future GTA/Talos suspend traces show whether CE stayed on the proven callback backend instead of re-initializing it mid-suspension.
- GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260420_215628_gtacrash_fsrfgcrashonresume` on build `0.1.2491` then showed the next narrower suspend/resume seam after that warm-backend fix. The bad session no longer logs a second callback-backend init during the menu suspend/resume family, so the old callback-backend churn really is gone. But GTA still freezes, and the dump again lands in the native-FSR `amd_fidelityfx_dx12!ffxQuery` worker-thread family. The new divergence is overlay ownership during the explicit native-FSR OFF teardown window, not callback-backend lifecycle anymore. During that long runtime-owned `enabled=0` window GTA logs `ProcessFrame - preserving native FSR present-callback overlay backend ...`, then immediately rebuilds the normal injected DX12 overlay on the same runtime-owned FFX queue (`[Overlay] Initializing DX12 backend ... queue=000001DB002444D0`). After native FSR later re-enables at `frameID=1615+`, the trace ends before any resumed callback-render line appears.
- The current tree now extends the same runtime-owned native-FG Present ownership invariant to separate injected overlay GPU work. `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` now teaches both `ShouldSkipSeparateOverlayGpuWorkForRuntimeOwnedFrameGeneration(...)` and `ShouldDisableDedicatedOverlayQueueForRuntimeOwnedFrameGeneration(...)` about `runtimeOwnedNativeFGPresentPath`, and `hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp` now feeds `HookHasRuntimeOwnedNativeFGPresentPath()` through those policy seams. The bridge predicate `ShouldBridgeOverlayViaFFXPresentCallback(...)` now also follows that stronger ownership helper instead of only the literal `runtime=FSR_FG` label. The generic rule is: once the runtime-owned native-FG Present path owns presentation, CE must stay on the runtime-cooperative callback-owned overlay path for that full ownership window, including the temporary explicit `ffxConfigure(frameGenerationEnabled=0)` teardown phase. A temporary `Off` configure edge is not sufficient proof that it is safe to fall back to the separate injected DX12 overlay path on the same FFX-owned queue.
- Short-run GTA V Enhanced validation in `installed/captureengine/logs/20260411_233821` confirms the current runtime-owned native FSR path no longer reproduces the immediate crash with the overlay active: the log shows authoritative FFX takeover, `FG publication` switching to `runtime=FSR_FG active=1`, repeated `DX12: FFX present callback rendered overlay on runtime-owned FSR path` entries, and no non-zero device-removal, watchdog-fire, or crash markers.
- That confirmation is still scoped to a short manual run. It proves the current approach survives the previously failing GTA V Enhanced overlay + FSR FG case, but it is not yet a long-soak guarantee.
- GTA V Enhanced `FSR -> DLSS` can drive native FFX teardown through `ffxDestroyContext()` while the inline-hook trampoline is still in use. The `20260412_011505` crash bundle showed the destroy trampoline at `00007FF8011D0300` copying `test rcx, rcx; jne +0x0B` from `amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll` without relocating that short branch. When GTA destroyed the FFX context during the handoff, the taken `jne` landed inside the trampoline's appended `FF 25` jump stub data and crashed with a null write at `00007FF8011D031B`.
- Inline-hook trampolines must therefore treat short control transfers that leave the copied block as relocations, not raw memcpy. This is a generic trampoline correctness invariant, not a GTA-specific rule.
- GTA V Enhanced DLSS FG startup can route `CreateSwapChainForHwnd` through EOS startup-overlay frames even when the live swapchain/queue actually belongs to Streamline. In `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_014238`, CE classified the new DLSS startup swapchain for the game HWND as an EOS third-party overlay swapchain and skipped normal swapchain side-effects, then later saw `OFF->ON->OFF->ON` DLSS FG churn followed by `Present STALLED` warnings. The generic fix is to let Streamline frame-generation stack evidence override startup-overlay caller identity during create-swapchain classification, just as native FFX stack evidence already does for FSR.
- GTA V Enhanced can also perform a later pre-FG runtime-owned swapchain handoff after CE has already observed a few stable startup overlay draws on the original game queue. In `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_022704`, CE marked startup compatibility as settled on the first successful overlay submit, then EOS/Streamline handed the live swapchain to a non-game queue before any real FG activation occurred. CE no longer considered startup compatibility active at that point, immediately ran the normal overlay path on the new runtime-owned queue, and GTA raised `ERR_GFX_STATE`.
- The generic fix is to let startup compatibility re-arm when a startup-blocking overlay is still present, the session has not yet observed any real FG activity, startup had previously been marked settled, and a later runtime-owned swapchain handoff appears. That keeps the conservative single-queue startup suppression active through the full startup handoff without re-entering startup-only behavior for later normal post-startup popups or FG suspension windows.
- In the later `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_023846` bundle, the same late pre-FG runtime-owned handoff did not crash immediately after the re-arm, but the overlay still disappeared before DLSS FG became active. The log shows CE resuming after startup-overlay warm-up while `ProcessFrame` continues routing on the runtime-owned non-FSR queue for almost a minute without any further overlay submit logs. The generic correction is to keep startup compatibility logically active through that whole late pre-FG runtime-owned window while allowing rendering again once the handoff queue has actually settled, instead of requiring runtime ownership to disappear entirely.
- The same `20260412_023846` bundle also showed `OFF->ON->OFF->ON` Streamline churn followed by repeated `Present STALLED` warnings. Fresh DLSS reactivation now clears stale Streamline-off teardown grace before the new activation, so CE no longer keeps ignoring newly resurfacing wrapper/direct queues from the old OFF transition during the next ON transition.
- In `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_034953`, the late pre-FG runtime-owned swapchain handoff still re-armed startup compatibility on the correct queue, but the re-arm condition was level-triggered instead of handoff-edge-triggered. Once CE had settled and resumed rendering on the original game queue, `ProcessFrame` immediately re-armed startup compatibility again on the next frame because the runtime-owned swapchain was still present. That produced thousands of repeated `Re-arming startup overlay compatibility after late runtime-owned swapchain handoff before any real FG activity` / `Startup overlay probe complete - rendering stably` cycles right up until DLSS activation instead of converging once per handoff.
- The same `20260412_034953` bundle also showed that Streamline stall detection was only watching `DetourPresent` traffic. If the runtime/game moved forward through `Present1`, CE could falsely conclude that Present had stalled even though top-level present traffic was still alive. The generic stall signal therefore needs aggregate top-level DXGI present traffic, not `Present`-only traffic.
- The `20260412_034953` automatic freeze dump further showed that the 30-frame Streamline stall dump request was executing synchronously on the target present thread itself (`targetTid=18308`, same as the calling thread), and the later dump captured that thread inside `capture_hook_x64!DX12_WaitForOverlayCompletion` while dump capture was in progress. Immediate dump requests targeting the current thread must therefore be deferred to the watchdog thread; otherwise the diagnostic path itself can become the freeze.
- In `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_133431`, CE got past the earlier wrapped-startup classification bug and the repeated startup re-arm churn, but DLSS FG still hit a startup-time `OFF->ON->OFF->ON` sequence. The hook log shows a fresh authoritative Streamline runtime-owned swapchain handoff at `13:36:03.404-13:36:03.430`, then `Streamline Hook: FG state transition OFF->ON via GetState`, a synthetic Streamline re-entrant Present, `ON->OFF via GetState`, and only afterward the explicit `OFF->ON via SetOptions` activation. The freeze dump for that run puts the target thread inside `sl_dlss_g` throwing a C++ exception rather than inside CE's dump path, so the bad transition happened before the watchdog dump machinery intervened.
- The generic correction is to treat a newly observed authoritative Streamline runtime-owned swapchain handoff as a short fresh-activation suppression window for `slDLSSGGetState`-only DLSS FG activation while the runtime still reports `Off` / `StreamlineNoFG`. Explicit `slDLSSGSetOptions` enable requests already clear that suppression immediately, so CE still converges once the real activation arrives, but it no longer lets a transient `GetState` activation race ahead of the startup handoff and collide with the later explicit enable.
- In the later `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_135934` bundle, CE got past that earlier startup race and reached the real `OFF->ON via SetOptions` activation, but top-level `DetourPresent` traffic stopped immediately after a later authoritative Streamline runtime-owned swapchain handoff while SL wrapper ECL traffic kept flowing. The dump `GTA5_Enhanced.exe_FREEZE_2026-04-12_14-01-19_400.dmp` again puts the target present thread down inside `sl_dlss_g`, and the hook log shows the second runtime-owned swapchain came through `CreateSwapChainForHwnd INLINE` without the same Present-hook refresh that the deep/global create-swapchain paths already perform.
- The generic correction is to refresh Present hooks for newly created real DX12 swapchains in the inline `CreateSwapChainForHwnd` success path too, not just in the deep/global create-swapchain paths. A runtime-created swapchain can expose a different Present implementation or vtable than the startup swapchain, and if CE only tracks the new swapchain queue without refreshing the detour path, top-level Present traffic can disappear right when Streamline takes over that new swapchain.
- In `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_142710`, the inline CreateSwapChainForHwnd Present-hook refresh was already in place, but GTA V Enhanced DLSS FG still froze after the `OFF->ON->OFF->ON` churn. The freeze dump `GTA5_Enhanced.exe_FREEZE_2026-04-12_14-28-54_777.dmp` shows the game's present thread (T:5C88) stuck inside `sl_dlss_g` throwing `std::_Throw_Cpp_error` (a C++ standard library threading/mutex error), with `sl_interposer` catching the exception and trying to write its own crash dump via `MiniDumpWriteDump`. The new swapchain was on a different D3D12 device (`0000019D3E6D7670`) than the game's original device (`0000019A02992040`), and during the churn CE was repeatedly installing and removing the PostSL callback, resetting the PostSL lifecycle epoch, draining overlay GPU queues, and clearing cached real-queue state. This repeated full teardown and re-init cycle on every OFF/ON transition during the startup transition window likely interfered with DLSS FG's fragile multi-device initialization threading.
- The generic correction is to keep the PostSL callback pointer installed but dormant when DLSS FG goes OFF via GetState during the startup transition window. Instead of clearing the callback pointer, waiting for in-flight callbacks, draining overlay GPU work, and resetting the lifecycle epoch, CE just disables callback execution. On the subsequent ON via SetOptions, CE re-enables the existing callback rather than re-installing it, and does not reset the lifecycle epoch. This avoids the repeated install/remove/drain cycle that can interfere with DLSS FG's initialization on multi-device configurations.
- In `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_151606`, the dormant-callback fix was already in place, but GTA V Enhanced DLSS FG still froze after the `OFF->ON->OFF->ON` churn on a multi-device configuration (third swapchain on device `0000022B8D0C2C50` vs game's `00000228DA094240`). The freeze dump again shows the game's present thread stuck inside `sl_dlss_g` throwing `std::_Throw_C_error` (threading/mutex error). The key observation: during the OFF via GetState at 37.471ms, `g_StreamlineFGRunning` was set to `false`, changing CE's Present routing mid-initialization. Then at the second ON via SetOptions at 37.747ms, `g_StreamlineFGRunning` went back to `true`. This toggling of the routing signal during SL's fragile multi-device startup likely changed timing enough to expose the threading race in `sl_dlss_g`.
- The generic correction is to defer `g_StreamlineFGRunning` OFF updates during the Streamline startup transition window. When `ApplyCombinedStreamlineRuntimeState(false)` is called while the window is active, `g_StreamlineFGRunning` keeps its current value (true) instead of being set to false. The `DX12_OnStreamlineFGStateChanged` callback is also suppressed during this deferral, so the PostSL callback state machine stays stable. After the window expires, the next GetState or SetOptions call processes the real state normally. This keeps CE's Present routing stable throughout DLSS FG initialization churn, avoiding timing changes that can trigger threading races in SL's multi-device configuration.
- In `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_162416`, the earlier startup-churn fixes still were not enough. This time the log reached the real `OFF->ON via SetOptions` activation on a later runtime-owned Streamline swapchain/device handoff, emitted one synthetic Streamline re-entrant Present, kept seeing SL wrapper ECL traffic, and then hit `Present STALLED` while the freeze dump again landed inside `sl_dlss_g` throwing the same threading/mutex exception. Two runtime-state issues stood out together: CE was still blanket-skipping the ExecuteCommandLists vtable hook on non-origGame runtime-owned queues (`DX12: Skipping vtable hook for FG runtime queue ... — preserving FSR timing`), which is correct for native FSR timing but too broad for authoritative Streamline DLSS handoffs, and the startup transition window was being re-armed by later active DLSS state traffic instead of only by fresh activation/handoff edges.
- The generic correction is twofold. First, only fresh DLSS activation edges should arm the Streamline startup transition window; steady-state active `GetState` / `SetOptions` traffic must not keep extending a startup-only OFF-deferral window into normal runtime operation. Second, authoritative Streamline runtime-owned swapchain queues must stay hookable for ExecuteCommandLists tracking even though generic runtime-owned queues remain unhooked for native FSR safety. CE now keeps the FSR timing safeguard for non-Streamline runtime queues, but it hooks authoritative Streamline runtime queues so later DLSS handoffs do not strand PostSL on wrapper-only queue state. The real-swapchain Present hook refresh path is also now centralized so the deep, global, and inline create-swapchain success paths all refresh Present interception consistently.
- In `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_165947`, a later GTA V Enhanced freeze still showed `CreateSwapChainForHwnd INLINE` on a fresh authoritative Streamline runtime queue immediately followed by one synthetic Streamline re-entrant Present, continued SL wrapper `ECL captured` traffic, and then `Present STALLED for 10/30 frames` before the dump again landed inside `sl_dlss_g`. The repo source at that point already had the earlier Present-refresh and queue-hook policy fixes, but queue capture was still recomputing caller authority after the original `CreateSwapChain*` call returned. That made two separate decisions share one transient boolean: whether a non-origGame queue should stay treated as an authoritative Streamline runtime queue at all, and whether that queue capture represented a fresh handoff edge that should re-arm the startup transition window.
- The generic correction is to preserve authoritative create-swapchain evidence through the later queue-capture step, and to split those two decisions. A Streamline runtime queue remains authoritative for hookability as long as the queue is non-origGame and the create-swapchain caller was authoritatively Streamline, even if a duplicate inline/global capture path sees the same queue again later in the same handoff. The startup transition window, however, should still only re-arm on the fresh handoff edge when the queue actually changes. CE now threads explicit queue-capture evidence through the deep/inline/global create-swapchain paths, keeps authoritative Streamline queue hookability stable across duplicate capture paths, and logs each real-swapchain Present-hook refresh explicitly so future traces can confirm that path directly.
- In the later GTA V Enhanced bundle `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_172854`, DLSS FG still froze after those fixes. The old `RIP=0x0 -> gameoverlayrenderer64!OverlayHookD3D3` crash family is gone in this run; instead CE survives the startup Present family, logs repeated `DetourPresent: Post-FSR startup normal-route bypass ...`, reactivates PostSL, finishes warm-up, and then reaches the first real post-FSR queue/probe stage. - The current generic correction is to tighten post-FSR queue selection one level further. `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` now blocks `ShouldUsePostSLWrapperBootstrapQueueAfterFSR(...)` once the comeback already has both stronger recovery signals: a preserved runtime-owned swapchain queue and a safe post-FSR bootstrap topology. `hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp` now passes both states into that policy. The generic rule is now consistent: wrapper bootstrap is only a weak fallback while CE is still missing stronger topology evidence, not something it should keep using after that stronger evidence already exists.
- In the GTA V Enhanced bundle `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_214313`, DLSS FG still froze even after those layered warm-up and signal-coherence fixes. The dump again showed `sl_dlss_g` throwing `std::_Throw_C_error` inside the present thread. The specific sequence this time was: DLSS FG created the authoritative swapchain on a **different D3D12 device** than the game device, then went through `OFF->ON->OFF->OFF->ON` churn. The startup transition window (500ms at the time) **expired before the churn finished** — the second ON arrived at +1.28s while the window expired at +0.88s. PostSL activated during the churn because the `useTopLevelHandoffWrapperProgress` bypass let it skip the startup-window ECL deferral, and the warm-up callback fired through SL's Present chain during SL's fragile multi-device initialization.
- The generic corrections are now fivefold. First, the startup transition window is extended on each deferred OFF signal, but extensions no longer reset the one-shot `streamlineStartupTopLevelPresentConsumed` latch (`hook/common/dxgi_shared.h` now separates `ExtendStreamlineStartupTransitionWindow()` from the fresh-handoff `Arm...` path). That preserves the original invariant of exactly one promoted top-level startup-handoff Present per handoff even when DLSS churn repeatedly extends the window. Second, the startup transition window duration remains 1500ms (`hook/common/dxgi_shared.h`), covering the longer churn windows seen on multi-device DLSS FG configurations. Third, the `useTopLevelHandoffWrapperProgress` bypass remains removed from `ShouldDeferPostSLRenderingDuringStartupTransitionWindow()` (`hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h`), because wrapper ECL progress only proves queue topology stability, not that SL's internal pipeline has settled. Fourth, CE now has an earlier dump trigger for the pure-DLSS startup-handoff black-window family: if the one-shot top-level handoff has already been consumed, wrapper ECL progress keeps advancing, startup is still half-armed, and top-level `ProcessFrame` has been dormant for about a second, `hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp` requests an immediate watchdog dump instead of waiting for a later `SetOptions` poll or the full 30-second watchdog timeout. Fifth, the new regression tests in `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` lock both behaviors in place.
- In the next GTA V Enhanced bundle `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_224959`, those two fixes were both clearly working: the log showed only one promoted top-level startup-handoff Present, the deferred OFF path logged `extended startup window` instead of reopening a fresh handoff, and the 30-frame stall path again produced a watchdog dump. - The current generic correction is to keep the PostSL callback itself dormant until the startup transition window expires for exactly that pure-DLSS top-level-handoff wrapper-progress family. `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` now exposes `ShouldDeferPostSLCallbackUntilStartupTransitionWindowExpires()`, and `hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp` now uses it in `PostSLOverlayRenderGated()` before the in-flight callback path starts. When the startup window is still active, the one-shot top-level handoff has already been consumed, wrapper ECL progress has already proven the runtime path is live, and startup is still half-armed, CE now skips the callback entirely instead of entering PostSL just to spend the only decisive callback on warm-up/deferral. - In the later GTA V Enhanced bundle `installed/captureengine/logs/20260412_225856`, that callback-dormancy fix was clearly working: the promoted handoff Present logged `DX12: PostSL gated callback deferred until startup transition window expires`, so CE was no longer perturbing Streamline by entering PostSL during the fragile window. When CE promotes a Streamline startup-handoff Present to the top-level live path, it still runs the normal CE routing/bootstrap logic, but on the way out it now prefers the bypass trampoline / original DXGI Present so the handoff Present is not recursively re-submitted into Streamline. - In the GTA V Enhanced bundle `installed/captureengine/logs/20260413_192027`, `[Overlay] enabled=false` was not a true no-interference baseline. `installed/captureengine/config.ini` disabled the visible overlay, but `hook_debug.log` still showed `DX12: ProcessFrame - first overlay render attempt`, `DX12: Streamline FG ON — installed gated PostSL callback`, `DX12: Streamline FG ON — pre-armed PostSL callback for startup routing`, and then the usual promoted startup-handoff Present plus `Present STALLED`. - The current active-mode refinement on build `0.1.2288` therefore narrows the structural rule without undoing it. `hook/common/dxgi_shared.h/.cpp` now apply the confirmed-standalone-live early-out only after the explicit `HookIsPostSLOverlayConfirmedButStartupSettling()` window has ended. During that short settling phase, standalone Streamline Presents still classify as synthetic first, which lets the existing `ShouldInvokePostSLCallbackWhileKeepingStreamlinePresentOnNormalRoute()` split keep PostSL rendering advancing while the Present itself still returns on the normal SL route. `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` now adds `ConfirmedPostSLStandaloneStreamlinePresentStaysSyntheticDuringStartupSettling` to lock this boundary in place.
- The next active validation `installed/captureengine/logs/20260415_144726` on `0.1.2288` showed that the startup-settling fix is working, but also exposed one final visibility seam immediately afterward. GTA now reaches `DX12: PostSL WARMUP COMPLETE`, `DX12: PostSL CONFIRMED rendering via re-entrant Present`, and `DX12: Post-SL overlay SUBMIT #1` through `#8`, so the visible PostSL path survives through the full explicit startup-settling window with no crash. But as soon as `stableFrames` reaches `8`, the visible overlay stalls again: no more `Post-SL overlay SUBMIT` lines appear, `skip=1` stays active, and `DX12: PostSL warmup — suppressing stall fallback ...` climbs until FG turns off. That shows GTA's later confirmed standalone Streamline Presents after settling are indeed live/non-synthetic Presents, but they still need to drive PostSL on the normal SL route because this runtime family does not surface a separate later re-entrant callback stream once startup settling ends. Build `0.1.2289` therefore adds one more generic split: confirmed standalone Streamline Presents with no active Present owner now invoke the PostSL callback while still remaining on the normal SL route after the explicit startup-settling window has ended.
- The follow-up GTA V Enhanced validation `installed/captureengine/logs/20260415_151044` on `0.1.2289` confirmed that this last split closes the loop. The trace reaches `DX12: PostSL CONFIRMED rendering via re-entrant Present`, continues through `Post-SL overlay SUBMIT #1..#8`, then repeatedly logs `DetourPresent: Invoking PostSL on confirmed standalone Streamline Present while keeping the normal SL route ...` and keeps submitting visible PostSL frames for the rest of the DLSS FG window. The session contains no `DetourPresent: Treating Streamline-originated Present as synthetic re-entrant`, no `Present STALLED`, no `CrashMirror`, and no `DEVICE_REMOVED`. Routing-state diagnostics during the long active phase show `runtime=DLSS_FG`, `postSLCallback=1`, `postSLActive=1`, `skip=1`, and `stableFrames` continuing to rise into the thousands, which is now the correct healthy state: pre-SL is suppressed because PostSL is continuously rendering successfully. This is the first confirmed GTA V Enhanced DLSS FG validation in this sequence where the overlay stays visible and the game stays stable through the whole active FG interval.
- The next Talos validation `installed/captureengine/logs/20260415_164322` on the same `0.1.2289` build showed a different seam that the GTA repair did not cover. Talos reaches `PostSL CONFIRMED rendering`, `Post-SL overlay SUBMIT #1..#8`, and one confirmed-standalone-normal-route callback at `#1`, then stops rendering visibly after `SUBMIT #9` even though synthetic Streamline Presents keep arriving by the thousands. The key marker is the timing of a late `DX12: [outer] SL FG ON` immediately after `SUBMIT #9`: that outer ON edge was still driving the generic fresh-transition reset path, so Talos fell into `PostSL stats: calls=500 renders=9 skipOther=490`, then `calls=1000 renders=9 skipOther=990`, and so on. Build `0.1.2290` therefore narrows that outer state management too: if Streamline surfaces a late outer `SL FG ON` edge after PostSL has already confirmed rendering, CE now preserves the already-confirmed active PostSL path instead of resetting confirmed/active state, re-arming cooldown, clearing stable frames, and forcing startup-style re-capture on a path that is already proven good. This is intended to restore Talos without regressing the newly confirmed GTA-good standalone-normal-route behavior.
- The follow-up GTA V Enhanced validation `installed/captureengine/logs/20260415_022108` on the same `0.1.2279` source line showed the next remaining gap: visible overlay rendering. The run stayed stable with `overlay_enabled=1`, but after DLSS FG activation the overlay disappeared. The trace reached synthetic activation and `PostSL REACTIVATED`, then stayed stuck in the half-armed startup family: `Suppressing pre-SL draw during SL FG startup — waiting for PostSL ...`, no `PostSL CONFIRMED rendering`, no `Post-SL overlay SUBMIT`, and decisive synthetic startup Presents still normal-routed through at least `#1700` until Streamline turned back off. Talos differs here because its healthy DLSS FG path still surfaces a real re-entrant PostSL callback that quickly reaches `CONFIRMED rendering` and submit. GTA's runtime family in this case does not, so waiting purely for a later re-entrant Present leaves the overlay invisible even though the startup-routing path is now safe.
- The current active-mode refinement on build `0.1.2280` therefore adds a generic ECL-driven bridge for the first visible PostSL confirmation. `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` now exposes `ShouldContinueECLDrivenPostSLStartupProgress()`, and `hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp` now uses cached-swapchain ECL progress not only at the one-time startup-window expiry edge, but also during the later activated-but-unconfirmed phase when the overlay is visible and a valid cached swapchain is still available. In that family CE now re-enters `PostSLOverlayRenderGated()` from ECL context at a controlled rate until the first visible PostSL render finally confirms, instead of waiting forever for a re-entrant Present callback that GTA never surfaces. `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` now locks that policy in place.
- The follow-up GTA V Enhanced validation `installed/captureengine/logs/20260415_023816` on `0.1.2280` showed that the visible-overlay bridge worked. CE now reached `DX12: PostSL WARMUP COMPLETE`, `DX12: PostSL CONFIRMED rendering via re-entrant Present`, and two `DX12: Post-SL overlay SUBMIT` lines before the crash. So the latest GTA problem is no longer "overlay never confirms"; the overlay now becomes visible. The crash moved one seam later: immediately after `Post-SL overlay SUBMIT #2`, the very next line is `DetourPresent: Treating Streamline-originated Present as synthetic re-entrant #1`, and the mirrored dump `external_71bce012-9f7a-4425-bdb2-04901d895cdb.dmp` is still the same `dxgi!CDXGISwapChain::Present+0x5` / `capture_hook_x64` / `sl_dlss_g` breakpoint-corruption family.
- The current active-mode refinement on build `0.1.2281` therefore widens the startup-family normal-route guard one more step, but still generically. `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` now exposes `ShouldTreatConfirmedPostSLRenderingAsStartupSettling()`, `hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp` exports that short confirmed-but-still-settling state via `HookIsPostSLOverlayConfirmedButStartupSettling()`, and `hook/common/dxgi_shared.h/.cpp` now keep Streamline-originated Presents off the synthetic/bypass path not only while startup is pending or PostSL is active-but-unconfirmed, but also for the first few confirmed PostSL frames right after the first successful submit. The point is not to special-case GTA; it is to keep the pure-DLSS startup family on the normal SL route until the freshly confirmed PostSL path has survived more than the very first successful render callback.
- The follow-up GTA V Enhanced validation `installed/captureengine/logs/20260415_025500` on `0.1.2281` showed that this new guard was only half of the correct split. The crash disappeared, but the overlay stayed visually absent for the rest of the DLSS FG window. The trace still reached `DX12: PostSL CONFIRMED rendering via re-entrant Present` and `DX12: Post-SL overlay SUBMIT #1`, so the first visible render did happen. After that, though, `stableFrames` stayed at `1`, the routing logs kept showing `settling=1`, and `DX12: PostSL warmup — suppressing stall fallback ...` climbed into the thousands while decisive synthetic startup Presents kept staying on the normal route. That exposed the real missing split: in `0.1.2281`, keeping those startup-family Presents on the normal SL route also stopped using them to drive the PostSL callback, so the visible PostSL path never advanced beyond the first confirmed frame.
- The current active-mode refinement on build `0.1.2282` therefore separates those two decisions explicitly. `hook/common/dxgi_shared.h` now exposes `ShouldInvokePostSLCallbackWhileKeepingStreamlinePresentOnNormalRoute()`, and `hook/common/dxgi_shared.cpp` now uses it in both `DetourPresent` and `DetourPresent1`: during the short confirmed-startup-settling window, Streamline-originated Presents still avoid the synthetic/bypass return path, but they now also explicitly invoke the PostSL callback before continuing on the normal SL route. That lets GTA's confirmed-startup family keep advancing `stableFrames` and visible PostSL rendering without reopening the old crash seam.
- The follow-up GTA V Enhanced validation `installed/captureengine/logs/20260415_033913` on `0.1.2283` proved that split works, but also showed the next remaining boundary. The overlay now stays visible for a few frames: the trace reaches `DX12: Post-SL overlay SUBMIT #1` through `#4`, and the in-game observation matches that DLSS FG status finally became visibly correct for a moment. But the crash then moved one seam later again. Right after `stableFrames` reached `2`, the next Streamline-originated Present fell back to `DetourPresent: Treating Streamline-originated Present as synthetic re-entrant #1`, and the mirrored dump `external_3dd0a200-60f8-42ad-b666-60fcd5368f37.dmp` is still the same `dxgi!CDXGISwapChain::Present+0x5` / `capture_hook_x64` / `sl_dlss_g` breakpoint-corruption family.
- The current active-mode refinement on build `0.1.2284` therefore stays minimal: it does not add another new startup state, it just widens the existing confirmed-startup-settling window. `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` now keeps `ShouldTreatConfirmedPostSLRenderingAsStartupSettling()` true through the first 6 stable PostSL frames instead of only the first 3, and `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` now documents that wider invariant directly. The runtime evidence now shows GTA's startup family needs more than a couple of visible PostSL submits before it is safe to drop back to the ordinary synthetic/bypass Streamline Present path.
- The latest Talos validation `installed/captureengine/logs/20260416_015012` on build `0.1.2313` showed the next mixed-family seam after `lastWorkingQueue` reuse was the first post-FSR startup-handoff Present itself. CE preserved the fresh post-FSR `scQueue`, kept that handoff logically on the normal SL route, but the recovered swapchain still needed bypass transport before PostSL could reactivate. `hook/common/dxgi_shared.h/.cpp` now apply `ShouldBypassPresentForPostFSRStartupHandoffPresentOnNormalRoute(...)` in both `DetourPresent` and `DetourPresent1`, and `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` locks `PostFSRStartupHandoffNormalRouteUsesBypassTransport`.
- The generic rule stays the same: post-FSR routing can advance startup state, but actual Present transport must remain on bypass until the recovered hook chain is safe again.
- GTA V Enhanced `installed/captureengine/logs/20260416_031434` on build `0.1.2315` showed the next refinement after that transport split. The late failing family is a post-FSR `FSR_FG -> STREAMLINE_NO_FG -> DLSS_FG` comeback after several earlier successful transitions. CE preserves the fresh post-FSR `scQueue`, logs `OFF->ON via SetOptions`, and the first protected startup callback reaches `DetourPresent: Post-FSR startup normal-route bypass #1`, but the mirrored Streamline dump storm starts before any `PostSL synthetic startup waiting for safe bootstrap path ...` or `PostSL REACTIVATED` line appears. Later ECL diagnostics still say `safeBootstrap=0`, so the remaining mismatch is narrower than transport: callback-on-normal-route was still allowed to enter PostSL on the post-FSR startup family before the bootstrap topology was safe.
- Build `0.1.2315` tightened `ShouldInvokePostSLCallbackWhileKeepingStreamlinePresentOnNormalRoute(...)` to require both `explicitSetOptionsActivation` and `safePostFSRBootstrapPath` for post-FSR callback-on-normal-route. That stopped crashes on unsafe topologies, but it also stranded PostSL indefinitely when `safePostFSRBootstrapPath` was false only because `g_RealD3D12ECL` had been cleared during FSR teardown while the SL wrapper queue was still available. Build `0.1.2554` relaxes both gates: `ShouldDelayPostSLActivationUntilSafeBootstrapPath` now accepts the SL wrapper queue as a viable bootstrap path without realECL, and `ShouldInvokePostSLCallbackWhileKeepingStreamlinePresentOnNormalRoute` no longer requires `explicitSetOptionsActivation` once `safePostFSRBootstrapPath` is true. The callback gate now matches the ECL fallback, which never required explicit SetOptions. `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` updates both test suites to lock the relaxed invariants.
- GTA V Enhanced `installed/captureengine/logs/20260416_033646` on build `0.1.2316` showed that the callback-entry fix was real but still not the final seam. The same late `FSR_FG -> off -> DLSS_FG` comeback preserves the fresh post-FSR `scQueue=0000024F705E4380`, logs `OFF->ON via SetOptions`, and immediately reaches `DetourPresent: Post-FSR startup normal-route bypass #1`. There is still no `PostSL synthetic startup waiting for safe bootstrap path ...` line and no `PostSL REACTIVATED` line before the mirrored `sl-sha-11cf43f.dmp` storm begins, while the later ECL-side path still logs `safeBootstrap=0`. That proves the earlier callback gate is holding. The remaining boundary is now transport choice on the protected post-FSR normal-route family itself.
- The current generic correction narrows that transport rule to actual third-party Present-hook risk instead of applying bypass unconditionally on every post-FSR comeback. `hook/common/dxgi_shared.h/.cpp` now thread `staleThirdPartyPresentHookRisk` into `ShouldBypassPresentForPostFSRStartupHandoffPresentOnNormalRoute(...)`, `ShouldBypassPresentWhileKeepingStreamlineStartupPresentOnNormalRoute(...)`, and `ShouldBypassPresentForConfirmedStandaloneStreamlinePresentOnNormalRoute(...)`. Today that risk is keyed to the existing Steam DX12 bypass detection path, so post-FSR normal-route Presents stay on bypass only when CE actually sees the stale Steam-style Present-hook chain that motivated the earlier Talos fixes. Comebacks without that hook-chain risk keep their logical normal-route behavior without being forced through unconditional bypass transport. `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` now locks the narrower transport invariant. The callback-on-normal-route expectation was later relaxed in build `0.1.2554` so that `safePostFSRBootstrapPath` alone is sufficient (explicit `SetOptions` is no longer required), preventing deadlocks when the bootstrap topology is safe but SetOptions has not yet been observed.

## Current Practical Guidance
- Any FG fix should be reasoned through as a state-transition problem, not as a one-off title quirk.
- When you need a strict injected baseline, use `[Overlay] observer_only=true`; do not treat `enabled=false` alone as equivalent.
- After the strict passive baseline is clean, use `[Overlay] observer_only=true` plus `[Overlay] observer_policy_only=true` to reintroduce only the Streamline startup-policy family without re-enabling PostSL or special startup Present routing.
- If that remains stable, use `[Overlay] observer_only=true`, `[Overlay] observer_policy_only=true`, and `[Overlay] observer_startup_present_only=true` to reintroduce only the remaining non-Streamline startup-Present probe pieces while PostSL callback install/use and rendering still stay passive.
- If that staged seam still freezes on `0.1.2269` or newer, the next suspect is no longer any special Streamline Present routing path, because observer mode now keeps both the promoted and synthetic Streamline-originated startup Present families passive again.
- With `20260414_232934` now stable, the remaining gap has shifted back to active mode: observer probing shows GTA's reproduced crash requires special Streamline Present routing during startup, while the passive startup-policy-only path is stable. Re-check the active pre-armed PostSL plus special Streamline Present routing family next.
- With `20260415_002110` now analyzed, the next active validation target is narrower still: confirm whether removing both special startup Present seams from active mode is enough to stop the crash while preserving the startup-policy/window machinery and later wrapper-progress-backed PostSL activation path.
- If a change touches queue ownership, runtime classification, startup bypass, post-FSR recovery, or metrics publication, assume both Talos-style and GTA-style regressions are possible until proven otherwise.
- Preserve generic signals such as runtime mode, queue provenance, swapchain ownership, and stack evidence. Do not replace those with per-title conditions.
- If a change would make the correct path depend on the executable name, stop and justify that carefully before proceeding.

## Regression Families Already Present
- `off -> DLSS -> off -> FSR`
- `FSR -> DLSS -> off`
- `DLSS suspend -> DLSS resume`
- `startup bypass -> normal routing`
- `FSR FG <-> DLSS FG` visible overlay label switching
- `DLSS FG -> off` visible overlay reset
- `native/runtime-owned FSR FG` must not emit injected `FG overlay SUBMIT` traffic on the FFX-owned queue
- `native/runtime-owned FSR FG` should render via the chained FFX `presentCallback` path instead of separate injected overlay queue work

## Regression Families Worth Expanding
- `off -> FSR -> off`
- `off -> DLSS -> off` with more routing detail than the visible-status tests currently cover
- `DLSS -> FSR`
- `DLSS -> FSR -> off`
- `FSR -> DLSS -> FSR`
- `FSR off while third-party startup overlay windows are still active`
- `heuristic FSR takeover while SL hook remains present`
- `FSR -> DLSS` with native FFX context destruction while CE inline hooks are active
- `startup-blocking overlay wraps DLSS FG swapchain creation`
- `startup overlay appears settled, then runtime-owned swapchain handoff arrives before first real FG activation`
- `startup overlay re-arms for a late pre-FG runtime-owned handoff, then must resume visible overlay before DLSS FG actually turns on`
- `late pre-FG runtime-owned handoff re-arms exactly once per handoff instead of on every subsequent frame`
- `DLSS stall detection still sees forward progress when the runtime uses Present1 instead of Present`
- `automatic immediate dump request targeting the current present thread is deferred to watchdog thread`
- `authoritative Streamline startup handoff suppresses fresh GetState-only DLSS activation until explicit SetOptions enable arrives`
- `PostSL callback stays dormant during DLSS FG OFF->ON->OFF->ON churn in startup transition window`
- `g_StreamlineFGRunning OFF signal deferred during startup transition window to prevent multi-device DLSS FG threading race`
- `startup transition window only re-arms on fresh Streamline activation edges, not steady-state active polls`
- `authoritative Streamline runtime-owned swapchain queues stay hookable even while generic runtime-owned queues remain unhooked for native FSR timing safety`
- `duplicate inline/global create-swapchain capture of the same authoritative Streamline runtime queue preserves hookability but does not falsely re-arm startup handoff state`
- `deep/global/inline DX12 create-swapchain success paths all refresh real-swapchain Present interception consistently`
- `pure DLSS startup does not get stranded behind a callback-countdown synthetic PostSL activation gate when Streamline only emits one short synthetic Present burst`
- `synthetic/re-entrant Streamline Present paths refresh the live swapchain Present hook anchor when runtime activation moves onto a different vtable path`
- `startup transition window survives the first successful PostSL startup submit so an immediate transient ON->OFF->ON bounce does not trigger a full PostSL teardown`
- `pure DLSS PostSL prefers direct/original ECL submission on the selected live swapchain queue once that queue already resolves to the real D3D12 ECL path`
- `pure DLSS cold-start uses layered stabilization (reduced cooldown + first-epoch warmup + startup window rendering gate + churn re-arm) before first PostSL ECL submission`
- `late Streamline startup-handoff Presents that arrive after a recent large top-level Present gap must not all be forced down the synthetic bypass path; but only the expected game-present thread should be allowed to consume a one-shot top-level live Present bootstrap during that startup window`
- `startup transition window is extended on each deferred OFF signal so it stays active through the entire OFF->ON->OFF->ON churn; window duration increased from 500ms to 1500ms for multi-device DLSS FG configurations; wrapper ECL progress bypass removed from startup-window ECL deferral because queue topology stability does not prove SL internal pipeline stability`
- `a promoted Streamline startup-handoff Present may use the top-level CE processing path, but must return through the bypass/original DXGI Present path instead of being fed back into Streamline's external Present hook again`
- `when a promoted startup-handoff Present bypasses the synthetic PostSL activation path and no synthetic Presents arrive to drive PostSL, the PostSL callback must be triggered directly when the startup window expires — using two independent mechanisms: (a) the suppressed-OFF flush path in DetourPresent/DetourPresent1 (covers the case where suppressed OFF exists when window expires) and (b) the ECL hook transition detection (covers the case where ON re-arrived and cleared the suppressed OFF before window expiry, AND ProcessFrame has stalled so the normal ProcessFrame-based deferred callback never fires)`
- `activationPending alone (g_PostSLSyntheticStartupActivationPending) is the ground-truth condition for "PostSL activation has not completed through the Present callback path" — the callback being installed (callbackInstalled) does not mean PostSL is rendering-active; the callback being deferred (postSLActive=false) is irrelevant to whether we should attempt activation`
- `overlay hidden`, `observer_only`, and `observer_policy_only` must stay distinct: `observer_only=true` is the strict passive injected baseline, while `observer_policy_only=true` may preserve the Streamline startup transition window and related SetOptions/GetState startup policy without re-enabling PostSL callback use or synthetic/startup Present routing
- `observer_only` must still preserve Streamline transition heuristic cleanup so transient `ON->OFF->ON` churn does not masquerade as heuristic `FSR_FG` during passive diagnosis
- `observer_policy_only` must stay passive in DX12/DXGI routing even while the Streamline hook re-enables startup-policy mutation; FFX startup Present bypass, early/PostSL callback install/use, and promoted/synthetic startup Present routing must remain suppressed in this staged mode
- repeated native-FSR epochs must be allowed to refresh FFX API hooks on later module instances; a one-shot successful `FFXHook::Init()` is not sufficient if the runtime unloads/reloads its FFX DLLs or later exports lose CE's detour patch
- Talos `installed/captureengine/logs/20260423_044543` on build `0.1.2551` exposed a new overlay disappearance seam after a long FSR/DLSS FG mode-switching sequence. After FSR turned off, then DLSS turned off, `ShouldDeferOverlayInitUntilCommandQueueSettlesAfterRecentStreamlineTeardown` locked the overlay out for ~600 frames because both `scQueue` and `lastWorkingQ` were null. `lastWorkingQ` had been cleared during the earlier FSR→DLSS ON transition (`ShouldInvalidatePostSLLastWorkingQueueOnFreshPostFSRStreamlineHandoff`) and was never repopulated because PostSL never activated during the subsequent DLSS epoch (`safeBootstrap=0`). The deferral policy skipped the `commandQueueMatchesPrimaryGameQueue` escape hatch when `hasSwapchainQueue` was false, so the perfectly valid primary game queue could not satisfy the recovery condition. Build `0.1.2552` evaluates that escape hatch even without a swapchain queue, restoring overlay visibility promptly after Streamline teardown.
- The same `20260423_044543` session also crashed with exception `0x00008000` inside `sl_dlss_g` (Streamline DLSS FG) on the present thread, called via `sl_interposer`. This is a Streamline internal threading/mutex exception (`0x00008000` is a user-mode software exception raised by `sl_dlss_g`), distinct from the older `std::_Throw_Cpp_error` or `dxgi!CDXGISwapChain::Present+0x5` breakpoint-corruption families. CE's VEH catches it and returns `EXCEPTION_CONTINUE_SEARCH`, but no SEH handler catches it and the game terminates. The rapid ON/OFF toggling (FSR→DLSS ON, OFF, ON, OFF within ~40 seconds) stresses Streamline's fragile multi-device initialization/teardown. The overlay-deferral fix may mitigate this indirectly by restoring normal GPU work promptly instead of leaving the game in a deferral loop for hundreds of frames, but there is no obvious non-invasive CE-side suppression for the exception without risking Reflex or other Streamline Present-hook features.

## Scope
This page records current guardrails and tested transition families for no-FG, DLSS FG, and FSR FG switching. The goal is generic support across games, not a pile of title-specific hacks.

## Project Guardrails
- We must be careful not to break DLSS FG and FSR FG in GTA again when fixing any FG issue in Talos.
- Talos and GTA are validation families, not excuses for game-specific runtime hacks.
- Switching FG must work gracefully in both Talos and GTA validation scenarios, in all directions and combinations, without crashes, without lost overlay rendering, and with the correct visible FG status.
- Fixes must stay generic so DLSS FG and FSR FG support scales across multiple games instead of accumulating title-specific branches.
- The pseudo-overlay is not an injected-overlay replacement for FG. It must not be used to paper over DLSS FG or FSR FG injected-overlay failures.

- **CURRENT FOREIGN-OVERLAY THREAD-PROVENANCE INVARIANT (2026-08-09):** Talos session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260809_015416` froze after rapid intro skipping moved live presentation from the tracked source/RHI thread `0x6878` to DLSS-G worker `0x0B44`. Two dumps five seconds apart captured that worker inside CE's synchronous guarded Steam Present call, blocked on a Steam event while engine threads waited downstream. Plugin-lookup and NULL-callback guards prevent crashes but do not establish thread affinity. Whenever Streamline/PostSL/FSR/runtime-owned state can issue worker Presents, a synchronous third-party Present handler—whether explicitly invoked or reached naturally through Steam's E9 hook—may run only on the exact tracked game Present thread; unknown or worker provenance uses the native bypass and retains the established CE overlay route. The Steam E9/vtable path keeps `s_slRoutingActive=false` by design, so its late block is a lifetime transport guard rather than a startup-state predicate. No timeout, cancellation, new worker, overlay suspension, title branch, or FG disable is permitted.

Confirmed normal return disables PostSL, invalidates its queue/lifecycle proof, and retires only swapchain-scoped RTV/sync state while preserving the warm device/format adapter. An already-entered PostSL callback is cancellation-epoch checked before synchronization and ECL submission, and transition cleanup synchronizes on the render mutex without sleeps. This is generic for late `OFF -> DLSS`, `OFF -> FSR`, mixed FSR/DLSS switches, and `DLSS -> OFF`; fresh runtime validation remains mandatory.
- **CURRENT NORMAL-RETURN QUEUE-BASELINE INVARIANT (2026-07-12):** session `20260712_223915` proved that the normal-return classification and PostSL retirement above are insufficient if the FSR queue-change heuristic still carries the departed Streamline queue. Leftover Streamline ECL traffic cannot become the baseline or a phantom FSR edge. Once observed, the boundary is consumed so a later real OFF -> FSR queue change is detected without an arbitrary delay. This rule applies even when no PostSL callback remains armed and uses no timer, sleep, copy, extra queue, or steady-state GPU work.

- **CURRENT POST-FSR EXACT-SWAPCHAIN OWNERSHIP INVARIANT (2026-07-14):** GTA session `installed/captureengine/logs/gtacrashafterextendedswitchingbetweendlssfgandfsrfg` ended in GTA's deliberate `ERR_GFX_STATE` breakpoint/dialog, not a CE/GTA CPU AV. Streamline's OFF pass-through can omit a later re-entrant callback, so ProcessFrame invokes the gated PostSL renderer directly, prefers the retained last-successful direct queue over a stale epoch lock, and marks coverage only when a per-thread success sequence proves a healthy real submit. Normal proof then preserves the existing cancellation-epoch retirement and immediate original-route draw. The transition adds no copy, queue, allocation, reinit, GPU/CPU wait, sleep, timer, title branch, FG-status mutation, or steady-state work. - **CURRENT FFX OWNER-QUEUE INVARIANT (2026-07-14; supersedes the older CE-independent-queue active/suspension descriptions below):** the three FFX FrameGenerationSwapChain DX12 creation descriptors expose `gameQueue`, the queue AMD orders into its internal present handoff. Usually CE retains and submits on that exact queue. A Streamline-created FFX swapchain can instead expose Streamline's wrapper queue/device while its UI/backbuffer resources belong to the real device. CE may unwrap only when the descriptor queue's device is the most recent device accepted by `slSetD3DDevice` **and** the retained original game queue's device owns the actual draw target; arbitrary cross-device substitution remains forbidden. CE records one overlay command list immediately before proxy Present. Active no-callback FG targets the registered/CE-substituted UI resource; explicit retained suspension and disabled protected startup target the proxy's current presented backbuffer because AMD ignores the UI resource in passthrough. All use `dx12_ffx_suspend_overlay` per-proxy state, a CE fence, and a command/upload slot forced to the proxy buffer index. There is **no CE-created queue, no foreign-queue swapchain access, no copy, no guessed queue, and no per-present CPU wait**. An incomplete slot is refused without waiting/overwriting; target resources and incomplete generations remain retained until completion proof. The presenter fallback deduplicates multiple real/generated Presents against the accepted UI-registration sequence. FFX context retirement is proxy-keyed, not queue-wide, because two contexts may share a game queue.
- **CURRENT FG OVERLAY PERFORMANCE INVARIANT (2026-07-12):** active and suspended native FSR render exactly once per accepted source UI registration on the validated owner queue before proxy Present, with queue ordering instead of a copy, cross-queue Signal/Wait, dedicated queue, or CPU completion wait. The legacy presenter fallback is coverage-only and sequence-deduplicated. DLSS steady-state PostSL uses the already-warm native DX12 backend and one command-list submission; its allocator selection scans the entire fenced ring from the round-robin preference, so a busy nominal slot cannot trigger a 1 ms Present-thread wait while another slot is reusable. The bounded wait remains only for genuine full-pool GPU pressure. Transition probes/copies remain topology-gated bootstrap safety work, not steady-state per-frame work.
- **CURRENT PRE-RESOLVED FFX EXPORT ROUTING INVARIANT (2026-07-11):** a client can resolve and cache `ffxCreateContext`, `ffxConfigure`, and `ffxDestroyContext` before CE's dynamic/IAT routing wins startup. CE scans only pointer-aligned slots in writable, non-executable, non-discardable PE sections of eligible client modules and atomically replaces exact live original-export values; it never scans executable sections or patches AMD code for this route. This preserves exact creation-time `gameQueue` capture and observes the very first suspend/resume edge. Once a durable client-owned `ffxConfigure` slot is routed, CE restores and permanently retires the protected-runtime VEH breakpoint across context destruction; the next epoch remains observable through the durable pointer. Successful configure packets are still forwarded individually, but duplicate enabled/routing state no longer repeats global FG transition bookkeeping. The first proxy Present after a real route change logs its selected target and whether submission succeeded.
- **CURRENT FFX UI PUBLICATION INVARIANT (2026-07-11):** `RegisterUiResource` interception is transactional. Target/substitute preparation occurs before the provider call, but the cache and substitute re-registration descriptor are committed only after `FFX_API_RETURN_OK`; failure/stale sequence preserves the prior known-good generation. Substitute reuse requires matching COM device identity, geometry, format, and exact initial resource state (COMMON/PRESENT is valid numeric zero). A re-registration failure means the active draw is not proven consumed and must not publish proxy-driver coverage. Present-hook replacement/teardown keeps the real-present fallback active until a successful prework, quiesces new prework, and drains entered detours before releasing renderer state.
- **CURRENT POST-FSR STREAMLINE PREWARM INVARIANT (2026-07-11; first-Present ownership tightened 2026-07-16):** `logs/20260711_172959` showed that the first PostSL callback after FSR-to-DLSS spent about 17-20 ms rebuilding an unnecessarily discarded overlay adapter while DLSS presentation was already starting. On a fresh authoritative post-FSR Streamline DX12 proxy, the queue and buffers exist before `slDLSSGSetOptions(ON)`. If the retiring overlay was fully live, CE retains the device/format-scoped warm adapter and creates only the replacement swapchain's RTV and sync objects during that pre-enable window, without recording/submitting a draw or changing backbuffer state. User-watched run `20260716_132719` proved the proxy's first Present can also precede SetOptions and must not pass through generic replacement cleanup: doing so destroyed the exact prewarmed backend and caused one uncovered Present/188 ms. Completed prewarm therefore publishes identity-only, one-Present ownership for that exact proxy. Its matching first Present preserves the backend only while overlay/sync/RTV/command-list state is complete, exact captured queue/runtime ownership remains valid, FSR/native presentation is absent, and the device is healthy; it consumes the proof even across COM-pointer ABA reuse. Session `logs/20260711_175014` separately proved durable `g_HadFSRFGPhase` must disqualify runtime-inactive no-FG startup preservation. Pure-DLSS cold start and all unproven/failed-guard paths keep conservative fallback. Expected diagnostics are `PostSL handoff prewarm READY before DLSS enable`, `Armed exact prewarmed PostSL handoff backend`, and `First exact prewarmed PostSL handoff Present preserved`; generic teardown between those breadcrumbs is a regression.
- **CURRENT FIRST-DLSS-OUTPUT UI COVERAGE INVARIANT (2026-07-12):** official UI coverage remains valid when an integration publishes a usable tag before activation, but Talos does not. `logs/20260712_004201` had every global/frame/evaluate hook installed before GetState ON; no API supplied a UI resource until `slSetTagForFrame` type 23 roughly 1.6 seconds later. Same-queue startup must therefore be event-driven: the first proven PostSL callback activates immediately regardless of a recent normal-frame timestamp. The existing draw-count accounting provides make-before-break—preserve/account a pending normal draw and defer PostSL drawing one callback, otherwise draw PostSL now—so neither zero-draw nor double-draw frames occur. Separate-queue/GTA and post-FSR families do not satisfy the proof and keep the dormant/cooldown protections. This is not a shorter timeout. Global/frame/evaluate hooks, exact UUID filtering, ECL completion, and no-copy/no-extra-queue/no-wait properties remain as opportunistic coverage.
