### Historical implementation facts (superseded where they conflict with the current 2026-07-11 invariants above)

- During native no-callback FSR FG (GTA-style), the overlay is rendered by the **fenced CE-owned-queue composite** (2026-06-23, supersedes the unfenced ECL bundle that crashed GTA — see case-studies / recent.md): `DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoFFXUiResource` (`hook/apis/dx12_hook_main.cpp`) draws the overlay onto the game's registered/CE-substituted FFX UI resource, **submits on CE's OWN dedicated DIRECT queue** `g_FFXUiCompositeQueue` (AMD/NVIDIA/Streamline do NOT track it), **signals its own fence, and CPU-waits for completion before returning** (plus a per-slot allocator fence wait before reuse). **Driver split (2026-07-02, session 20260701_213656):** the PRIMARY driver is the **FFX proxy-present prework** — CE vtable-hooks the game-facing FI-proxy swapchain's Present/Present1 (`DX12_TryInstallFFXProxyPresentHook`, proxy captured from `ffxConfigure(FrameGeneration).swapChain`, Present entry must resolve into the FFX runtime module — `ShouldInstallFFXProxyPresentHook` policy) and `DX12_RunFFXProxyPrePresentWork` runs `DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoCachedFFXUiResource()` + `FFXHook_ReRegisterSubstituteUiResource()` on the GAME thread BEFORE AMD's proxy Present (which snapshots/copies the registered UI resource per present under its criticalSection). `DetourPresent` on AMD's internal real swapchain runs on the **"AMD FSR Presenter Thread"** and is passthrough while `DX12_IsFFXProxyPresentHookDriving()`; otherwise it drives the composite as a FALLBACK (composite only — NEVER the re-assert). The bundle (`RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL`/`TryAppendNoCallbackBundleOverlay`/`EnsureFFXUiCompositeBundleResources`) and the dead `DX12_ShouldCompositeOverlayOntoFFXUiResource()` gate were REMOVED — do NOT reintroduce appending CE's overlay CL to the game's ECL with unsynchronized allocators (that is exactly the `nvwgf2umx` null-deref). **Invariant:** under active no-callback FSR FG interpolation CE does overlay GPU work ONLY on `g_FFXUiCompositeQueue` — never the game ECL, never AMD's present queue, never the backbuffer.
- `DetourPresent` (`hook/common/dxgi_shared.cpp`) chooses the no-callback FSR FG overlay route via `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute(runtimeOwns, liveQueueIsOrigGame, fsrFGDisabledSuspendPending, uiResourceCached, bundleOverlayActivelyFiring)`. **REVISED 2026-07-03 (session 20260703_210021):** while AMD OWNS the swapchain (runtime-owned, live queue != origGame) the route is ALWAYS `kSkipBundleCovers` — the backbuffer submit is NEVER used there, whether AMD is interpolating OR suspended. The old `runtimeOwns && !fsrFGDisabledSuspendPending` relaxation that sent a suspension to the backbuffer is GONE: the backbuffer submit on AMD's runtime-owned swapchain doesn't just crash during active interpolation — during a SUSPENSION its GPU-completion fence never signals (AMD stops flushing its runtime queue while suspended) so `DetourPresent` stalls ~1s EVERY present (app → ~1 fps). `fsrFGDisabledSuspendPending` no longer gates the route. `kSkipBundleCovers` → bundle composite on CE's own fenced queue (prework drives on the game thread; DetourPresent passthrough while the proxy hook is live, composite-only fallback otherwise); `kMinimalBackbuffer` is reached ONLY when the game owns its OWN native swapchain (`liveQueueIsOrigGame`, stale-latch recovery) or AMD does not own the swapchain (non-runtime-owned escape hatch, `bundleOverlayActivelyFiring` still consulted). If AMD does not composite the UI resource during a suspension the overlay is at worst blank — never a crash, never a stall.
- **RETAINED NO-CALLBACK SUSPENSION VISIBILITY RULE (2026-07-02, session 20260702_142655 — test app overlay blank for the whole FSR suspension):** during a retained no-callback FSR suspension the "inactive runtime-owned swapchain init queue-settle" defer must NOT apply (`ShouldDeferInactiveRuntimeOwnedSwapchainOverlayInit(..., retainedNoCallbackFSRSuspension)`): AMD keeps the FI swapchain+queue latched while the app renders on origGame, so cmdQ==scQ can never settle — the defer stranded overlay init (and the coverage gate was blind to it). The suspension-approved render path is the backbuffer on the runtime-owned swapchain queue (`kUseRuntimeOwnedSwapchainQueue` routing). Both queue-settle defer sites now attribute `[OVERLAY COVERAGE]` gates, and `[OVERLAY DOUBLE-DRAW]` flags two different overlay routes rendering in the same present window.
- **NO-CALLBACK FSR SUSPENSION RIDES THE BUNDLE, NEVER THE (STALLING) BACKBUFFER (2026-07-03, TWO sessions on the same `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` suspend edge):** the overlay-route decisions (`ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` at present time AND `ShouldSkipSeparateOverlayGpuWorkForRuntimeOwnedFrameGeneration` at the init/dedicated-queue gate) must AGREE, and while AMD owns the swapchain that agreement is: overlay rides the UI-resource composition BUNDLE (CE's own fenced queue), CE submits ZERO backbuffer/separate work on AMD's runtime queue — active OR suspended. Two failed iterations proved why:
  - **20260703_204119 (blank):** the skip decision fed the raw cached-UI-texture latch `DX12_IsFFXUiResourceCachedForBundle()` (a pointer, set once, never cleared on suspend) as "bundle covers" → `skip=true` deferred overlay init the whole suspension, while the router had been sending the suspend to `kMinimalBackbuffer` — net "nobody draws" = blank.
  - **20260703_210021 (perf death):** the "fix" that made the suspend actually take the backbuffer (`DX12_ProcessFrameMinimal`) collapsed the app to **~1 fps** — `DescFree GPU-completion wait timed out (guard=1 completed=0)` + `DetourPresent TOTAL SLOW ~999ms` EVERY present (40+ times). AMD stops flushing its runtime queue while suspended, so the overlay's GPU-completion fence never signals and CE waits the full ~1s timeout per frame. Dump: game/present thread parked in `WaitForSingleObjectEx` inside CE's wrapped-present path, called from `amd_fidelityfx_framegeneration_dx12` Present. This **DISPROVED** the "suspension backbuffer is safe (AMD not interpolating)" assumption (session 20260623_054929): safe-from-crash ≠ non-stalling.
  - **ROUTING RESOLUTION:** `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` drops the `&& !fsrFGDisabledSuspendPending` gate → `runtimeOwns` (active OR suspended) always returns `kSkipBundleCovers`; the skip decision matches (`bundleCovers = ffxUiResourceCompositionActive && !liveSwapchainQueueIsOriginalGameQueue`, no suspend gate). `kMinimalBackbuffer`/`skip=false` is reachable ONLY at a stale latch (game recreated its own native swapchain, `liveQueueIsOrigGame` — backbuffer on the game's own actively-flushed queue is safe) or non-runtime-owned. So CE submits ZERO work on AMD's runtime queue in either active or suspended runtime-owned states.
  - **VISIBILITY RESOLUTION (session 20260703_212441 proved AMD does NOT composite the UI resource in passthrough — the overlay was drawn onto the UI texture every frame yet blank):** during the suspension the proxy-present prework draws the overlay DIRECTLY onto the game-facing FI-proxy's CURRENT backbuffer (`DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoSuspendBackbuffer`, `GetCurrentBackBufferIndex`+`GetBuffer`, `PRESENT→RT→PRESENT`, blend on top, no clear) instead of the (ignored) UI texture — but STILL on CE's own dedicated composite queue `g_FFXUiCompositeQueue` (untracked by AMD, CPU-waited before Present), NEVER AMD's runtime/game queue (that submit is the ~1fps stall). The UI-texture composite is kept EXACTLY as-is for active FG (GTA path, byte-for-byte untouched); the backbuffer function is a separate, isolated, gracefully-skipping function. STRICTLY GATED to `DX12_IsNativeFSRFGSuspendedDisablePending()` in the prework, so GTA's active FSR FG (0 suspensions, session 20260703_213508) never reaches it. Diagnostic: `FSR-suspend overlay drawn onto PRESENTED BACKBUFFER via CE queue ...`; prework log gains `route=suspend-backbuffer|ui-resource`. Units: `NativeFSRNoCallbackSuspendRidesBundleNeverStallingBackbuffer`, `SuspendBackbufferOverlayUsesCEQueueGatedToSuspension` (wiring + CE-queue-only invariant), revised `NoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRouteNeverSubmitsBackbufferWhenRuntimeOwnsSwapchain`. **OPEN — needs on-hardware validation:** (a) test app overlay now visible + full-speed during suspend; (b) GTA/Talos still crash-free (the backbuffer function only runs if a real game ever suspends FSR FG — GTA didn't, but if it does, `GetBuffer`-on-proxy + the `PRESENT`-state barrier assumption are the unproven parts, guarded to skip-not-crash).
- **RETAINED-SWAPCHAIN LEAK BOUNDARY (2026-07-02, session 20260702_092933 — GTA crash on FSR→DLSS APPLY):** the retained Streamline startup-activation swapchain is an AddRef'd COM reference; while CE pins it, DXGI refuses a replacement swapchain on the same HWND (E_ACCESSDENIED) and a runtime-managed create failure is FATAL (GTA null-derefs the missing swapchain). Rules: (1) startup-transport retains (bypass / overlayless-handoff present paths) STOP at PostSL confirmation (`ShouldRetainStreamlineStartupActivationSwapchainFromStartupTransport` — the slot is never consulted after confirmation, so later retains are pure leaks; the single release fires AT confirmation); (2) the post-FSR Streamline runtime swapchain create releases the retained chain BEFORE forwarding (make-before-break, INLINE defer block); (3) E_ACCESSDENIED is NEVER blindly passed through — runtime-managed/third-party creates get the minimal CE unpin (release retained chain, no overlay teardown/GPU flush) + retry, escalating to the full overlay cleanup only if the HWND stays pinned (`ChooseCreateSwapchainAccessDeniedRecovery`). Regression tests in `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` (retain gate, recovery choice, source invariants).
- **DEADLOCK BOUNDARY (2026-07-02, session 20260701_213656 — permanent GTA freeze on the FIRST FSR-FG frame):** CE must NEVER call `ffxConfigure` (RegisterUiResource or anything else) from AMD's presenter thread — i.e. never from `DetourPresent`/real-swapchain present paths during runtime-owned no-callback FSR FG. Proven mechanism (freeze dump + FSR SDK v1.1.3 `FrameInterpolationSwapchainDX12.cpp`): AMD's proxy `Present` takes its swapchain `criticalSection` on the game thread, then `waitForFenceValue(compositionFenceCPU, previousFramesSentForPresentation)` **spins on `ID3D12Fence::GetCompletedValue` with NO timeout while HOLDING the criticalSection**; only the presenter thread advances that fence via the real present; AMD's `registerUiResource` takes the SAME criticalSection. CE's re-assert from the presenter thread closed the cycle. Enforcement: `MayReassertSubstituteUiResource(driver)` policy + hard runtime guard in `FFXHook_ReRegisterSubstituteUiResource` (refuses + logs outside the proxy prework, thread_local `t_InsideFFXProxyPresentPrework`), regression tests `FFXUiCompositeDriverPolicyTest.*` and `DXGISharedSourceTest.NoCallbackSubstituteUiResourceReassertOnlyFromProxyPrework`. Also: no heavy CE work (backend init took ~70ms on frame 1) on the presenter thread — the prework's lazy init now lands on the game thread; the presenter-thread stall was what pushed AMD into the CS-held fence-spin state in the first place.
- Freeze diagnostics for this area: `[ffx-proxy-present-freeze-diag]` (hook installed/driving, prework count/tid/qpc) and `[subst-rereg-freeze-diag]` (re-assert in-flight bracket qpc/tid — a stuck bracket IS the registerUiResource lock-wedge signature), both emitted with `[ffx-ui-composite-freeze-diag]` from the freeze watchdog.
- Open/stale-risk: after the `ffxConfigure` VEH permanently disarms on no-callback detection, intra-module `RegisterUiResource` calls stop being intercepted, so `g_CachedFFXUiTexture` may freeze at a startup-window pointer. The composite re-draws onto that texture every present (fine if GTA reuses one UI resource — the `20260623_060436` log showed it did for the ~18 frames before the crash), but if GTA rotates UI textures the overlay would flicker/blank. `SetBundleTargetTexture` logs the cached pointer + change flag so one GTA run answers the rotation question. The per-present re-assert (proxy prework) re-forwards CE's SUBSTITUTE each frame, so for the GTA degenerate-1x1 path the cache-freeze question is moot; it remains open only for hypothetical rotating **game-tex** UI resources. GTA validation of the proxy-prework driver (visible overlay + no freeze) is PENDING — the 20260701 session froze on frame 1 before any visibility evidence.
- The tree now has a shared FG session/planner layer in `hook/common/fg_session_state.{h,cpp}` that captures the current mixed DX12/Streamline/FFX FG state, computes a concrete `FGActionPlan`, and emits structured transition/session logs. It is currently used as the common authority for diagnostics and publication, while some low-level queue/route/transport execution still remains in the older DX12/DXGI code paths.
- `hook/common/dx12_fg_transition_model.cpp` is now a compatibility adapter over that planner-backed session snapshot instead of a separate competing reducer. Existing transition/replay tests still validate the same public transition contract, but the underlying snapshot now comes from the shared FG session layer.
- The planner currently sees explicit hook events from DX12, Streamline, FFX, and top-level Present observation for at least: authoritative Streamline startup handoff, authoritative FFX takeover, native-FSR configure on/off, PostSL callback install/remove, PostSL activation complete, PostSL first confirmed render, swapchain invalidation, Streamline runtime updates, and top-level Present observation.
- Intercepted `slGetFeatureFunction` lookups for DLSSG feature functions should return CE's stable wrapper when a callable original/trampoline exists, even when inline patching reports ready. This keeps cached game/app feature pointers observable across Streamline export reload/repair during mixed-FG switches; direct import and inline hooks still cover direct callers.
- Fresh `sl.*.dll` module-load notifications must not proactively call Streamline feature-function lookup. `installed/captureengine/logs/20260601_152148` crashed inside Streamline during `slInit` after CE's load-notification path re-entered plugin/feature lookup while Streamline was still mutating plugin state. Module-load inspection may use direct exports/IAT readiness, but DLSSG/Reflex feature lookup is deferred to normal runtime calls. Healthy logs include `Deferred proactive feature-function lookup during module load`.
- A post-FSR DLSS handoff with safe bootstrap proof is stronger than generic startup evidence. It may bypass the repeated-callback PostSL activation countdown and reactivation warmup so the overlay does not visibly blank during the short FSR->DLSS interval. Pure-DLSS cold startup still keeps the warmup.
- Pure-DLSS startup can be proven either by explicit `slDLSSGSetOptions(ON)` or by official active state from `slDLSSGGetState` (`updateActive=1` / CE `g_StreamlineFGRunning=1`). The latter is still stronger than mere Streamline DLL presence and is enough to invoke normal-route PostSL callbacks and bypass the startup callback deferral; logs should show `activeDLSSSignal=1`.
- Pure `DLSS FG -> off` menu suspend/resume with no FSR history, no FSR API active, no runtime-owned native-FSR present path, a healthy device, and a live overlay/sync/swapchain queue can rebuild immediately after the safe drain. Do not spend the generic 60-frame FG handoff cooldown blanking the overlay in that case. Mixed/post-FSR paths keep the stricter cooldown because their queue/swapchain teardown proof is different.
- Current trace-replay tests explicitly cover:
  - Talos-style `off -> DLSS -> off -> FSR`
  - GTA-style `FSR -> DLSS` without a clean `off`
  - GTA-style DLSS suspension and resume during loading
  - startup coexistence using startup bypass first and normal routing after settle
- Current overlay status tests explicitly cover visible label switching between `FSR FG` and `DLSS FG`, plus clearing back to `FG` when frame generation turns off.
- Talos `installed/captureengine/logs/20260423_215138` / `20260423_220858` and GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260424_020300` showed that generic FG switching correctness also depends on CE actually observing the last Streamline feature-call edge. When Streamline export inline patching fails or a title uses newer feature entrypoints, CE still needs generic direct-import / dynamic-lookup interception for `slDLSSGSetOptions`, `slDLSSGGetState`, current Reflex `slReflexSetOptions`, and legacy `slReflexSetConstants`, and that fallback has to be armed on the actual owner module of the failing export rather than only on the core Streamline DLLs. Otherwise CE can miss either the menu-side `DLSS FG -> off` edge that clears the overlay label or the Reflex `frameLimitUs` traffic needed to diagnose stale half-rate caps after DLSS FG is disabled.
- Talos `installed/captureengine/logs/20260425_002642` on build `0.1.2584` sharpened that rule: the game turned DLSS FG off in the 2D menu, but CE only saw steady active `slDLSSGGetState` and never saw an explicit OFF edge before the user noticed the stale label. Feature-hook discovery now covers every loaded `sl.*.dll`, not just `sl.interposer.dll` / `sl.common.dll`, and direct-import fallback retries are idempotent so late-loaded/menu-side imports can be patched without corrupting the original target.
- Talos `installed/captureengine/logs/20260425_173428` on build `0.1.2587` sharpened the 2D-menu `FSR FG -> DLSS FG` path. A fresh authoritative Streamline handoff created a new runtime-owned swapchain queue and CE detected DLSS FG through active `slDLSSGGetState`, but PostSL remained dormant because `safeBootstrap=0` while no SL wrapper queue appeared in the menu. The current guard now marks that fresh handoff as pending immediately to suppress false queue-change `FSR_FG` relabels, and accepts a runtime-owned Streamline swapchain queue as safe post-FSR bootstrap evidence when it is the live command queue and its ECL submit path is already tracked.
- GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260425_000339` showed that a pure-DLSS enable can still produce transient `slDLSSGGetState` OFF jitter after PostSL has already confirmed and submitted more than the short frame 9-12 stale-OFF stabilization window. The current guard now keeps only GetState OFF deferred until the 30-frame PostSL warmup proof threshold; explicit `slDLSSGSetOptions(OFF)` uses the older shorter guard so user/requested disables are not broadened by the GetState-only protection.
- Explicit native-FSR off via `ffxConfigure(frameGenerationEnabled=0)` is now treated as stronger evidence than queue-change/ECL heuristics during runtime-owned teardown. That prevents `FSR_FG -> off` from immediately re-latching heuristic `FSR_FG` on the lingering runtime-owned queue and leaving the overlay status stale. GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260519_144449` sharpened the endpoint: if FSR has explicitly configured OFF and a later swapchain queue proof returns to `origGame` while no authoritative FSR runtime is active, CE must end the runtime-owned native-FG teardown instead of preserving ownership solely because the stale native-FG present path latch is still true.
- FFX present-callback bridge installation is only for enabled native-FSR frame-generation configures that actually provide a real app/default present callback to wrap. Disabled `ffxConfigure(frameGenerationEnabled=0)` packets can repeat rapidly during teardown; they should be treated as OFF evidence and diagnostic breadcrumbs, not as a reason to reinstall CE's callback bridge. Existing bridge state may remain available for any final already-in-flight runtime callback until context destroy. GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260519_191243` sharpened the startup re-enable variant: a fresh runtime-owned native-FSR takeover can send an initial disabled startup-arming configure before the real enabled configure. CE preserves the authoritative FSR-arming state for that packet, but still forwards the disabled configure unmodified and waits for an enabled configure before installing the CE callback bridge. GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260602_161000_gtafreezestartwithfsrfg` sharpened the no-callback variant: if enabled native FSR supplies `presentCallback=null`, CE must preserve AMD's internal no-callback composition path instead of synthesizing its own FFX present callback and taking over current-to-output composition. Expected diagnostics include `Native FSR disabled startup-arming configure forwarded without CE present-callback bridge`, `Native FSR disabled configure used for startup arming`, `Native FSR enabled with no app present callback`, and `Native FSR present routing configured ... internalNoCallback=1`.
- Official AMD FFX startup swapchain creation before direct enabled FFX API proof is a protected pass-through. GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260520_012459` showed process exit `0xC0000409` immediately after `amd_fidelityfx_dx12.dll` created a runtime-owned swapchain behind EOS, before any `ffxConfigure` line. CE latches native-FSR startup arming and FSR history there and returns from the nested create/present path before Present-hook refresh, queue-ownership mutation, FFX hook retry/export inspection, deferred probes, capture, or normal overlay GPU work. Live Streamline/PostSL is quiesced immediately. The staged Direct queue is deferred takeover/topology evidence only; it must never receive pre-enable overlay work. GTA freeze dumps `20260525_195848_gtafreeze` and `20260602_153554` disprove progress-only graduation and staged-queue overlay ECLs, while GTA hang session `20260714_142550` further disproves the later sustained-progress dormant normal draw. The only visibility exception is the already-hooked game-facing proxy Present: `protected-startup-backbuffer` draws onto the proxy's passthrough buffer on the target-validated game/producer queue before AMD's internal handoff. Expected diagnostics include `keeping nested real-swapchain work tracking-only`, `protected-startup-backbuffer`, backend preservation, and sustained-progress-remains-quiesced. Old overlay-only/staged-queue normal draws, protected-startup cooldown bypasses, sync/reinit bootstrap, or progress finalization breadcrumbs are regressions.

- The 2-second timeout enforcement (build 0.1.3409) and the overlay completion fence (build 0.1.3410) both **failed** — the AMD FSR FG runtime rejects ANY unexpected `ExecuteCommandLists` on the shared device, regardless of fencing or timing. The root cause is not about GPU work completion (inconsistent backbuffer) but about the AMD driver actively monitoring the queue and removing the device when unexpected ECLs appear.

- The current official AMD FFX bridge path has two safe interception layers. Official AMD modules still skip standard inline JMP export hooks, but use IAT and dynamic `GetProcAddress` routing for `ffxCreateContext`, `ffxConfigure`, and `ffxDestroyContext`; `FFXHook::RegisterDynamicHooks()` must run before process-wide `GetProcAddress` interception is enabled so an early native-FSR preload cannot cache original unwrapped FFX entrypoints. Build `0.1.3610` adds a narrow guarded re-arming int3/VEH fallback for official DX12 `ffxConfigure` because some SDK dispatch-table or intra-module calls bypass both dynamic lookups and caller IAT thunks. Expected diagnostics include `FFX Hook: Registered module-filtered dynamic hooks for FFX exports`, `FFX Hook: Using IAT/dynamic hooks for protected official FFX module ... guarded ffxConfigure VEH fallback enabled`, `FFX Hook: Armed VEH breakpoint for ...!ffxConfigure`, `GetProcAddress: Intercepted FFX API ffxConfigure` when the dynamic route is used, `FFX Hook: Installed DX12 overlay present-callback bridge for context=...`, and `DX12: FFX present callback rendered overlay on runtime-owned FSR path`.

- The FFX present-callback overlay backend should be allowed when official/direct FFX evidence exists and a real callback bridge is active, even if `HookHasRuntimeOwnedNativeFGPresentPath()` is still false. `ShouldBridgeOverlayViaFFXPresentCallback(...)` trusts any of: runtime-owned native-FG path, authoritative FSR API-active state, direct FFX confirmation, or an FSR runtime mode. This matters for the local `dx12_fsr_fg_test.exe` path, where the callback bridge can be installed and active before the older native-FG-present-path latch is set. While native FSR owns presentation through an active CE callback bridge, separate normal `ProcessFrame` overlay work should remain suppressed. The exception is official native FSR with no app present callback: AMD's runtime keeps its internal composition path, CE should not expect FFX callback progress, and normal DX12 overlay work is allowed on the runtime-owned swapchain queue. Healthy no-callback diagnostics are `Native FSR uses AMD internal no-callback composition; allowing normal overlay rendering`; callback-bridge sessions should still show `DX12: FFX present callback rendered overlay on runtime-owned FSR path`. After a protected official-FFX startup reaches enabled `ffxConfigure`, `FSR FG active but scQueue=null, SKIPPING overlay` is now suspicious unless a prior `Protected official FFX startup could not stage runtime queue` explains why no Direct queue was available.

- **No-app-callback native FSR overlay goes through the game's UI RESOURCE, not AMD's present queue (2026-06-18, commit 8593c70; dumps `20260618_155443` + `20260618_201038`).** SUPERSEDES the older "draw the overlay through the normal DX12 route on the runtime-owned swapchain queue" guidance — that route (separate overlay ECL+`Signal` on AMD's runtime present queue via `SubmitOverlayCommandList`) WEDGES AMD's presenter in ~200-300 frames, the same `amd_fidelityfx_dx12!ffxQuery` pacing wedge as the synthesized present-callback (~8 frames): AMD's presenter parks INFINITE on its auto-reset pacing event while the game render thread spins in AMD's QPC-timed fence poll (`ffxQuery+0x225fe`). CE's overlay GPU work itself completes (breadcrumb) — the wedge is AMD's pacing reacting to a foreign submission on its present queue. The escape: GTA (and any FSR3.1 game using HUD composition) registers a UI resource every frame via `ffxConfigure` **type=0x00030002** (`FrameGenerationSwapChain RegisterUiResource` on the swapchain context); AMD composites it onto real+generated frames POST-interpolation on its OWN queue. CE intercepts that configure (`Hooked_ffxConfigure`) and draws the inject overlay ONTO the game's registered UI texture (`DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoFFXUiResource`), submitting on `g_OriginalGameQueue` — NEVER AMD's runtime present queue — then forwards unchanged. `ShouldSkipSeparateOverlayGpuWorkForRuntimeOwnedFrameGeneration` skips the legacy runtime-queue submit while `DX12_IsFFXUiResourceCompositionActive()` (recency-gated). Zero AMD-pacing-queue perturbation → no wedge; post-interpolation → no ghosting. Healthy diagnostics: `FFX UI-composite overlay drawn onto game UI resource ... on GAME queue ... — no AMD-runtime-queue submit`. INVARIANT: never put CE overlay GPU work (ECL or fence Signal) on AMD's runtime-owned present queue for native FSR FG; the legacy runtime-queue route remains only as a fallback when a game registers no UI resource. GTA runtime validation pending. **(2026-06-22 update — see the crash-boundary entry directly below: the LIVE per-frame UI-composition path is the game-ECL bundle `RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL`, NOT `DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoFFXUiResource` (that separate-ECL/CE-queue composite is now dead code, never wired up); and for GTA's 1×1 placeholder the bundle draws onto a CE-substituted backbuffer-sized texture.)**
- **CRASH BOUNDARY + CE-substituted UI texture for GTA's 1×1 placeholder (2026-06-22; crash dump `installed/captureengine/logs/20260621_191028`).** Iteration-1's `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` picked `kMinimalBackbuffer` (→ `DX12_ProcessFrameMinimal`) when the bundle was not firing, submitting overlay GPU work on AMD's runtime/swapchain queue while AMD owned the swapchain → `amd_fidelityfx_dx12!ffxQuery` null-deref AV (no CE frame on the stack). **INVARIANT (the crash boundary): under runtime-owned native FSR FG, CE performs ZERO GPU work on AMD's runtime present queue OR the swapchain backbuffer.** `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute(runtimeOwnsSwapchain, cached, firing)` now ALWAYS returns `kSkipBundleCovers` when AMD owns the swapchain (the overlay rides UI composition only); `kMinimalBackbuffer` is reachable only when AMD does NOT own the swapchain. `DetourPresent` gates on `DoesFGRuntimeOwnSwapchain() || HookHasRuntimeOwnedNativeFGPresentPath()` and has a defensive guard-rail that refuses (and loudly logs) any backbuffer submit under runtime-owned FG. **GTA registers a 1×1 placeholder UI texture** (composition enabled, `flags=0x2`, but empty), so drawing onto it is useless (and trips `list->Reset` E_INVALIDARG). `DX12_PrepareFFXUiOverlayTarget` (called from `Hooked_ffxConfigure` RegisterUiResource) uses `ChooseFFXUiOverlayTarget(gameTexW/H, backbufferW/H)`: a usable full-size game UI texture → blend overlay onto it (test app); a **degenerate** placeholder → create a CE-owned **backbuffer-sized** texture (`EnsureCEUiSubstituteTexture`), **substitute** it into the forwarded `RegisterUiResource` desc (AMD then composites CE's texture), and cache it as the bundle target with a transparent-clear flag. The per-frame refresh is still the game-ECL bundle (`RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL`, no per-frame ffxConfigure interception needed); it now SKIPS any degenerate target (never the 1×1 garbage submit) and clears the CE substitute to transparent each frame. **Rejected: per-frame `RegisterUiResource` interception (plan Part C)** — verified not viable for GTA's call pattern: inline/export hooks fail-fast AMD, the IAT patch does NOT catch GTA's per-frame calls (cache froze the instant the one-shot VEH disarmed), and the re-armed 0xCC VEH is the documented multi-threaded wedge. **OPEN (GTA-run-gated):** if GTA natively re-registers its 1×1 every frame after the VEH disarms, it overrides CE's substitute (substitution only lands on registers caught before disarm) → overlay invisible again but NO crash. The `SetBundleTargetTexture` `changed` flag + `Substituted CE full-size UI texture ...` logs settle it. Healthy diagnostics: `Substituted CE full-size UI texture %p (%ux%u ...)`, `FFX UI-bundle target ce-substitute-tex=...`, `FFX UI-bundle overlay appended to game ECL`, `Cached no-callback FSR FG backbuffer geometry ...`. Regression: any `GUARD — refusing minimal backbuffer ProcessFrame under runtime-owned no-callback FSR FG`. Units: `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` (`NoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRouteNeverSubmitsBackbufferWhenRuntimeOwnsSwapchain`, `FFXUiOverlayTargetSubstitutesForDegenerateGameTexture`). **Live-queue bundle (2026-06-22, `logs/20260622_172043`):** the game-ECL bundle must fire on the queue the game ACTUALLY renders on — once AMD's FfxFrameInterpolationSwapchain owns presentation the game submits on the FG-runtime-owned swapchain queue and `g_OriginalGameQueue` goes idle, so an origGame-only bundle never fires and (with the backbuffer route gone) the overlay blanks. The shared `TryAppendNoCallbackBundleOverlay` helper accepts `pThis == g_OriginalGameQueue || pThis == g_SwapchainQueue` and is wired into the no-callback ECL fast-path (attempts the bundle before force-forwarding non-origGame ECLs); appending to the game's own runtime-queue submission (NumLists+1, same ECL call) is NOT a separate submit, so it stays within the crash boundary. Per-frame latch reset via `DX12_ResetNoCallbackBundleFrame()` from `DetourPresent` (replaces the `DX12_ProcessFrameMinimal` reset). Unit: `NoCallbackBundleFiresOnLiveFGRuntimeQueueNotOnlyOrigGame`.
- **SUPERSEDED 2026-06-23 (GTA crash `installed/captureengine/logs/20260623_060436`): the game-ECL bundle described in the two entries above was REMOVED — it crashed GTA.** The bundle reused its 3-slot allocators with no GPU fence (it "rode the game's fence", which does NOT gate CE's allocator reuse); during GTA's FSR-takeover churn the GPU fell >3 frames behind and CE reset an allocator whose appended command list was still executing → `nvwgf2umx` null-deref inside `ExecuteCommandLists`. The substitution / crash-boundary / route / suspend / FSR→off machinery from the two entries above is UNCHANGED — only the per-frame *drive mechanism* (bundle → composite) changed. The retired names (`RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL`, `TryAppendNoCallbackBundleOverlay`, `EnsureFFXUiCompositeBundleResources`, `DX12_ResetNoCallbackBundleFrame`, `DX12_IsFFXUiBundleOverlayActivelyFiring`, `DX12_ShouldCompositeOverlayOntoFFXUiResource`) and the `FFX UI-bundle …` log strings no longer exist; healthy diagnostics are now `FFX UI-composite overlay drawn via CE queue … fenceCompleted=… waitTimedOut=0` + `FFX UI-composite target ce-substitute-tex=…`. - `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` is now the local mixed-runtime stress test for real-world FG mode switching. It starts with all FG off, automatically switches OFF -> FSR -> DLSS -> FSR, and supports live keys `1` off, `2` DLSS, and `3` FSR without restarting the process. Default auto timings are intentionally asymmetric now: FSR starts after 3 seconds, DLSS starts after 12 seconds, and the return to FSR waits until 30 seconds so DLSS-G has enough time to initialize and report generated frames. Config keys/CLI overrides are `auto_fsr_start_seconds` / `--auto-fsr-start`, `auto_dlss_start_seconds` / `--auto-dlss-start`, and `auto_return_fsr_seconds` / `--auto-return-fsr`. FSR sessions now default to `fsr_present_callback_toggle_stress=1`: each FSR entry starts with `presentCallback=null` / AMD internal no-callback routing, then alternates into the app-callback route every `fsr_present_callback_toggle_interval_seconds` seconds (`--fsr-present-callback-interval`, default 6). The on-screen test-app status appends `INT` during the internal no-callback route, and logs `presentCallbackRoute=amd-internal` or `presentCallbackRoute=app-callback`. It writes `[FG-DIAG] Switching FG mode` / `Mode now` lines so a single app log can prove transition order, official SDK result codes, cleanup behavior, callback routing, and resolved auto timings. **Opt-in degenerate-UI mode (default OFF, preserves universal coverage):** `[Stress] fsr_degenerate_ui_resource=1` / `--fsr-degenerate-ui` registers a 1×1 UI placeholder instead of the full-size UI texture, mimicking GTA V Enhanced's degenerate no-callback FSR FG registration so an INJECTED run exercises CE's substitution path (`DX12_PrepareFFXUiOverlayTarget` → `EnsureCEUiSubstituteTexture`). It is a synthetic proxy for the GTA 1×1 case that isolates "does AMD composite a CE-substituted texture at all" from GTA's per-frame re-registration behavior; the default run still registers the full-size UI texture (the composite-onto-game-texture path). Diagnostic: `[FG-DIAG] Degenerate-UI mode: registering 1x1 UI placeholder ...`; the placeholder is device-bound and released/recreated across FSR→DLSS→FSR switches.

- Leaving active FSR FG at runtime is not just an API flag change in the test apps. A disabled but still FSR-owned swapchain can stop advancing the frame-latency waitable, and normal overlay submissions on a disabled/inactive FSR-owned swapchain can still remove the D3D12 device with `0x887A002B`. The test-app runtime OFF path therefore destroys the FSR context and recreates a native swapchain; cleanup does not recreate a native swapchain because the process is exiting. CE must continue treating FSR-owned presentation as callback-only until ownership is actually gone **for callback-bridge sessions**; the internal no-callback composition route is the explicit exception (see the suspension invariant below) because it has no bridge that could render the overlay.
- **A game-created swapchain after explicit native-FSR OFF/destroy ends the runtime-owned teardown (2026-06-11, `installed/captureengine/logs/20260611_191950`).** Runtime ownership was classified as `pQueue != origGame`, so a game that recreates its swapchain on a FRESH queue after leaving FSR FG stayed misclassified as runtime-owned forever: the FSR_FG->Off transition armed the 60-frame draw cooldown ("preserving FSR queue ownership until a stronger off signal appears"), the swapchain change armed the 90-frame recent-FG reinit cooldown, and stale heuristics could re-latch FSR_FG on the plain game queue. Current invariant: a swapchain created by a caller that is neither an FG runtime, an FFX stack, nor a third-party overlay, while explicit native-FSR OFF or contexts-destroyed evidence is pending, IS the stronger off signal (`ShouldEndRuntimeOwnedNativeFGTeardownOnGameSwapchainCreation`): CE ends ownership, clears the no-callback latch/heuristics/arming state at the create hook, records the recovery queue, exempts the FSR_FG->Off transition cooldown (`IsGameSwapchainRecoveryToggleAfterNativeFSROff`), and reinits the overlay immediately on the recovery swapchain change (`ShouldReinitOverlayImmediatelyAfterGameSwapchainRecoveryFromNativeFSROff`). Same session also proved two robustness facts: the test app's generation-1 raw FFX export pointers can bypass the `ffxDestroyContext` dynamic hook entirely (only `ffxConfigure` has the VEH fallback), and swapchain pointer reuse can defeat `g_LastSwapChain` change detection (destroyed AMD swapchain and the new game swapchain shared the same heap address), so the recovery edge must not depend on either signal alone. Expected diagnostics: `Game-created swapchain after explicit native FSR OFF/destroy — ending runtime-owned native-FG teardown`, `gameSwapchainRecoveryToggle=1` in the no-cooldown transition log, `Swapchain change is game-created swapchain recovery after explicit native FSR OFF/destroy — immediate overlay reinit`. **Follow-up (2026-06-12, `installed/captureengine/logs/20260612_000936`)**: ending ownership alone made the overlay disappear FOREVER, because the accidental keep-alives (runtimeOwns latch, heuristic FSR) were what had kept ProcessFrame alive: frame classification still counted ECLs against the game's RETIRED original queue, so every present on the recovered swapchain classified as zero-ECL/interpolated and `ShouldSkipProcessFrameForZeroECLPresent` starved ProcessFrame. Current invariant: the recovery edge also RE-BASELINES `g_OriginalGameQueue` to the game-created recovery queue (pointer-guarded; Talos-style same-queue recreates no-op), so classification/routing/future FG-cycle proofs anchor on the queue that actually presents, and `ShouldSkipProcessFrameForZeroECLPresent` has a recovery-queue escape as defense-in-depth (presents on the game-created recovery swapchain are real game frames by construction). Expected diagnostic: `Re-baselined original game queue to game-created recovery queue`.
- **No-callback native-FSR suspension must keep the normal overlay route alive (2026-06-11, `installed/captureengine/logs/20260611_142923`).** A disabled `ffxConfigure` with no bridge and no app callback while the runtime-owned swapchain is still the live present path is a suspension, not a teardown: `g_NativeFSRInternalNoCallbackComposition` is retained (`ShouldRetainNativeFSRInternalNoCallbackCompositionForDisabledConfigure`), separate overlay GPU work stays allowed, and `DecideSwapchainOverlayRouting` keeps the FSR swapchain queue (`nativeFSRInternalNoCallbackCompositionLive` parameter) instead of the post-FSR original-queue recovery (which would be a cross-queue mismatch against the still-live FSR backbuffers). The latch is force-cleared on contexts destroyed, explicit teardown end via origGame swapchain return, Streamline FG comeback, and shutdown. FSR_FG<->Off mode toggles skip the 60-frame draw cooldown only when the overlay backend already renders on the exact runtime-owned swapchain queue (`IsLiveNoCallbackNativeFSRSuspensionToggle`); and the swapchain change right after a finalized enabled-configure FFX takeover reinits the overlay immediately instead of blanking through the 90-frame cooldown (`ShouldReinitOverlayImmediatelyAfterNoCallbackFFXTakeoverSwapchainChange`). All bypasses require enabled-`ffxConfigure` proof, so pre-enable protected startup and app-callback/bridge sessions keep all existing cooldowns. Expected diagnostics: `Native FSR suspension retains internal no-callback composition route`, `retainedNoCallbackSuspension=1`, `liveNoCallbackNativeFSRSuspensionToggle=1`, `Swapchain change is finalized no-callback official FFX takeover — immediate overlay reinit`, `Cleared retained native FSR internal no-callback composition route`. Unit coverage: `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` (`SuspendedNoCallbackNativeFSRKeepsFSRSwapchainQueueRouting`, `LiveNoCallbackNativeFSRSuspensionToggle*`, `NativeFSRNoCallbackCompositionRetainedAcrossSuspension`, `FinalizedNoCallbackFFXTakeoverReinitsOverlayImmediately`).
- **[OVERLAY COVERAGE] is the FG-transition blank regression gate (2026-06-13; tightened 2026-07-16).** Every processed present (top-level `DX12_ProcessFrameExternal` plus independently routed `PostSLOverlayRenderGated` invocations) is accounted covered/uncovered from the draw-counter delta of all overlay routes; an inline PostSL keep-alive called inside ProcessFrame belongs to that enclosing Present and is not double-counted. Zero-ECL interpolated frames and SL-owned transport Presents inherit coverage only when the active route proves it. Interruption/restoration logs report `missed/longestStreak/gate/route`; transition edges and shutdown log summaries. Current validation requires zero blank presented outputs and no `INTERRUPTED/UNPROVEN` or uncovered-streak marker; the older 1-2-present tolerance is superseded. `gate=` attributes any regression to the responsible skip site. User-watched run `20260716_132719` showed a desktop pixel sampler can miss a real 188 ms interruption, so automated transition tests must treat runtime coverage markers as strict failure gates alongside pixels, never pixels as the sole final oracle.
- **FG-detection heuristic evidence is reset at every transition/recovery edge (2026-06-13, session `logs/20260612_215439`).** `RequestFGDetectionHeuristicReset()` resets both the queue-change heuristic AND the ECL-count-pattern counters. Stale interp counts from a finished FG phase re-latched phantom `FSR_FG` on the fresh post-FSR-off swapchain and the resulting double label flip armed two 60-frame draw cooldowns (61-present blank on a healthy overlay). Defense-in-depth: `IsHeuristicOnlyRuntimeModeFlip` — a mode flip with `sl_signal 0->0`, no runtime ownership, no authoritative FSR, and the overlay backend live on the current queue is a label change, not a transport change, and must not arm the draw cooldown. `IsLiveNoCallbackNativeFSRSuspensionToggle` accepts `kStreamlineNoFG` as the non-FSR side (with SL DLLs merely loaded the classifier never reports `kOff`); the hard proof requirements (enabled-configure no-callback latch, runtime ownership, backend bound to the exact live scQueue) are unchanged.
- **DX12 overlay backends are device-scoped and stay WARM across FG transitions (2026-06-13).** `CustomOverlay::DX12Backend` stores but never uses its bound queue; the DescFree backend fetches the backbuffer per frame. Warm reuse is device+format scoped (`CanReuseWarmDX12OverlayBackend`); FG transitions rebuild only swapchain/queue-bound state (RTVs via `CleanupRTVs`, allocators/fence via `InitOverlaySync`) after the existing GPU drains. The x64 DescFree backend survives `CleanupRTVs` and is rebuilt only on device/RTV-format change (`EnsureDescFreeBackendForDeviceAndFormat`), x86 Texture2D selection, or shutdown. The x86 Texture2D adapter keeps its original swapchain-scoped teardown.
- **Pure-DLSS engage is no-blank only under the explicit-enable proof (2026-06-13).** `HasExplicitEnablePureDLSSColdStartProof` (explicit per-comeback `slDLSSGSetOptions(ON)` provenance + retained startup-activation swapchain + installed PostSL callback) bypasses the 8-callback pure-DLSS countdown and the 15-callback cold-start warmup. GetState-only enables keep both protections — that is the historical GTA startup-churn/hang family. GTA/Talos validation gates this proof; rollback is dropping the proof from the two bypass sites.
- **The explicit-enable warmup bypass must SURVIVE the retained-swapchain release; a confirmed render in the epoch is the authoritative bypass (2026-06-13, session `logs/20260613_044046`).** `HasExplicitEnablePureDLSSColdStartProof` requires `hasRetainedStartupActivationSwapchain`, but the FIRST confirmed PostSL render RELEASES that retained swapchain (`ReleaseStreamlineStartupActivationSwapchain`, the "never pin a swapchain" invariant). So the explicit-enable proof bypassed the cold-start warmup only on reactivation frame 1; frames 2..15 lost the proof and fell back into the 15-frame `kPostSLColdStartWarmup`, blanking a LIVE overlay for **14 presents (~118 ms)** — gate=`postsl-reactivation-warmup`, a direct violation of the C1 no-blank principle. Root cause fix: the warmup exists only to protect the FIRST ECL submit on DLSS-FG's fragile init; once a CONFIRMED render lands (`devRemoved=0`) that first ECL already succeeded, so a confirmed render in the CURRENT reactivation epoch (`g_PostSLConfirmedRenderInCurrentReactivationEpoch`, epoch-scoped: reset at the genuine-reactivation block, set at the confirmed-render edge) bypasses the remaining warmup via a new route-agnostic leg in `ShouldBypassPostSLReactivationWarmup(... postSLConfirmedRenderInCurrentEpoch)`. This CANNOT widen the GTA GetState-only hang family: that family gets no frame-1 bypass, so it produces no confirmed render during the warmup and the leg stays false until the warmup naturally completes. Unit: `ConfirmedRenderThisEpochBypassesRemainingReactivationWarmup`. GTA/Talos GetState-only DLSS-engage re-test gates it; rollback is dropping the leg.
- **HISTORICAL / SUPERSEDED — the four FSR→DLSS-comeback `missed=1` gaps were once treated as a safe architectural floor (2026-06-13, session `logs/20260613_044046`).** `overlay-backend-uninitialized` / `live-overlay-kept-drawing` / `zero-ecl-skip` single-present streaks were attributed to the first present on the freshly-created runtime-owned Streamline swapchain taking the startup normal-route bypass. - **`[OVERLAY COVERAGE]` now brackets blanks start+end (2026-06-13).** Streak onset logs `[OVERLAY COVERAGE] uncovered streak STARTED: gate=… route=… source=… confirmed=… present=…` (capturing start tick + whether PostSL was already confirmed-rendering); streak end adds `durationMs=` and `confirmedDuringStreak=` (a streak with `confirmedDuringStreak=1` is the clearest no-blank-principle red flag). - **DLSS-FG SUSPEND must not blank the live overlay through the FG-off reinit cooldown (2026-06-13, sessions `logs/20260613_145008` and `logs/20260613_150750`).** `slDLSSGSetOptions(off)` (proxy stays alive, DLSS-G stops generating) blanks a confirmed-live overlay because the suspend can take EITHER of two handlers and both armed a draw-suppressing cooldown that the make-before-break keep-alive could not cover (the cooldown deferred the overlay reinit, leaving `overlayInit=false`, which also blocks the C1 keep-drawing path). This is the "not always" — the two repros hit different handlers:

With the cooldown zeroed the forced reinit proceeds immediately, so the blank drops to the ~1-2-present warm-reinit floor.

Fix: `ShouldReinitOverlayImmediatelyAfterConfirmedPostSLSuspensionSwapchainChange` (keep-alive latch + `!streamlineFGRunning` + `!fsrFGApiActive` + `!nativeFSRInternalNoCallbackComposition` + `runtimeOwnsSwapchain` + scQueue==live cmdQueue) joins the existing immediate-reinit fast paths; it does the EXACT same flag resets as the 90-frame branch it replaces — only the cooldown value changes (0 vs 90).
  Both fixes are timing-only changes of an already-proven-safe warm reinit; a suspend has no Streamline teardown to wait for, so the post-teardown first-ECL DEVICE_REMOVED hazard does not apply. Units: `ConfirmedPostSLSuspensionBypassesReinitCooldownEvenWithFSRHistory`, `ConfirmedPostSLSuspensionReinitsOverlayImmediatelyInsteadOfBlanking`. **GTA/Talos DLSS-suspend re-test gates this**; rollback is dropping the two predicates.
- **A warm PostSL resume MUST preserve its live proxy swapchain queue — never clear it as "stale FSR" (2026-06-13, session `logs/20260613_151646`).** The suspend bypass above keeps the overlay rendering through the suspend, which keeps `g_PostSLConfirmedRendering` true, so the resume (`slDLSSGSetOptions(on)`) takes the make-before-break **warm resume** (`resumeConfirmedPostSLFromKeepAlive`, `dx12_hook_main.cpp:7204`): PostSL goes active with NO synthetic-startup re-arm (assumes its direct path persists) and sets `streamlineStartupHandoffPending=false`. - **Coverage inheritance is only valid while `overlayInit` is true (2026-06-13, session `logs/20260613_145008`).** The DLSS-suspend blank above was MASKED from the `[OVERLAY COVERAGE]` gate (longestStreak stayed 2) because the proxy's zero-ECL presents inherited coverage (`isInterpolatedFrame`) while `overlayInit=false` and nothing was drawing — the inheritance model assumes the FG runtime composites the last overlay-covered frame, but a suspended runtime presents FRESH game frames with no CE overlay. `coverageInheritsFGComposedOverlay` (`dx12_hook_main.cpp` ProcessFrameExternal) is now gated on `g_State.overlayInit`: when the backend is not bound to the current swapchain, zero-ECL/SL-owned presents count as UNCOVERED so the blank is measured instead of hidden. - GTA `installed/captureengine/logs/20260531_151041_gtacrashondlssfgtofsrfg`, `installed/captureengine/logs/20260531_185019`, `installed/captureengine/logs/20260531_230629_gtafsrfgblackwindowcontent`, and `installed/captureengine/logs/20260602_161000_gtafreezestartwithfsrfg` refined the FFX present-callback copy/mirror policy. - The FFX present-callback bridge must be idempotent and self-recursion-safe. - Note: the earlier **universal 2-second max overlay suspension** approach (build `0.1.3409`) was **REJECTED** — it caused `ERR_GFX_STATE` (D3D device removal) in GTA V Enhanced with FSR FG because overlay GPU work was submitted without a completion fence, allowing the FFX runtime to read an inconsistent backbuffer. - Crash-like process exits that bypass CE's VEH/UEF path now have a narrow pre-termination dump guard. The hook DLL application-import/intercepts current-process fail-fast/termination APIs for crash-like NTSTATUS exit codes such as `0xC0000409`, captures at most one supplemental CE dump via temp/rename, then forwards to the original API. Windows-directory modules are excluded from fatal IAT patching. Non-FG normal exits, debugger-only `RaiseException` traffic, and CE's own external-dump-storm termination code are ignored; active/recent-FG exits may capture one diagnostic dump so FG teardown remains inspectable. The fallback includes inline hooks for `RaiseFailFastException`, `TerminateProcess`, `ExitProcess`, `RtlExitUserProcess`, and `NtTerminateProcess` so direct export calls that bypass patched application imports still get one dump attempt. Exception-raising primitives remain byte-identical and are covered through VEH plus IAT/dynamic interception with static-import forwarding. For KERNELBASE/kernel32 forwarded inline-hook pairs (`RaiseFailFastException`, `TerminateProcess`, `ExitProcess`) and Nt/Zw aliases, CE installs only one successful target per pair. Every callable trampoline is atomically published before its inline patch becomes live and before its application-import route becomes reachable. `HookedRtlExitUserProcess` must use the hook DLL's static ntdll `RtlExitUserProcess` fallback; `ExitProcess` is recursively equivalent on Windows and caused the seven `0xC00000FD` shutdown dumps in `20260716_025345`. Expected diagnostics include `FatalExitDump: Installed pre-termination dump hooks`, `FatalExitDump: Installed inline pre-termination hook`, and `FatalExitDump: Capturing pre-termination dump before crash-like process exit or active FG runtime exit`.
- Crash dump writing is now minimal-first for the normal crash-handler worker and the pre-termination fatal-exit guard. Talos `installed/captureengine/logs/20260524_182433` produced only a zero-byte `.dmp.inprogress` when the earlier richer dump attempt did not complete. The current invariant is: first write/promote a `MiniDumpNormal` artifact (`minimal-primary` / `minimal-no-exception`), then try broader compatibility/rich variants only after a usable dump exists. Expected diagnostics include `CrashHandler: using minimal-first crash dump attempts`, `minimal-primary`, and `FatalExitDump: Using minimal-first pre-termination dump attempt`.
- Current-process pre-termination dumps are still narrow, but the policy includes active/recent FG runtime exits as a diagnostic boundary in addition to crash-like NTSTATUS exits. A clean auto-exit from the FG switch app while FG was recently active may therefore produce a `crash_external_fatal_exit_RtlExitUserProcess_00000000_*.dmp`; that is a diagnostic artifact, not by itself evidence of a crash.
- The DXGI swapchain wrapper destructor must avoid optional DXGI side-channel mutation while the wrapper is being destroyed by its final `Release()`. Talos `installed/captureengine/logs/20260524_182433` stopped immediately after the wrapper's external refs reached zero, before a useful dump was produced. The current policy skips destruction-callback unregister and `IDXGISwapChain::SetPrivateData(WRAPPED_SWAP_CHAIN_GUID, nullptr)` during releasing destruction, while still releasing promoted swapchain interfaces, queue refs, the real swapchain ref, and device refs. Expected diagnostics include `SwapChain: Destroying wrapper`, `Skipping destruction callback unregister during releasing destruction`, and `Skipping private-data clear during releasing destruction`.
- `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` now has additional hardening knobs for reproducing real-game FG lifecycle stress: `--duration` / `auto_exit_seconds`, `--startup-recreates` / `startup_native_swapchain_recreate_count`, `--bootstrap-native-swaps` / `bootstrap_native_swapchain_stress_count`, and `--fsr-suspend-interval` / `fsr_suspend_interval_seconds`. Startup recreates exercise native swapchain recreation after FG runtimes have loaded but before FG is enabled. Shutdown isolated native-wrapper probes exercise CE's swapchain-wrapper final-release teardown after SL/FSR cleanup. Keep those probes after FG cleanup; placing isolated native probes before the main Streamline recreate can perturb Streamline's own swapchain creation and produce `E_ACCESSDENIED`, which is test pollution rather than the target overlay fault.
- `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` now keeps the heavy startup stress path opt-in by default. Startup native recreate stress, bootstrap native swapchain stress, disabled FSR-context startup probes, and eager initial FG runtime preloads can still be enabled through config/CLI, but a default launch should become visible quickly and only then warm FG runtimes. This avoids masking overlay-injection startup latency with deliberate test-app load stalls while preserving the harder knobs for targeted regressions.
- The switch app supports asynchronous runtime preload diagnostics. The default path schedules FSR preload after the visible OFF phase. General asynchronous Streamline preload remains intentionally skipped while FSR owns presentation: the historical mixed-runtime crash session entered `slInit` while CE's module-load path re-entered Streamline feature lookup, and concurrent runtime initialization made the ordering more hostile. The transactional FSR->DLSS exception above is serialized on the render thread only after FSR is disabled, one covered passthrough Present succeeds, FFX Presents drain, and the GPU is idle; CE feature lookup begins only after `slInit` returns. The disabled proxy stays alive strictly as the current presentation surface until the replacement is ready, and FSR retirement/preload waits until the replacement and first DLSS-active Presents both succeed. Outstanding preload threads are joined during cleanup. `testapp/testapp_common.h` logging is thread-safe because preload and render logs can interleave. Expected diagnostics include `Async FSR runtime preload scheduled`, `Async Streamline preload skipped during active/native FSR ownership`, and matching `finished` lines for scheduled work.
- Mixed-runtime validation must distinguish app-side FG state from CE overlay-route state. `installed/captureengine/logs/20260531_233633` / `installed/testapp/dx12_fg_switch_test.log` reached real DLSS-G from FSR (`Mode now DLSS FG`, `slDLSSGGetState ... genFrames=2`) and later returned to FSR, but the hook log did not contain `Post-SL overlay SUBMIT`.
