### 2026-06-04 - Audio codec finalization and silence hardening (build/test 0.1.3735/0.1.3737)

- **Input**: Follow-up WGC codec logs were not perfect after the earlier codec/layout work. AAC still exposed final audio about one padded tail fragment past video, and Opus still crashed/corrupted output. The user also called out a missing validation case: recordings where a track is entirely silence or has inactive/gapped sources must still be correct for every codec, because codecs/container players can treat silence/gaps differently.
- **Root causes**:
  - Opus crash/corruption: `AudioEncoder::Flush()` allocated packed/interleaved silence as `samples * bytes_per_sample * planes`; for packed stereo `planes=1`, so the buffer was half-sized and `av_audio_fifo_write()` could read beyond it. Correct allocation is `samples * bytes_per_sample * channels` for total storage, with one plane pointer for packed formats and per-channel plane offsets only for planar formats.
  - AAC external overrun: final packet clamping used the codec-padded frame boundary as both the submission limit and visible packet end. AAC needs padded submission, but the packet duration exposed to mux/probe must clamp to the exact video-authoritative sample target and carry end-skip metadata for the padded tail.
  - Pure-silence tracks: the pending recording-start reset was applied only on the first real `EncodeSamples()` call. If a track produced no samples before stop, `Flush()` never learned the start time and therefore had no video duration target to encode silence toward.
  - Long silent tails: the old pre-fill path capped tail silence at 3 seconds. This was memory-safe but wrong for inactive tracks or long source gaps; silence must be chunked, not truncated.
- **Fix**: Audio finalization now keeps separate `targetSamples` (exact video duration) and `maxSamples` (codec submission limit). It feeds required silence through the normal FIFO/encoder path in frame-sized chunks until `maxSamples`, allocates packed/planar zero buffers correctly for all channel counts, applies pending start during flush while preserving the already-set end time, clamps final packet durations to `targetSamples`, and writes 10-byte `AV_PKT_DATA_SKIP_SAMPLES` side data (`end reason=padding silence`) for padded AAC/Opus tails. `VideoEncoder` now reopens the completed file after trailer write and logs `[VideoEncoder] Post-mux duration probe ...` as the external stream-duration authority.
- **Silence invariant**: enabled tracks are encoded as real zero samples through the selected codec when sources are silent/inactive; sparse container gaps are not the compatibility contract.
- **Regression coverage**: Added `AudioSyncUtilsTest.PackedSilenceBufferIncludesEveryChannel`, `FinalPacketDurationClampsToVideoSampleTarget`, `AudioEncoderTest.AacFlushClampsPaddedFinalPacketToVideoTarget`, `OpusFlushPadsPackedSilenceWithoutPacketsPastTarget`, and `SilenceFlushIsBoundedForEveryAudioCodec` (AAC/ALAC/FLAC/Opus/PCM pure-silence matrix with AAC/Opus skip metadata checks).
- **Verification**: Focused build/test passed 72/72 with `python build.py --skip-updates --run-tests --gtest-filter=AudioEncoderTest.*:AudioSyncUtilsTest.*:AudioResamplerTest.*:ConfigTest.AudioDerivedSourcesInheritQualityAndDownmix:ConfigTest.AppAudioCanOverrideInheritedDownmixAndQuality` (build 0.1.3735). Full test-only pass succeeded with `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` (894/894, metadata 0.1.3736). Required plain build passed with `python build.py --skip-updates` (build 0.1.3737).
- **Source anchors**: `mediaengine/audio_encoder.cpp`, `mediaengine/audio_sync_utils.h`, `mediaengine/mediaengine.cpp`, `mediaengine/video_encoder.cpp`, `tests/test_audio_encoder.cpp`, `tests/test_audio_sync_utils.cpp`, `llm-wiki/multi-audio-capture.md`, `llm-wiki/cfr-capture-sync.md`.
- **Stale risk**: Fresh runtime recordings are still required for WGC and inject across AAC/ALAC/FLAC/Opus/PCM; the new post-mux probe line should show zero external stream-duration delta, and ffmpeg decode should stay free of parser/tail errors.

### 2026-06-04 - x86 Alt+Tab DX12 DEVICE_HUNG = overlay UPLOAD-ring data race (DescFree per-slot fence, v12) — SUPERSEDED as the freeze root cause (see 2026-06-06)

> **SUPERSEDED (2026-06-06)**: the live freeze persisted after v12. A fresh manual dump (`logs/20260605_231633`) showed the Present thread stalled in the **Windows loader** (`GetModuleHandleA` for not-loaded overlay modules), not in `ExecuteCommandLists`. The v12 UPLOAD-ring per-slot fence is a legitimate GPU-safety hardening and is kept, but the actual x86 Alt+Tab freeze was the per-Present loader walk; see the 2026-06-06 entry. Treat the "SOLVED" claim below as "GPU race hardened", not "freeze fixed".

- **Root cause (proven, not guessed)**: The injected x86 `dx12_test.exe` froze with `DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG (0x887A0006)` on Alt+Tab. DRED (`logs/20260604_011053`) showed the hung GPU work was CE's **own overlay command list** (`DRAWINDEXEDINSTANCED`, `completedOps=2/7`, INCOMPLETE) with **`pageFaultVA=0`** = pure execution hang, not a bad address. The manual freeze dump's render thread was blocked in `dx12_test!Render -> capture_hook_x86!DetourExecuteCommandLists -> D3D12Core!CCommandQueue::ExecuteCommandLists -> nvwgf2um (AllocateCB) -> win32u!NtGdiDdDDICreateAllocation` — a **kernel GPU allocation waiting on the wedged GPU**, exactly one ~1.9s stall (`heartbeat gap=1923ms`) that tripped the 2s TDR. Only the render thread was involved (no CE-worker contention). The test app uses **one** queue for both ECL and present (`g_CommandQueue`); CE submits the overlay on that same queue (no cross-queue issue).
- **The actual bug**: `DX12DescFreeBackend::Render` (in `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp`) round-robins `kPoolSize=4` persistently-mapped UPLOAD vertex/index buffers (`slot = frameIdx_ % kPoolSize`) and `memcpy`s new geometry into the slot **with no fence guarding GPU read completion** — fully decoupled from `g_State.fence`/`fenceValues`. While the GPU keeps up the slot is free by the time it's reused (4 frames later). During the iflip<->composited mode switch the GPU stops retiring for hundreds of ms while the CPU keeps drawing the overlay at ~140fps → within 4 frames the CPU **wraps and overwrites vb/ib data the GPU is still reading** → corrupted draw → GPU wedges → TDR. x64 (faster/shorter pause) and the bare app (no overlay) stay under the wrap; RTSS fences its own uploads. This is why it was x86/WoW64-only and why the debug layer (timing change) masked it.
- **Fix (v12, never hides the overlay)**: Per-slot GPU-completion fence on the DescFree UPLOAD ring. Each render site publishes `s_descFreeSlotFence = g_State.fence` and `s_descFreeSlotGuardValue` (= `currentFenceValue+1` non-FG, `0` for FG/PostSL paths which already sync via their own completion fence). `Render` waits (`WaitForSlotGpuComplete`) for the prior occupant's guard before reusing a slot, then records the new guard. Decisions extracted to `ce::dx12_overlay_policy::DecideOverlayUploadSlotGuardValue` / `ShouldWaitForOverlayUploadSlot` (unit-tested). The fence is the real sync; the wait has a 1000ms (< 2s TDR) liveness bound that logs on timeout (a separate FG-transition path can legitimately discard a pending signal). Result: overlay is drawn every frame (never hidden) and the CPU paces to the GPU only when genuinely ahead — like RTSS.
- **Invariant**: The DescFree overlay UPLOAD ring must never be reused before the GPU has finished the previous frame that used that slot. Guard keyed on the overlay fence (`g_State.fence`); disabled (0) only when FG advances a separate completion fence or there is no overlay fence.
- **Diagnostic signature (durable)**: x86 DX12 present thread stuck in `NtGdiDdDDICreateAllocation` inside `ExecuteCommandLists` + DRED INCOMPLETE overlay `DRAWINDEXEDINSTANCED` with `pageFaultVA=0` = GPU wedged by a corrupted overlay draw, not a real fault. Suspect UPLOAD/ring reuse without a fence.
- **Verification**: `python build.py --skip-updates` clean (x64+x86 `dx12_hook.cpp` recompiled); full suite `889/889` incl. new `DXGISharedTest.OverlayUploadSlotGuardDisabledForFGAndMissingFence`, `OverlayUploadSlotWaitsOnlyWhenGpuBehindActiveGuard`, `OverlayUploadRingGuardPreventsModeSwitchStomp` (the ring sim fails against the pre-fix unguarded path). Binary-string marker bumped to `policy=v12 ...`. **Pending: live 32-bit Alt+Tab-spam repro to confirm the freeze is gone.**
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`DX12DescFreeBackend::Render`/`WaitForSlotGpuComplete`/`Shutdown`, `s_descFreeSlotFence`/`s_descFreeSlotGuardValue`, 4 render sites ~10968/11017/15971/16061, v12 policy marker), `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (two new helpers), `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`, `tests/test_crash_handler.cpp`, `installed/captureengine/logs/20260604_011053` (DRED + dump).

### 2026-06-04 - Audio codec sync, quality, and multichannel hardening (build 0.1.3722)

- **Input**: Existing WGC test recordings showed ALAC as the only likely-good baseline; AAC, FLAC, Opus, and PCM still needed validation. Opus output had audible distortion and parser/tail errors; `codec=pcm` produced no audio stream because the literal `pcm` alias was being passed to FFmpeg as an encoder name.
- **Config fix**: `[Microphone]`, `[Microphone.N]`, and `[AppAudio.N]` now inherit `[Audio]` quality/layout fields consistently. This closes the previous drift where microphone sections missed inherited `downmix` and app-audio sections defaulted `downmix=false` instead of inheriting.
- **Format/layout fix**: MediaEngine resolves an audio format per output track before encoder creation: sample rate, channel count, Windows channel mask, FFmpeg layout, bit depth, and codec policy. `downmix=true` forces stereo; `downmix=false` preserves the main source layout for that track. WASAPI endpoint probing preserves `WAVEFORMATEXTENSIBLE` masks when available, app audio requests the resolved track format, and resampling/mixing stays float32.
- **Codec fix**: `pcm` now resolves to `pcm_s24le` by default, `pcm_s16le` for 16-bit, and `pcm_f32le` for 32-bit. `opus` resolves to `libopus`, forces/logs 48 kHz, sets `application=audio`, and never falls back to native Opus. AAC/Opus bitrate is treated as a stereo quality target and scales for wider layouts: 5.1 = `*3`, 7.1 = `*4`. ALAC/FLAC/PCM use 24-bit by default.
- **FFmpeg packaging fix**: The existing custom FFmpeg bundle lacked `libopus` and the concrete PCM encoders, so Opus/PCM tests initially failed before encoding. `build.py` now enables `libopus`, `pcm_s16le`, `pcm_s24le`, and `pcm_f32le`, requires the MSYS2 opus package, copies `libopus-0.dll`, and installs the bundled libopus license. The timestamp-precision patch was refreshed against the current FFmpeg source so the one-time FFmpeg rebuild applies cleanly. Normal `--skip-updates` builds now reuse that refreshed bundle.
- **Finalization fix**: AAC/Opus no longer receive arbitrary short final frames. Final audio follows video duration by sample accounting; mux stream duration tags are written from the final encoded video duration for all streams so codec padding and container rounding do not make audio tracks appear longer than video.
- **PCM live encode fix**: PCM encoders report no fixed frame size. The live encode loop now emits available samples up to a bounded chunk size instead of waiting for an arbitrary 4096-sample FIFO threshold, so short/multichannel PCM chunks produce packets immediately.
- **Diagnostics**: New/expanded logs show endpoint/app requested format, channel masks, resampler layouts, resolved codec alias, Opus sample-rate adjustment, and per-track final deltas. Unknown channel masks are logged before falling back to FFmpeg default layouts.
- **Regression coverage**: Added config inheritance/override tests for `downmix`, `bitrate`, `sample_rate`, and `bit_depth`; audio encoder tests for PCM alias/depth variants, Opus/libopus 48 kHz policy, multichannel lossy bitrate scaling, and multichannel PCM packet output; audio resampler coverage for channel-mask-preserving 5.1 paths.
- **Non-audio build hygiene**: The worktree already contained a DX12 DescFree slot-fence draft. The missing slot-fence fields/helper are now present so the file compiles, but the slot guard remains disabled unless a render site publishes a concrete fence/value pair. This was not runtime-validated as an Alt+Tab fix.
- **Verification**: One-time FFmpeg refresh passed with `python build.py --force-rebuild`. Focused command passed: `python build.py --skip-updates --gtest-filter=AudioEncoderTest.*:AudioResamplerTest.*:ConfigTest.AudioDerivedSourcesInheritQualityAndDownmix:ConfigTest.AppAudioCanOverrideInheritedDownmixAndQuality`. Full unit suite passed with `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` (886/886). Full required build passed with `python build.py --skip-updates` (build 0.1.3722).
- **Source anchors**: `common/config.{h,cpp}`, `mediaengine/audio_capture.{h,cpp}`, `mediaengine/app_audio_capture.{h,cpp}`, `mediaengine/audio_resampler.{h,cpp}`, `mediaengine/audio_encoder.{h,cpp}`, `mediaengine/mediaengine.cpp`, `mediaengine/video_encoder.cpp`, `build.py`, `patches/ffmpeg/0001-matroska-add-timestamp-precision-option.patch`, `tests/test_config.cpp`, `tests/test_audio_encoder.cpp`, `tests/test_audio_resampler.cpp`, `llm-wiki/multi-audio-capture.md`, `llm-wiki/cfr-capture-sync.md`.
- **Stale risk**: Fresh runtime recordings are still required: WGC across AAC/ALAC/FLAC/Opus/PCM, then the same media-engine duration/layout validation for injected capture. Synthetic tests prove the policy and packet paths, not every real endpoint's channel-mask mapping.

### 2026-06-03 - Decisive clue: 64-bit test app does NOT freeze; cache the per-Present module-loader walk

- **Clue**: the user ran the **64-bit** dx12_test.exe (x64 hook, WoW64:0) with the same CE build (v11r) and Alt+Tab spam — it did NOT crash (`logs/20260603_201148`: no device removal, overlay renders fine). Only the **32-bit/WoW64** build crashes (`logs/20260603_200513`: same DRED hang on CE's overlay DRAW). Same source, same overlay path → the freeze is an **x86/WoW64 timing sensitivity, not a logic bug**. This is also why the D3D12 debug layer (which changes timing / disables iflip) masked it, and why RTSS — which survives 32-bit — must have a leaner present path.
- **What the dumps kept showing**: the x86 present thread is always deep in `ce::overlay_compat::GetLoadedThirdPartyOverlayModuleName -> GetModuleHandleA -> ntdll loader (LdrGetDllHandle / LdrpLogInternal)`. That function did **16 `GetModuleHandleA` loader-lock walks on EVERY Present** (called from `DetourPresent`). In the freeze repro no third-party overlay is loaded, so all 16 miss and it walks the loader 16x per present. Under WoW64 that's slow thunked loader-lock traffic, and it **contends with DWM's `d3d11.dll` load during the iflip<->composited Alt+Tab mode switch** — the worst possible moment.
- **Fix (perf, not a timing bandaid)**: `GetLoadedThirdPartyOverlayModuleName()` now caches its result behind a generation counter (`ThirdPartyOverlayModuleCacheGeneration`) that is bumped only when a DLL loads (`InvalidateThirdPartyOverlayModuleCache()` called from `NotifyHookModuleLoaded` in `hook/main.cpp`, which is driven by the existing `LdrLoadDll` hook). Steady-state Presents now cost one atomic load+compare instead of 16 loader-lock walks; it re-scans only when a module actually loads. The loaded-module set only changes on a DLL load, so this is behavior-preserving.
- **Hypothesis/validation**: this removes the biggest x86-specific per-Present overhead the dumps point at and the loader-lock contention with DWM during the mode switch. It is the strongest lead from the x86-vs-x64 clue, but it is a timing-shift mitigation — NOT proven to fully close the underlying GPU race (CE's overlay draw vs the mode switch). Awaiting a 32-bit Alt+Tab-spam repro to confirm. If it still freezes, the present path has other per-Present overhead to trim (the COM swapchain wrapper + DetourPresent double-hook) or we capture RTSS via PIX/GPUView.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/common/overlay_compat.h` (cache + generation), `hook/main.cpp` (`NotifyHookModuleLoaded` invalidation), `installed/captureengine/logs/20260603_201148` (64-bit no-crash), `installed/captureengine/logs/20260603_200513` (32-bit crash).

### 2026-06-03 - v11 residency attempt caused INVALID_CALL black screen; REVERTED (v11r)

- **Regression**: v11's `ID3D12Device1::SetResidencyPriority(MAXIMUM)` calls on CE's overlay resources caused `DXGI_ERROR_INVALID_CALL (0x887A0001)` device removal during overlay init — the test app showed NO window content (black) under CE inject. Do NOT reintroduce `SetResidencyPriority` on these objects without first verifying which object type the driver rejects (likely the command allocators/fence, or the call itself under this NVIDIA driver) — it removes the device. - **Current state**: overlay draws EVERY frame (never hidden on focus — the user's firm requirement) + the v8 not-presentable hold (occluded/iconic/zero). The bare app's per-frame GPU work is `ClearRenderTargetView` only (no input resources, no PSO) and survives; CE's overlay binds a PSO and reads input resources and pure-hangs (`pageFaultVA=0`) on the DRAW during the switch. Holds (v7 full-unfocused / v10 transition) are the only freeze-free options but they hide the overlay (rejected) and v10 still froze under rapid toggling. The remaining unknown is RTSS's exact technique. NEXT: get ground truth — instead of more hypothesis-driven guesses (v8-v11 all failed). DONE: wired the D3D12 debug layer diagnostic (`CE_DX12_DEBUG_LAYER=1` debug layer, `=2` + GPU-based validation; armed in `DX12Hook::Init`, `ID3D12InfoQueue` drained to the hook log every ProcessFrame + on device-removed as `DX12 DBGLAYER [...]`). # llm-wiki Log — Archive 2026-W23b

### 2026-06-03 - v10 hold rejected+insufficient; v11 pins overlay resources resident so the draw never stalls

- **v10 repro** (`installed/captureengine/logs/20260603_151656`): still froze. The log shows RAPID Alt+Tab (focus edges every ~0.5s); the 60-present transition hold EXPIRED mid-thrash (`Resuming … foreground=0`), CE resumed the direct draw, and DRED again showed CE's overlay `DRAWINDEXEDINSTANCED` pure-hung (`pageFaultVA=0`). So the hold both (a) hides the overlay — which the user firmly rejects ("must never disappear, not even temporarily") — and (b) can't reliably cover rapid toggling. v10 is abandoned.
- **Decisive user data**: the BARE app (no injection) NEVER freezes on extreme Alt+Tab spam, and app+RTSS NEVER freezes — only CE freezes. So CE's overlay GPU work is the specific cause; a single render+present per frame survives the mode switch fine.
- **Root-cause reasoning**: the bare app's per-frame GPU work is `ClearRenderTargetView` only — NO input resources, NO PSO. CE's overlay command list binds a PSO and READS input resources (font ByteAddressBuffer + vertex/index UPLOAD buffers). DRED shows a PURE hang on CE's DRAW (not a fault). Under the WDDM residency model, the iflip<->composited mode switch makes DWM allocate large composition surfaces and can trim the game process's residency budget; if CE's overlay resources get evicted, the DRAW stalls paging them back in → TDR. The app's input-less clears never stall. RTSS (a mature overlay) survives, consistent with it keeping its resources resident.
- **Fix (v11)**: pin ALL CE overlay GPU resources at `D3D12_RESIDENCY_PRIORITY_MAXIMUM` via `ID3D12Device1::SetResidencyPriority` (`TrySetMaxResidencyPriority` in `dx12_hook.cpp`): the DescFree backend's font ByteAddressBuffer, the vertex/index UPLOAD pools (+ on resize), the two PSOs, the command allocators + fence (`InitOverlaySync`), and the offscreen RT (`EnsureOffscreenRT`). With resources pinned, CE renders the overlay EVERY frame — focused, unfocused-visible, AND through the transition — and never hides (v10's transition hold is removed; the transition window is now telemetry-only and widens the DRED dump window). Marker `DX12 focus-loss sync policy=v11 max-residency-no-hold`; per-transition log `Focus-change mode switch active — overlay STILL RENDERING (residency-pinned, not held)`. The v8 not-presentable hold (occluded/iconic/zero) still applies.
- **Validation**: build x64+x86, 878 tests pass; `HookDllContainsLazyExecRegressionStrings` pins the v11 markers. DRED stays armed.
- **OPEN / stale-risk**: This is a strong hypothesis (it explains the bare-app-vs-CE contradiction) but UNVERIFIED — UPLOAD-heap resources are in system memory, so whether the WDDM trim actually evicts them on this GPU is unconfirmed (ample VRAM may mean no eviction at all, in which case residency is not the cause and the hang is e.g. PSO/pipeline-revalidation or RT-bind related). If v11 still hangs, the DRED breadcrumb + the fact that the bare app's clears survive narrows it to the PSO/full-pipeline-draw vs fixed-function-clear difference; next step is the D3D12 debug layer (available: `d3d12SDKLayers.dll` present) gated by an env flag to capture the exact validation/hazard, or a PIX capture of RTSS's command stream. The predicate `ShouldHoldD3D12OverlayBackbufferWorkDuringFocusTransition` is now used as telemetry, not a hold (name is legacy).
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`TrySetMaxResidencyPriority` + calls in DescFree font/buffers/PSOs, `InitOverlaySync`, `EnsureOffscreenRT`; v11 hold removal in `ProcessFrame`; marker), `tests/test_crash_handler.cpp`, `installed/captureengine/logs/20260603_151656`.

### 2026-06-03 - v9 offscreen copy ALSO hung; v10 holds backbuffer work only during the focus-transition mode switch

- **v9 repro** (`installed/captureengine/logs/20260603_150241`, x86): still froze. DRED (armed, confirmed) breadcrumbs this time showed the hung list (node#15, INCOMPLETE 2/10) as the OFFSCREEN composite path: `OP, RESOURCEBARRIER, COPYTEXTUREREGION (bb->offscreen), RESOURCEBARRIER, DRAWINDEXEDINSTANCED...` — it hung on the `COPYTEXTUREREGION` that READS the live backbuffer. `pageFaultVA=0x0` again (pure hang). So **ANY backbuffer touch — direct draw (v8) OR offscreen copy (v9) — pure-hangs the GPU during the iflip<->composited mode switch**; moving the draw offscreen didn't help because the path still reads the backbuffer.
- **Timing**: the hang was at the REFOCUS edge — `Focus-loss foreground reacquire Present proof accepted ... remaining=12` (≈3 presents after regaining foreground), then the present thread blocked ~2.5s and TDR'd. So the unsafe window is the brief mode switch around a focus change, NOT steady unfocused. This reconciles with v7 (never touched bb through the transition → no hang) and RTSS (renders fine in steady unfocused-visible).
- **Fix (v10)**: retire the v9 offscreen route. Hold ALL CE backbuffer overlay/capture work ONLY during the focus-change transition window: a foreground-change EDGE (either direction) arms `g_FocusTransitionHoldFrames = 60`, decremented per wrapped Present; while > 0, `skipOverlayDraw`. Steady states — focused AND unfocused-but-visible — render directly (like RTSS), so the overlay is only briefly absent during the actual mode switch (when the screen is transitioning anyway), never during steady visible use. Predicate `ShouldHoldD3D12OverlayBackbufferWorkDuringFocusTransition(...)`; the v8 not-presentable hold (occluded/iconic/zero) still applies first. Edge detection + countdown live in `DX12_NoteWrappedD3D12PresentResult` (`s_lastForegroundState`). Marker `DX12 focus-loss sync policy=v10 focus-transition-hold`; logs `Focus-change edge (regained/lost foreground) — holding ...` and `Holding overlay/capture backbuffer work during focus-change mode switch` / `Resuming ...`.
- **Validation**: build x64+x86, 878 tests pass; new policy test `D3D12FocusTransitionHoldGatesOnlyTheModeSwitchWindow`; `HookDllContainsLazyExecRegressionStrings` pins the v10 markers. The removed v9 predicate/test/log are gone.
- **OPEN / stale-risk**: (1) `kFocusTransitionHoldFrames=60` is a present-COUNT, so its real-time coverage scales with FPS (~360ms at ~166fps; ~1s at 60fps). If a hang recurs DURING the hold window the count is too small (raise it / consider a real-time settle); if it recurs in STEADY unfocused (`transitionHoldRemaining==0`, no recent edge) then steady unfocused-visible direct draw is NOT safe and only a full v7-style unfocused hold avoids it (which hides the overlay — would need a non-backbuffer overlay surface). (2) DRED stays armed. Re-run the x86 Alt+Tab-in/out repro to confirm.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`g_FocusTransitionHoldFrames`, edge detect in `DX12_NoteWrappedD3D12PresentResult`, hold in `ProcessFrame`, `focusLossOffscreenComposite=false`), `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ShouldHoldD3D12OverlayBackbufferWorkDuringFocusTransition`), `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`, `tests/test_crash_handler.cpp`, `installed/captureengine/logs/20260603_150241`.

### 2026-06-03 - DRED root cause: overlay direct-draw pure-hangs the GPU during mode switch; v9 offscreen-composite while unfocused (build 0.1.3693+)

- **DRED finally captured the culprit** (`installed/captureengine/logs/20260603_020053`, x86, after the arming was moved to `DX12Hook::Init` and exported). `DX12 DRED: armed auto-breadcrumbs ... (context1=1)` confirmed arming ran before device creation. On the device-hung (`0x887A0006`) the breadcrumbs showed:
  - `node#15 ... completedOps=2/7 <-- INCOMPLETE`: ops `RESOURCEBARRIER`, `DRAWINDEXEDINSTANCED` (last completed), then more `DRAWINDEXEDINSTANCED`. This is **CE's OWN overlay command list** (ImGui-style indexed draws). The game's list is `node#17` (`CLEARRENDERTARGETVIEW` x127 — the test app only clears, never draws indexed).
  - `pageFaultVA=0x0` -> **pure GPU hang, not an invalid access**.
- **Root cause**: CE's overlay command list completed the `PRESENT->RT` barrier and one indexed draw, then the GPU hung on the next draw. The direct overlay DRAW on the LIVE swapchain backbuffer hangs while the window is unfocused / mid iflip<->composited mode switch — the backbuffer is transiently owned by DWM/the display (DWM was loading `d3d11.dll` for its composition device during the ~1.9s stall before the TDR). This reconciles all prior data: v7 never touched the backbuffer while backgrounded (no hang, overlay hidden); v8 drew directly while unfocused-visible (overlay visible, but hung); RTSS keeps its overlay visible without hitting this.
- **Fix (v9)**: `ShouldUseD3D12UnfocusedOffscreenOverlayComposite(...)`. While unfocused — or within the post-refocus transition window (`g_FocusLossForegroundReacquirePresentProofRemaining > 0`) — CE renders the overlay to its OFFSCREEN RT (app-owned, never grabbed by the display) and composites onto the backbuffer with implicit-promotion copies, instead of the direct `PRESENT->RT` barrier + draw. The hang-prone DRAW moves off the live backbuffer; the overlay stays VISIBLE. Steady FOCUSED frames keep the fast direct path (no steady-state copy cost). The v8 not-presentable hold (occluded/iconic/zero-size) still applies first. FG / runtime-owned / dedicated-queue / Steam-deferred routes are excluded. Marker: `DX12 focus-loss sync policy=v9 unfocused-offscreen-composite`; per-use log `DX12: Unfocused overlay via offscreen composite ...`.
- **DRED arming reliability**: arming was moved out of the (dead, `#ifdef ENABLE_D3D12_WRAPPER`, no `d3d12_wrappers.dll`) `Wrapped_D3D12CreateDevice` to `DX12Hook::Init()` (worker thread, ~1.2s before the game's device is first seen — early enough for fresh launches), and the DRED entry points are `__declspec(dllexport)` so `-Wl,--gc-sections` can't strip them on x86. Confirmed `DX12 DRED: armed` now logs at runtime.
- **Validation**: build (x64+x86), 878 unit tests pass. New policy test `D3D12UnfocusedOverlayUsesOffscreenCompositeNotDirectDraw`; `HookDllContainsLazyExecRegressionStrings` pins the v9 + offscreen markers.
- **OPEN / NEXT**: This is the evidence-based fix but carries one residual uncertainty — the offscreen path still touches the backbuffer via CopyTextureRegion (read bb->offscreen, write offscreen->bb). The DRED proved a DRAW hung (copies untested in this exact transition; v4 history suggests copies while focus-lost did not hang). DRED stays armed: if a hang recurs, the new breadcrumb will show whether a COPY op (not a draw) hung. If so, the fallback is a brief transition-only skip of all backbuffer touches. Re-run the x86 Alt+Tab repro to confirm.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`DX12Hook::Init` arming, `ProcessFrame` `focusLossOffscreenComposite` gating + offscreen render block), `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ShouldUseD3D12UnfocusedOffscreenOverlayComposite`), `hook/common/dx12_dred.{h,cpp}`, `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`, `tests/test_crash_handler.cpp`, `installed/captureengine/logs/20260603_020053`.

### 2026-06-03 - First v8 repro: overlay stays visible but device still hangs; x86 DRED arming fixed (build 0.1.3691)

- **Repro**: User Alt+Tab repro `installed/captureengine/logs/20260603_013011` (injected x86 `dx12_test.exe`, build 0.1.3689) still froze. Confirmed two things from the hook log:
  - **v8 works as intended**: NO `Swapchain presentability changed` and NO `Holding ... NOT presentable` lines ever fired — the window stayed visible (never occluded), so CE kept rendering the overlay directly the whole time. The overlay is no longer hidden on focus loss.
  - **The device still hung anyway**: `DX12: GPU device removed (0x887A0006)` while visible, followed by ~330 `Present ... device-lost hr=0x887A0005`. Lead: `DX12: Overlay perf: ... submit=5954us` (~6ms, ~1000x normal) at frame 300, ~1.9s before the TDR — the overlay `ExecuteCommandLists` on the game queue blocked, consistent with the earlier `ExecuteCommandLists -> AllocateCB -> NtGdiDdDDICreateAllocation` stack during the iflip<->composited mode switch. Fix: the DRED entry points are now `__declspec(dllexport)` (`CE_DRED_API`), an unconditional GC root on PE for both arches; `noinline` is kept so the single call site in `Wrapped_D3D12CreateDevice` stays a real call. Verified both `capture_hook_x86.dll` and `capture_hook_x64.dll` now contain `DX12 DRED: armed auto-breadcrumbs`. **Lesson**: on this build, retaining a single-call-site helper requires `dllexport`, not just `used`; `used` is x64-only here. 877 tests still pass.
- **Next**: re-run the same x86 Alt+Tab repro with the armed build; the device-removed dump now carries `GetAutoBreadcrumbsOutput1` (hung list + last op) and `GetPageFaultAllocationOutput1` (faulting VA + recently-freed allocations). Use that to pick the targeted fix (most likely the overlay `PRESENT->RT` barrier / direct backbuffer touch across the mode switch).

### 2026-06-03 - x86 DX12 overlay no longer hidden on focus loss; DRED added (build 0.1.3690)

- **Input**: The v3-v7 "fix" for the injected x86 `dx12_test.exe` Alt+Tab device-hung (`0x887A0006`) only worked by **holding all CE backbuffer overlay/capture work while the process was not foreground** (plus a 16-frame post-refocus proof), so the overlay disappeared on any focus loss. The user reported this regression: with RTSS the overlay stays visible while the app runs as a visible borderless background window and survives the refocus-to-fullscreen transition, so CE must match that — never hide on focus loss, and fix the freeze properly. User chose diagnostic-first (DRED).
- **Root-cause status**: The `0x887A0006` is a GPU-side fault, but there was **no DRED / debug-layer / `GetDeviceRemovedExtendedData` instrumentation anywhere** in the hook — all 7 prior attempts were guesses. One captured stack (`installed/captureengine/logs/20260602_030350`) shows the stall inside `ExecuteCommandLists -> D3D12Core!...AllocateCB -> win32u!NtGdiDdDDICreateAllocation` (kernel GPU-allocation during the fullscreen-optimized iflip <-> composited mode switch that focus changes trigger), but no GPU breadcrumb/page-fault was ever recorded. The exact fault is still unknown; DRED now captures it on the next repro.
- **Two-part change**:
  1. **DRED GPU-fault diagnostics** (`hook/common/dx12_dred.{h,cpp}`): `ArmBeforeDeviceCreation()` forces auto-breadcrumbs + page-fault + breadcrumb-context ON via `D3D12GetDebugInterface` (resolved dynamically) and is called in `Wrapped_D3D12CreateDevice` BEFORE the real device is created. `DumpOnDeviceRemoved()` walks `GetAutoBreadcrumbsOutput1` (hung queue/list, last completed op, context strings) and `GetPageFaultAllocationOutput1` (faulting VA + existing/recently-freed allocations — the smoking gun for stale-backbuffer access across the mode switch). Wired into both `ProcessFrame` device-removed sites and the freeze watchdog dump (`DX12_DumpDredIfDeviceRemoved`). CE overlay list/allocators/fence/queue/offscreen-RT are now `SetName`'d so DRED output identifies them. Gated by env `CE_DX12_DRED` (default on this cycle).
  2. **Visibility-gated hold (v8)**: `ShouldHoldD3D12OverlayBackbufferWorkForNonPresentableSwapchain(...)` replaces the focus-based `ShouldHoldD3D12FocusLossBackgroundBackbufferWork` / `...ForegroundReacquire...` / `ShouldUseD3D12FocusLossOffscreenOverlayComposite`. CE now holds backbuffer GPU work ONLY when the swapchain is genuinely not presentable — `DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED` (tracked in `DX12_NoteWrappedD3D12PresentResult` via `g_SwapchainPresentOccluded`), minimized, or zero-sized. A merely-unfocused but visible window keeps presenting `S_OK` and renders the overlay directly to the backbuffer, exactly like RTSS. Focus is no longer an input. Marker: `DX12 focus-loss sync policy=v8 visibility-gated-backbuffer-hold`.
- **ThinLTO trap (important)**: The hook DLL is ThinLTO + `--gc-sections`. `ArmBeforeDeviceCreation` (one caller) was being inlined and then **dead-stripped** — `D3D12GetDebugInterface` and the arming log vanished from the linked DLL, which would have silently disabled DRED. Fixed by marking the public DRED entry points `__attribute__((used, noinline))` (`CE_DRED_KEEP`). The `CrashHandlerBinaryTest.HookDllContainsLazyExecRegressionStrings` binary-string test caught this; it now also pins the v8 + DRED markers. Any new "log-must-survive" code in single-call-site helpers should heed this.
- **Validation**: `python build.py --skip-updates` built `0.1.3690` (x64+x86). `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` passed all 877 tests. Verified via `llvm-strings` that the arming strings (`DX12 DRED: armed auto-breadcrumbs`, `D3D12GetDebugInterface`) and dump strings are present in `capture_hook_x64.dll`. New policy tests: `D3D12NonPresentableSwapchainHoldsBackbufferWork`, `D3D12UnfocusedButVisibleSwapchainKeepsOverlayVisible` (regression: would have held/hidden under the old focus policy), `D3D12NonPresentableHoldPolicyIsPresentPathAgnostic`.
- **Manual validation still needed (user/interactive)**: Inject x86 `dx12_test.exe`, Alt+Tab so it becomes a visible background window, confirm (a) overlay stays visible, (b) app keeps updating, (c) refocus to fullscreen does not crash, across many irregular cycles. If a hang still occurs, the log now carries `DX12 DRED: ===== device-removed extended data` with the hung list + page-fault VA + recently-freed allocations — use that to choose the Step-3 targeted fix (stale swapchain-derived state refresh across the mode switch, one-frame transition guard, or allocation-churn reduction).

- **Input**: GTA V Enhanced froze when started with FSR FG in `installed/captureengine/logs/20260602_161000_gtafreezestartwithfsrfg`. The user also noted that freeze dump creation often seemed to need an Alt+Tab out/in before it triggered.

  - DX12 route state now distinguishes an active FFX callback bridge from AMD internal no-callback composition. In the no-callback shape, callback-stall detection is disabled and normal DX12 overlay rendering is allowed on the runtime-owned swapchain queue instead of forcing CE's callback bridge.
  - FSR context destroy now clears callback-routing state and the runtime-presentation watchdog monitor.
  - `FreezeWatchdog` has a separate runtime-presentation monitor so FG-owned presentation keeps freeze detection active in the background. Status logs include `runtimePresentation=1`.
  - `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` now defaults to FSR present-callback toggle stress: each FSR entry starts with `presentCallback=null` / AMD-internal routing and later alternates into the app-callback route. The app log records `presentCallbackRoute=amd-internal` / `app-callback`, and the on-screen status appends `INT` during the internal route.
- **Validation**:
  - `python build.py --skip-updates` first built the main artifacts but hit a transient file lock on `installed/testapp/x86/dx12_test.exe`; after confirming no target processes were running, the clean rerun passed as build `0.1.3678`.
  - `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` passed all 875 tests (displayed metadata `0.1.3679`).
  - Standalone `installed/testapp/dx12_fg_switch_test.exe --duration 22 --auto-fsr-start 1 --auto-dlss-start 14 --auto-return-fsr 19 --fsr-present-callback-interval 2` exited with code 0 and logged a return-to-FSR session beginning with `presentCallbackRoute=amd-internal`, later switching to `presentCallbackRoute=app-callback`.
- **Manual validation still needed**: Re-run GTA start-with-FSR and mixed FSR/DLSS menu switching with CE injection. Healthy GTA no-callback logs should show the no-callback routing breadcrumbs above, not `Installed DX12 overlay present-callback bridge` for a null `originalPresent` enabled configure. If a freeze still occurs, the watchdog should dump without requiring focus churn.

  - Protected official FFX startup swapchain pointer changes preserve the existing overlay backend/resources and clear only cached swapchain refs; CE no longer tears down and immediately rebuilds the normal overlay backend against the staged FFX queue before proof.
  - Disabled startup-arming FFX configure logs are throttled so long menu-side disabled-configure loops stay diagnosable without flooding the session.
  - Binary/regression strings were updated away from the old overlay-only breadcrumbs and focused tests now lock: no separate overlay-only before proof, no protected-startup FG-cooldown bypass, and backend preservation across protected-startup swapchain changes.

### 2026-06-01 - x86 DX12 focus-loss same-frame overlay fence sync (build 0.1.3652 / tests 0.1.3653)

- **Inputs**:
  - Follow-up x86 `dx12_test.exe` focus-loss freeze session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260601_212556` still froze after the frame-latency waitable and post-Present fence-wait attempts. The hook log showed the DXGI frame-latency waitable returning immediately signaled, no post-Present overlay-fence breadcrumbs, then `DX12: GPU device removed (0x887A0006)` / device-lost Present HRESULTs after CE continued rendering to the D3D12 backbuffer while the process was unfocused.

  - CE submitted inject-overlay command lists before wrapped `Present`, but the safe same-frame fence value was not guaranteed to be signaled and waited before the app could continue. On unfocused, uncapped x86 D3D12 frames, the game could spin into the next frame while CE backbuffer work had not been proven complete.

For eligible focus-lost single-queue frames, it signals `g_State.fence` immediately after CE's overlay ECL submit, updates `g_State.currentFenceValue` and the allocator fence slot, and leaves the existing pre-Present `DX12_WaitForOverlayCompletion` to sync that same-frame work before the real Present path returns to the app. Normal foreground frames keep the deferred post-Present signal path to preserve NVIDIA stall avoidance.
  - If a focus-loss fence wait cannot complete, CE records a pending fence and temporarily holds only new backbuffer overlay/capture work until completion or focus return; overlay backend/resources/state stay live. The wrapper now logs both flushed deferred signals and the focus-lost `no deferred DX12 overlay fence signal` case expected when v3 signaled before Present. Frame-latency waitable probes remain labeled as telemetry only.

### 2026-06-01 - Talos official-FFX startup no-blank and Streamline module-load reentry hardening (build 0.1.3645 / tests 0.1.3646)

- **Inputs**:
  - Injected `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` crash session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260601_152148` produced dumps that landed inside Streamline (`sl_deepdvc!slGetPluginFunction+...`) during `slInit`, while CE's fresh module-load path was proactively resolving DLSSG/Reflex feature functions.
  - Talos startup session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260601_154932` had no crash and staged the official FFX Direct runtime queue, but CE's overlay disappeared for several seconds. The log showed the then-current overlay-only protected-startup path followed by generic `Deferring overlay reinit during FG transition cooldown` until the later enabled configure/callback bridge. That overlay-only path was superseded by the 2026-06-02 GTA freeze investigation above.
  - Local injected stress run `installed/captureengine/logs/20260601_155833` exercised `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` with a long DLSS window and FSR suspend/resume churn.
- **Root causes**:
  - `StreamlineHook::OnModuleLoaded()` treated a fresh `sl.*.dll` load as permission to call feature-function lookup immediately. During `slInit`, that can re-enter Streamline's plugin manager while it is still mutating state and crash inside the SDK runtime.
  - The switch app could start an async Streamline preload while FSR still owned presentation, making the mixed-runtime init order more hostile than intended for CE overlay routing.
  - `InjectionManager::Update()` held `injectMutex` while calling public already-injected / recently-failed query helpers that also lock the same mutex, so startup-scan pending injection could stall before launching the deferred injection thread.
  - Protected official FFX startup already had a staged Direct queue and intentionally allowed overlay-only rendering at that point in history, but the generic FG transition cooldown still blocked overlay init/draw and caused the visible Talos startup gap. The later 2026-06-02 GTA freeze rejected the pre-enable overlay-only assumption.
- **Fix**:
  - `hook/apis/streamline_hook.cpp` now defers proactive DLSSG/Reflex feature lookup from module-load notification and logs `Deferred proactive feature-function lookup during module load`; normal runtime `slGetFeatureFunction` interception remains the eager observable path.
  - `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` skips async Streamline preload while active/native FSR owns presentation, calls `slShutdown` and clears Streamline pointers after failed `slInit`, and exposes configurable auto timings. The defaults now wait long enough for DLSS-G init: FSR at 3s, DLSS at 12s, return to FSR at 30s.
  - `captureengine/injection.cpp` now uses locked already-injected/recent-failure checks from the pending-injection scan and a pure `ShouldLaunchPendingInjection(...)` policy helper.
  - Historical fix, superseded for protected official FFX startup rendering: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` then let protected official FFX startup bypass the generic FG transition reinit/draw cooldown only for overlay-only rendering on the staged Direct queue. The still-current part is that heavy side effects remain quiesced until direct enabled `ffxConfigure` or FFX callback proof.
- **Validation**:
  - `python build.py --skip-updates` passed (build `0.1.3645`).
  - `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` passed all 851 tests (displayed metadata `0.1.3646`).
  - Injected switch-app run `installed/captureengine/logs/20260601_155833` exited with app exit code 0, no `.dmp`, no `SKIPPING overlay`, no `suspending overlay`, no device-removal/unhandled-exception markers, 52 `FFX present callback rendered overlay` lines, 10731 `Post-SL overlay SUBMIT` lines, 12 deferred Streamline module-load feature-lookup lines, 10 `slDLSSGSetOptions`, and 10 `slDLSSGGetState`.

### 2026-06-01 - FSR-to-DLSS switch-app handoff keeps DLSS status observable and skips proven-safe PostSL blanking (build 0.1.3636 / tests 0.1.3637)

- **Input**: `installed/captureengine/logs/20260601_150654` from `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` showed the app successfully enabling DLSS-G after FSR (`Mode now DLSS FG`, later `slDLSSGGetState ... genFrames=2`), while CE could either briefly hide the overlay during the FSR->DLSS handoff or stay hook-side inactive (`STREAMLINE_NO_FG`) because the later `slDLSSGSetOptions(ON)` edge was not observed.

# llm-wiki Log — Archive 2026-W23c

### 2026-06-01 - Pseudo-overlay foreground-acquire grace period for Alt+Tab-in settle (later full builds/tests passed)

- **Input**: User request to add a short wait time (~2s) when Alt+Tabbing back into a game so the controller-side pseudo-overlay does not race Windows MPO / fullscreen buffer rebinds. Observation: the pseudo-overlay's 500ms timer used to call `EnsureOverlayWindows` + `ShowWindow(SW_SHOWNA)` + `SetWindowPos` + `UpdateLayeredWindow` immediately on the first tick after the whitelisted PID became foreground. On some games/drivers this can destabilize the post-focus MPO re-attach and freeze the game window. Possibly a Windows MPO bug, not a CE code bug, but the safer default is to not race it.
- **Fix**:
  - New config knob `foreground_acquire_grace_ms` (default 2000, range 0-10000) on `PseudoOverlayConfig` (`common/config.h:283-285`) and the `[pseudo-overlay]` ini section (`captureengine/config.ini.template`).
  - Pure policy helper `ce::pseudo_overlay::ComputeFocusGraceDecision(...)` in `common/pseudo_overlay_focus_grace.h/.cpp`. Fully unit-testable without Windows APIs. Detects focus-acquire transitions (first detection, PID swap, no-target→target), tracks grace expiry, and exposes abort signals (recording state change).
  - `PseudoOverlay` now tracks `lastForegroundAcquireTick_`, `lastForegroundAcquirePid_`, `hadForegroundTarget_`, `prevIsRecording_`. `OnTimerTick` updates the transition tracking; `UpdateOverlay` evaluates the helper and skips `EnsureOverlayWindows` / `ShowWindow` / `SetWindowPos` / `UpdateLayeredWindow` while the decision says `suppressVisibleOverlay=true`. Sticky anchor and warning blink phase still advance during grace so the first post-grace frame is in-position and in-phase.
  - Asymmetric: focus-OUT (Alt+Tab away) destroys the windows immediately. Only the focus-IN direction is debounced.
  - `recordingStateChanged` aborts grace immediately so the user never sees "I pressed the hotkey but no indicator" after Alt+Tab-in. `UpdateConfig` resets in-flight grace when the knob is changed so the new value is honored on the next acquire.
  - Logging breadcrumbs (`LogInfo`): `Foreground grace started pid=… grace=…ms`, `Foreground grace elapsed pid=… waited=…ms`, `Foreground grace aborted: focus_lost`, `Foreground grace reset: grace_ms changed N -> M`, `Foreground grace skipped: grace_ms=0`.
  - Focused unit coverage in `tests/test_pseudo_overlay_focus_grace.cpp`: grace disabled, first detection, mid-session PID swap, focus lost, recording abort, grace clamping, grace boundary, no-transition steady state.
- **Validation**:
  - Later full project build/test runs on 2026-06-01 passed; keep manual Alt+Tab-in validation on at least one whitelisted game as the practical check for whether the 2s default feels right. The user can raise `foreground_acquire_grace_ms` up to 10s if a particular game/driver needs more settle time.
- **Source anchors**: `common/config.h`, `common/config.cpp`, `common/pseudo_overlay_focus_grace.h`, `common/pseudo_overlay_focus_grace.cpp`, `captureengine/pseudo_overlay.h`, `captureengine/pseudo_overlay.cpp`, `tests/test_pseudo_overlay_focus_grace.cpp`, `captureengine/config.ini.template`, `llm-wiki/pseudo-overlay.md`.
- **Wiki updates**: `llm-wiki/pseudo-overlay.md` now documents the grace period semantics, abort signals, asymmetry, and source anchors. `llm-wiki/current.md` `Last cross-checked` updated to 2026-06-01 with the new entry.

### 2026-06-14 - Constant "audio slightly late" A/V offset: diagnosed + harness can now catch it + stimulus crackle FIXED (superseded by 2026-06-16 fix above)

- **Driven by user session** `installed/captureengine/logs/fortniteaudiodelayed` (WGC + ALAC, Fortnite, 120 fps). The MKV was packet/zero-drift perfect (`maxPacketDelta=0`, `residual_samples=0`, `ratePpm=+0.00`) yet audio played slightly late. **Root cause**: uncompensated render/process-loopback audio capture latency (WASAPI `GetStreamLatency()` reports 0 for loopback). Codec-independent; affects WGC and inject.
- **Why the harness missed it**: `tools/run_av_sync_matrix.py` applied a hidden method-aware stimulus "audio lead" (56 ms WGC / 45-50 ms inject) via `resolve_app_audio_lead_ms`, deliberately cancelling exactly this offset before the analyzer measured it. **Added `--raw-offset-gate`** (forces `--app-audio-lead-ms 0` → measures the true offset; reliably fails on the real ~40-72 ms offset), **`--audio-capture-latency-ms`** (writes `[General] audio_capture_latency_ms` into the scenario config for fix validation), and device-period/buffer fields on the `[AudioCapture] Started` log.
- **Stimulus crackle FIXED (prerequisite — it was corrupting the measurement)**: `dx12_av_sync_test.exe` `AudioRenderer::FillAudio` re-derived `baseOffsetSeconds` from the audio device clock every ~10 ms fill (`audioClockScheduling=1`), injecting a per-fill phase jump → audible crackle. Fix (`testapp/dx12_av_sync_audio.h`): establish the phase anchor ONCE, then advance the waveform phase monotonically by `sampleCursor_`. Decoded audio: continuous clicks → 1 benign startup tick at 0.15 s. This collapsed the analyzer's system-track per-event offset span from ~92 ms to ~8 ms and run-to-run variance from ±30 ms to ±1-2 ms. Regression test `AvSyncStimulusTest.AudioWaveformIsPhaseContinuousAcrossSegmentBoundaries`.
- **Measured stable offsets (120 fps, reliable oracle)**: WGC system loopback (192 kHz) ~72 ms, WGC app loopback (48 kHz) ~46 ms, inject ~39-47 ms audio-late. The offset is **per-source** (192 kHz system endpoint ~26 ms more latency than 48 kHz process loopback).
- **Compensation design (IN PROGRESS, not yet wired)**: cannot advance live audio (no earlier data → pipeline pads/underruns, encoded-cursor re-pins). Must delay VIDEO content by the latency (WGC selection hook `GetWgcSelectionTargetQpc` now has an `extraSelectionDelayQpc` param + unit test) — but a naive bias fights the live clamp + warmup discard. Full "0 ms desync, equal length, co-terminous, no audio artifacts" needs per-source audio delay (delay faster sources to the slowest = safe direction, exempt from startup rebase trim) + video content delay (selection bias + clamp/warmup coordination) + inject equivalent + per-source `capture_latency_ms` config + full-matrix validation. Measurement floor is ±half a frame (±8.3 ms at 120 fps). Staged `audio_capture_latency_ms` config field + policy param landed but inert (0).

Audio and final media duration evidence stayed clean, but WGC visual cadence still showed the bad family: large live visual debt, stale drops, too-new repeats, and capacity pressure sometimes logged as `normal_pressure` / delivery-held low-source recovery instead of encoder-limited smoothness.
- **Root cause**: the classifier did not fully split true source-under-target from CE/encoder delivery pressure. Under healthy or buffered source input, `wgcEncoderRecoveryLimitedCurrent` could still fail to activate the tight near-live encoder-limited source-selection path, letting the old `250 ms` live-debt window survive into encoder overload.
- **Fix**: `common/capture_pipeline_policy.h` now has explicit helpers for true WGC input-below-target, healthy-enough source input, and buffered-source encoder-limited recovery. `captureengine/media_main.cpp` treats capacity pressure plus healthy/buffered source as encoder-limited smoothness, adds a mode-mismatch warning when recovery state and smoothness policy disagree, prunes stale history before near-live selection, blocks selected-source timestamp backtracking, and exposes low-source-bypass / mode-mismatch / source-backtrack counters in cadence and smoothness logs. CFR timestamps, audio cursors, final stream lengths, and codec finalization are unchanged.
- **Analyzer and runner**: `tools/analyze_capture_av.py` now reports `wgc_encoder_overload_policy_fault` separately from `wgc_encoder_limited_judder` and keeps audio faults separate. `tools/analyze_av_sync_stimulus.py` now timestamps raw decoded CFR playback frames from the declared stream frame rate when FFmpeg expands rawvideo frames, avoiding a false p6/p7 drift caused by mixing sparse FFprobe packet rows with raw frame output. `dx12_av_sync_test.exe --encoder-stress-scene` adds deterministic high-entropy animated content outside marker/motion/event regions, and `tools/run_av_sync_matrix.py --wgc-overload-gate` adaptively tries 4K/120 p5/p6/p7 with `--require-overload`. The gate now accepts the fixed overload signature: bounded shortfall plus explicit encoder-limited source drops, not the old 80ms+ visual-debt failure.
- **Validation**: `tools/analyze_capture_av.py --session-dir installed/captureengine/logs/strangebrigadeencoderoverloadjudder` classifies the old log as `wgc_encoder_overload_policy_fault`/`ce_visual_timeline_fault` with `audio=0`. ### 2026-06-13 - D3: three remaining FG-switch overlay blanks (14 / 60 / 90 presents) → ≤1-2-present floor

- **Driven by user session** `installed/captureengine/logs/20260613_202646` (`dx12_fg_switch_test.exe`, default OFF→FSR→DLSS→FSR + present-callback toggle + suspend stress). The `[OVERLAY COVERAGE]` gate showed exactly THREE multi-present blanks remaining (everything else is the documented ≤1-present floor); real-world Talos was re-tested and NOT regressed.
- **Blank #1 — 14 presents / 125 ms, FSR→OFF game-swapchain recovery, gate=live-overlay-kept-drawing.** C1 kept the overlay live (`overlayInit=true`) but the **scene-transition cooldown** still `goto skip_overlay_draw`'d. Root cause: the scene block in `DX12_ProcessFrameExternal` only runs ~1 Hz while FSR renders the overlay via the FFX callback route, so its frame-delta reads a phantom `gap≈1001ms` and arms a 30-frame cooldown every ~1.2 s; that cooldown never ticks during FSR (the draw is skipped before the decrement) and then blanks the NORMAL route on FSR-exit. Fix: `ShouldSuppressSceneTransitionCooldownForRuntimeOwnedOverlayRoute` (suppress arming on runtime-owned / FSR-callback / PostSL / protected-FFX routes) + discard any gap that SPANS such a route (`s_lastSceneBlockSuppressedRoute`) + clear `g_SceneTransitionCooldown` at the C1 keep-drawing edge so a stale cooldown can never blank a live overlay. New gate label `scene-transition-cooldown` for attribution.
- **Blank #2 — 60 presents / 453 ms, `confirmedDuringStreak=1`, DLSS suspend WITH FSR history.** The `DX12_OnStreamlineFGStateChanged` "after FSR history" branch (`dx12_hook.cpp:7519-7555`) tore down `overlayInit`+`CleanupRTVs` and armed a 60-frame reinit deferral even though the make-before-break keep-alive was just latched. The D2 `[outer]` bypass (`ShouldBypassConfirmedPostSLSuspensionOverlayReinitCooldown`) never ran because the `[outer]` block guard (`:15288`) needs `overlayInit && syncInit`, already torn down here. Fix: gate the deferral cooldown on `keepConfirmedPostSLAliveAcrossOff` (= `ShouldKeepConfirmedPostSLAliveAcrossStreamlineOff`, captured at function entry before the teardown) + `!deviceRemoved` → `cooldownFrames=0` with override ⇒ immediate warm reinit; FSR/native-FG/device-removed keep the strict 60.
- **Blank #3 — 90 presents / 875 ms, DLSS suspend after FSR with a fresh proxy swapchain pointer.** `ShouldReinitOverlayImmediatelyAfterConfirmedPostSLSuspensionSwapchainChange` required `scQueue==cmdQueue`, but at the suspend edge the live confirmed-PostSL queue is the DLSS-G proxy queue (`scQueue == g_PostSLLastWorkingQueue`, 180+ confirmed submits) while the live wrapper `cmdQueue` is a separate object → it fell into the generic 90-frame cooldown. Fix: the predicate now accepts `scQueue == confirmedPostSLRenderQueue` as an alternative to `scQueue == cmdQueue`; the call site passes `currentSwapchainQueue == g_PostSLLastWorkingQueue`.
- All three are timing-only changes of an already-proven-safe warm reinit (the eventual reinits in the source log all succeeded with `devRemoved=0`). Blanks #2/#3 share one user action (post-FSR DLSS suspend) hitting two different handlers depending on whether a proxy-swapchain pointer change lands at the suspend edge.
- **Regression tests** (`tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`): `SceneTransitionCooldownSuppressedForRuntimeOwnedOverlayRoute`, `ConfirmedPostSLSuspensionReinitsImmediatelyWhenSwapchainQueueIsConfirmedPostSLQueue` (+ updated the existing suspension test for the new 7th arg), `ConfirmedPostSLSuspensionAfterFSRHistoryResolvesReinitCooldownToZero`. Build `0.1.3971`, `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` all green.
- **Open / validation (USER manual run)**: re-run the injected `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` matrix and assert `[OVERLAY COVERAGE] uncovered streak ended` has **no `missed`>2** and no `confirmedDuringStreak=1`; confirm `Scene transition detected (gap=...)` no longer appears during FSR and the new bypass breadcrumbs fire. **Mandatory GTA/Talos** FG-switch re-test (no crash, no lost overlay, correct visible status) — this is the crash-prone subsystem; rollback = revert the three predicates/gates.
- **Stretch (zero-frame double-buffering) — NOT shipped, by design.** Investigation showed the residual ≤1-present floor on these transitions is structural: the overlay backend lifecycle is break-then-make (swapchain change → `overlayInit=false` → next-ProcessFrame reinit that re-evaluates a long sequence of documented crash-safety gates). True make-before-break needs either a full shadow-set rewrite of the 30+-field `DX12OverlayState` or bypassing that gate sequence — high risk on the most crash-prone path, not landable without the GTA/Talos validation loop. Recommended as a focused follow-up after the core fixes are validated, driven by a fresh log of the exact residual.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (scene block ~16565 + decrement ~16772, C1 keep-drawing clear ~16226, after-FSR-history branch ~7519-7575, suspension swapchain-change call site ~13706), `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ShouldSuppressSceneTransitionCooldownForRuntimeOwnedOverlayRoute`, relaxed `ShouldReinitOverlayImmediatelyAfterConfirmedPostSLSuspensionSwapchainChange`, reused `ShouldBypassConfirmedPostSLSuspensionOverlayReinitCooldown` / `ShouldKeepConfirmedPostSLAliveAcrossStreamlineOff` / `ResolveTransitionCooldownFrames`), `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`.

### 2026-06-13 - WGC encoder-overload smoothness hardening: Strange Brigade p5 session exact audio but bad visual cadence

- **Implementation direction**: WGC now has an encoder-limited smoothness mode only when source input is healthy and encoder/mux capacity is the limiter. It keeps CFR timestamps/audio exact but tightens live visual debt to about `50 ms` / `3` output frames, coalesces old visual slots as `encoder_limited_source_drop`, and logs `[WGC CFR CADENCE EVENT]` plus `[WGC CFR SMOOTHNESS SUMMARY]`. Source-starved episodes stay source-starved and should not be reclassified as encoder-limited judder.

The CFR compensation lane now has a wider about-80 ms deadband, so healthy runs stop with `ratePpm=+0.00`, `compDelta=0`, `sat=0`. Stop-tail source padding is also tagged with `forceDrain=1` and classified separately from live underruns.

### 2026-06-13 - D2: DLSS-FG SUSPEND ~672ms overlay blank + coverage inheritance blind spot

- **Driven by the D1 build's new streak logging on session `logs/20260613_150750`**: a DLSS-FG suspend (`slDLSSGSetOptions(off)`, proxy stays alive) blanked the confirmed-live overlay for `missed=60 durationMs=672 confirmedDuringStreak=1 gate=overlay-backend-uninitialized`. The user reported "still disappears, not always."
- **Telemetry blind spot (fixed first, so the blank is measurable)**: `[OVERLAY COVERAGE]` had counted the suspend as covered (longestStreak stayed ≤2) because the proxy's zero-ECL presents inherited coverage (`isInterpolatedFrame`) while `overlayInit=false` and nothing was drawing — the inheritance model assumes the runtime composites the last overlay-covered frame, but a SUSPENDED runtime presents fresh game frames with no CE overlay. `coverageInheritsFGComposedOverlay` (ProcessFrameExternal) is now gated on `g_State.overlayInit`; when the backend is not bound to the current swapchain, zero-ECL/SL-owned presents count UNCOVERED. Telemetry-only (no render change); steady-state active FG keeps inheriting. This is what surfaced the real 60-present blank above.
- **Functional root cause — TWO handlers, "not always"**: a DLSS suspend can take either path and both armed a draw-suppressing cooldown the keep-alive couldn't cover (the cooldown defers the overlay reinit → `overlayInit=false` → also blocks C1 keep-drawing):
  - **`[outer] SL FG OFF` handler (this repro):** `ShouldBypassPureStreamlineFGOffOverlayReinitCooldown` requires `!hadFSRFGPhase`; the sticky `g_HadFSRFGPhase` is true once any FSR phase ran this session, so a post-FSR DLSS suspend took `g_FGTransitionCooldown=max(..,60)` then `[outer]` forced `overlayInit=false`+`CleanupRTVs` ("stale SL backbuffers"). Fix: `ShouldBypassConfirmedPostSLSuspensionOverlayReinitCooldown` — replaces the `!hadFSRFGPhase` exclusion with the `g_PostSLExplicitOffKeepAlive` keep-alive latch + `g_PostSLConfirmedRendering` proof (confirmed this epoch ⇒ overlay ECL on the SL queue already succeeded ⇒ device healthy ⇒ nothing to wait for); FSR/native-FG-active + device-removed guards unchanged. Cooldown zeroed ⇒ reinit immediate ⇒ ~1-2-present floor.
  - **swapchain-change handler (the 145008 repro):** fresh proxy swapchain pointer on the same live queue; `ShouldPreserveConfirmedPostSLBackendDuringActiveFGSwapchainChange` requires `streamlineFGRunning` (false at suspend), so it took the 90-frame cooldown. Fix: `ShouldReinitOverlayImmediatelyAfterConfirmedPostSLSuspensionSwapchainChange` joins the immediate-reinit fast paths.
- Both suspend-bypass fixes are timing-only changes of an already-proven-safe warm reinit (identical flag resets, cooldown 0 vs 60/90). A suspend has no Streamline teardown to wait for, so the post-teardown first-ECL DEVICE_REMOVED hazard does not apply.
- **FOREVER-BLANK regression from the suspend bypass, and its proper fix (session `logs/20260613_151646`)**: with the suspend bypass keeping the overlay rendering through the suspend, `g_PostSLConfirmedRendering` stays true, so the resume takes the make-before-break **warm resume** (`dx12_hook.cpp:7204`) — NO synthetic-startup re-arm, and it sets `streamlineStartupHandoffPending=false`. That `false` armed `ShouldClearSwapchainQueueAsStaleFSROwnershipOnStreamlineOn` (`hadFSR && scQueue≠origGame && !handoffPending`), which **nulled `g_SwapchainQueue`** ("cleared stale FSR swapchain queue 84EDB990"). With `scQueue=null` + FSR history, PostSL refused the wrapper bootstrap (`refusing SL wrapper bootstrap without direct path` ×1023) and the overlay disappeared **forever** after resume. The queue was the LIVE DLSS-G proxy (180+ confirmed submits, persists across the suspend), NOT a stale FSR queue. **Proper fix**: `ShouldClearSwapchainQueueAsStaleFSROwnershipOnStreamlineOn` gains a `warmPostSLResumeFromKeepAlive` arg (returns false when set); the call passes `resumeConfirmedPostSLFromKeepAlive`. The warm resume now keeps its live proxy queue, so `scQueue` is non-null and PostSL resumes via the proven `scQueue->ExecuteCommandLists` path (`:12055`). The cold FSR→DLSS transition (no warm resume) STILL clears (prevents DEVICE_REMOVED). INVARIANT: warm resume and the stale-FSR-queue clear are contradictory — when PostSL warm-resumes, its swapchain queue is the live proxy and must be preserved.
- **Regression tests**: `ConfirmedPostSLSuspensionBypassesReinitCooldownEvenWithFSRHistory`, `ConfirmedPostSLSuspensionReinitsOverlayImmediatelyInsteadOfBlanking`, `StaleFSRQueueClearSkippedForWarmPostSLResume`, source-invariant `StaleFSRQueueClearReceivesWarmResumeFlag`.
- **Open / validation**: user manual re-run of DLSS suspend→resume (expect: NO forever-blank — `warm PostSL resume` WITHOUT a following `cleared stale FSR swapchain queue`, no `refusing SL wrapper bootstrap` storm, `scQueue submit` resumes immediately; `[OVERLAY COVERAGE]` longest streak ≤1-2 across the whole cycle). **Mandatory GTA/Talos** DLSS suspend/resume AND cold FSR→DLSS (the cold transition must still clear the stale queue without DEVICE_REMOVED). This crash-prone path regressed three times; runtime proof on both games gates the change. Rollback = revert the suspend bypass + the warm-resume clear gate together.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`[outer]` FG-off bypass ~15302/15330; swapchain-change immediate-reinit ~13700; warm-resume clear gate ~7295; coverage inheritance overlayInit gate in ProcessFrameExternal), `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ShouldBypassConfirmedPostSLSuspensionOverlayReinitCooldown`, `ShouldReinitOverlayImmediatelyAfterConfirmedPostSLSuspensionSwapchainChange`, `ShouldClearSwapchainQueueAsStaleFSROwnershipOnStreamlineOn` warm-resume arg), `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`.

The coverage gate (`dx12_hook.cpp:15557-15564`) shows `overlay-backend-uninitialized` fires only with `allowOverlayRender=true && !suspendOverlayRender && overlayInit=false`, and the log has `runtimeOwnsSwapchain=1` there — so `overlayInit=false` is PROTECTIVE (blocks a normal-route ECL on a becoming-SL-owned queue = the documented 0x887A002B). Forcing an eager rebuild/draw is rejected (re-enables the unsafe draw for ~7 ms imperceptible gain); loosening the gate is rejected (papering over). ### 2026-06-13 - PRINCIPLE: never blank a live overlay (C1) + PostSL keep-alive across SL churn (C2)

- **User directive shift**: keep the overlay visible 100% of the time across all FG transitions; if a draw would crash, fix the crash at root, do NOT revert to hiding the overlay. The draw-suppressing cooldown/probe/warmup mechanisms are themselves the defect, not just their gaps. Per-case exemption widening (F1/B1) was not converging — every session surfaced a new permutation.
- **C1 (commit 5c0dfad) - never blank a live overlay**: session `logs/20260613_041204` had a 60-present (~400ms) blank on an OFF->FSR FG enable. The no-callback FFX takeover finalized with the swapchain REUSED (swapchainEpoch unchanged) and `syncInit=true` kept (`resources work on any queue`), yet the inner transition armed `cooldown=60`. The overlay backend was fully live: device-level allocators/fence/cmdList work on any DIRECT queue, RTVs valid (same swapchain), and the per-frame submit-queue resolution already retargets to the new FSR queue — nothing needed rebuilding. When the cooldown expired the normal route drew fine on that exact FSR queue, proving immediate drawing was always safe (AMD no-callback route explicitly allows normal overlay rendering). `ShouldKeepDrawingLiveOverlayThroughFGTransitionCooldown` (overlayInit && syncInit && !protectedFFXStartup && !slFGRunning && !appCallbackBridgeFSR) zeroes the cooldown and keeps drawing this frame at the draw-suppression site. The draw suppression is retained only for the proven-unsafe/owned-elsewhere windows (pre-enable protected FFX startup wedges AMD's presenter; SL FG = PostSL owns it; app-callback FFX bridge = separate ECL is the documented 0x887A002B). Transition bookkeeping (GPU drain, queue/heuristic resets) still runs — only the multi-frame draw suppression is removed. This is the principled generalization of the F1/B1 narrow exemptions for the normal route. Diagnostic: `Keeping live overlay drawing through FG transition cooldown — no blank`, gate=`live-overlay-kept-drawing`.
- **C2 (shipped in commit 5c0dfad) - PostSL keep-alive across SL-signal churn**: during DLSS, SL FG churned `OFF->ON via SetOptions` repeatedly (GetState/SetOptions jitter); each ON ran a cold-start `PostSL REACTIVATED epoch` (warmup + probe) with a 1-present gap. Root cause: the **pre-SL fallback** (SL-FG-not-active branch in ProcessFrame) called `SetPostSLCallbackInstalled(false, "DX12: pre-SL fallback")` ~10ms after the OFF, which cleared the F4 keep-alive latch and uninstalled the callback, so the rapid re-ON could not warm-resume. Fix: gate that uninstall on `!g_PostSLExplicitOffKeepAlive` — while a confirmed-PostSL suspension keep-alive is active, the callback stays installed and the confirmed flag stays set (the normal route still draws during the suspension, overlay visible), so the re-ON takes the warm-resume path (no reactivation epoch, no probe, no 1-present gap). The keep-alive's existing event-driven retirement (Streamline unload / swapchain invalidation / authoritative disable) is unchanged. Diagnostic: `pre-SL fallback rendering normal route during confirmed-PostSL suspension keep-alive — callback stays installed for warm re-ON`.
- **Regression tests**: `LiveOverlayKeepsDrawingThroughFGTransitionCooldown`, `PreSLFallbackRespectsConfirmedPostSLSuspensionKeepAlive` (source invariant).
- **Open / validation**: user manual re-test of the full matrix (target `[OVERLAY COVERAGE] longestStreak == 0`); GTA + Talos required because C1 removes draw suppression on the crash-prone FSR path — any crash that surfaces is fixed at root (keep drawing safely), not by re-introducing the blank.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ShouldKeepDrawingLiveOverlayThroughFGTransitionCooldown`), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (draw-suppression cooldown block; pre-SL fallback keep-alive gate), `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`.


### 2026-06-13 - 100% overlay visibility round 2: FSR->OFF-after-DLSS cooldown blank + post-FSR DLSS probe seam

- **Driven by `[OVERLAY COVERAGE]` again**: session `logs/20260613_035221` (after round-1 F1-F4/FA): OFF<->FSR and FSR-suspend fully blank-free; remaining blanks were one 60-present (~400ms) FSR->OFF cooldown blank and three ~3-4-present (~25ms) FSR->DLSS engage probe seams.
- **B1 (commit afe39b7) - 60-present FSR->OFF blank after a DLSS phase**: the SECOND FSR->OFF (after an earlier DLSS phase left Streamline DLLs loaded) ran the game-swapchain-recovery edge correctly (ended runtime-owned teardown, re-baselined origGame, fgOwned=0) but the inner `prev_mode=FSR_FG next_mode=STREAMLINE_NO_FG` classification re-armed the 60-frame draw cooldown. Root cause: `IsGameSwapchainRecoveryToggleAfterNativeFSROff` required `next==kOff`, but with SL loaded the recovered non-FG state classifies as `kStreamlineNoFG` (same kOff-vs-kStreamlineNoFG blind spot fixed for the no-callback suspension toggle in round 1). The exemption now accepts `kStreamlineNoFG` with the same hard requirements (no SL FG signal, recovery queue == live swapchain queue). ### 2026-06-12 - Fast zero-drift A/V gate and sample-exact CFR audio cursor

### 2026-06-12 - FIXED: duplicate app-audio routing stall + unsafe writer double-finalize crash

### 2026-06-12 - FIXED CRASH: stale Streamline hook generations on repeated OFF<->DLSS toggling (sl module unload invalidation)

- **Symptom (crash dump + logs `installed/captureengine/logs/20260612_003407`)**: toggling all-FG-off <-> DLSS FG repeatedly crashed the test app with an AV WRITE to 0xBF6A inside `sl.common.dll` on the game thread during the second DLSS enter, right after `CreateDXGIFactory1`.
- **Root cause (cdb + log proven)**: the app fully unloads and reloads the Streamline stack per OFF<->DLSS cycle. CE's Streamline hook bookkeeping was per-function-name and process-global: `g_Original_*` (gen-1 trampolines), `g_*Target` addresses, `g_*Hooked` flags, and the interposer/common install/IAT masks all survived the unload; the per-name mask dedupe then silently refused to re-hook the fresh instances ("Installed hooks for sl.common.dll" appears only once in the session). The dump shows the reloaded `sl.common.dll` (35730000-35807000) occupying the previous generation's `sl.interposer.dll` range (35760000), so the call-time `IsSavedStreamlineOriginalCallable` guard — which only checks "target belongs to a loaded module" — passed, and the stale gen-1 trampoline jumped mid-instruction into the NEW module (a CE trampoline-pool address was still live in RSI at crash time). Address-space reuse defeats call-time validation; this is the module-level analogue of the swapchain pointer-reuse lesson.
- **Fix**: event-driven + load-time self-heal. (1) `StreamlineHook::OnModuleUnloaded` (dispatched from the loader DLL-unload notification in `hook/main.cpp`, loader-lock-safe: interlocked/atomic writes + light logging) invalidates every hook slot whose patched target or saved original lies inside the departing image — original cleared FIRST so detours fail safe through the existing null-callable paths — plus the import-fallback attempted-target slots, and clears the per-module install/IAT mask bits so the next load re-hooks the fresh instance. (2) Load-time self-heal in `InstallHooksForModule`: when a core module name arrives with its mask bit set but none of the stored core targets belong to the arriving instance, the mask is a stale generation — core slots belonging to no live core instance are cleared and the fresh instance is re-hooked (covers environments where `LdrRegisterDllNotification` is unavailable).
- **Regression tests**: `StreamlineModuleUnloadDispatchesHookInvalidation`, `HookSlotInvalidationMatchesUnloadedImageRange`, `ReloadedCoreModuleMaskIsStaleWhenNoTargetBelongsToArrivingInstance` in `tests/test_streamline_runtime_policy.cpp`. Full suite 965 passed.
- **Expected diagnostics**: `Streamline Hook: Invalidated <fn> hook slot for unloaded sl.*`, `Module sl.* unloaded ... invalidated N stale hook slot(s); the next load of this name re-installs hooks`, `reloaded at ... installed-module mask refers to a previous unloaded generation`.
- **Brief overlay blanks in the same session**: CE-attributable gaps were already small — DLSS engage used the pure-DLSS clamped 8-frame cooldown (~60ms) and DLSS->OFF used the `pure Streamline FG OFF — bypassing generic reinit cooldown` immediate rebuild (~26ms to first submit). The visually longer freezes are app-side NGX init/teardown windows where the last presented frame (still containing the overlay) stays on screen. Stale-hook breakage in the crash cycle could also blank by missing `slDLSSGSetOptions` interception; fixed by the per-generation re-hooking.
- **Open hardening item**: the FFX guarded `ffxConfigure` VEH breakpoint stores a raw target address; an FFX module reload at a different base could re-arm 0xCC into re-mapped foreign memory — same unload-invalidation treatment if evidence ever lands there.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/streamline_hook.cpp` (`OnModuleUnloaded`, `InstallHooksForModule` self-heal, `GetModuleImageSizeBytes`), `hook/apis/streamline_hook.h`, `hook/main.cpp` (`OverlayDllNotificationCallback` unload dispatch), `hook/common/streamline_runtime_policy.h` (new policies).

### 2026-06-12 - FIXED: overlay disappeared FOREVER on all-FG-off -> DLSS FG (pure-DLSS PostSL preserve + cooldown tick guard)

- **Symptom (user log `installed/captureengine/logs/20260612_002523`)**: OFF -> DLSS FG rendered 10 confirmed PostSL overlay submits, then the overlay disappeared permanently (`PostSL stats: calls=1500 renders=10 skipOther=1489`).
- **Root cause (two stacked defects)**: (1) the ProcessFrame swapchain-pointer catch-up after PostSL had ALREADY confirmed on the live Streamline swapchain took the ordinary cleanup path (the preserve policy required FSR history), arming the 90-frame cooldown and deactivating PostSL; (2) the same retired-original-queue zero-ECL starvation as the FSR case (the switch app recreates its render queue when entering DLSS mode) meant ProcessFrame never ran again, so the cooldown never ticked and PostSL stayed disabled forever.
- **Fix**: `ShouldPreserveConfirmedPostSLBackendDuringActiveFGSwapchainChange` no longer requires `hadFSRFGPhase` — PostSL confirmation is by definition proof on the LIVE swapchain (the present callback hands CE the presenting swapchain), so a confirmed warmup-protected PostSL backend on a runtime-owned queue is preserved across the pointer change with or without FSR history. Deadlock guard: `ShouldSkipProcessFrameForZeroECLPresent` gains `fgTransitionCooldownActive` — armed FG transition cooldowns must always be allowed to tick, regardless of zero-ECL classification.
- **Regression tests**: pure-DLSS preserve case added to `PostFSRConfirmedPostSLBackendSurvivesActiveSwapchainChange`; new `ArmedFGTransitionCooldownAlwaysTicksDespiteZeroECLClassification`. Full suite 962 passed.
- **Expected diagnostics**: `Preserving confirmed PostSL backend during active Streamline FG swapchain change` (now also with `hadFSR=0`).
- **Open**: ProcessFrame starvation during Streamline FG with a retired original game queue still degrades inject capture/metrics in the switch app (classification never counts the game's recreated render queue while SL owns the swapchain); needs a classification-queue successor concept if real games show the same shape.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ShouldPreserveConfirmedPostSLBackendDuringActiveFGSwapchainChange`, `ShouldSkipProcessFrameForZeroECLPresent`), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (preserve branch log, zero-ECL gate call site).

### 2026-06-12 - FIXED: overlay disappeared FOREVER after FSR FG -> all off (frame classification starved ProcessFrame)

- **Symptom (user log `installed/captureengine/logs/20260612_000936`)**: with the game-created-swapchain teardown-end edge in place, FSR FG -> all FG off made the overlay disappear permanently. The recovery edge fired correctly (`Game-created swapchain ... ending runtime-owned native-FG teardown`, scQueue captured, fgOwned=0), but afterwards NO ProcessFrame activity appeared at all — only DetourPresent heartbeats and ECL diagnostics.
- **Root cause**: the previous "working" blanks were kept alive by ACCIDENTAL keep-alives — the stale runtimeOwns latch and re-latched heuristic FSR satisfied escapes in `ShouldSkipProcessFrameForZeroECLPresent`. Once the recovery edge correctly cleared them, the underlying defect surfaced: `GetFrameClassificationQueue()` prefers `g_OriginalGameQueue`, which the game had RETIRED when it recreated its swapchain on a fresh queue. ECLs on the new queue were never counted (classification-queue mismatch), every present classified as zero-ECL/interpolated, and ProcessFrame was skipped forever.
- **Fix**: (1) the recovery edge re-baselines `g_OriginalGameQueue` to the game-created recovery queue (AddRef new / Release old, pointer-equality no-op for Talos-style same-queue recreates) — the game itself retired the old queue, so every consumer (frame classification, routing fallbacks, future FG-cycle takeover/teardown proofs, queue-vtable hook decision) must anchor on the live present queue; (2) defense-in-depth: `ShouldSkipProcessFrameForZeroECLPresent` gained a `liveSwapchainQueueIsGameRecoveryQueue` escape — presents on the game-created recovery swapchain are real game frames by construction even if classification lags.
- **Regression tests**: `GameRecoverySwapchainPresentsDriveProcessFrameDespiteZeroECLClassification` in `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`; full suite 961 passed.
- **Expected diagnostics**: `Re-baselined original game queue to game-created recovery queue %p (was %p; old queue retired by the game itself)`.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`DX12_SetSwapchainQueue` recovery block re-baseline, `ProcessFrameExternal` zero-ECL gate call), `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ShouldSkipProcessFrameForZeroECLPresent`).
