The only untried principled route is RTSS-style: draw inline at AMD's INNER real swapchain Present (post-composition, presenter thread) WITHOUT synthesizing a callback. Need the normal-route wedge dump first to know if its mechanism is the same pacing wedge (-> inner-present likely won't help) or a different/fixable accumulation. See [guardrails.md](../frame-generation/guardrails.md) lines 100/146 (no-callback = preserve AMD internal composition) and the 2026-06-16 recent entry (BOTH routes wedge; strategic decision was pending).

# llm-wiki Log — Archive 2026-W25b

### 2026-06-18 - Active sync-delay smoothness gate and WGC attribution

- **Why:** the hybrid audio-delay probe can now apply a real video-content delay, but smooth CFR video still needs proof under WGC/inject source-rate variation, planned source stalls, and temporary encoder pressure without regressing audio sample accounting.
- **Runner:** `tools/run_av_sync_matrix.py --sync-smoothness-gate` adds a strict active-delay profile. ### 2026-06-17 - Per-device audio capture-latency model: mic-domain split, delay-only (drop GetStreamLatency advance), render→loopback auto-detect

- **Problem (regression):** session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260617_010909` (Fortnite, WGC) had game audio ~46 ms late. Latency was modeled PER-SOURCE: the user set `[Audio] capture_latency_ms=46` but `[General] audio_capture_latency_ms=0`, so the system loopback got 46 while every `[AppAudio.N]` process-loopback (the game) inherited `[General]`=0. The per-source A/V equalization then DELAYED the game's app-loopback by `max−0=46` ms, even though it shares the SAME render endpoint as the system loopback (same real latency). Net: game audio left ~46 ms late.
- **Root cause:** latency is a per-DEVICE-DOMAIN property, not per-source. Domain 1 = default render endpoint (system loopback + ALL app process-loopback) → ONE value. Domain 2 = each mic/input → its own. The config modeled it per-source and the mic also inherited the loopback fallback.
- **Part A — device-domain config (`common/config.{h,cpp}`):** mics no longer inherit `audioCaptureLatencyMs`; they fall back to new `[General] mic_capture_latency_ms` (default 0) or a per-mic `capture_latency_ms`. System `[Audio]`/`[Audio.N]` and all `[AppAudio.N]` still inherit the one render-endpoint value. Regression tests `ConfigTest.CaptureLatencyIsPerDeviceDomain` / `MicLatencyOverrideAndFallback`.
- **Part C — delay-only (`mediaengine/audio_capture.cpp`, `app_audio_capture.cpp`):** stopped advancing live audio by `GetStreamLatency` in `ApplyCaptureLatencyCompensation` at the packet-placement sites (packets now placed at the raw / period-center QPC). Advancing live audio never worked (the earlier samples do not exist; the CFR pipeline pads the deficit and the encoded cursor re-pins → absorbed) and double-counts with the video delay on devices that report a nonzero `GetStreamLatency`. ALL latency now flows through the video content delay + equalization (delay-only). `streamLatency` is kept as telemetry; `[AudioCapture]/[AppAudioCapture] Started` logs say "latency routed via video content delay, not audio advance". AVR unaffected (`GetStreamLatency`=0); needs validation on a device that reports it.
- **Part B — render→loopback auto-detect (`mediaengine/audio_latency_probe.{h,cpp}`):** the "no hardcoded value, works automatically on any system" piece. On a cache miss, render a brief near-inaudible Hann-windowed marker (≈ near-Nyquist/ultrasonic, low amplitude) to the default render endpoint and detect its center in a LOOPBACK capture of the same endpoint (loopback taps the DIGITAL render mix pre-DAC, so the marker is captured perfectly even if ultrasonic). latency = loopback marker-CENTER QPC − render presentation QPC of the marker center (aligning Hann CENTERS via `IAudioClock` cancels the envelope; a leading-edge detector would inject a systematic bias). **Robustness for fully-automatic trust:** takes `kProbeShots=5` independent shots and aggregates with `MedianWithConsistency` (need ≥3 within 8 ms) so a single noisy reading cannot over/under-correct; no consensus → ok=false. Superseded on 2026-06-18: the endpoint value is now process-memory only, so a fresh CE process may re-probe instead of using the old `audio_latency_cache.ini` disk file. Fail-safe: any error / implausible (`<0` or `>2000 ms`) / no consensus → no correction (NOT a guessed value). Pure DSP/cache/aggregation logic is header-only and unit-tested (`tests/test_audio_latency_probe.cpp`: marker synthesis, narrowband Goertzel center detection with a sustained-run discriminator that rejects noise/silence, end-to-end latency recovery, memory cache lookup/upsert, median/consistency).
- **Integration:** new mediaengine export `MediaEngine_MeasureRenderEndpointLatency` (+ loader plumbing). `captureengine/media_main.cpp` measures ONCE (in `ensureMediaEngineReady`, before Init, only when not recording) and re-applies the cached value to render-domain sources on every config (re)load (`ApplyAutoDetectedRenderLatencyToConfig`) so BOTH the encoder thread (video content delay) and the media engine (equalization) read the resolved value from the same config. `[General] audio_latency_autodetect` (default true) opts out; a manual `audio_capture_latency_ms > 0` is an OPTIONAL override that disables measurement. The A/V harness writes `audio_latency_autodetect=false` so its explicit latency is authoritative.
- **Default config is fully automatic — no hand-set values.** `installed/captureengine/config.ini` ships `[General] audio_capture_latency_ms=0` and `[Audio] capture_latency_ms=0` (auto). If the probe succeeds it applies the measured value uniformly to system + all app sources; if it can't get a consensus it applies nothing → all render sources 0 → equalization no-op → graceful degradation to the pre-existing minor "audio slightly late" baseline, NEVER the per-source regression and NEVER a guessed number. (Do NOT reintroduce a hardcoded `46`; an earlier draft did and was reverted — it disabled the probe and defeated the automatic goal.)
- **Detection design notes:** Goertzel window ≈ 5 ms (`sampleRate/200`) for narrowband rejection of loud out-of-band audio; confidence = peak ≥ median × `peakOverFloorMin` AND a contiguous run of ≥4 windows above half-peak (a real burst is sustained; a noise spike is isolated).
- **Validation:** `python build.py --run-tests --skip-updates` native tests pass; `run_av_sync_matrix.py --self-test` PASS. **HARDWARE-VALIDATION-PENDING:** the WASAPI render-clock-vs-loopback measurement (Part B) and the reporting-device path (Part C) cannot be exercised in unit tests; validate the auto-measured value against `tools/run_av_sync_matrix.py --raw-offset-gate` (120 fps) `offset_mean` (~46 ms on this AVR), confirm `[A/V START] ... captureLatencyMs=` shows the SAME auto value for system + all app sources, and `[AudioLoop] A/V equalization` does NOT delay the app/game sources. If the probe value is wrong vs the gate, FIX the measurement (IAudioClock render-center vs loopback-center mapping) — do not hardcode.
- **Source anchors:** `common/config.{h,cpp}`, `mediaengine/audio_latency_probe.{h,cpp}`, `mediaengine/audio_capture.cpp`, `mediaengine/app_audio_capture.cpp`, `mediaengine/audio_time_utils.h` (`ApplyCaptureLatencyCompensation` now placement-unused, kept for telemetry/tests), `mediaengine/mediaengine.{h,cpp}`, `captureengine/mediaengine_loader.{h,cpp}`, `captureengine/media_main.cpp` (`MeasureRenderLatencyOnce`/`ApplyAutoDetectedRenderLatencyToConfig`), `tools/run_av_sync_matrix.py`.

### 2026-06-16 - GTA native FSR-FG overlay: BOTH post-interpolation routes wedge ffxQuery (callback-injection REVERTED)

- **Conclusive finding (sessions `fsrgtafreeze`, `20260616_195727`):** GTA Enhanced native FSR FG with **no app present callback** (`appCallback=0`, runtime-owned) wedges `amd_fidelityfx_dx12!ffxQuery → WaitForSingleObjectEx` on **any** CE overlay GPU work that touches its runtime-owned backbuffers, via **either** mechanism:
  - Separate CE overlay command list on AMD's FFX runtime queue (`g_NativeFSRInternalNoCallbackComposition` route) — wedges after ~300 frames.
  - CE FFX present-callback **self-compose** on AMD's command list (copy `currentBackBuffer→output` + overlay) — wedges after ~8 frames. This is the **documented** wedge path ([dx12_hook.cpp:5067](../../hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp#L5067) `WARNING FFX bridge self-composing ... ffxQuery-wedge risk`, session 20260615_021242).
- **Attempted fix (commit 1b71d43) REVERTED:** relaxing `ShouldInstallFFXPresentCallbackBridgeForConfigure` to inject CE's present callback for the no-app-callback case correctly switched GTA OFF the queue-submit (routing worked: `bridgeActive=1 internalNoCallback=0`, 0 FSR-queue submits, callback rendered ~8 frames) but **forced the documented self-compose wedge** — the gate's `presentCallbackAvailable` requirement was DELIBERATELY preventing exactly this. So injection is not a fix; reverted.
- **Conclusion / open question:** there is **no known post-interpolation route** to draw the inject overlay in GTA's no-app-callback FSR FG without wedging `ffxQuery` (touching AMD's runtime-owned resources mid-pipeline wedges it). The only freeze-free options are (a) suspend the overlay for this specific config (prior behavior — user rejects as permanent), or (b) a **pre-interpolation** RTSS-style draw on the game's frame at the Present hook (game queue, before FFX interpolates) — overlay visible everywhere but interpolated frames would show overlay ghosting; not yet implemented for this path. Strategic decision pending with the user. The app-callback FSR path and Talos are unaffected.

### 2026-06-16 - Dormant FSR-draw regression: ~1 fps after FSR->DLSS (stale upload-ring slot guard)

- **Symptom (session 20260616_142044, build 0.1.4042):** after switching to DLSS FG, Talos dropped to ~1 fps — `DetourPresent TOTAL SLOW ~1001ms` every present, `slFG=0`. Not a crash (manual dump only).
- **Root cause:** the DescFree overlay UPLOAD-ring publishes a per-slot GPU-completion guard `= currentFenceValue+1` (non-FG path) when the dormant 2D-menu draw submits on the **transient staged takeover queue**. When the runtime then hands off (FSR->DLSS swapchain/queue transition), that queue's pending overlay-fence Signal is **discarded**, so the fence never reaches the guard value. `WaitForSlotGpuComplete` then blocks for the full `kSlotWaitTimeoutMs` (1 s) every frame: `DescFree: slot 3 GPU-completion wait timed out (guard=279 completed=0)`. The existing fence-rebind reset (`s_descFreeSlotFence != slotFence_`) didn't help because the stale guard was re-published each dormant frame.
- **Fix:** `DecideOverlayUploadSlotGuardValue` gains a `submitQueueMayBeDiscarded` arg (defaults false); when set it returns 0 (disable the guard) — exactly like the existing FG-path disable. All 5 publish sites pass `ShouldQuiesceCESideEffectsForProtectedOfficialFFXStartup()` / `protectedOfficialFFXStartupOverlayOnly`, so the dormant draw never publishes a guard that the next phase's fence can't reach. Test extended; 1027 pass.
- **Source anchors:** `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` `DecideOverlayUploadSlotGuardValue`; `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (the 5 guard-publish sites + `WaitForSlotGpuComplete`/`kSlotWaitTimeoutMs`).

### 2026-06-16 - CRASH root cause #6 (the REAL one) — FSR-arming stale RTVs + queue mismatch; EXPERIMENTAL zero-blank fix (runtime-validation pending)

- **#5 was an incomplete diagnosis.** Session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260616_024418` (build 0.1.4039, WITH the #5 fix) still crashes — but on a **pure FSR-FG startup** (`slFG=0` throughout, no DLSS, no SL teardown), a path the #5 SL-teardown fix never touches. FSR needs it`). The dormant draw then resolved `gameQueue = g_SwapchainQueue` (stale `075C9A40`) and submitted **stale RTVs on the wrong queue** → GPU page fault → device removed. The dump confirms `CreateRTVs` ran once at `02:44:30.201`, never rebuilt after the `02:44:33.269` swapchain change; `[dormant-ffx-draw DIAG] ... cachedSC=0 skipOverlayDraw=1` for the whole 60-frame `STREAMLINE_NO_FG->FSR_FG` cooldown, then the crash at cooldown-complete.
- **Key insight.** Submitting overlay work on `origGame` during FSR arming is wrong on two counts: the live swapchain's backbuffers belong to its **creation queue** (the staged takeover queue `4CC784C0`), not `origGame` (documented invariant: render on the swapchain's creation queue, else cross-queue DEVICE_REMOVED); and the RTVs must be rebuilt against the live swapchain.
- **EXPERIMENTAL zero-blank fix** (user explicitly chose "attempt zero-blank now" over the safe quiesce; **RUNTIME-VALIDATION-PENDING**, carries the documented GTA wedge risk of touching the staged queue pre-enable). All in `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp`, gated strictly on `ShouldReinitOverlayDuringDormantProtectedOfficialFFXStartup()`:
  1. **Stale-RTV rebuild trigger** (just before the reinit block): when the dormant draw arms and the preserve-block left stale RTVs (`overlayInit && rtvDescHeap && cachedSwapChain==null`), `CleanupRTVs(); overlayInit=false; syncInit=false` so the reinit block rebuilds a FRESH overlay against the LIVE swapchain. (The swapchain change fires at progress=1, before the dormant draw arms at progress>=5, so the rebuild must be triggered here, not in the preserve block.)
  2. **Submit queue = live swapchain's creation queue**: the dormant `gameQueue` resolves to `protectedOfficialFFXStartupQueueRef` (the staged takeover queue) instead of the stale `g_SwapchainQueue`/`origGame`.
  3. **Keep drawing through the FG-transition cooldown**: the `STREAMLINE_NO_FG->FSR_FG` 60-frame cooldown's `skipOverlayDraw` gate is bypassed for the dormant case (it blanked the menu ~450 ms and then the first post-cooldown stale submit crashed).
  Retained from #5: the reverted teardown-skip (always drop stale SL RTVs on FG->off), the quiesce-return / settle-defer / reinit-cooldown bypasses, and the device-health guard.
- **Validation:** build green; 341 `DXGISharedTest.*` pass (runtime-only logic — no new unit coverage possible without a live D3D12 swapchain). **Talos runtime re-test REQUIRED**, expect: `Dormant protected-FFX — preserved RTVs are stale ... forcing a fresh overlay rebuild`, `rendering overlay on the LIVE swapchain's creation queue (gameQueue=<stagedTakeover> ...)`, overlay visible the whole menu, NO `DEVICE REMOVED` / `TerminateProcess`. If it still wedges/crashes on the staged queue, the fallback is the safe quiesce (overlay briefly blanks during arming).

### 2026-06-15 - DLSS->FSR menu forever-blank — root cause #4 (the actual trigger): [outer] FG-off tears down overlayInit

- **The `[dormant-draw DENY]` diagnostic nailed it** (session 20260615_220545): overlayInit is `1` for progress 1-4, then flips to **`0`** at progress 6 and stays 0 forever (syncInit stays 1). Every dormant relaxation requires `overlayInit`, so once it's 0 they all deny → ProcessFrame quiesces → the backend never re-inits → forever blank. The teardown is at the exact frame `DX12: [outer] SL FG OFF ... forcing overlay reinit (stale SL backbuffers)` fires (`DX12_OnStreamlineFGStateChanged`, `dx12_hook.cpp:15804`): DLSS turning off in the DLSS->FSR transition tears down `g_State.overlayInit` for "stale SL backbuffers".
- **Why that teardown is wrong here**: in the dormant 2D-menu protected-FFX window the overlay renders on the game's OWN queue (`scQueue==origGame`, `runtimeOwns=0`), NOT the stale SL proxy — so there are no stale SL backbuffers to reinit away. (This is the same `[outer] FG->off` teardown guarded for the no-callback takeover in `ShouldKeepOverlayLiveAcrossDLSSToFSRNoCallbackTakeover`; the protected-FFX-pending dormant case needs the same guard.)
- **Fix #4**: guard the teardown with `keepOverlayLiveForDormantProtectedFFX = ShouldDrawOverlayOnOrigGameDuringDormantProtectedOfficialFFXStartup()` (overlayInit is still true at that point, so the no-arg predicate holds). When true, skip the `overlayInit=false`/`CleanupRTVs` teardown → the overlay stays live and keeps drawing on origGame through the whole menu. The instant the runtime takes over, the predicate is false and the teardown resumes. Combined with fixes #1-#3 (sync bootstrap, zero-ECL bypass, quiesce-return bypass), the overlay should now stay visible in the 2D menu. Diagnostic: `[outer] FG→off — dormant protected-FFX startup is drawing the overlay on origGame ... keeping it live`.
- **Validation**: build green; 1026 native tests + Python self-tests pass. **Runtime re-validation pending** — repro DLSS->FSR in the menu; expect `[dormant-draw DENY]` to STOP after the transition (overlayInit stays 1), the `keeping it live` breadcrumb, overlay SUBMITs, no forever `protected-ffx-startup-quiesce` streak, overlay visible in the menu.
- **Source anchor**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp:15804`.

### 2026-06-15 - DLSS->FSR menu forever-blank — root cause #3 (the real preempt): unconditional quiesce return in ProcessFrame

- **Session 20260615_215017** still forever-blanked. The dormant-draw breadcrumb (ProcessFrameExternal) fired AND `Protected official FFX startup suppressing separate overlay GPU work` fired on the SAME frames, while `[dormant-ffx-draw DIAG]` (render block) + bootstrap + zero-ecl-skip all = 0. Contradiction (both gate the same dormant predicate) pinned the real preempt.
- **Root cause #3 (preempts #1 and #2)**: ProcessFrame's gameQueue-resolution block has `if (protectedOfficialFFXStartupOverlayOnly) { log "suppressing separate overlay GPU work"; return; }` at `dx12_hook.cpp:14138` — an **unconditional return** whenever the BROAD quiesce (`ShouldQuiesceCESideEffectsForProtectedOfficialFFXStartup`) is active. It runs BEFORE the dormant-draw render relaxation, the staged-sync bootstrap (fix #1), and the zero-ECL bypass (fix #2) — so none of those were ever reached; this return blanked the overlay every frame. (Round-2 Case B relaxed the LATER `ShouldSkipSeparateOverlayGpuWorkForCurrentSwapchain` seam, but this earlier return preempts it on the DLSS->FSR path.)
- **Fix #3**: gate that return with `ShouldDrawOverlayOnOrigGameDuringDormantProtectedOfficialFFXStartup(/*inSyncInitBootstrap=*/true)` — when the dormant-draw should run, set `gameQueue = g_SwapchainQueue (== origGame)` and FALL THROUGH to the normal render path instead of returning. Capture / FFX-retry / probe / create-time side effects stay quiesced via the unchanged broad checks elsewhere; the instant the runtime takes over, the predicate is false and the full quiesce return resumes. Combined with #1 (sync-init bootstrap) and #2 (zero-ECL bypass), ProcessFrame now reaches the render path and draws on origGame in the dormant 2D menu. Diagnostic: `Protected official FFX startup DORMANT — rendering overlay on game's own queue instead of quiescing`.
- **Validation**: build green; 1026 native tests + Python self-tests pass. **Runtime re-validation pending** — repro DLSS->FSR in the menu; expect the `... DORMANT — rendering overlay on game's own queue ...` breadcrumb, `[dormant-ffx-draw DIAG]` now firing, overlay SUBMITs, and the overlay staying visible in the menu.
- **Source anchor**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp:14138`.

### 2026-06-15 - DLSS->FSR menu overlay disappears FOREVER — root cause #2: ProcessFrame skipped entirely (zero-ECL)

- **Follow-up to the sync-init chicken-and-egg fix below** — that fix was real but session 20260615_213846 still showed the forever blank because of a SECOND, earlier gate. The `[dormant-ffx-draw DIAG]` (in ProcessFrame's render block) fired 0x while the dormant-draw attribution breadcrumb (in ProcessFrameExternal) fired continuously, and NO logged ProcessFrame skip fired — proving ProcessFrame was never even called.
- **Root cause #2**: `DX12_ProcessFrameExternal` skips calling `ProcessFrame` for "zero-ECL/interpolated" presents (`ShouldSkipProcessFrameForZeroECLPresent`, `dx12_hook.cpp:18866`, `return` before the `ProcessFrame(sc3)` call at `:18904`). During a dormant protected-FFX startup CE passes the game's ECLs through **tracking-only** (not counted for the per-frame ECL counter), so the menu present looks like a zero-ECL/interpolated frame → ProcessFrame is skipped → the dormant-draw overlay never reaches the render path at all. (This sits BEFORE the staged-sync gate, so the chicken-and-egg fix could never run.)
- **Fix #2**: gate the zero-ECL skip with `!ShouldDrawOverlayOnOrigGameDuringDormantProtectedOfficialFFXStartup(/*inSyncInitBootstrap=*/true)` — keep calling ProcessFrame whenever the dormant-draw should run (syncInit-bootstrap variant so it also works before sync is re-initialized). ProcessFrame then bootstraps sync (fix #1) + renders the overlay on origGame via the dormant relaxation. The instant the runtime takes over, the predicate is false and the zero-ECL skip resumes. Together with fix #1 (sync-init chicken-and-egg) this should keep the overlay live in the 2D menu (it already recovered when 3D resumed via the FFX callback).
- **Validation**: build green; 1026 native tests + Python self-tests pass. **Runtime re-validation pending** — repro DLSS->FSR in the menu; expect `[dormant-ffx-draw DIAG]` to now fire (ProcessFrame reached), then the `Bootstrapping overlay sync ...` breadcrumb and overlay SUBMITs, and the overlay staying visible.
- **Source anchor**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp:18866`.

### 2026-06-15 - DLSS->FSR menu overlay disappears FOREVER — FIXED (sync-init chicken-and-egg)

- **Root cause (confirmed, session 20260615_212947)**: a DLSS->FSR menu transition arms AMD's protected official FFX swapchain AND clears `g_State.syncInit` (overlayInit stays true). ProcessFrame then enters the staged sync-init block (`dx12_hook.cpp:15074`, `overlayInit && !syncInit && cooldown<=0`), which gates sync-init on `ShouldSkipSeparateOverlayGpuWorkForCurrentSwapchain`. The only relaxation there is the dormant-protected-FFX draw, but `ShouldAllowNormalOverlayDrawDuringDormantProtectedOfficialFFXStartup` **requires `syncInit==true`** — the very thing this block would create. So it returns at `:15104` ("Keeping staged sync init deferred"), `syncInit` stays false **forever**, the render block (`:16956`) is never reached, and the 2D menu never sends an enabled `ffxConfigure` to lift the quiesce → overlay gone forever. (The Round-2 dormant-draw attribution breadcrumb in ProcessFrameExternal fired because it doesn't require syncInit, masking that ProcessFrame had deadlocked — the new `[dormant-ffx-draw DIAG]` at the render block fired 0× while the breadcrumb fired, which pinned it.)
- **Fix**: `ShouldDrawOverlayOnOrigGameDuringDormantProtectedOfficialFFXStartup(bool inSyncInitBootstrap=false)` — when called from the staged sync-init path it passes `inSyncInitBootstrap=true`, treating `syncInit` as satisfied (we are about to create it). New `ShouldInitOverlaySyncDuringDormantProtectedOfficialFFXStartup()` uses that, and the staged-sync-init gate (`:15077`) no longer defers when it's true → InitOverlaySync + CreateRTVs run on the new AMD swapchain (origGame queue, AMD dormant = the safe Round-2 Case B sub-state), `syncInit` becomes true, and the next frame the dormant-draw renders on origGame. This also rebinds the backend RTVs to the new AMD swapchain (the swapchain changed DLSS-proxy->AMD-FFX). Diagnostic: `Bootstrapping overlay sync during dormant protected official FFX startup ...`.
- **Safety**: strictly the dormant sub-state (protectedPending, runtimeOwns=0, scQueue==origGame, staged AMD queue differs, no direct FFX/callback, sustained origGame progress) — the same gate Round-2 Case B validated for rendering on origGame; sync-init on origGame is part of that. The instant the runtime takes over (enabled ffxConfigure / callback / runtime ownership), the predicate returns false and full quiesce resumes. GTA-unvalidated.
- **Validation**: build green; 1026 native tests + Python self-tests pass. **Runtime re-validation pending** — repro DLSS->FSR in the menu; expect the `Bootstrapping overlay sync during dormant ...` breadcrumb, no forever `protected-ffx-startup-quiesce` streak, and the overlay staying visible.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`ShouldDrawOverlayOnOrigGameDuringDormantProtectedOfficialFFXStartup` `:3050`, `ShouldInitOverlaySyncDuringDormantProtectedOfficialFFXStartup`, staged-sync-init gate `:15077`).

Earlier investigation (now resolved):

- **Driven by Talos session** `installed/captureengine/logs/20260615_165803` (build `0.1.4022`): switching DLSS FG -> FSR FG while staying in the 2D game menu makes the overlay disappear forever. Also confirms the same-queue startup fix worked (startup blank now 5 presents/78ms vs 437ms).
- **Coverage**: `[OVERLAY COVERAGE] uncovered streak STARTED gate=protected-ffx-startup-quiesce present=4155` with **no matching "ended"** = forever blank. Zero `overlay SUBMIT` after the transition.
- **Root-cause chain (partly traced)**: DLSS->FSR in the menu arms AMD's protected official FFX swapchain. The swapchain CHANGES (DLSS proxy `oldSC=...BFCE0` -> AMD FFX `newSC=...887280`); CE preserves the overlay backend on the OLD swapchain (`Preserving overlay backend across protected official FFX startup swapchain change`). The game keeps presenting the NEW AMD swapchain on its OWN queue (`runtimeOwns=0 scQueue==origGame`, staged AMD queue differs) — the dormant-protected-FFX sub-state. The Round-2 Case B dormant-draw breadcrumb DOES fire (`Rendering overlay on origGame during dormant protected official FFX startup`, count=601, directFFX=0) — but that is only the ProcessFrameExternal coverage ATTRIBUTION (`dx12_hook.cpp:18385`). The ACTUAL render in ProcessFrame is silently skipped: both render gates are inside `if (!skipOverlayDraw)` and neither logged a skip, so `skipOverlayDraw` was set true earlier by the SL-teardown routing (DLSS turning off) across the swapchain change. Net: attribution says "drawing" but nothing submits, and the 2D menu never sends an enabled `ffxConfigure`/FFX callback to lift the quiesce -> forever blank. The project mandate lists DLSS FG -> FSR FG as a must-work transition.

One re-run pinpoints the exact silent gate (expected: `skipOverlayDraw=1`).

Deliberately NOT guess-fixed yet — this is the most crash-prone path.

### 2026-06-15 - Talos pure-DLSS startup blank fixed via same-queue topology proof (countdown + warmup)

- **Driven by Talos session** `installed/captureengine/logs/20260615_162947` (build `0.1.4020`): overlay briefly disappears at startup with DLSS FG. `[OVERLAY COVERAGE] uncovered streak ended: missed=29 durationMs=437 gate=postsl-inactive lastGate=postsl-reactivation-warmup` (hadFSR=0, epoch=1). Enabled via **GetState** (`explicit=0`), so the explicit-enable proof can't apply.
- **Root cause**: the pure-DLSS GetState cold start runs the synthetic-startup countdown (`postsl-inactive`/`postsl-startup-countdown`, clamped to 8) + the 15-frame cold-start warmup (`postsl-reactivation-warmup`) — both the documented DLSS-G-init crash protection. All existing bypass proofs were false (`safeBootstrap=0 confirmedResume=0 explicitEnableColdStart=0 confirmedThisEpoch=0`).
- **Key insight — Talos uses a SINGLE queue**: `PostSL locked to queue X (origGame=X scQueue=X cmdQueue=X slWrapper=0)`. DLSS FG presents on the game's OWN queue with NO separate SL/runtime proxy queue. The documented GTA hang family instead "moves to a runtime-owned swapchain" (a SEPARATE queue), and CE's ECL on that separate proxy-init pipeline is what corrupts DLSS-G. With no separate queue, CE's overlay ECL is just another submit on the game's own queue (the no-FG route, what RTSS does) — no separate init pipeline to corrupt.
- **Fix**: `ShouldTreatSameQueuePureDLSSColdStartAsSafe(hadFSR, scQueue==origGame, noSeparateCommandQueue, hasSeparateSLWrapperQueue, deviceRemoved)`, computed every PostSL callback. When true it bypasses BOTH the synthetic-startup countdown (activate from callback #1) AND the cold-start warmup (new leg in `ShouldBypassPostSLReactivationWarmup`) → overlay renders from the first re-entrant present (0-frame startup blank). Re-checked per callback, so a title that later creates a separate runtime queue (GTA) flips it false and the countdown/warmup resume — the separate-queue init-corruption window is never opened. device-removed is caught by the PostSL render's pre-submit GetDeviceRemovedReason bail; a pure GPU hang is caught by the freeze watchdog. Diagnostics: `bypassing pure-DLSS countdown — same-queue topology ...`, `bypassing reactivation warm-up ... sameQueueColdStart=1`. Units: `SameQueuePureDLSSColdStartIsSafeToRenderEarly`, `SameQueuePureDLSSColdStartBypassesReactivationWarmup`.
- **Why this avoids the crash regression**: it excludes the documented GTA hang family by construction (GTA uses a separate runtime queue → proof false) and is re-evaluated per callback (a transient same-queue window before a title creates its proxy is caught the moment the separate queue appears). **GTA-unvalidated** (user tests later); the same-queue gate + device-removed bail + freeze watchdog are the safety layers.
- **Validation**: build green; all native tests + Python self-tests pass. **Runtime re-validation pending** — re-run Talos start with DLSS FG; expect no `gate=postsl-reactivation-warmup` / `postsl-inactive` startup streak, the `same-queue topology` breadcrumbs, and `[OVERLAY HANDOFF]` first present `drawObserved=1`.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (PostSLOverlayRender: same-queue proof compute ~:10244, countdown bypass ~:10305, warmup call ~:10578), `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h`, `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`.

### 2026-06-15 - FFX present-callback toggle WEDGE (AMD ffxQuery hang) root-caused + fixed

- **Driven by synthetic `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` hang dump** `installed/captureengine/logs/20260615_021242` (build `0.1.4018`, manual `.dmp`). The app "semi-freezes" after switching to FSR FG. cdb (`~*k`) shows the present thread spinning in `amd_fidelityfx_framegeneration_dx12` → `RtlQueryPerformanceCounter` (the documented AMD `ffxQuery` wedge), entered via CE's `capture_hook_x64` present path; `ProcessFrame SLOW 999.6ms`.
- **NOT caused by the overlay-blank work**: the last 5 commits don't touch the FFX bridge path (`git log -- hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp`), and the DLSS→FSR keep-alive breadcrumbs fired 0× this session. Pre-existing ("seen before").
- **Root cause**: `fsr_present_callback_toggle_stress` flips FSR between app-callback and null-callback every ~6s. During the app-callback phase CE installs its bridge (`DX12_RenderOverlayViaFFXPresentCallback`) wrapping the app callback. On the toggle to **enabled null-callback**, the `ffxConfigure` else-branch CLEARED the bridge's retained original (`ffx_hook.cpp:432-433`) — but **AMD retains CE's bridge** (it does NOT revert to internal composition) and keeps calling it. CE's bridge then ran with `originalCallback==null`, so `ShouldComposeFFXPresentSourceToOutput` → CE self-composed currentBackBuffer→output via `CopyResource` on AMD's command list (`composing current backbuffer into output because no app/default composition callback is available`, fired only 8× right at the freeze), wedging AMD's presenter. `g_DefaultPresentCallback` (the SDK `ffxFrameInterpolationUiComposition`) was never resolved this build, so there was no clean delegate either.
- **Fix**: `ShouldRetainFFXPresentCallbackBridgeForEnabledNullCallbackToggle(recognizedFGConfigure, enabled, appCallbackProvided, hasExistingBridgeWithOriginal)` + helper `DX12_HasFFXPresentCallbackBridgeWithOriginal()`. On an enabled null-callback configure where a bridge with a non-null original still exists, CE now KEEPS the bridge installed and delegating to that retained app callback (correct composition) instead of clearing it → no self-`CopyResource` → no wedge. Genuine no-original null-callback startup still preserves AMD internal composition (unchanged). Diagnostics: `Retained DX12 overlay present-callback bridge across enabled app->null-callback toggle ...`, plus a WEDGE-PRECURSOR warning at the self-compose path logging raw `currentBackBuffer.state`/`outputSwapChainBuffer.state` (to attribute the FFX-vs-native state encoding if it ever recurs). Unit: `RetainsFFXBridgeAcrossEnabledAppToNullCallbackToggle`.
- **Validation**: build green; all native tests + Python self-tests pass. **Runtime re-validation pending** — re-run FSR with the present-callback toggle stress; expect the `Retained ... app->null-callback toggle` breadcrumb, no `composing current backbuffer ... no app/default composition` self-compose, and no `ProcessFrame SLOW ~1000ms` / ffxQuery hang. GTA-unvalidated.
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/ffx_hook.cpp` (~:432 else-branch retain), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`DX12_HasFFXPresentCallbackBridgeWithOriginal`, wedge-precursor warning), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.h`, `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h`, `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`.

The scratch probe guards the FSR→DLSS first-ECL DEVICE_REMOVED crash family, but in the `fast=1` safe-bootstrap case it's redundant: the render path already has a pre-submit `GetDeviceRemovedReason()` bail + a post-submit device-removed check, and on the SL-owned swapchain queue (the non-origGame, non-crash case the fast proof requires) the real render is itself the health proof. So the probe present only cost the frame.
- **Fix**: `ShouldRenderOverlayDirectlyOnFirstPostFSRDLSSReactivation(fastPostFSRDLSSProbe, postFSRProbeLevel)` (true only at probe level 0 under the fast-bootstrap proof) → the PostSL path sets `g_PostFSRProbeLevel=3` and renders the overlay directly on the first reactivation present. Engage seam drops 1 present → **0**. The slower graduated probe (scratch→copy→render) is retained for the unproven / off-swapchain-queue fragile paths. Diagnostic: `PostSL post-FSR fast bootstrap — rendering overlay directly on first reactivation present ...`.
- **Decision**: user prioritized 100% overlay visibility over the GTA-crash-window margin for now ("don't care about GTA at this point ... care about potential regressions later"). This removes the last scratch-barrier canary on the FSR→DLSS engage. **GTA-UNVALIDATED**; independently revertible (drop the predicate use site).
- **Validation**: build green (`0.1.4011`→bumped); `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` passed all native tests + Python self-tests, incl. new unit `RendersOverlayDirectlyOnFirstPostFSRDLSSReactivationUnderFastBootstrap`. **Runtime re-validation pending** (re-run the synthetic matrix; expect no `postsl-bootstrap-reactivation` streak, `missed=0` on DLSS engages).
- **Source anchors**: `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (probe-skip at the graduated-probe block, ~:11231), `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ShouldRenderOverlayDirectlyOnFirstPostFSRDLSSReactivation`), `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`, `llm-wiki/frame-generation/guardrails.md`.

### 2026-06-15 - D4 Round-4: RTSS-style present-time eager overlay draw across a runtime DLSS-FG toggle-ON (opt-in, default OFF, UNVALIDATED)

- **Driven by Talos session** `installed/captureengine/logs/20260614_030417` (build `0.1.3986`, rounds 1-3 in). The last remaining FG blank: `slDLSSGSetOptions(ON)` at runtime blanks the overlay ~437 ms / 4 presents (`gate=postsl-inactive`→`fg-transition-cooldown`).
- **Root cause (traced)**: with Steam loaded, `DXGIShared::DetourPresent` routes the toggle-on presents through the Steam-safe bypass trampoline and `return presentBypass(...)` BEFORE CE's overlay draw (`HandleDX12ProcessFrame`, `dxgi_shared.cpp:2628`) — so those presents carry NO overlay. PostSL activates+confirms the instant DLSS-G generates (`explicitEnableColdStart=1`, warmup already bypassed); the blank is purely the bypassed, overlay-less frozen frame. (The `Suppressing pre-SL draw during SL FG startup` log never fires in that window → the bypass is taken, the overlay draw is not reached.)
- **Why RTSS can do it**: RTSS draws its overlay present-time on the backbuffer every present (incl. the frozen one) on the game's own queue, and does not skip its draw for a Steam-safe bypass. That is the SAME plain present-time ECL CE already submits on the no-FG normal route — NOT the PostSL re-entrant ECL submitted into DLSS-G's pipeline that the cold-start warmup protects against.

(2) `ShouldEagerlyDrawPreSLOverlayDuringDLSSToggleOn` un-suppresses the pre-SL draw at `dx12_hook.cpp:16825` so the draw lands. Gate (tight, so steady-state FG + rounds-1..3 untouched): kill-switch ON, D3D12, DLSS FG turning on, PostSL not yet confirmed, pure DLSS (`!g_HadFSRFGPhase`), `!g_FGRuntimeOwnsSwapchain`, overlay/sync live, and **same queue** (`g_SwapchainQueue != null && == g_OriginalGameQueue` → no separate SL proxy queue → the ECL lands on the game's own queue, no cross-queue `DEVICE_HUNG`).
- **Safety**: present-time ECL on the game's own present queue (RTSS parity), not the PostSL init ECL; the Steam-safe bypass STILL performs the real present (the eager draw is a separate GPU submit, not a present, so it does not re-enter Steam's stale Present hook); same-queue gate avoids the cross-queue hang; default OFF → all prior wins unaffected unless explicitly enabled.
- **Diagnostics**: `Eager present-time overlay draw before Streamline-startup bypass (RTSS-style, site=...)`, `Keeping pre-SL overlay live during DLSS toggle-on (RTSS-style, scQueue==origGame=...)`; coverage gate `dlss-toggle-on-eager-presl-draw`.

### 2026-06-16 - Constant "audio slightly late" A/V offset FIXED (delay video content) — WGC + inject, all codecs

- **FIX (implemented, committed f4651e1):** loopback audio is captured ~46 ms later than the video content clock (WASAPI `GetStreamLatency()==0` for loopback). Advancing audio is impossible (live-edge deficit → silence padding), so CE delays VIDEO CONTENT by the configured loopback latency, leaving audio samples and the CFR PTS grid byte-exact (track length / start-end / zero-drift preserved; codec-agnostic).
  - **WGC**: `ce::capture_policy::GetWgcSelectionTargetQpc` extra-delay term IS the selection lag (replaces the dormant 1-tick delay); `ShouldApplyWgcSelectionDelay(..., contentDelayActive=true)` applies it continuously for live recording so the bounded "too new for slot" path self-builds/holds the delay buffer. The live-window clamp only engages under shortfall, so the healthy path is unaffected.
  - **Inject** (`bufferedInjectFrames`, pops oldest above a reserve): retain `ceil(L / frameInterval)` extra frames in `minBufferedInjectFrames`, widen `maxBufferedInjectFrames` and `maxInjectLiveAgeQpc` so the oldest popped frame is ~L old. Frame-quantized (e.g. 6 frames=50 ms at 120 fps vs 46 ms target → ~4 ms over); WGC is QPC-precise.
  - **Config**: per-source `capture_latency_ms` (falls back to global `[General] audio_capture_latency_ms`); video delay = max enabled-source latency. `audio_capture_latency_ms=0` is a no-op (default for unconfigured users → zero behavior change; the fast quick gate passes unchanged). This machine's config set to 46.
  - **Validation (120 fps reliable oracle, lead 0):** WGC+inject × ALAC/AAC/Opus offsets collapse from ~46 ms to ~0 (within the ±half-frame measurement floor), cadence clean (no judder), all tracks `diff=+0`, `Final packet maxPacketDelta=0`, zero-drift. Inter-track spread stays in the pre-existing 0–6 ms band (baseline inject is also 3–6 ms; the project's green matrix accepts ≤5.99 ms); occasional strict `missing` is an analyzer startup-boundary sensitivity, not a recording defect. Fast quick gate (default latency 0) passed all 6 scenarios → no regression. 1019 native tests pass.
  - **Logging**: `[EncoderThread] A/V content delay armed: ... method=wgc-selection-bias|inject-buffer-reserve` and `[A/V START] Audio source reset ... captureLatencyMs=` per source.
  - **Per-device latency model (commit 111b3aa, OBS-equivalent):** A/V sync is auto-corrected from OS-reported `GetStreamLatency` (CE already subtracts it via `ApplyCaptureLatencyCompensation`) for devices that report it - no value needed. `capture_latency_ms` is the manual override (OBS "Audio Sync Offset" equivalent) for endpoints Windows under-reports - the dev's 192 kHz HDMI/AVR returns 0 from BOTH a loopback and a render client (confirmed), so its ~46 ms must be set per-device on the source section (not a global magic number). The A/V offset is buffer-of-source INDEPENDENT (varying the stimulus app buffer 5->60 ms left it ~52 ms) = a device capture-path property, but it is the cross-clock WASAPI-loopback-vs-WGC-composition difference that no API exposes and CE can't self-correlate at runtime, so for under-reporting devices a measured value is required (same as OBS).
  - **Per-source equalization (commit 76e3889):** a single video delay aligns only the slowest (max-latency) source; faster sources (e.g. a ~0 ms mic mixed with 46 ms loopback) would land early. Each source is delayed by `(max_latency - its capture_latency_ms)` of leading silence so all sources sit at the common max latency and align with the delayed video + each other on mixed tracks. Implemented in the audio-loop startup placement (`mediaengine.cpp`): the delay is added to `packetStartSamples` (the gap path inserts the silence) and the per-source startup-rebase cap is raised by the delay so it is not trimmed. Slowest source(s) -> delay 0 -> all-equal-latency case byte-identical (no regression). Validated 120 fps: system=46/app=20 -> app delayed exactly 26 ms (inter-track spread 25 ms), delay survives the rebase. Harness `--app-latency-ms` sets a per-source latency for this test. CAVEAT: a mixed system-loopback + same-app process-loopback on ONE track double-captures the game (comb-filter "weird" audio) - a routing issue, not the sync fix.

# llm-wiki Log — Archive 2026-W26a

### 2026-06-27 - FIX: WGC abnormal old-frame/ghost judder class -> copy-pool lease/generation guard + split surface budget

- **User bug/evidence:** fresh real-game WGC session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260627_052028` (DX12 borderless VRR, 4K/120, GPU often 100%, fast p1) had abnormal visual judder/ghost-image artifacts around recording-sec 20-40 even though the game Present hook stayed smooth (max present gap about 10.842 ms) and audio/mux/encoder evidence was clean. The old log had no pool lifetime evidence, so analyzer now reports this shape as WGC/source/visual-lifetime suspicious instead of encoder or mux pressure.
- **Root cause class fixed:** the WGC retained copy pool previously had no explicit ownership token for queued, selected, buffered, last-frame, or currently encoding textures. A larger WGC playout reservoir made it possible to keep more old pool textures live, so reusing a slot without a lifetime guard risked showing stale/overwritten content that looks harsher than ordinary CFR repeats.
- **Fix:** every retained WGC texture now carries `poolSlot`, `poolGeneration`, and a move-only `WgcPoolSlotLease` from `WGCCapturedFrame` through direct callbacks, `QueuedFrame`, startup candidates, `g_FrameQueue`, `bufferedWgcFrames`, and `g_LastFrame`. `CopyFrameToPool` copies only into unleased slots. If all slots are leased, CE logs/drops the incoming WGC frame as `wgc_pool_saturated_safe_drop` instead of overwriting queued/selected/encoding content. Leases release on queue/cache drops or after `MediaEngine_ProcessFrameD3D11` returns; if media-engine WGC input ownership becomes asynchronous, this must be extended to a GPU completion fence. Pool generations make stale releases harmless after a pool recreate.
- **Budget/sync fix:** WGC source frame-pool buffers and CE copy-pool slots are now budgeted separately under `wgc_smoothness_buffer_vram_budget_mb` (default 2048 MB). The budget reserves source buffers first (default 8, min 3), then sync-delay frames and 4 safety slots, then extra smoothness frames. At 4K FP16/120 with the default budget the expected shape is about 8 WGC source buffers plus 24 copy-pool slots, leaving about 16 extra smoothness frames after sync/safety. The smoothness extra delay is selected at startup only and applied to the shared audio/video anchor; later WGC deficits become CFR repeats with clear source/budget attribution, not live audio retiming.
- **Diagnostics/analyzer:** `[WGC Perf]` and smoothness summaries now log source frame-pool buffers, copy-pool slots, budget surfaces, sync/extra/safety frames, leased max/free min, saturated safe drops, overwrite-prevention skips, lease mismatches, and cap-limited state. `tools/analyze_capture_av.py` has `--recording-window START:END` alignment and verdicts for `wgc_pool_slot_lifetime_fault`, `wgc_pool_saturated_safe_drop`, and `wgc_pool_evidence_missing`; false encoder/mux attribution is suppressed unless overload flags, mux backpressure, or wait times prove it.
- **Validation:** `python tools\analyze_capture_av.py --self-test` passed. The required build passed (`python build.py --skip-updates`, build 0.1.4309). The required test-only run passed (`python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates`, 1157 native tests plus Python self-tests; displayed metadata 0.1.4310). `tools\analyze_capture_av.py --session-dir installed\captureengine\logs\20260627_052028 --recording-window 20:40` classifies the old log as missing WGC pool evidence with clean audio/mux/encoder pressure rather than proving encoder overload.
- **Remaining validation risk:** `tools\run_av_sync_matrix.py --fast-zero-drift --keep-going` at `installed/captureengine/avsync_runs/20260627_092127` is not fully green: the late-app WGC/inject scenarios passed, but quick representatives still fail strict analyzer thresholds (WGC quick audio offset/slope, one inject marker-repeat case, one inject audio-slope case) without CE encoder/mux/audio/visual faults. `tools\run_av_sync_matrix.py --sync-smoothness-gate --sync-smoothness-latency-mode modeled --keep-going` at `installed/captureengine/avsync_runs/20260627_092650` is also not green and includes inject failures, so it is not solely a WGC pool regression. Fresh 4K120 VRR/GPU-bound WGC capture and matching inject validation remain the required runtime proof that the old-frame/ghost judder is gone and inject remains low-latency/smooth.
- **Source anchors:** `common/wgc_pool_lease.h`, `common/capture_pipeline_policy.h` (`WgcSmoothnessSurfaceBudget` / arming helpers), `captureengine/wgc_capture.cpp` (`CopyFrameToPool`, pool budget/recreate/logging), `captureengine/media_main.cpp` (lease propagation/release, startup smoothness anchor, WGC perf/smoothness logs), `common/frame_queue.h`, `tools/analyze_capture_av.py`, `tests/test_capture_pipeline_policy.cpp`, `tests/test_frame_queue.cpp`, `tests/test_config.cpp`.

### 2026-06-26 - FIX (iter 5): iter-3 "keep delay through live-recovery" was INCOMPLETE → the selection TARGET still collapsed the realized delay; + make the realized-delay metric content-honest

- **The reported symptom:** occasional abnormal "ghost image" judder in the recorded video — *not* normal CFR repeat/drop judder, but the picture momentarily showing **much older content then snapping** — a "singular event ca. 28s" in real session `logs/20260626_050554` (build 0.1.4283 = iter-4, **Fortnite** 4K120 WGC, 10-bit, av1_nvenc fast p1, avDelay=31.5ms, GPU~100%, DX12 borderless VRR, output to a `Z:` network drive).   - `[WGC CFR SMOOTHNESS DELAY] realizedDelayMin=7us .. realizedDelayMax=108818us` (target 31.5ms), `delayResidualEarlyMax=77301us`. Per-window `[Cadence Health]` shows the realized delay rubber-banding then, from ~31s, **collapsing to ~0 and LATCHING there for the entire rest of the recording** (`resLate≈31500us`, i.e. the full 31.5ms delay lost, every window 31s→stop) the moment `Recover=1` (WGC live-recovery) engaged. A perpetually-below-output VRR source (`SrcFps≈105-115` < 120) keeps live-recovery latched forever, so the collapse never self-heals. Collapsed delay = video running ~31.5ms ahead of the loopback audio it is meant to align with; the collapse *transition* is the visible content fast-forward the user sees.
  - Separately, the encoder/cadence thread woke **27-88ms late** repeatedly across sec 22-39 (`SelMax` column; GPU contention + `Z:` mux I/O), which inflated `realizedDelayMax` to 108ms even though the content placed in each PTS slot was grid-correct (the metric, not the file, was wrong here).
- **Two root causes:**
  - **(A, the real defect) The selection TARGET dropped the content delay during latched live-recovery.** iter-3 (commit `2f2fb98`) added `ShouldLiveRecoverySuppressWgcSelectionDelay` and used it for the per-tick *flag* `wgcSelectionDelayAppliedThisTick` — but `computeWgcSelectionTargetForTick` (`media_main.cpp`) STILL gated the delay with a raw `!wgcLiveRecoveryModeActive`. So the flag said "delay applied" while the target silently went near-live. iter-3's "keep delay through live-recovery" therefore never actually held on the target path; iter-4 inherited the latent collapse, which this Fortnite session exposed.
  - **(B, telemetry honesty) Realized delay was measured against wall-clock `selectionNowQpc`**, folding encoder-thread late-wake jitter into a *content*-delay metric → false `wgc_active_delay_realized_delay_unstable`.
- **Fix (iter 5):**
  - **(A)** New single-source-of-truth `GetWgcActiveDelaySelectionTargetQpc` (`capture_pipeline_policy.h`) composes `recordingOutputLive && applyLiveDelay && !ShouldLiveRecoverySuppressWgcSelectionDelay(liveRecovery, uniformCadence)` and feeds `GetWgcSelectionTargetQpc`. `computeWgcSelectionTargetForTick` now routes through it, so the flag and the target can never diverge again. On the uniform-cadence path the content delay is HELD through live-recovery (even holds at the floor absorb the below-target source; live-recovery still drives max-rate capture refill); the legacy reservoir path still yields to live-recovery.
  - **(B)** `recordWgcDelayRealization` then measured `realizedDelay = scheduledSampleQpc − frame.timestamp` (the slot's GRID time, == the audio anchor reference), not `selectionNowQpc − frame.timestamp`. Encoder-thread wake jitter stayed visible separately as `SchedSel`/`SelMax`; the realized-delay counter became content-honest. Superseded detail: the 2026-07-23 overload fix now uses the immutable `scheduledOutputQpc` packet-grid coordinate for selection and delay realization so a recovery rebase cannot move this reference.
- **Inject:** re-confirmed **structurally immune** to both — it selects nearest-to-delayed-grid via `SelectFrameClosestToGridIf` + `ComputeDelayedContentGridStartQpc` (grid-anchored, no `wgcLiveRecoveryModeActive`, no wall-clock reference), so its content delay can neither collapse during recovery nor absorb thread jitter into the metric. Left unchanged.
- **Audio/sync safety:** the fix changes only WHICH WGC frame fills a video slot; audio PTS/anchoring is untouched. It *improves* A/V content sync (delay stays the intended 31.5ms instead of collapsing to 0) and smoothness (no fast-forward-to-live on recovery entry, no freeze on exit). No audio trim/pitch/length change.
- **Validation:** build clean (0.1.4287); **1148/1148** unit tests + Python self-tests. New tests: `WgcActiveDelaySelectionTargetHoldsDelayThroughLiveRecoveryOnUniformPath` (the exact composition that was buggy — uniform+liveRecovery must still subtract the delay; would have returned the collapsed `scheduled` before), `WgcNearestPlayoutPinsDelayThroughLatchedLiveRecovery` (end-to-end sim: latched live-recovery on the uniform path keeps realized delay pinned, legacy path collapses — proving the sim discriminates). `RunNearestPlayout` now computes its target through `GetWgcActiveDelaySelectionTargetQpc` so any future delay-composition regression collapses the simulated delay. **Still needs a real-game WGC soak** (fresh Fortnite/Strange Brigade capture under 100% GPU VRR): watch `[WGC CFR SMOOTHNESS DELAY] realizedDelayMin/Max` stay tight ~25-40ms (not 7us..108ms), `resLate` NOT pinned at ~31500us once `Recover=1`, and analyzer not emitting `wgc_active_delay_realized_delay_unstable`.

### 2026-06-25 - FIX (iter 4): the whole inject-parity Bresenham pacer was the wrong model → replace with fixed-latency nearest-target jitter-buffer playout

- **The iter-3 setpoint depth-cap (build 0.1.4277) did NOT fix it.** Real session `logs/20260625_180512` (Strange Brigade 4K WGC, 10-bit, avDelay=29.8ms, fast p1, GPU~100%, VRR borderless, av1_nvenc) still had harsh abnormal stutter in recording sec 20-50 with the **game render provably smooth there**. - **Two layered root causes:**
  - **(Layer 1, inherent) WGC frame *delivery* is bursty/gappy under GPU-bound VRR borderless.** DWM hands frames to the capture frame pool irregularly: `[WGC Perf]` shows delivery dipping to `MinIn250=24..110` with `JitMax=174ms`/`CbGap=203ms` even though the game presents at 242fps with 10.5ms max interval.   - **(Layer 2, the bug) the oldest-first Bresenham pacer AMPLIFIED that delivery jitter into harsh stutter.** The count-based depth cap **bulk-dropped** a whole delivered burst in one tick (`depthBefore=10/12/16` trimmed to 6) and then the buffer ran dry across the following lull, so a ~115fps source produced `tickDup≈20` **AND** `dropObs≈14` in the **same second** (drop+dup churn — far harsher than uniform CFR judder).   - **Why iter-1/2/3 all failed:** they all kept the count/oldest model. A count-based reservoir + oldest-first emit fundamentally cannot reconstruct smooth CFR from bursty delivery — the realized delay = oldest-frame age, which swings with batch composition.
- **Fix (iter 4):** replace the Bresenham count/oldest pacer with a **fixed-latency jitter-buffer playout** (`DecideWgcNearestPlayout` + `ShouldDropWgcFrontForNearerPlayout`, `capture_pipeline_policy.h`). Each output tick selects the buffered frame **nearest the grid playout target** `computeDelayedWgcSelectionTargetQpc` (= `gridTick − contentDelay`, **unclamped** so low-source/recovery doesn't collapse the delay): drop frames the audio timeline already passed (older than target when a closer not-too-new successor exists; `playoutLeadToleranceQpc = GetWgcActiveDelayResidualToleranceQpc`), emit the slot frame once aged in, else hold (even source-limited repeat) keeping newer frames as reserve. This **consumes at the source rate by construction** (no over-drain, no clustered "too-new" holds like the old grid-rate timestamp reservoir; no bulk-dump churn), **pins the realized delay near `contentDelay`** regardless of delivery burstiness, and after a true gap resumes by **dropping the audio-passed backlog** (not replaying it → no rubber-band; the in-gap freeze stays clean). Jitter within the ~30ms budget is fully absorbed; jitter beyond it still forces even holds (unavoidable at a 30ms budget; deeper adaptive A/V buffer is a future option the user deferred).
- **Logging:** retired `[WGC CFR] active-delay reservoir over target` → `[WGC CFR] active-delay playout catch-up: dropped N audio-passed frame(s) after a WGC delivery gap ... NOT a game render hitch` (throttled, ≥3 drops). `delayPaceCapTrim` now counts age-based playout catch-up drops. Retired the now-unused `wgcDelayCreditAccumulator`.
- **Inject:** confirmed **structurally immune** and left as-is — it already selects nearest-to-delayed-grid (`SelectFrameClosestToGridIf` + `ComputeDelayedContentGridStartQpc`, `idealQpc = nowQpc − contentDelay`) over an abundant per-present (non-batched) stream, and decimates one-at-a-time (no bulk dump). Regression-locked by a new test proving its realized delay stays pinned even with an abundant buffer (where oldest-first would give ~2x delay).
- **Validation:** build clean (0.1.4283); 1146/1146 unit tests + Python self-tests. New tests: `WgcNearestPlayoutDropsAlreadyPastFramesForCloserSlot`, `WgcNearestPlayoutEmitHoldDecision`, `WgcNearestPlayoutAbsorbsDeliveryJitterWithinBudget` (smooth source + within-budget bursty delivery → 0 holds, pinned delay), `WgcNearestPlayoutEvenHoldsAndStableDelayUnderGapBeyondBudget` (gap>budget → bounded delay, no drop+dup-same-tick, holds bounded by gap), `FrameTimingUtilsTest.InjectDelayedGridSelectionPinsRealizedDelayUnderAbundantBuffer`. **Needs real-game soak (WGC + inject)** — runtime smoothness is the required proof: watch `realizedDelayMin/Max` tight (~25-40ms not 0..243ms), per-second `tickDup` without simultaneous `dropObs`, no `wgc_active_delay_realized_delay_unstable`. `DecideWgcActiveDelayPace`/`GetWgcActiveDelayPaceMaxDepthFrames` kept as tested building blocks but retired from production.
- **Source anchors:** `common/capture_pipeline_policy.h` (`DecideWgcNearestPlayout`, `ShouldDropWgcFrontForNearerPlayout`, `WgcNearestPlayoutDecision`), `captureengine/media_main.cpp` (`useInjectParityDelayPacing` block ≈4762, `playoutTargetQpc`/`playoutLeadToleranceQpc`), `tests/test_capture_pipeline_policy.cpp`, `tests/test_frame_timing_utils.cpp`.

### 2026-06-25 - FIX (iter 3): inject-parity pacer still rubber-banded the realized delay 0..248ms → setpoint depth-cap + keep delay during live-recovery

- **Two coupled root causes in the iter-2 design:**
  - **(A) No restoring force toward the floor.** `DecideWgcActiveDelayPace` was a pure source-rate matcher. A VRR/GPU-bound source whose present rate *transiently rises above* the 120 output (`SrcFps` spikes to 144) piles surplus frames into the buffer that the rate-matcher never drains back, so the realized delay drifts up without bound until a starvation empties it. (The inject path bounds this via `maxBufferedInjectFrames` + `ShouldTrimStaleInjectLiveFrame` age-trim; the WGC uniform path had no equivalent.)
  - **(B) Live-recovery latches and disables the delay.** `ShouldExitWgcLiveRecoveryMode` requires the source at/above the output target (`!ShouldEnterWgcLowSourceMode`) to exit. A GPU-bound VRR source runs below 120 most of the time, so once live-recovery latches (entered on any momentary below-target shortfall, even with a full 23-frame buffer per `IsWgcTrueSourceStarvedForRecovery`) it stays latched — here **48s** (`delaySourceRecoveryTicks=5927`) — during which `wgcSelectionDelayAppliedThisTick=false` turns the content delay OFF → realized delay collapses to ~0 (the 0ms half of the swing).
- **Fix (iter 3):**
  - **(A)** `DecideWgcActiveDelayPace` gains a `maxDepthFrames` setpoint cap (`GetWgcActiveDelayPaceMaxDepthFrames` = reservoir target + `kWgcActiveDelayPaceMaxExcessFrames`(1) = floor+2). It trims the oldest surplus down to the cap every tick (even, because surplus arrives gradually), pinning the realized delay at ~floor regardless of VRR spikes. Trims counted as `WgcActiveDelayPaceResult::capDrops`.
  - **(B)** `ShouldLiveRecoverySuppressWgcSelectionDelay(liveRecovery, uniformCadenceActiveDelay)`: on the uniform-cadence path the content delay is maintained continuously through live-recovery — below-target source is the STEADY STATE absorbed by even holds at the floor (which also rebuilds the reserve after a true gap). Live-recovery still drives capture-rate refill; the legacy reservoir path keeps yielding to it.
  - **Logging:** throttled `[WGC CFR] active-delay reservoir over target: trimmed N surplus frame(s) ... ~realizedDelay= target=` warning + `delayPaceCapTrim=` in `[WGC CFR CADENCE EVENT]` and `[WGC CFR SMOOTHNESS REPEAT]`.
  - **Analyzer:** `wgc_realized_delay_spread_us` no longer treats `realizedDelayMin=0` as "no data" (a full collapse is the worst case) — `wgc_active_delay_realized_delay_unstable` now correctly fires on this session (it silently missed the 248ms spread before).
- **Inject:** verified it already bounds the realized delay (age-trim ≈ avDelay+2 frames) and doesn't use WGC live-recovery, so it has neither bug — left unchanged.
- **Validation:** build clean (0.1.4278); 1141/1141 unit tests (3 new: depth-cap bound, VRR-above-output simulation stays bounded, live-recovery delay-maintenance) + analyzer self-tests incl. new min=0 collapse fixture; analyzer re-run on `20260625_135221` now flags `wgc_active_delay_realized_delay_unstable`. **Needs real-game soak (WGC + inject)** — runtime smoothness/realized-delay tightness cannot be proven here.
- **Source anchors:** `common/capture_pipeline_policy.h` (`DecideWgcActiveDelayPace` 4-arg, `GetWgcActiveDelayPaceMaxDepthFrames`, `kWgcActiveDelayPaceMaxExcessFrames`, `ShouldLiveRecoverySuppressWgcSelectionDelay`), `captureengine/media_main.cpp` (uniform pacer cap-trim block, `liveRecoverySuppressesDelay`), `tools/analyze_capture_av.py` (`wgc_realized_delay_spread_us`), `tests/test_capture_pipeline_policy.cpp`.

### 2026-06-25 - FIX (iter 2): WGC active-delay judder is buffer over-drain under a VRR sub-output source → inject-parity input-rate pacing

- **The iter-1 fix (reserve-defense disable) did NOT fix it.** New run `logs/20260625_131333` (build 0.1.4273) with `uniformCadence=120`/window still stuttered in recording sec 20-70, with the GAME render smooth. Decisive evidence: the hook CSV `source_current_fps` shows the game runs **VRR at 105-159fps, dipping below the 120 output** for sustained stretches (30-40s=118fps, 60-70s=110fps), and `[WGC Perf]` `In` MATCHES it (~110 when game~110). So WGC delivers at the game's variable present rate (the user's VRR hypothesis was right) — NOT a compositor throttle, and `DropPool/DropFull=0` confirms we lose nothing we received.
- **Real root cause:** with the source present rate below the 120 output, the timestamp-target path advances toward `grid − L` every output tick (120/s) while the source feeds ~110/s, so it **over-drains the buffer**: `oldest=~25ms` never reaches the 31ms slot → repeated "too-new-for-slot" holds (`buffered=4 lead=6-9ms syncSourceLimited=1`) that **cluster** = abnormal stutter. Inject never hits this because it hooks Present (sees the full game rate) AND paces unique advances at the source rate (Bresenham credit), so its unavoidable repeats are uniform.
- **Fix:** give the WGC active-delay path the inject pacing model. New policy `DecideWgcActiveDelayPace` + `GetWgcActiveDelayPaceFloorFrames` (`capture_pipeline_policy.h`): keep a frame-count delay floor (~4), advance unique frames at `smoothedInputPerTick` rate via a dedicated `wgcDelayCreditAccumulator`, decimate evenly when source>output, hold evenly when source<output, never drain below the floor. Emitted frame is always ~floor source-frames old → realized delay stable (~28-36ms for a 31ms target across 110-144fps) so **A/V sync is preserved** (contradicts my earlier "let delay float" framing — input-rate pacing keeps the buffer fed, so the delay does NOT need to collapse). Integrated at the WGC CFR selection call in `media_main.cpp` behind the same `wgc_active_delay_uniform_cadence` flag; the timestamp-target path is kept for `false` (A/B). Realized-delay telemetry reused via `recordWgcDelayRealization(residual,residual)` with `residual = requestedDelay − (now − emittedTs)`.
- **Validation:** build clean (0.1.4275); 1138/1138 unit tests incl. 2 new pacer tests (`WgcActiveDelayPaceFloorMatchesReservoirDelayFrames`, `WgcActiveDelayPaceAdvancesAtSourceRateAndHoldsAtFloor`); analyzer self-test PASS. **Needs real-game soak** (this is the 2nd attempt; I cannot validate runtime smoothness here). Watch `[AVSyncApply] wgc_cadence_policy`, the per-window `uniformCadence=`, realized-delay min/max spread in `[WGC CFR SMOOTHNESS DELAY]` (should now be tight, not 22.9-44.4ms), and confirm even repeats vs clusters. **Inject still needs its own measured check** under the same VRR-sub-output condition.
- **Source anchors:** `common/capture_pipeline_policy.h` (`DecideWgcActiveDelayPace`, `GetWgcActiveDelayPaceFloorFrames`, `WgcActiveDelayPaceResult`), `captureengine/media_main.cpp` (`wgcDelayCreditAccumulator`, `useInjectParityDelayPacing` block), `tests/test_capture_pipeline_policy.cpp`.

### 2026-06-25 - INVESTIGATION: the ~16ms 60fps A/V offset is frame quantization, NOT a latency bug (no fix)

- **Question:** a real-world 3h capture (`logs/20260625_040155`) plus a 60fps quick matrix run showed ~16-21ms `av_mean_offset_ms` (audio-late), borderline over the ±15ms gate. Is the render-latency auto-detect under-compensating → could it make audio feel delayed?
- **Decisive same-method matrix comparison (`avsync_runs/20260625_074235`, `--fast-zero-drift --fps 120`):** compensated offset SCALES with frame period → it's video-frame quantization, not a fixed latency error. **120fps: ~2-10ms, centered on zero (both signs)** (−6.5/−4.9, +1.8/+2.0, −3.5/−9.3). **60fps: ~12-21ms, consistently positive** (+11.6/+14.4, +12.4/+12.6, +18.2/+21.1) ≈ one 60fps frame (16.7ms). Raw UNcompensated offset (preflight shots) was ~40-47ms, so the auto-detect correctly removes ~40ms; the residual is the frame-rate floor.
- **Code confirms intent:** `audio_latency_probe.cpp` deliberately APPLIES the priming-inclusive `startAnchor` (render Start → loopback). The present-anchored value (~16ms, `presentAnchor`) is DIAGNOSTIC ONLY — the comment notes "an earlier revision applied this; it under-measures the render-domain delay by the priming term." So the under-comp path was already considered and rejected; there is no probe bug.
- **Conclusion:** NO fix. The recorded A/V is within one frame at 60fps and ~0 at 120fps — below perceptual thresholds (ITU-R BT.1359 audio-late ~+45ms). For tightest sync, record at 120fps. Do not chase the 60fps ~16ms; it is the quantization floor.
- **Bonus regression check:** the same matrix run PASSED across WGC/inject, 60/120, ALAC/AAC, and late-app scenarios — independent confirmation that the recent defer-suppress (`54b9be2`) + catastrophic-resync (`4223cd9`) fixes did NOT regress A/V sync or WGC smoothness.
- **On the other two candidate improvements:** (A) during-stall receive-side ring bounding is low-benefit (the stall-period audio is unsavable either way; it only shrinks the recovery seam from ~30s drop to ~2s) and — more importantly — must NOT ship without a deterministic stall test to validate recovery; it stays gated behind that test (task chip `task_7a0264ad`). The decision helpers (`ShouldSuppressBufferDeferForCatchup`, `ComputeCatastrophicBacklogResyncTrim`) are already unit-covered; the end-to-end stall reproduction is the remaining gap and is correctly scoped as its own focused session.

### 2026-06-25 - FIX: multi-app track freeze (the actual root cause of app audio going permanently silent)

- **Real repro on the build with the prior resync fix** (`logs/20260625_022047`, build 0.1.4262, ~49 min): app audio STILL died after ~13 min. The catastrophic resync fired 11 times but only at 30s ring saturation (~once per 14 min); Track 2 was `fullSilence` ~25 of ~49 min. So the resync was a backstop, not the cure.
- **Actual root cause (a multi-source interaction the resync could not reach):** when one app (Fortnite) falls behind after a read-stall, its track passes >2s behind the live target and enters the CFR large-backlog warp branch (`mediaengine.cpp` ~2371), which clamps the pull chunk to `MAX_SILENCE_CHUNK` (0.5s). The buffer-wait defer (`ShouldDeferCfrAudioPullForSourceBuffer`, ~2397) then requires EVERY co-mixed source to have ≥0.5s buffered — but a second app (Brave) sitting at the live edge has only ~100ms and can NEVER accrue 0.5s (consumed as fast as produced), so the whole track defers every iteration via `break`+`continue`. The track cursor FREEZES (proof in `[AppDiag] place`: backlog growing at real-time `102.29→104.29s in 2s`, `encodedCursor` frozen, `writeMinusEncoded` climbing linearly to 27M samples, `ringAvail=1440000/1440000` pinned). The stalled app's ring saturates to 30s, and the catastrophic resync — which lives in the consume loop AFTER the defer `continue` — never runs until saturation briefly resumes consumption.
- **Fix (`ShouldSuppressBufferDeferForCatchup`, pure + unit-tested; wired at the defer call):** a track more than 2s behind the live target MUST make forward progress on every pull and never defer waiting for an under-buffered live source. With the defer suppressed, the per-source consume + the existing catastrophic resync run again, so the stalled app resyncs to the live edge and the track catches up (silence for the stall gap, then live audio) instead of freezing into permanent silence. Only triggers when already multiple seconds behind, so healthy pulls keep the defer/buffer-wait protection untouched. `initialTrackCatchup` (legitimate startup) is never treated as a stall.
- **Why the prior resync alone failed:** it was placed in the consume loop, but the defer froze the track BEFORE the consume loop ran — so the resync only executed at the rare moments consumption resumed (ring already saturated). The freeze fix is what lets the resync (and normal draining) actually run during catch-up.
- **Tests:** 2 new `AudioSyncUtilsTest` (suppress only when catastrophically behind; never during legitimate startup catch-up). Full suite 1133/1133; build clean x64+x86. (User asked to skip the A/V matrix this round; the change is inert in clean scenarios — it only arms >2s behind, which a clean 12s run never reaches.)
- **Source anchors:** `mediaengine/audio_sync_utils.h` (`ShouldSuppressBufferDeferForCatchup`), `mediaengine/mediaengine.cpp` (`trackLargeBacklogDrain` + defer guard ~2397), `tests/test_audio_sync_utils.cpp`. Builds on the resync from `4223cd9` (still needed: it drops the stale backlog so catch-up stays live instead of fast-forwarding it).
