### 2026-06-25 - HARDENING: sample_rate parsing can no longer crash encoder init (unguarded std::stoi)

- **Found in source-audit:** `config.sampleRate` is read as a raw INI string (to support the `default` sentinel) and was parsed at three encoder-init sites with bare `std::stoi` (`mediaengine.cpp ParseAudioSampleRate`, `audio_encoder.cpp Init`, `video_encoder.cpp AddAudioStream`). A hand-edited typo (`sample_rate=48kHz`, a negative value, or an out-of-range number) made `std::stoi` throw `std::invalid_argument`/`std::out_of_range` — an unhandled C++ exception that terminated the capture process with no diagnostic. `common/utils/scanner.cpp` already had a `try/catch`, so it was not affected.
- **Fix (defense-in-depth):** (1) new `ce::audio::ParseSampleRateOr` (`mediaengine/audio_time_utils.h`, unit-tested) — strict (whole string must be a positive integer), never throws, falls back to a caller-provided default; replaces all three `std::stoi` sites. (2) boundary validation `NormalizeSampleRate` in `config.cpp LoadConfig` (applied to `[Audio]` and `[AppAudio.N]` raw reads; other sections inherit the already-normalized value) logs `[Config] Invalid sample_rate "..." in [section]; falling back to default (48000)` once and stores `default`. Strict semantics chosen over the old lenient `std::stoi` (which would have parsed `48kHz`→48 Hz): a malformed value now yields a clear warning + safe 48000, never a bogus 48 Hz stream.
- **Tests:** 6 new `AudioTimeUtilsTest.ParseSampleRate*` cases (default/empty, valid rates, malformed-without-throw, strict partial-number rejection). Full suite **1127/1127 PASS**; `python build.py --skip-updates` clean (x64+x86, 0 compiler warnings).
- **Source-audit notes (no code change):** the full `-Wall -Wextra` build is already 0-warning. clang-tidy (`bugprone-*`/`performance-*`) and clang-format remain intentionally non-fatal in `build.py`; clang-format has large pre-existing drift (`clang-format 21.1.8` reports ~921 violations in `video_encoder.cpp` alone) and `video_encoder.cpp`'s committed blob has MIXED CRLF/LF line endings — so mass-reformatting or flipping those gates to fatal is a separate, deliberately-deferred decision (would produce huge unrelated diffs). When editing `video_encoder.cpp`, use byte-level edits that preserve its mixed endings (the Edit tool / `clang-format -i` normalize the whole file and create thousands of spurious line-ending diffs).
- **Source anchors:** `mediaengine/audio_time_utils.h` (`ParseSampleRateOr`), `common/config.cpp` (`NormalizeSampleRate` + two call sites), `mediaengine/mediaengine.cpp`, `mediaengine/audio_encoder.cpp`, `mediaengine/video_encoder.cpp`, `tests/test_audio_time_utils.cpp`.

### 2026-06-24 - FIX: app-audio read-stall recovery (bound backlog, resync to live edge)

- **Root cause (now fully pinned, see the CORRECTION entry below for the trace):** a sustained READ-stall — the consume/encode side frozen by an alt-tab, a DPC latency spike, or encoder overload while live process-loopback capture keeps writing — grows a CFR app source's per-source ring backlog. WGC-CFR deliberately never trims app-audio backlog (`kWgcPreferVideoRepeatsOverAudioCuts=true`, `tier2Applied=0`, overflow-trim gated `!isCfrRecording`), so it grows unbounded until the 30s ring saturates; then `WriteRetainNew` discards the samples the reader still needs and the source can NEVER recover → the app track goes permanently silent while system loopback (a different ring) stays full. The capture stream itself is healthy throughout. The user's directive: alt-tab/DPC/overload are unavoidable, so the pipeline must survive them gracefully.
- **Fix (`mediaengine/audio_sync_utils.h` `ComputeCatastrophicBacklogResyncTrim`, wired in `mediaengine.cpp` `[PullAudio]` overflow block ~2826):** bound the app-source backlog. Below a catastrophic threshold the no-trim CFR policy is preserved untouched (healthy steady state is ~100-200ms backlog). Above `SAMPLE_RATE*2` (2s — far beyond any legitimate jitter, so only a real stall hits it) resync to the live edge: `Skip` the stale backlog down to a small live cushion (`max(target, 100ms)`), keep the newest audio, fade the seam (`CaptureDropFadeAnchor`). One unavoidable discontinuity after a multi-second stall instead of a dead track. Logged as `[PullAudio] App source catastrophic backlog resync ...` with a dedicated `catastrophicResyncSamples`/`Events` counter. Scoped to CFR app-audio (`src.sourceType==AppAudio`), so system/mic and non-CFR paths are unchanged.
- **Why this is allowed under the "no audio cuts in CFR" rule:** that rule targets ROUTINE sub-second drift, where cutting audio is an audible artifact for no benefit. A multi-second backlog from a real stall is a different regime: the only alternatives are unbounded latency or permanent silence. A controlled, faded resync is the lesser evil and the only way to stay live. It is a distinct CATASTROPHIC-recovery event, not routine trimming, and never fires in clean scenarios.
- **Tests/validation:** 4 new `AudioSyncUtilsTest` cases (gating to CFR app-audio, healthy backlog untouched, drop-to-cushion, target-cushion floor). Full suite 1123/1123; build clean x64+x86. Fast A/V matrix (`run_av_sync_matrix.py --fast-zero-drift`) confirmed the resync stays INERT on healthy runs (0 resync events, backlog peaked ~0.88s << 2s, all strict audio-event gates pass, video perfect). The lone matrix FAIL was `av_mean_offset_ms` 15.5/17.6ms vs the ±15ms gate with a flat slope — this machine's uncompensated render→loopback latency in the quick profile, unrelated to this change (the resync code never executed).
- **Still open / pending:** the alt-tab/DPC recovery itself is bounded by construction but not yet confirmed on a real repro (the user could not deterministically reproduce; a 68s clip with one brief silence stayed healthy). The diagnostics from the prior commit plus the new resync log will confirm on the next real occurrence: a stall now produces `App source catastrophic backlog resync` and the track stays live, instead of `headroom exhausted` + permanent `fullSilence`. Consider adding a deterministic consumer/encode-stall scenario to `run_av_sync_matrix.py` so this becomes a standing regression gate.
- **Source anchors:** `mediaengine/audio_sync_utils.h`, `mediaengine/mediaengine.cpp` (resync branch + `catastrophicResync*` fields + `[AppDiag]` diagnostics), `tests/test_audio_sync_utils.cpp`.

### 2026-06-24 - CORRECTION: app-audio "stops after game silent once" is a DOWNSTREAM CFR bug, not stream death (diagnostics added)

- **Reopened:** the `ab37c31` stream-recovery fix below did NOT resolve the user's app-audio death. New repro `installed/captureengine/logs/fortniteappaudiodeath` (build 0.1.4247) proves the prior diagnosis was the WRONG LAYER.
- **What the logs actually show:** Fortnite process-loopback CAPTURE is healthy the entire 1150s (continuous `Source Sync (22020)`, drift 0.00ms; no error, no stall → recovery correctly never fires). System loopback (track 3) = full real audio for all 1150s, so Fortnite was audible the whole time. But the app track (track 2) = `realMixed`≈150s then `fullSilence`≈1000s. The source ring buffer fills to its 30s capacity and retain-trims ~48M samples (`CFR audio headroom exhausted ... retainedTrim=48051412`) while the reader logs 161 `Source underrun` + 407 `Large single padding event`. So writes outpace reads and the source stops being consumed into the mix after the game's first silence.
- **Conclusion:** this is a downstream CFR ring placement/consumption bug (`mediaengine.cpp` `[PullAudio]` ring-drain ~2867 + qpc packet placement ~4170-4390), triggered when the process-loopback timeline and the CFR read/encoded cursor desynchronize after the first audio gap and never reconverge. It is NOT capture/stream death. The `ab37c31` recovery + watchdog remain valid hardening for genuine device-invalidation/stream-death (a different real failure mode) and were not reverted.
- **Diagnostics added (log-only, no behavior change):** `[AppAudioCapture] Content (PID)` per-window `peakAbs` + silent-flag/zero-frame ratios (is captured content real or silent?); `[AppDiag] place` per app-source placed-pos vs write cursor vs encoded/read cursor (`writeMinusEncoded`) + ring fill + gap/overlap; `[AppDiag] consume` realCopied vs postResampleBuf vs ringAvail + `syncReady`, flagging `STARVED_WITH_RING_DATA`. One short "go silent once" repro will pin hypothesis A (stuck-silent content), B (placement races ahead → ring fills, reader underruns), or C (drain stalls despite ring data). Full suite 1119/1119; build clean.
- **Source anchors:** `mediaengine/app_audio_capture.cpp` (Content telemetry), `mediaengine/mediaengine.cpp` (`[AppDiag] place`/`consume`, `lastAppPlaceDiagTick`/`lastAppConsumeDiagTick`).

### 2026-06-24 - HARDENING: WASAPI capture stream re-activation (device-invalidation) + process-loopback silent-stall watchdog

- **Trigger:** user report (no log available) — after prolonged capture (~60–70 min) OR after temporarily suspending an app's audio (alt-tabbing out of a game that auto-mutes), **application** audio stops recording while **system** audio continues (codec AAC, but codec is incidental — capture death is upstream of the encoder).
- **Root-cause gap (effectively a bug):** neither `AppAudioCapture::CaptureLoop` nor `AudioCapture::CaptureLoop` had ANY recovery path. On `AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED` (device/driver/power flap over a long session) `GetNextPacketSize`/`GetBuffer` fail forever; on a process-loopback silent stall (app tore down + recreated its audio session on alt-tab mute, mixer didn't reattach) the stream yields zero packets with no error. In both cases `isCapturing` stayed `true`, so the name-based monitor's `!isCapturing` restart branch never fired and PID-based capture (no monitor thread) never restarted → the app track silence-padded to the end of the recording. System audio survived because its endpoint was not the one that died (and endpoint loopback has no silent-stall mode). Two secondary defects: a latent `static int errCount` in the app loop that swallowed all error logging after the first session (**why the user had no log**), and a silent `if (FAILED(hr)) break;` GetBuffer path; plus a single transient `IsProcessRunning` miss could permanently kill a live PID-based capture.
- **Is the API prone to this? Yes.** Per-process loopback (Win10 20348+) is a thin layer over AudioSes `CLoopbackMixer`, bound to the target process's session lifecycle; it is documented/observed to die on endpoint changes and to not reattach after the target recreates its session. Correct posture: assume the stream can die and recover from it.
- **Fix:** new pure, unit-tested `mediaengine/audio_recovery_policy.h` (`IsFatalWasapiStreamError` — narrow device-invalidation family; `NextRecoveryBackoffMs`/`RecoveryBackoffElapsed` — exp backoff base 1 s → cap 30 s; `ShouldReactivateForSilentStall` — arms only after ≥1 packet + ≥10 s silence). Both capture loops re-activate the client IN PLACE on a fatal error (capture thread/queue/downstream track stay alive; healthy `GetBuffer` resets backoff). App audio also runs the silent-stall watchdog (endpoint loopback gets fatal-error recovery only). App re-activation = `ReactivateClientForPID`→`AbandonClientInterfaces` (abandons, never releases, the process-loopback COM — respects the AudioSes teardown crash boundary; leaked wrappers tiny + backoff-bounded). System re-activation = `ReactivateClient` re-resolves the endpoint via extracted `ResolveCaptureDevice`/`ActivateAndStartClientOnDevice` and safely `Release()`s (only `Stop()` trips the AudioSes crash for endpoint loopback). App process-exit now needs 3 consecutive `IsProcessRunning` misses. Per-session throttled error logging replaces the `static` counter; loud re-activation + end-of-session recovery-summary logs added.
- **Not a timing bandaid:** recovery is event-driven (responds to the real `AUDCLNT_E_DEVICE_INVALIDATED` signal / zero-packet stall), not a sleep/poll race fix. No game-specific logic; generic for all apps/devices.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_audio_recovery_policy.cpp` (9 cases: fatal classification, backoff progression/gate incl. backwards clock, silent-stall arming/window/backoff/backwards-clock). Full suite **1119/1119 PASS** (build 0.1.4244); `python build.py --skip-updates` clean (x64+x86).
- **PENDING real-hardware validation:** the 60–70 min device-invalidation and alt-tab-mute stall could not be reproduced locally; the recovery + watchdog need a real soak/alt-tab session to confirm app audio resumes (watch for `FATAL stream error ... attempting re-activation`, `Process-loopback silent stall ...`, `Re-activation succeeded`, and the `Stream recovery summary`).
- **Source anchors:** `mediaengine/audio_recovery_policy.h` (new), `mediaengine/app_audio_capture.{h,cpp}` (`ActivateClientForPID`/`ReactivateClientForPID`/`AbandonClientInterfaces`/CaptureLoop recovery + watchdog + process-exit streak), `mediaengine/audio_capture.{h,cpp}` (`ResolveCaptureDevice`/`ActivateAndStartClientOnDevice`/`ReactivateClient`/CaptureLoop recovery + `deviceId_`), `tests/test_audio_recovery_policy.cpp`, `llm-wiki/multi-audio-capture.md`.

### 2026-06-24 - GTA no-callback FSR FG overlay invisible (1x1 override) + overlay DPI 100% instead of Windows scale

- **Context:** after the composite landed + the cache-null fix (`4becc4b`), GTA no longer crashes and the composite runs every present (session `20260624_004915`: GTA frames 1..1500+, fences completing, no crash; test app works too). But the GTA overlay was still INVISIBLE, and separately the overlay rendered at 100% instead of the Windows 150% scale.
- **GTA invisibility root cause (confirmed from the log):** the composite correctly draws CE's overlay onto CE's substitute texture every present, but `Substituted CE full-size UI texture` / `RegisterUiResource forwarded` log only TWICE (`cfgFrame` stops at 4). GTA registers a **1x1 placeholder UI resource EVERY frame**; once the one-shot `ffxConfigure` VEH disarms, GTA's per-frame `RegisterUiResource(1x1)` calls reach AMD directly and REVERT AMD's registered UI resource to the empty 1x1, so AMD composites nothing. (The test app works because it keeps registering its OWN real texture — which CE drew on — every frame.) This is the previously-documented per-frame-override open risk, now proven for GTA.
- **GTA fix (re-assert the substitute each present):** CE stores the substituted `RegisterUiResource` desc + the FFX swapchain context + the REAL `ffxConfigure` when it substitutes (`StoreSubstituteUiReRegistration`, ffx_hook.cpp), then `FFXHook_ReRegisterSubstituteUiResource()` re-calls the real `ffxConfigure(RegisterUiResource, CE-substitute)` once per present from `DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoCachedFFXUiResource` — AFTER the composite draws the overlay onto the substitute, BEFORE the real Present that triggers AMD's UI composition. It is the SAME lightweight config call GTA makes per frame (NOT GPU work on AMD's present queue/backbuffer → stays within the crash boundary). Gated to the degenerate-substitute path (test app's game-tex path never stores → no-op) and to active no-callback FSR FG. `FFXHook_ClearSubstituteUiReRegistration()` (called from `ReleaseFFXUiCompositeInfra`) stops it when the substitute is released (dangling-desc safety). **UNVALIDATED / residual risk:** re-asserting at present is temporally serialized with AMD's composition, but GTA registers on its render thread, so a tiny concurrency window with AMD's `ffxConfigure` remains — worst case a 1-frame flicker (AMD's per-frame config must tolerate repeated calls). Watch a GTA run for the `re-registered CE substitute UI resource` heartbeat + overlay visibility + no new wedge/dump.
- **DPI fix (generic):** all overlay backends derive `dpiScale` from `GetWindowsDpiScale(this->hwnd)`. The main `g_OverlayAdapter` gets `SetHwnd(gameWindow)` → 1.50, but the descriptor-free `g_D3D11On12Adapter` (DX12DescFreeBackend) never gets `SetHwnd`, so it fell back to `GetForegroundWindow()` — a 96-DPI launcher/splash during GTA startup → **1.00**. Fix: `OverlayAdapter::SetHwnd` now records the valid game window in a file-static `g_SharedOverlayDpiHwnd`, and `GetWindowsDpiScale` prefers it over `GetForegroundWindow()` when the passed hwnd is invalid. Generic — fixes every adapter that inits without its own hwnd. (`hook/common/overlay_adapter.{h,cpp}`.)
- **Tests:** new source-guard `NoCallbackSubstituteUiResourceIsReRegisteredEachPresent` (re-register wired into the composite wrapper + cleared on release; store only on the substitute path; re-register forwards to the REAL ffxConfigure). Full suite PASS; x64/x86 hook DLL + test app build clean.
- **Source anchors:** `hook/apis/ffx_hook.cpp` (`StoreSubstituteUiReRegistration`, `FFXHook_ReRegisterSubstituteUiResource`, `FFXHook_ClearSubstituteUiReRegistration`, substitution-site store), `hook/apis/ffx_hook.h`, `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoCachedFFXUiResource` re-register, `ReleaseFFXUiCompositeInfra` clear), `hook/common/overlay_adapter.{h,cpp}` (DPI reference hwnd), `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`.

### 2026-06-23 - GTA no-callback FSR FG: replace the crashing unfenced game-ECL bundle with the FENCED CE-owned-queue composite

- **Why:** GTA V Enhanced under native FSR FG crashed (`installed/captureengine/logs/20260623_060436`): `0xC0000005 READ from 0x0` inside `nvwgf2umx.dll` (NVIDIA UMD) on the faulting stack `nvwgf2umx!... → D3D12Core!CCommandQueue::ExecuteCommandListsImpl → capture_hook_x64!... (CE's ECL detour forwarding [gameCLs, overlayCL]) → sl_interposer → GTA5_Enhanced`. `hook_debug.log` proved the CE substitute texture worked (`Created CE substitute UI texture 3840x2160`, overlay drawn frames 1→18) then crashed ~18 frames in, ~0.2 s after the FFX takeover (mid-startup churn: EOS swapchain create + Streamline quiesce + FFX takeover). Device constant `...3956D20` the whole session — NOT a device mismatch.
- **Root cause:** the game-ECL bundle (`RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL` + `TryAppendNoCallbackBundleOverlay`, appended CE's overlay CL to the game's own `ExecuteCommandLists`, NumLists+1) reused a 3-slot allocator rotation with **NO GPU fence** — by design it "rode the game's fence", but the game's fence does NOT gate CE's allocator reuse. During GTA's FSR-takeover churn the GPU fell **>3 frames behind**, so CE reset an allocator whose appended command list was **still executing** → corrupted command list → NVIDIA driver null-deref inside `ExecuteCommandLists`. The simpler test app stayed within 3 frames so never hit it. The bundle's "append to the game's ECL, no separate submit" design fundamentally **cannot fence its own allocators** (no submission to signal a fence on).
- **Fix:** drive the overlay through the already-existing-but-dead `DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoFFXUiResource` instead of the bundle. It builds a **CE-owned DIRECT queue** `g_FFXUiCompositeQueue` (AMD/NVIDIA/Streamline do NOT track it) + fence + 3 allocators, draws the overlay onto the cached/substituted UI texture, **submits on the CE queue, signals the fence, and CPU-waits for completion before returning** (incl. a per-slot allocator fence wait before reuse). New exported `DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoCachedFFXUiResource()` (loads `g_CachedFFXUiTexture/State/Flags` under `g_FFXUiCompositeMutex` so a concurrent substitute-resize can't free the texture mid-composite) is called from `DetourPresent`'s no-callback `kSkipBundleCovers` arm, BEFORE the real Present forward. Added to the composite: the **transparent-clear** for CE's substitute target (plumbed `g_BundleTargetNeedsTransparentClear`) + the **degenerate-target guard** (skip a 1×1 cached target — blank-but-safe). The CPU-wait makes CE's write GPU-complete before AMD composites the registered UI texture post-interpolation. Cost: one CE submit + <1 ms CPU-wait per present.
- **Why AMD/NVIDIA-safe where the bundle wasn't:** overlay GPU work runs on **CE's own fenced queue** (never the game's ECL with unsynchronized allocators, never AMD's runtime present queue, never the backbuffer), is **properly fenced** (no in-flight allocator reuse), and the CPU-wait orders CE's write before the real Present. **Invariant:** under active no-callback FSR FG interpolation, CE performs overlay GPU work ONLY on `g_FFXUiCompositeQueue`.
- **Retired (no dead code):** `TryAppendNoCallbackBundleOverlay`, `RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL`, `EnsureFFXUiCompositeBundleResources`, `LogBundleOverlaySkip`, `DX12_ResetNoCallbackBundleFrame`, `DX12_IsFFXUiBundleOverlayActivelyFiring`, `DX12_ShouldCompositeOverlayOntoFFXUiResource` (dead `false` gate), and the `g_BundleOverlay*` state. The no-callback ECL fast-path now just forwards non-origGame ECLs (still skips CE's per-ECL overhead for AMD pacing). `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` is UNCHANGED; the present site now passes `bundleOverlayActivelyFiring=false` — the *correct* value in every case the route consults it (suspend/non-runtime → backbuffer; active interp is decided before firing is read). Passing true would self-sustain the composite across a suspension (AMD stops compositing there) and blank the overlay — so this also protects the validated test-app suspend.
- **Kept intact (validated working):** `DX12_PrepareFFXUiOverlayTarget` / substitution / `ChooseFFXUiOverlayTarget` / `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` / the crash-boundary guard-rail / suspend (`DX12_IsNativeFSRFGSuspendedDisablePending`) + FSR→off (`DX12_IsLiveSwapchainQueueOriginalGameQueue`, `ShouldEndRuntimeOwnedNativeFGTeardownOnGameSwapchainCreation`) fixes. Only the *drive mechanism* (bundle → composite) changed.
- **Diagnostics:** composite heartbeat now logs `frame/fenceVal/fenceCompleted/waitTimedOut/clear` (proves the fence completed before Present); degenerate-skip logged; `Substituted CE full-size UI texture` / `FFX UI-composite target … changed=` / `no-callback FSR FG window STARTED/ENDED` retained; the freeze timeline ring buffer (`DX12_LogFFXUiCompositeFreezeDiagnostics`) unchanged.
- **Tests:** replaced the two bundle source-guards with `NoCallbackPresentDrivesFencedCompositeNotBundle` (dxgi_shared drives `DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoCachedFFXUiResource` from the kSkipBundleCovers arm; bundle drive + dead gate absent from dx12_hook; wrapper forwards to the composite) and `FFXUiCompositeClearsSubstituteTargetTransparent` (composite reads `needsTransparentClear` + `ClearRenderTargetView(rtv` + degenerate guard). Removed `FFXUiBundlePerFrameFlagLogic`. Route/substitution/teardown policy tests unchanged + green. `test_stubs.cpp`: added `DX12_CompositeOverlayOntoCachedFFXUiResource`, removed `DX12_ResetNoCallbackBundleFrame`/`DX12_IsFFXUiBundleOverlayActivelyFiring`. Unit suite PASS; x64/x86 hook DLL + test app build clean, no warnings.
- **Verification pending — primary acceptance is a real GTA V Enhanced + FSR FG run (user):** no `nvwgf2umx`/`amd_fidelityfx` crash, no new `.dmp`; `hook_debug.log` shows `Substituted CE full-size UI texture` + the composite heartbeat with `waitTimedOut=0` + `fenceCompleted` advancing; overlay visible + stable during FSR FG and across off↔FSR↔suspend. Compare to crash baseline `20260623_060436`. Also re-run injected `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` (+ `--fsr-degenerate-ui`): overlay visible across off↔FSR↔suspend, no crash/blank.
- **Open risks:** the composite was previously DEAD code — watch device/queue selection at takeover, the CPU-wait perturbing AMD pacing over a long run (watch `ffxQuery` stalls), and the cross-queue write/read of the substitute texture. No-callback SUSPEND in GTA remains a known residual (CE may be blind to the per-frame `ffxConfigure(disable)` because the one-shot VEH is permanently disarmed) — separate from this crash fix.

### 2026-06-23 - No-callback FSR FG SUSPEND blank: crash boundary is ACTIVE INTERPOLATION, not mere runtime-ownership

- **Why:** with FSR→on/off fixed, the overlay sometimes disappeared when SUSPENDING FSR FG (FG paused, not full off; `installed/captureengine/logs/20260623_054929`). The session also ran the present-callback toggle stress (amd-internal ↔ app-callback every ~6s). During a no-callback suspension the log shows hundreds of `present routing configured (enabled=0 ... internalNoCallback=1 retainedNoCallbackSuspension=1 runtime=Off)` — the no-callback latch is RETAINED (suspension), so DetourPresent stays in the no-callback branch.
- **Root cause:** my crash-boundary change skipped the backbuffer submit for ANY runtime-owned no-callback FSR FG. But the `ffxQuery` wedge is the **interpolation pacing** path — it only applies while AMD is ACTIVELY INTERPOLATING. During a no-callback SUSPENSION (`ffxConfigure frameGenerationEnabled=0`, AMD keeps the swapchain but does not interpolate) separate overlay GPU work on the backbuffer is SAFE (the pre-existing documented suspension behavior, guardrails.md). By skipping the backbuffer there too, the overlay had only the bundle route, and when the bundle had a coverage gap during the suspension → blank.
- **Fix:** the crash-boundary skip now applies only when AMD is **actively interpolating** = runtime-owned AND NOT disabled/suspended AND the live present is on AMD's FG queue (not origGame). The reliable, non-heuristic suspend signal is `g_ExplicitNativeFSROffPendingRuntimeOwnedTeardown` (set by the disable configure, cleared by the next enable — does NOT flicker under active interpolation, unlike the runtime-mode heuristic). New `DX12_IsNativeFSRFGSuspendedDisablePending()`; `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute(runtimeOwns, liveQueueIsOrigGame, fsrFGDisabledSuspendPending, cached, firing)` returns `kSkipBundleCovers` for active interpolation; during a suspension it skips only if the bundle is actually covering, else draws on the (now-safe) backbuffer. The guard-rail refuses the backbuffer only for `amdActivelyInterpolatingOnFGQueue`. Active GTA FSR FG is unaffected (enabled + interpolating → unchanged skip → bundle).
- **Tests:** `NoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRouteNeverSubmitsBackbufferWhenRuntimeOwnsSwapchain` extended with the suspension legs (suspended+bundle-gap → backbuffer; suspended+bundle-firing → skip; active → always skip). `test_stubs.cpp` stubs `DX12_IsNativeFSRFGSuspendedDisablePending`. 1110 PASS; x64/x86 + test-app builds clean.
- **Verification pending:** re-run inject test app, suspend/resume FSR FG repeatedly — overlay stays visible (no blank). Re-confirm active FSR + FSR→off still good.
- **Source anchors:** `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`DX12_IsNativeFSRFGSuspendedDisablePending`), `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` active-interpolation gate), `hook/common/dxgi_shared.cpp` (`DetourPresent` route + guard-rail), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.h`, `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`, `tests/test_stubs.cpp`.

### 2026-06-23 - No-callback FSR FG FSR→off blank: the REAL fix — end the teardown on a game-created swapchain while no-callback is active

- **Why:** the prior origGame-based stale-latch route-leg did NOT fix the FSR→off blank (`installed/captureengine/logs/20260623_053805`). The hook log (lines 2334–2348) showed the OFF native swapchain (`...F382E1F0` on queue `...D4AC0C0`) was created by the GAME (`callerFFX=0 caller=...dx12_fg_switch_test.exe`) but CE marked it **`fgOwned=1`** — because the test app recreates its device/queue for FSR, so the live queue (`...D4AC0C0`) is a FRESH queue, NOT origGame (`...F753250`, the retired pre-FSR queue). So both the queue-based ownership AND the origGame route-leg are wrong; the bundle kept appending on the OFF native queue (`...D4AC0C0`) onto a stale UI texture AMD no longer composites → invisible.
- **Root cause:** CE preserves runtime-owned FSR ownership until a "stronger off signal"; under the no-callback route ALL off-signals are missed (ffxDestroyContext bypassed by raw export pointers; the one-shot ffxConfigure VEH permanently disarmed) AND the game recreates on a fresh queue (so the origGame-return teardown never fires) → `g_NativeFSRInternalNoCallbackComposition` + `g_FGRuntimeOwnsSwapchain` latch forever. The reliable signal CE DOES have: the swapchain CREATOR (`callerFFX`). FSR-on swapchains are FFX-created (`callerFFX=1`); the FSR→off native swapchain is game-created (`callerFFX=0`). The present-callback toggle only RECONFIGURES (does not recreate the swapchain — `dx12_fg_switch_fsr.inl:173`), so an active FSR session produces NO game-created swapchain → no false positive.
- **Fix:** `ShouldEndRuntimeOwnedNativeFGTeardownOnGameSwapchainCreation` gains a `nativeFSRInternalNoCallbackCompositionActive` trigger — a game-created swapchain while the no-callback composition is active is itself sufficient proof of OFF (no explicit-off/destroy pending needed). When it fires, the existing block clears `g_FGRuntimeOwnsSwapchain`, `ForceClear`s the no-callback latch (+ re-arms the VEH), and re-baselines origGame to the new native queue — so DetourPresent resumes the normal ProcessFrame backbuffer route and the overlay reappears. The 2026-06-23 origGame-based route-leg (`DX12_IsLiveSwapchainQueueOriginalGameQueue`) is RETAINED as a defensive net (covers a disable-without-recreate stuck latch) but is no longer the primary FSR→off mechanism.
- **Tests:** `GameSwapchainCreationEndsRuntimeOwnedNativeFSRTeardown` extended with the no-callback-active leg (game-created + no explicit signal + no-callback active -> end teardown). 1110 PASS; x64/x86 + test-app builds clean.
- **Verification pending:** re-run the inject test app off↔FSR — overlay visible + continuous in BOTH directions; a `no-callback FSR FG window ENDED` edge + `Game-created swapchain ... ending runtime-owned native-FG teardown` should appear at FSR→off. Re-confirm GTA crash boundary (active FSR keeps the FFX-created swapchain → `gameCreatedSwapchain=false` → no premature teardown).
- **Source anchors:** `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ShouldEndRuntimeOwnedNativeFGTeardownOnGameSwapchainCreation` + no-callback trigger), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp:~7624` (call site passes `g_NativeFSRInternalNoCallbackComposition`), `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`.

### 2026-06-23 - No-callback FSR FG: stale latch on FSR→off blanked the overlay (crash-boundary removed the masking fallback)

- **Why:** FSR FG overlay now works (visible + glyphs), but switching back to all-off blanked the overlay (`installed/captureengine/logs/20260622_180830`). The test app ran fine at 144fps in OFF for ~6s (its own `dx12_fg_switch_test.log` proves it). The hook log's final segment is lost on process exit (it routes through the IPC SHM ring buffer the logger service doesn't fully drain on shutdown), so the off-transition never appears in `hook_debug.log`; diagnosed from the test-app log + code.
- **Root cause:** on FSR→off CE PRESERVES runtime-owned FSR ownership "until a stronger off signal arrives" (`dx12_hook.cpp:~7715`), but in the test app's path every off-signal is missed: `ffxDestroyContext` can be bypassed (raw export pointer), the one-shot `ffxConfigure` VEH is permanently disarmed, and the native-swapchain-return-to-origGame is explicitly preserved. So `g_NativeFSRInternalNoCallbackComposition` AND `g_FGRuntimeOwnsSwapchain` stay latched. The crash-boundary change (no backbuffer submit under runtime-owned no-callback FSR FG) then keeps the overlay on the bundle-only route — but AMD's FfxFrameInterpolationSwapchain is GONE (native swapchain), so AMD no longer composites the UI texture → invisible. The old `kMinimalBackbuffer` fallback used to mask the stale latch by drawing on the backbuffer.
- **Fix (stale-latch recovery, AMD-safe):** the reliable real-time signal is the live present queue — during ACTIVE no-callback FSR FG the game presents on AMD's SEPARATE FG queue (`g_SwapchainQueue != origGame`); once FSR is off and the game recreates a native swapchain it presents on its OWN queue (`g_SwapchainQueue == origGame`). New `DX12_IsLiveSwapchainQueueOriginalGameQueue()`; `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute(runtimeOwns, liveSwapchainQueueIsOriginalGameQueue, cached, firing)` returns `kMinimalBackbuffer` whenever the live queue is origGame — even if the runtime-owned latch is still set — because AMD's FG queue is by definition != origGame, so the backbuffer submit is SAFE (NOT the crash boundary). The DetourPresent guard-rail now refuses the backbuffer submit ONLY when `runtimeOwns && live queue != origGame` (AMD genuinely owns a separate FG queue). Active FSR FG is unaffected (`g_SwapchainQueue != origGame` there → unchanged skip → bundle). Independently revertible.
- **Tests:** `NoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRouteNeverSubmitsBackbufferWhenRuntimeOwnsSwapchain` extended — runtime-owned on AMD's FG queue (liveQueue!=origGame) always skips (crash boundary); runtime-owned with liveQueue==origGame always draws via backbuffer (stale-latch recovery), all bundle states. `test_stubs.cpp` stubs `DX12_IsLiveSwapchainQueueOriginalGameQueue`. 1110 PASS; x64/x86 + test-app builds clean.
- **Verification pending:** re-run the inject test app off↔FSR — overlay visible + continuous in BOTH directions (no blank switching back to all-off). Re-confirm GTA's crash boundary is intact (active FSR keeps `g_SwapchainQueue != origGame`).
- **Source anchors:** `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`DX12_IsLiveSwapchainQueueOriginalGameQueue`), `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` stale-latch leg), `hook/common/dxgi_shared.cpp` (`DetourPresent` route + refined guard-rail), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.h`, `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`, `tests/test_stubs.cpp`.

### 2026-06-23 - Pseudo-overlay mode-2 record-start visibility leak + pump-stall diagnostics (Finding B groundwork)

- **Context:** review of the controller-side pseudo-overlay + WGC capture for game-window-freeze and wasted-perf causes. Two code-proven issues found and fixed/instrumented; two larger items deliberately deferred.
- **Fix 1 (mode-2 visibility leak):** `SetRecordingState(true)` did NOT clear `warnActive_`/`warnVisible_` — they were only cleared by the next 500 ms timer tick. So starting a recording while the "NOT RECORDING" warning was in its visible phase (≈2/3 duty cycle, and it is visible by definition right before you record) left the layered topmost warning window up (and re-rendered "NOT RECORDING") for up to ~500 ms into the recording — violating the mode-2 "inactive while recording" contract (overload + screenshot notifications are the only sanctioned exceptions). Fixed by clearing the warn flags synchronously in `SetRecordingState(true)` AND routing the top-level visibility decision through a new pure helper `ce::pseudo_overlay::ShouldPseudoOverlayBeVisible` (`common/pseudo_overlay_visibility.h`) that gates the NOT-RECORDING term on `!isRecording` (single source of truth). Defense-in-depth: the warning-window `showW` term in `UpdateOverlay` is also gated on `!isRecording`.
- **Fix 2 (pump-stall diagnostics for Finding B):** the topmost layered overlay windows are owned by the controller's single main thread, which performs multi-second NON-pumping blocking waits (`EnsureLimiterProcessReady(10000)` on record-start [main.cpp ~679]; `SyncLoggerAndSensorProcesses` 5s+5s + `SyncLimiterProcess` 10s on config-reload [main.cpp ~1341]; `ShutdownIpcChildProcess`/process-sync). While blocked, the topmost windows stop pumping — a non-responsive topmost window can wedge a game foreground/MPO fullscreen transition and present as a frozen game window (matches the reported "with and without WGC" freeze; also explains why mode-2 recording *feels* safe — no topmost window alive then). Added: `[PseudoOverlay] Message-pump stall: Nms between timer ticks` (gap ≥ 1500 ms = 3× interval, in `OnTimerTick`) + `[Controller] Main-thread blocked Nms in <label>` (RAII `MainThreadBlockTimer` around the record-start limiter wait and the config-reload service sync). Correlating the two pinpoints which blocking section starved the pump.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_pseudo_overlay_visibility.cpp` (13 cases: mode-2 stale-warn inactive, overload/screenshot exceptions still show, overload suppressed when disabled, indicator/ghost/blink behavior preserved). Full suite **1110 PASS**; `python build.py --skip-updates` + `--run-tests` clean.
- **Deferred (NOT a fix yet):** (a) **Finding B root-cause fix** — move the overlay windows to a dedicated never-blocking UI thread (or convert the controller waits to pumped waits). Intentionally gated behind the new diagnostics: needs a real-hardware trace correlating a freeze with a pump stall before a threading refactor lands (can't reproduce the MPO freeze in-repo; refactor risks racy/fragile behavior). (b) **Superseded on 2026-07-01:** the WGC dirty-region cursor-skip path was later activated in `ReportOnly` mode, then removed after `20260701_092742` showed it was not safe for DirectFlip/VRR.
- **Source anchors:** `common/pseudo_overlay_visibility.h` (new helper), `captureengine/pseudo_overlay.cpp` (`SetRecordingState`, `ShouldOverlayBeVisible` delegation, `OnTimerTick` pump-stall, `UpdateOverlay` `showW` gate), `captureengine/pseudo_overlay.h` (`lastTimerTickMs_`, `kPumpStallWarnMs`), `captureengine/main.cpp` (`MainThreadBlockTimer` + record-start/config-reload wraps), `tests/test_pseudo_overlay_visibility.cpp`, `llm-wiki/pseudo-overlay.md`.

### 2026-06-22 - 8ch/7.1 endpoint produced a recording with NO audio (ALAC channel-layout rejection)

- **Why:** `logs/20260622_181002` (build 0.1.4215) recorded zero audio. `MediaEngine::Init` logged `audio sources count=6` but `Init complete. Audio sources: 0, unique tracks: 0` - every track's encoder failed. Root cause in the per-track `AudioEncoder::Init`: the default render endpoint was now **8ch / 7.1 (side), mask `0x63f`, 192 kHz** (vs 2ch in earlier sessions). Both system- and app-audio sources probe that render endpoint, so all tracks resolved to 7.1. ALAC supports `7.1(wide)` (FL FR FC LFE BL BR FLC FRC) but NOT plain `7.1` (…SL SR), so `avcodec_open2` returned EINVAL (-22) for `alac` on EVERY track → all encoders dropped → silent recording. There was no fallback: an unsupported channel layout silently killed all audio.
- **Fix (generic, codec-agnostic):** `mediaengine/audio_encoder.cpp` validates the resolved layout against `AVCodec::ch_layouts` before open (`CodecSupportsChannelLayout`) and, when rejected, remaps via `PickSupportedChannelLayout`: prefer a SAME-channel-count supported layout applied as a RELABEL (keep `outputChannelMask` so the EncodeSamples resampler still emits the original layout - identity channel map - and the encoder just tags the data with the codec layout; e.g. 7.1 data stored in ALAC's 7.1-wide slots, all 8 channels preserved losslessly), else downmix to stereo (retarget `outputChannelMask`/`outputChannels`). Codecs with no `ch_layouts` restriction (PCM/FLAC/most) are untouched. Verified ALAC supported layouts via `ffmpeg -h encoder=alac`: `mono stereo 3.0 4.0 5.0 5.1 6.1(back) 7.1(wide)`.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_audio_encoder.cpp` - `AlacSevenPointOneRemapsToSupportedLayoutInsteadOfFailing` (Init now succeeds, keeps 8ch; fails pre-fix), `AlacSupportedLayoutIsLeftUnchanged` (5.1 untouched), `AlacSevenPointOneEncodesAndProducesPackets` (end-to-end: 7.1 float actually encodes through the relabeled layout and yields packets). Full suite 1097/63 PASS; production + tests-only builds clean.
- **Note / follow-up:** the track-layout resolver makes ALL tracks 8ch when the render endpoint is 7.1 (mic/app upmixed to 8ch) - wasteful but not the bug; users wanting stereo tracks can set `downmix=true`. Whether to cap non-surround tracks (mic/app) to stereo by default is an open design question, deferred (risk to existing multichannel behavior).
- **Source anchors:** `mediaengine/audio_encoder.cpp` (`CodecSupportsChannelLayout`, `PickSupportedChannelLayout`, `Init` layout validation/remap), `mediaengine/mediaengine.cpp` (`ProbeSourceTrackFormat`/`GetTrackAudioFormat` track-layout resolution), `tests/test_audio_encoder.cpp`, `llm-wiki/multi-audio-capture.md`.

### 2026-06-22 - No-callback FSR FG bundle: test-app passed a D3D12 state as the FFX UI-resource state → barrier StateBefore mismatch → Close fail (blank + no glyphs)

- **Why:** After the live-FG-queue bundle fix the test-app overlay reappeared under FSR FG but (a) blanked for several seconds during/after the transition and (b) showed only the frame-time graph line, NO text glyphs (`installed/captureengine/logs/20260622_173742`).
- **Root cause (one bug, two symptoms):** the test app registered the UI resource with `ffxApiGetResourceDX12(uiTex, testapp::dx12fg::kColorReadState, ...)`, but `kColorReadState` is a **D3D12_RESOURCE_STATES** (`PIXEL|NON_PIXEL_SHADER_RESOURCE` = **0xC0**), while `ffxApiGetResourceDX12`'s state param is an **FfxApiResourceState**. FFX/CE decode 0xC0 as `INDIRECT_ARGUMENT|PRESENT` (CE's `ce::ffx_api` enum is correct — matches `ffx_api_types.h`; the FFX equivalent of D3D12 PIXEL|NON_PIXEL SRV is `FFX_API_RESOURCE_STATE_PIXEL_COMPUTE_READ` = 0xC, NOT 0xC0). So `RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL` transitioned the UI texture from the WRONG `StateBefore` (`INDIRECT_ARGUMENT|PRESENT`) when it was physically in `PIXEL|NON_PIXEL SRV` → invalid barrier → `g_FFXUiCompositeList->Close()` failed (silently). Consequences: (1) the closed-list failure left the list OPEN → every subsequent `list->Reset` failed `E_INVALIDARG` → bundle stuck → seconds-long blank; (2) `UploadFontTextureIfNeeded` had already set `fontUploaded=true` while recording the font copy into that never-executed list, so the GPU font copy never ran and subsequent frames skip the upload → font texture permanently empty → only non-textured geometry (the graph line) drew, no glyphs.
- **Fix (test app — faithful to real games):** `RegisterFSRUiResource` now passes `FFX_API_RESOURCE_STATE_PIXEL_COMPUTE_READ` (the correct FFX state for a PIXEL|NON_PIXEL SRV texture) instead of the raw D3D12 `kColorReadState`. Real games declare the correct FFX state, so this makes the test app representative (it was a genuine test-app bug, not a CE bug). CE's barrier `StateBefore` now matches → `Close()` succeeds → the list executes → font copy runs (glyphs) and the bundle appends every frame (no blank).
- **Fix (CE hardening — defense-in-depth):** `RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL` no longer silently sticks on a `Close`/`Reset` failure. The `Close` failure is now logged (HRESULT + `ffxState`/`regState`, previously silent) and, on either a failed `Close` or a failed `list->Reset` (E_INVALIDARG = list left open), the command list is released so `EnsureFFXUiCompositeBundleResources` rebuilds a clean closed list next frame — a single bad-state frame can no longer blank the overlay permanently. (A persistent failure now points loudly at a game registering a UI resource with a state that doesn't match the texture's actual D3D12 state.)
- **Tests:** full suite 1094 PASS; x64/x86 + test-app builds clean.
- **Verification pending:** re-run the inject test app FSR-on — overlay visible WITH text glyphs, continuous across off↔FSR (no multi-second blank, no transition gap); no `command list Close FAILED` / `Reset FAILED` spam in `hook_debug.log`.
- **Source anchors:** `testapp/dx12_fg_switch_fsr.inl` (`RegisterFSRUiResource` FFX state), `testapp/dx12_fg_resources.h` (`kColorReadState` is a D3D12 state), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL` Reset/Close recovery + logging), `hook/common/ffx_api_parsing.h` (`ResourceState` enum, verified vs `build/fg_sdk_include/.../ffx_api_types.h`).

# llm-wiki Log — Archive 2026-W26b

### 2026-06-22 - No-callback FSR FG UI-bundle must fire on the LIVE FG-runtime queue (test-app overlay blanked after crash-boundary change)

- **Why:** After the crash-boundary change (runtime-owned FSR FG never does the backbuffer submit), the `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` overlay DISAPPEARED on switching to FSR FG (`installed/captureengine/logs/20260622_172043`). The crash-boundary change removed `kMinimalBackbuffer`, expecting the game-ECL bundle to cover — but the bundle never fired.
- **Root cause:** the bundle (`RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL`) only fired when `pThis == g_OriginalGameQueue`, and the no-callback ECL fast-path force-forwarded every non-origGame ECL. But once AMD's FfxFrameInterpolationSwapchain takes over, **the game submits its scene+UI on the FG-runtime-owned swapchain queue and `g_OriginalGameQueue` goes IDLE** (log: ECL heartbeat on `g_SwapchainQueue`=`...3032DD30`, `origGame`=`...2E158270` idle; `appended`=0). So the origGame-only bundle never fired and, with `kMinimalBackbuffer` gone, nothing drew.
- **Fix:** shared helper `TryAppendNoCallbackBundleOverlay(pThis, NumLists, ppLists)` whose queue eligibility is `pThis == g_OriginalGameQueue || pThis == g_SwapchainQueue` (the live FG-runtime queue). Wired into the no-callback ECL fast-path (it attempts the bundle BEFORE force-forwarding non-origGame ECLs) and the two origGame heavy-path sites (refactored to the helper). Appending to the game's OWN submission on the runtime queue is NOT a separate submit/Signal — it rides the call AMD already syncs (NumLists+1, same ECL call), so it stays within the crash boundary (unlike the removed `DX12_ProcessFrameMinimal`). Per-frame reset: `DX12_ResetNoCallbackBundleFrame()` (called from `DetourPresent`'s no-callback branch) replaces the `ProcessFrameMinimal` reset that no longer runs.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp::NoCallbackBundleFiresOnLiveFGRuntimeQueueNotOnlyOrigGame` (source-guard: helper accepts both origGame + `liveFgQueue`, and is called from ≥2 ECL paths incl. the fast-path). `tests/test_stubs.cpp` stubs `DX12_ResetNoCallbackBundleFrame`. Full suite 1094 PASS; x64/x86 + test-app builds clean.
- **Verification pending:** re-run `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` (inject) FSR-on — confirm `FFX UI-bundle overlay appended to game ECL (queue=... liveFgQueue ...)` and the overlay is visible + continuous across off↔FSR (no blank, incl. transition). Then the `--fsr-degenerate-ui` substitution path, then GTA.
- **Source anchors:** `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`TryAppendNoCallbackBundleOverlay`, `DX12_ResetNoCallbackBundleFrame`, no-callback ECL fast-path, two origGame bundle sites), `hook/common/dxgi_shared.cpp` (`DetourPresent` no-callback per-frame reset), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.h`, `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`.

### 2026-06-22 - GTA no-callback FSR FG overlay: crash boundary + CE-substituted UI texture (supersedes iteration-1 minimal-backbuffer)

- **Why:** Iteration-1 (commit `57fc052`, "Fix GTA overlay invisibility under native no-callback FSR FG") revived the ECL UI-bundle but **introduced a GTA crash** (`installed/captureengine/logs/20260621_191028`, build `0.1.4186`): `amd_fidelityfx_dx12!ffxQuery` null-deref AV (`READ from 0x8`, `mov rcx,[rsi+8]` with `rsi=0`), no CE frame on the faulting stack — AMD null-derefs because CE corrupted its presentation state. The test app tolerated it; GTA did not.
- **Root cause (two parts):** (1) **The crash** — `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` returned `kMinimalBackbuffer` whenever the bundle was not firing, so `DetourPresent` called `DX12_ProcessFrameMinimal`, which submits overlay GPU work on AMD's runtime/swapchain queue **while AMD owns the swapchain**. ANY CE GPU work on AMD's backbuffer/runtime queue under runtime-owned no-callback FSR FG wedges/null-derefs AMD inside `ffxQuery`. (2) **Why the bundle never fired in GTA** — GTA leaves UI composition ENABLED (`flags=0x2`) but registers a **1×1 placeholder** UI texture; drawing the overlay onto 1×1 is useless and trips `list->Reset` E_INVALIDARG. The cache also froze after the one-shot VEH disarm (intra-module `RegisterUiResource` calls stop reaching `Hooked_ffxConfigure`).
- **Verified, load-bearing finding (kills the plan's Part C):** there is **no pacing-safe per-frame `RegisterUiResource` interceptor for GTA's call pattern.** For the protected AMD module, inline/export hooks fail-fast AMD, the IAT patch demonstrably does NOT catch GTA's per-frame calls (the cache froze at 2 updates the instant the VEH disarmed), and the re-armed 0xCC VEH is exactly what wedges AMD (multi-threaded contention). So per-frame substitution interception was rejected.
- **Fix (Parts A + B + D):**
  - **A — crash boundary.** `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute(runtimeOwnsSwapchain, cached, firing)` now **always** returns `kSkipBundleCovers` when AMD owns the swapchain — the overlay rides UI composition ONLY, never a backbuffer/runtime-queue submit. `kMinimalBackbuffer` survives only for the non-runtime-owned escape hatch. `DetourPresent` passes `DoesFGRuntimeOwnSwapchain() || HookHasRuntimeOwnedNativeFGPresentPath()` and has a loud defensive guard-rail that refuses any backbuffer submit under runtime-owned FG.
  - **B — CE-controlled UI texture + substitution.** The per-frame overlay refresh is the existing **game-ECL bundle** (`RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL`, fires from `ExecuteCommandLists` every frame — needs NO ffxConfigure interception), which draws onto a cached **target** texture. New `DX12_PrepareFFXUiOverlayTarget` (called from `Hooked_ffxConfigure` RegisterUiResource) decides via `ChooseFFXUiOverlayTarget`: a usable full-size game UI texture → blend the overlay onto it (test app); a **degenerate** placeholder (GTA's 1×1) → create a CE-owned **backbuffer-sized** texture (`EnsureCEUiSubstituteTexture`), **substitute** it into the forwarded desc (so AMD composites CE's texture), and cache CE's texture as the bundle target with a **transparent-clear** flag. Backbuffer geometry is cached from the FG-enable swapchain (`DX12_TryCacheRuntimeOwnedCallbackHDRStateFromSwapchain` → `g_NoCallbackBackbufferWidth/Height/Format`). The bundle clears CE's substitute to transparent each frame (only the overlay composites over the game frame); the game's own texture is never cleared.
  - **Degenerate guard.** `RecordBundleOverlayForGameECL` now **skips** (never draws onto) a 1×1/much-smaller-than-backbuffer target — fixes the 1×1 garbage/E_INVALIDARG. Blank-but-safe when no substitute is available.
  - **D — teardown.** `ReleaseFFXUiCompositeInfra` releases the CE substitute texture + resets the clear flag (teardown/device-change only, never per-frame).
- **Why AMD-safe:** the bundle writes the (CE or game) UI texture on the **game queue** as part of the game's ECL; AMD reads it on its present queue with the same game-queue→present sync the game's own HUD already rides. Zero work on AMD's runtime present queue → no `ffxQuery` wedge; post-interpolation composite → no ghosting.
- **Residual GTA-visibility risk (settled only by a GTA run):** substitution happens only on the `RegisterUiResource` calls caught **before** the VEH disarm. If GTA natively re-registers its 1×1 **every frame** after disarm, AMD's registered UI resource reverts to 1×1 and overrides CE's substitute → overlay invisible again (but still no crash). Diagnostics decide it: `SetBundleTargetTexture` logs the target + `changed` flag; `Substituted CE full-size UI texture ...` logs each substitution; the degenerate-guard skip logs loudly. If GTA registers once / rarely, substitution persists and the overlay is visible.
- **Dead code removed:** `DX12_CacheFFXUiResourceForBundle` (refactored into internal `SetBundleTargetTexture` + `DX12_PrepareFFXUiOverlayTarget`); stub dropped from `tests/test_stubs.cpp`.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` — `NoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRouteNeverSubmitsBackbufferWhenRuntimeOwnsSwapchain` (the crash regression: runtime-owned never picks the backbuffer route, all 4 bundle states) replaces the old route test; `FFXUiOverlayTargetSubstitutesForDegenerateGameTexture` (1×1 / much-smaller → substitute, full-size → composite, unknown-bb only substitutes trivially-degenerate). `BundleOverlayRecordInitializesItsOwnResources` source-guard retained. Full unit suite PASS; production (x64+x86) + tests-only builds clean.
- **Test-app substitution coverage (opt-in, default OFF — universal coverage preserved):** `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` gains `[Stress] fsr_degenerate_ui_resource=1` / `--fsr-degenerate-ui` to register a 1×1 UI placeholder (GTA-style) instead of the full-size UI texture, so an INJECTED run exercises CE's substitution path on real AMD hardware — a synthetic proxy that isolates "does AMD composite a CE-substituted texture at all" from GTA's per-frame re-registration. Default run unchanged (full-size composite path + all existing FG-switch/stress scenarios). Placeholder is device-bound (released/recreated across FSR→DLSS→FSR). `testapp/dx12_fg_switch_{test.cpp,config.inl,fsr.inl}`.
- **Verification pending — primary acceptance is a real GTA V Enhanced FSR-FG run:** no `amd_fidelityfx_dx12!ffxQuery` crash/no new `.dmp`; `hook_debug.log` shows `Substituted CE full-size UI texture`, `FFX UI-bundle target ...`, and `FFX UI-bundle overlay appended to game ECL`; overlay visible + continuous across FG on→off→on. Compare to the `20260621_191028` crash baseline. If still invisible, the cache `changed`/substitution logs reveal whether GTA re-registers per frame (the open per-frame-override question).
- **Source anchors:** `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` 3-arg, `ChooseFFXUiOverlayTarget`, `FFXUiOverlayTarget`), `hook/common/dxgi_shared.cpp` (`DetourPresent` no-callback branch + guard-rail), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (`DX12_PrepareFFXUiOverlayTarget`, `EnsureCEUiSubstituteTexture`, `SetBundleTargetTexture`, backbuffer-geometry cache, bundle degenerate-guard + transparent-clear, `ReleaseFFXUiCompositeInfra`), `hook/apis/ffx_hook.cpp` (`Hooked_ffxConfigure` RegisterUiResource substitution), `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`.

### 2026-06-22 - Investigated "Src 4" app-audio backlog (logs/fortip5) - NOT a bug; clarified misleading drift log

- **Trigger:** A WGC-CFR Fortnite session (`logs/fortip5`, build 0.1.4191) showed a persistent `[PullAudio] Src 4 drift: trueDrift=8821 (rb=13621 expected=4800) tier1=0% tier2=1` (~184ms over target, tier2 flag set) for the whole 6-min recording. Flagged as a possible app-audio convergence bug while triaging a faint "audio slightly delayed" perception.
- **Finding (no bug):** (1) Index confusion — `Src N` in PullAudio/STOP is the EXPANDED `audioSources[]` index, while `MediaEngine::Init setting up audio source N` is the 5-entry config index; `Src 4` = `audioSources[4]` = Fortnite→track2 (an app process targeting tracks 1+2 takes two expanded entries), not the configured `source 4`=SB_Vulkan. SB_DX12/SB_Vulkan correctly logged `app-never-started`; no wrong-process capture/comb — the metallic-fix holds. (2) ALL sources prime at ~280ms (`realBuffered=13440`) and keep it: WGC CFR never trims audio (`kWgcPreferVideoRepeatsOverAudioCuts=true`; `ShouldAllowWallClockAudioAnchor` is false for CFR), so the tier2-trim gate is always false. The logged `tier2=1` was only `ShouldActivateTier2Trim` (threshold flag), never an actual cut. (3) Benign for sync: content placed by packet QPC, `maxAudioDelta=0`, `ovf=0`, `ringUnderruns=0`, exact track lengths. A real 280ms offset would be glaring lip-sync, not "ever so slight."
- **Change (diagnostics only, zero behavior change):** `[PullAudio] Src N drift` now logs `tier2=X tier2Applied=Y` — `tier2` = drift-threshold flag, `tier2Applied` = whether a trim actually ran (always 0 in WGC CFR). Prevents re-misreading the standing startup buffer as an active trim / convergence failure. No audio/video path touched → no sync/smoothness regression risk. Full unit suite 1092/63 PASS; production build clean. (Synthetic A/V matrix intentionally not run per request.)
- **Separately (the actual faint-delay lever, unchanged):** the render→loopback probe (31.441ms here, high confidence) measures engine startup+tap, a lower bound that excludes the game's own audio write-ahead buffer, so loopback audio can land marginally late. The principled, no-regression remedy is the existing `[General] audio_capture_latency_ms` override after measuring the true offset on a real recording — not a code change.
- **Source anchors:** `mediaengine/mediaengine.cpp` (`[PullAudio] Src N drift` log + tier2 gate ~line 2758), `mediaengine/audio_sync_utils.h` (`ShouldActivateTier2Trim`, `ShouldAllowWallClockAudioAnchor`), `common/config.cpp` (`audio_capture_latency_ms` docs), `llm-wiki/multi-audio-capture.md`.

### 2026-06-22 - 192 kHz-loopback bad_alloc crash: out-of-domain WASAPI qpcPosition → unbounded silence allocation

- **Why:** `installed/captureengine/logs/capturefail` (build 0.1.4191, Fortnite session). Crash dump `crash_20260622_013615_..._pid24596_tid12776.dmp` (exception code `0x20474343` = libunwind "GCC" C++ throw) shows `KERNELBASE!RaiseException` ← `mediaengine!_cxa_throw` ← `operator new` (merged symbol `weak._Znwy...__clang_call_terminate`) ← `MediaEngine::AudioLoop`. `ub` of the throw site: `cmp r13,[rsp+0D0h]; ja length_error; shl r13,2; mov rcx,r13; call operator new` — a `std::vector<float>` ctor. At fault `r13 = 0x00000f00000025f0` = 16,492,674,426,352 **bytes** (~16.5 TB) → `bad_alloc` → uncaught → `std::terminate`.
- **Root cause:** The crashing source was the **system-audio 192 kHz loopback** (`media.log`: `Started ... rate=192000 loopback=1`, track 3, type=0). Its first packet's WASAPI `qpcPosition` (taken verbatim from `IAudioCaptureClient::GetBuffer` in `audio_capture.cpp`) was ~497 days ahead of `recordingStartSystemQpc100ns` (the video-frame QPC anchor, same 100-ns domain). `AudioLoop` computed `packetStartSamples ≈ 2.06e12` (48 kHz) → `ComputeStartupAwarePacketTimelineAdjustment` gap ≈ 2.06e12 → `std::vector<float> silence(gap*channels)` ≈ 16.5 TB. The first-packet rebase has a hole (`ComputeStartupFirstPacketRebaseOffset` returns 0 when `!sawSyncPendingPackets`), so the bogus gap was never bounded. WASAPI driver-reported QPC positions are not trustworthy and were used verbatim to size an allocation.
- **Fix 1 (root cause, capture side):** `mediaengine/audio_time_utils.h` adds `SanitizeCaptureQpcPosition(reported, now, futureTol=1s, pastTol=5s)`. `AudioCapture::CaptureLoop` now reads the live QPC after each `GetBuffer`, converts via `RawQpcToHundredNanoseconds`, and substitutes `now` for any out-of-domain position (these are universal physical bounds, not device tuning — a capture read-timestamp can't be in the future or older than the endpoint buffer). Healthy positions pass through bit-identical; raw value preserved on `AudioPacket::rawQpcPosition`; warning throttled to 8/session.
- **Fix 2 (defense-in-depth, consumer side):** `mediaengine/audio_sync_utils.h` adds `ClampTimelineGapSamplesToCapacity(gap, ringCapacitySamples)`. `AudioLoop` clamps the leading-silence gap to the ring buffer capacity before allocating (`WriteRetainNew` drops the excess anyway), so no timestamp can ever size a pathological `std::vector` even if it bypasses Fix 1. Warns when it clamps.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_audio_time_utils.cpp` — `SanitizeCaptureQpc{PassesThroughHealthyPositions,ReplacesFarFutureGarbage,ReplacesFarPastGarbage,TrustsValueWhenNoReferenceClock}` (the far-future case uses the exact ~497-day value). `tests/test_audio_sync_utils.cpp` — `TimelineGapClamp{LeavesInRangeGapsUntouched,BoundsOversizedGapToRingCapacity (the 2.06e12 crash value),HandlesDegenerateInputs}`. Full suite 1092/63 PASS; production + tests-only builds clean.
- **Validation pending:** real recording on the 192 kHz-loopback machine — confirm the `out-of-domain WASAPI qpcPosition` warning fires at most a few times at start, no crash/dump, the gap-clamp warning never fires, and A/V sync / track lengths stay sample-exact (`ffprobe`).
- **Source anchors:** `mediaengine/audio_time_utils.h` (`SanitizeCaptureQpcPosition`, `kDefaultCaptureQpc*ToleranceUnits`), `mediaengine/audio_capture.cpp` (`CaptureLoop` QPC guard, `rawQpcPosition` preserve), `mediaengine/audio_sync_utils.h` (`ClampTimelineGapSamplesToCapacity`), `mediaengine/mediaengine.cpp` (`AudioLoop` silence-gap clamp), `tests/test_audio_time_utils.cpp`, `tests/test_audio_sync_utils.cpp`, `llm-wiki/multi-audio-capture.md`.

### 2026-06-22 - Defer app-audio ring buffer allocation (idle "capture-any-game" overhead)

- **Why:** After the metallic-audio fix, a Strange Brigade run (`logs/20260621_234429`) was clean and sample-exact, but the "capture whichever game is running" profile still listed three candidate app-audio processes (Fortnite, SB_DX12, SB_Vulkan) → tracks 1 & 2. Only SB_DX12 runs; the other two each pre-allocated a full 30 s CFR ring buffer (~11.5 MB at 48k stereo) per `(process, track)` even though they never capture — ~46 MB wasted RAM for the four idle sources.
- **Change:** App-audio per-source ring buffers are now allocated lazily. `InitAudioSourceBuffers` constructs app-audio sources with a small 1 s buffer and records `AudioSource::fullRingBufferCapacityFloats`; on the source's first captured packet, `AudioLoop` grows the buffer in-place to full capacity via the new `AudioRingBuffer::EnsureCapacity` (mutex-protected, grows only while empty, never shrinks). System/mic sources keep full capacity immediately. Idle candidate processes now hold ~384 KB instead of ~11.5 MB; late-joining processes still get full capacity the instant they produce audio (late-join contract preserved). Race-free: the ring buffer is touched only by the AudioLoop thread, and EnsureCapacity locks the buffer's mutex.
- **Why not more:** Per-`(process, track)` monitor threads (~1 process snapshot/s each) remain — they are required to detect a target process appearing/exiting for the late-join contract, and are very cheap. Sharing one capture per unique process (to also cut the running game's two loopback clients to one) was considered but deferred: it needs a packet-fanout change to the consume-once `GetNextPacket` model and is higher risk for marginal gain.
- **Tests:** `tests/test_audio_ring_buffer.cpp` — `EnsureCapacityGrowsEmptyBufferAndAcceptsFullWindow`, `EnsureCapacityNeverShrinksAndIsIdempotent`, `EnsureCapacityRefusesToGrowWhileHoldingBufferedAudio`. Full suite PASS; production + tests-only builds clean.
- **Source anchors:** `mediaengine/audio_ring_buffer.h` (`EnsureCapacity`), `mediaengine/mediaengine.cpp` (`AudioSource::fullRingBufferCapacityFloats`, `InitAudioSourceBuffers` small-initial alloc, `AudioLoop` first-packet grow), `tests/test_audio_ring_buffer.cpp`, `llm-wiki/multi-audio-capture.md`.

### 2026-07-03 - No-callback FSR SUSPENSION overlay: backbuffer draw on CE's own queue (iteration 3, visibility)

- **Continues the two entries below (same suspend edge).** Iter-2's bundle route fixed the ~1fps stall but session `logs/20260703_212441` showed the overlay STILL blank at full speed: `FFX UI-composite overlay drawn ... frame=1801 waitTimedOut=0` every frame, yet nothing on screen, and the game had STOPPED calling `RegisterUiResource` (`cfgFrame=41`, before the suspend). **Proved: AMD's `FfxFrameInterpolationSwapchain` does NOT composite the registered UI resource when frame-gen is disabled (passthrough) — it presents the app's backbuffer as-is.** So the overlay was faithfully drawn onto a texture AMD ignores.
- **GTA safety check first (`logs/20260703_213508`, user-provided):** GTA does DLSS-FG-in-menu → authoritative FFX takeover → FSR FG **stays active**; `ffxConfigure(enabled=0)` calls = **0**, runtime-owned FG-OFF = **0**, new suspend-fallback log = **0**. ### 2026-07-03 - No-callback FSR SUSPENSION: overlay rides the bundle, NEVER the stalling backbuffer (2 iterations)

- **Two user reports on the same `dx12_fg_switch_test.exe` suspend edge** (OFF → FSR FG ON → SUSPEND via `ffxConfigure frameGenerationEnabled=0` while AMD keeps its `FfxFrameInterpolationSwapchain`):
  - **Iter-1 `logs/20260703_204119` (blank):** overlay disappeared and never returned for the whole suspension. The overlay-INIT gate `ShouldSkipSeparateOverlayGpuWorkForRuntimeOwnedFrameGeneration` fed `DX12_IsFFXUiResourceCachedForBundle()` (raw cached-UI-texture pointer latch — set once, never cleared on suspend) as "bundle covers" → `skip=true` deferred overlay init the whole suspension (`overlayInit=0`), while `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` was sending the suspend to `kMinimalBackbuffer`. Net "nobody draws".
  - **Iter-2 `logs/20260703_210021` (PERF DEATH — my first fix's regression):** making the suspend actually take the backbuffer (`DX12_ProcessFrameMinimal`) collapsed the app to **~1 fps**. Log: `DescFree: slot N GPU-completion wait timed out (guard=1 completed=0)` + `DetourPresent TOTAL SLOW ~999ms` on EVERY present (40+). Manual dump: the game/present thread (0x55C4) parked in `WaitForSingleObjectEx` inside CE's wrapped-present path, called from `amd_fidelityfx_framegeneration_dx12` Present. Root cause: AMD stops flushing its runtime-owned queue while suspended, so the overlay's GPU-completion fence NEVER signals → CE waits the full ~1s timeout per frame. This **disproved** the standing "suspension backbuffer is safe because AMD isn't interpolating" assumption (session 20260623_054929) — safe-from-crash ≠ non-stalling.
- **Final fix (build 0.1.4451):** while AMD owns the swapchain (active OR suspended) the overlay rides the UI-resource composition BUNDLE (CE's own fenced queue via the proxy-present prework / DetourPresent composite) and CE submits ZERO backbuffer work. `ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` drops the `&& !fsrFGDisabledSuspendPending` relaxation → `runtimeOwns` always returns `kSkipBundleCovers`. `ShouldSkipSeparateOverlayGpuWorkForRuntimeOwnedFrameGeneration` matches: `bundleCovers = ffxUiResourceCompositionActive && !liveSwapchainQueueIsOriginalGameQueue` (no suspend gate). The backbuffer (`kMinimalBackbuffer` / `skip=false`) is reachable ONLY at a stale latch (game recreated its OWN native swapchain, `liveQueueIsOrigGame` — its queue is actively flushed, no stall) or non-runtime-owned.
- **GTA/Talos safety:** unchanged for active FG (already `kSkipBundleCovers`). The crash boundary is *strengthened* (backbuffer never used while AMD owns the swapchain, not even suspended). No game-specific logic.
- **Diagnostics:** the `ProcessFrame` no-callback fallback log now only fires for stale-latch / no-UI-resource (suspend no longer reaches it); reasons ∈ {stale no-callback latch (live queue back on origGame), no UI resource registered, no-callback composition}.
- **Source anchors:** `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h` (`ChooseNoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRoute` + `ShouldSkipSeparateOverlayGpuWorkForRuntimeOwnedFrameGeneration`), `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp` (~4338 call site + ~4380 log), `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp` (`NativeFSRNoCallbackSuspendRidesBundleNeverStallingBackbuffer` + revised `NoCallbackFSRFGOverlayRouteNeverSubmitsBackbufferWhenRuntimeOwnsSwapchain`), `llm-wiki/frame-generation/guardrails.md`.

### 2026-07-03 - WGC smoothness: startup warmup grace period + adaptive overcapture cap + stable underfeed recovery exit

- **User evidence:** `logs/fortibad2` vs `logs/fortibetter` — same game (Fortnite), same 120fps CFR WGC capture, same build 0.1.4433. Bad session: SrcAvg ~9.5ms (105fps), Dup ~112/s, FreshMiss ~960pm, WgcSelBias ~7.3ms, permanently in "recovery" ingress mode. Good session: SrcAvg ~7.6ms (131fps), Dup ~8/s, FreshMiss ~50pm, WgcSelBias ~3.7ms, reached "healthy". Both sessions had identical CbProc (~150-200us), Copy (~20us), Encode (~500us) — processing pipeline was NOT the bottleneck. Bad session's 33ms CbGap at startup (vs ~7ms in good) starved the reservoir and permanently latched recovery mode.
- **Fix 1: Startup warmup grace period.** Added `wgcWarmupUntilQpc` set to ~200ms after the first frame arrives (`liveStartQpc + targetIntervalTicks * 24`). During warmup: `wgcSourceHealthTelemetryReady` is forced false (blocks recovery mode entry), `pruneStaleWgcVisualDebt` skips all pruning, and the adaptive throttle holds the default 125% overcapture target. Prevents early startup starvation from permanently poisoning the entire session. One-time log: `[WGC CFR] Warmup active` / `Warmup ended`.
- **Fix 2: Source-capability-adaptive overcapture target.** Added `ComputeWgcAdaptiveCappedTargetFps(outputFps, sourceMin250Fps, overcaptureTargetFps)` to `capture_pipeline_policy.h`. When stable underfeed is detected (source below target for >= 3s, `wgcLowSourceDurationMs >= kWgcAdaptiveCapUnderfeedWaitMs=3000`), the adaptive throttle sets target to `sourceMin250Fps + 5` (clamped between outputFps and original 125% target) instead of the futile max-rate=0. New constants: `kWgcAdaptiveCapUnderfeedWaitMs=3000`, `kWgcAdaptiveCapHeadroomFps=5`.
- **Fix 3: Graceful recovery exit for stable underfeed.** `ShouldExitWgcLowSourceMode` gains a `durationInModeMs` parameter — after 5s of stable delivery with bounded empty-ticks and <4 buffered frames, exits even if source is below FPS target. `ShouldExitWgcLiveRecoveryMode` gains `stableUnderfeedExit` flag — when low-source exits via stable underfeed, live-recovery also exits so the overcapture cap can restore at an adaptive rate.
- **Diagnostics:** `[WGC CFR] Warmup active/ended`, `inWgcWarmup` can be derived from `liveTicksOutput < 24`. WGC Perf `Throttle` shows adaptive cap rate instead of 0 when stable underfeed is active. `[WGC CFR SUMMARY]` ends with `BiasClampCount=` (how many times the phase error clamp fired).
- **Implementation details:** `media_main.cpp`: `wgcWarmupUntilQpc` state variable (line ~2890), warmup gate at telemetry readiness (~5500), warmup skip in `pruneStaleWgcVisualDebt` (~3900), warmup override in adaptive throttle (~5725). `capture_pipeline_policy.h`: `ComputeWgcAdaptiveCappedTargetFps` (~877), modified `ShouldExitWgcLowSourceMode` (~1537), `ShouldExitWgcLiveRecoveryMode` (~1524).
- **Validation:** Full build + all 1236 unit tests pass (build 0.1.4437).
- **Source anchors:** `captureengine/media_main.cpp`, `common/capture_pipeline_policy.h`, `llm-wiki/wgc-capture.md`.

### 2026-07-03 - WGC smoothness Fix 4: Bounded phase error via source-rate selection-target clamping

- **Problem:** Bad session had WgcSelBias=7.3ms (vs good 3.7ms). Each frame was selected ~7.3ms older than ideal grid position — a persistent subtle offset through the entire recording, not just during transients.
- **Root cause:** When source delivers below output target (e.g., 105fps source → 120fps output), the CFR selection grid advances 8.33ms per tick but only ~1 new source frame arrives per 9.5ms. The grid outruns the source by ~1.17ms/tick, accumulating bias. Without any bound the bias grows to ~7ms+ before reactive duplicates reduce it.
- **Fix:** After computing `effectiveSelectionTargetQpc`, if low-source mode is active and the target has drifted >1 output interval ahead of the newest buffered frame, clamp it to `newestFrameQpc + targetIntervalTicks`. This keeps the selection target within one interval of the real source content, bounding WgcSelBias to ~8ms max. Does NOT touch the output PTS grid, audio timeline, or content delay reservoir — only the frame selection reference point is adjusted. `wgcBiasClampCount` reports how many clamps fired (available in `[WGC CFR SUMMARY]`). Bias decays when source catches up.
- **Source anchors:** `captureengine/media_main.cpp` (~5902-5914), `llm-wiki/wgc-capture.md`.
- **Validation:** Full build + all 1236 unit tests pass.

### 2026-07-03 - Hardware-cursor research + dup ground-truth 10-bit + fullscreen-game dup priority + R10 misdiagnosis correction

- **Research (user-driven, web-verified):** WGC capture sessions demote the live cursor from the hardware plane to DWM-composed (software) rendering — reported since March 2020 (microsoft/Windows.UI.Composition-Win32-Samples #51 by an OBS dev; #128 shows WGC can even make the cursor INVISIBLE in fullscreen games, explicitly not reproducible with DXGI dup/BitBlt), toggling `IsCursorCaptureEnabled` does not help, and Microsoft closed it without a fix → architectural, NOT a Windows-update regression. Desktop Duplication structurally preserves the hardware cursor (pointer delivered as separate metadata, consumer draws it). OBS Display Capture "Automatic" defaults to DXGI on normal desktops — which is exactly why the user's OBS monitor recording kept the hardware cursor while WGC (OBS and CE alike) lost it.
- **Dup 10-bit ground truth (fixes 20260702_194424):** the old init-time policy gate read `DXGI_OUTDUPL_DESC.ModeDesc.Format` (display-mode format, NOT the delivery — that session's `DuplicateOutput1` succeeded with an FP16/R10-only list while ModeDesc claimed BGRA8) and wrongly fell back to WGC, silently costing the hardware cursor. Now: always offer FP16/R10(+BGRA8 for SDR), never reject on format, log the FIRST DELIVERED frame's format + `sourceContentBits=8|10|16` (`GetDxgiDuplicationSourceContentBits` replaces `IsAcceptableDxgiDuplicationFormat`), WARN-once on explicit-10-bit-from-8-bit-desktop upconversion (equal information content to WGC monitor capture; P010 encode unchanged). BGRA8 delivery keeps a BGRA8 retained pool (VP→P010); FP16 SDR uses the shared compact FP16→R10 shader.
- **Fullscreen-game dup priority:** new `[General] auto_fullscreen_capture=dxgi_dup|wgc_window` (default dxgi_dup): auto-mode UNHOOKED fullscreen-like game targets (source-PID window, foreground candidate, hook-connected scan) capture the game's monitor via duplication (`primeDxgiDupForWindowMonitor`, policy `ShouldPreferDxgiDuplicationForFullscreenAutoTarget`) with WGC window capture as fallback; windowed targets and configured `wgc_window_detection` matches keep WGC window capture.
- **Dup cursor-plane tracking + double-cursor prevention:** per pointer update, `PointerPosition.Visible` + `GetCursorInfo`-in-monitor-rect classify hardware (separate pointer; encoder composes) vs software/embedded (frames already contain the cursor; encoder composition suppressed via new `MediaEngine_SetCursorCompositionSuppressed` → `VideoEncoder::CursorCompositionActive()` at every per-frame draw site — capability/init still keys on `captureCursor`). Transitions logged (`[DXGIDup] Cursor plane state changed`); `[WGC Perf]` gains `DupHwCursor`/`DupCursorEmbedded`/`DupPtrTransitions` — a live hw/sw cursor-plane detector.
- **R10 misdiagnosis corrected:** WGC R10 frame pools fail with `E_INVALIDARG` at the WinRT API level (all buffer counts, any driver — WGC supports only the BGRA8/FP16 family); the "R10+SHARED_NTHANDLE driver quirk" wiki claim was wrong and the 8→3 retry ladder was dead weight → removed (single attempt kept for future Windows). FP16 staging pool trimmed: `GetWgcSmoothnessPreferredSourceFramePoolBuffers` fps/15 (floor 8, cap 12) since compact-active source pools are staging-only (callback converts+releases in ~11-21µs) — 8 FP16 buffers at 4K120 (506MB, was 12/759MB), retained reservoir unchanged (45 frames).
- **Pre-existing test failures fixed (HEAD commit 78d2d501 "WGC smoothness fix attempt"):** `InputFrameRatePredictor::Update` folded stall-sized intervals into the cadence EMA before `SmoothMonotonicTimestamp` ran, inflating the stall-snap threshold past the stall itself (smeared stalls; test expected relock) → isolated gap outliers (>3x interval) no longer touch the EMA/jitter, 3 consecutive long intervals = accepted regime change (alpha 0.5). Duplicate raw timestamps no longer advance a full predicted interval (racing to the +maxDev clamp, then breaking the deviation bound via the monotonic +1) → minimal +1 advance, content time honestly static. 1236 unit tests green.
- **Validation pending:** real dup recording on this 25H2 machine — hardware cursor preservation, `sourceContentBits` ground truth (may genuinely be >8-bit on 25H2), embedded-cursor suppression on plane transitions, fullscreen-game dup routing, and the FP16 staging trim under GPU load (watch delivery min-windows/CbGap for new drops).

### 2026-07-02 - DXGI Desktop Duplication capture backend + auto-mode desktop fallback priority + recording-thread config snapshot race fix

- **User decision:** DXGI Desktop Duplication is now a supported capture method (supersedes the old "forbidden forever" wiki rule). Requested auto priority: inject (whitelisted game) > WGC window detection > DXGI duplication for pure desktop/monitor capture.
- **Architecture (maximum reuse, zero new CFR machinery):** `DxgiDuplicationSource` (`captureengine/dxgi_dup_capture.{h,cpp}`) is a frame SOURCE only — dedicated MMCSS acquire thread, QPC `LastPresentTime` timestamps, frame-on-change semantics, pointer-only updates mapped to cursor-only skips, `AccumulatedFrames` lag counting, ACCESS_LOST → reset request. It feeds the existing engine through `WGCCapture::Impl::PreflightSourceFrame`/`DeliverSourceTexture`, refactored out of `ProcessCapturedFrame` with identical semantics, so copy pool, slot leases, ingress admission, smoothness reservoir, uniform playout, anti-freeze floor, startup barrier, and all telemetry are literally the same code for both backends.

The original `dxgi_dup = overlay-only injection like wgc` coupling is historical and was superseded on 2026-07-12 by capture-method/injection independence. `ShouldPreferDxgiDuplicationForMonitorCapture` policy: explicit dxgi_dup always, explicit wgc never, auto for every monitor-scope prime. `primeWgcMonitorTarget` tries `InitForMonitorDuplication` first with WGC monitor fallback; window-scope targets unchanged (WGC window capture stays preferred for games per DirectFlip/VRR rationale). Explicit dxgi_dup ignores `wgc_window_detection` (monitor-scope only, logged).
- **Fail-safety:** duplication object only created at StartCapture (idle duplication would suppress MPO system-wide between recordings); prime does light validation (adapter/output match, rotation). If duplication fails at start (format policy, rotated/cross-adapter, API loss), `Impl::StartCapture` falls back IN PLACE to a WGC monitor item — recording start cannot fail on a dup-only problem. `ForceReset` recreates the dup target with WGC fallback. 10-bit/HDR policy enforced at DuplicateOutput1 format-list level + `IsAcceptableDxgiDuplicationFormat` (HDR→FP16 only; explicit 10-bit→R10/FP16, BGRA8 excluded → loud failure → WGC fallback which CAN request a high-precision pool).
- **Budget:** `ComputeWgcSmoothnessSurfaceBudget(..., requiresSourceFramePool=false)` — dup has no consumer-owned source frame pool, so the source-pool share funds retained copy slots; reservoir ≥ WGC split at equal budget (test `DuplicationBudgetSpendsSourcePoolShareOnCopySlots`).
- **Audit fix (real race):** `WgcCaptureThreadFunc`/`EncoderThreadFunc`/`InjectCaptureThreadFunc` were started with `std::ref(config)` while the media main thread reassigns `config` mid-recording (late hook connect → `refreshActiveConfig`, IPC ReloadConfig) — use-after-free on config strings/vectors. All three now receive a recording-lifetime `shared_ptr<const AppConfig>` snapshot (recording settings are per-session by design).
- **Audit notes:** VFR-mode WGC never consumes the deferred HDR recheck flag (pull-mode only; negligible: HDR toggles reset the session anyway). Auto-mode WGC startup fallback (inject produced no frames) still starts the standby WGC monitor target rather than re-running target selection with dup — follow-up candidate. `[WGC Perf]` gained `Backend:`, `DupIdleTimeouts:`, `DupMissed:` fields.
- **Tests:** config alias/predicate tests, monitor-backend policy tests, dup format-policy tests, dup budget test (build 0.1.4426+, 1228 unit tests green). Real-hardware dup recording validation PENDING (desktop recording, mode change/HDR toggle mid-recording, secure-desktop excursion, explicit 10-bit on 8-bit desktop → WGC fallback path).

### 2026-07-02 - RESOLVED game-side: GTA cold-start DLSS FG "not interpolating" reproduces WITHOUT CE
