R10-to-R10 canonical work is included in telemetry and logs identify backend/staging/timing basis. WGC keeps its same-device fast path.
- **CFR/audio correctness:** live scheduler rebase no longer skips output ticks; every CFR backend drains its accrued contiguous prefix at stop. Written packet timelines track maximum PTS gaps and finalization requires exact packet coverage plus <=1.01 ticks. Desired durations are no longer written over stream metadata. Packet/audio frame scans are the analyzer default. Packetless timeline-valid co-mixed sources become aligned silence; late sources join the current cursor. `AudioEncoder::EncodeSamples` reports accepted/submitted samples, track cursors advance only by accepted samples, deferred start preserves an assigned end, the first accepted batch is no longer cleared, and batches beyond the former five-second FIFO ceiling are retained/drained.
- **Configuration:** `wgc_allow_lossy_bgra8_pool=false` is canonical. `wgc_prefer_compact_10bit_pool` remains a deprecated alias only when the canonical key is absent. Explicit 10-bit/HDR ignore lossy BGRA8; DXGI never uses it.
- **Validation:** required clean build passed at `0.1.4521`; the canonical no-build run passed all `1322` native tests plus three Python tool self-tests at metadata build `0.1.4522`. Focused coverage includes the 625600-sample batch, packetless/sparse audio, CFR no-rebase/stop drain, reordered packet PTS gaps, and config alias precedence. A paired real-hardware rerun remains required.
- **Source anchors:** `captureengine/{wgc_capture,media_main}.cpp`, `mediaengine/{video_encoder,audio_encoder,mediaengine}.cpp`, `mediaengine/{audio_sync_utils,mux_invariants}.h`, `common/{capture_pipeline_policy,config}.{h,cpp}`, `tools/analyze_capture_av.py`, and focused tests.

### 2026-07-11 - Post-FSR Streamline prewarm cannot be bypassed by the no-FG startup-preservation heuristic

- **Evidence (`logs/fsrfgtodlssfgoverlaybrieflydisappear`, manifest session `logs/20260711_175014`, build `0.1.4502`):** FSR shut down at `17:50:22.201-22.226`; Streamline created a fresh six-buffer proxy at `17:50:25.048-25.054`; CE then logged `Fresh authoritative Streamline no-FG handoff preserved live overlay backend`. There was no `PostSL handoff prewarm READY before DLSS enable` breadcrumb before `slDLSSGSetOptions(ON)` at `17:50:25.115`. The first PostSL callback at `17:50:25.282` submitted successfully, but the intended pre-enable replacement-swapchain preparation had never run.
- **Root cause:** the runtime-inactive startup-preservation predicate relied on volatile `s_startupOverlayObservedAnyFG`. That state had reset by the post-FSR Streamline handoff, so a real FSR-to-DLSS transition was misclassified as the harmless Social/EOS no-FG startup-swapchain case. Preservation bypassed retiring the old swapchain-scoped RTV/sync resources, which in turn bypassed the prewarm introduced for this transition.
- **Fix / invariant:** durable `g_HadFSRFGPhase` history now explicitly disqualifies runtime-inactive startup preservation at both policy call sites. After any FSR phase, a fresh authoritative Streamline proxy retires the old swapchain-scoped resources while retaining the device/format-scoped adapter, then runs the existing pre-enable PostSL prewarm. Pure no-FG startup handoffs without FSR history retain their no-blank preservation behavior.
- **Regression / validation:** `SettledStartupOverlayStaysVisibleAcrossRuntimeInactiveStreamlineHandoff` now covers both sides of the distinction: no prior FG preserves the live startup backend, while prior FSR forces the real handoff/prewarm path. Required full x64/x86 build passed at `0.1.4509`; the focused policy test passed; canonical validation then passed all `1315` native tests and three Python tool self-tests at metadata build `0.1.4511` (one unrelated audio-ring publication test failed on the first run and passed on the complete rerun). Interactive FG switching remains with the user's test session to avoid process/log interference.
- **Source anchors:** `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp`, `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h`, `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`, `llm-wiki/frame-generation/guardrails.md`.

### 2026-07-11 - FSR-to-DLSS first-Present flicker: warm backend reuse plus pre-enable PostSL prewarm

- **Evidence (`logs/20260711_172959`, build `0.1.4494`):** the FSR context shut down cleanly at `17:30:20.477`; Streamline created its fresh six-buffer proxy at `17:30:22.921-22.935`; explicit `slDLSSGSetOptions(ON)` followed at `17:30:22.994`; the first PostSL callback arrived at `17:30:23.152`. Although that callback submitted successfully before returning to Present, CE spent about 17-20 ms inside it shutting down and rebuilding the DX12 overlay adapter (`InitImGui` `23.152 -> 23.169`, first draw `23.172`). DLSS's presenter can already emit output while that callback is blocked, matching the user's very brief overlay disappearance exactly at activation. There was no cooldown/probe miss or device removal.
- **Root cause:** fresh post-FSR Streamline handoff invalidated the old swapchain RTV/sync state but failed to request reuse of the already-live device/format-scoped overlay adapter. `InitImGui` therefore treated the queue change as a full backend replacement even though the adapter does not retain swapchain buffers or use its stored queue for submission. The replacement proxy and exact owner queue existed roughly 59 ms before DLSS enable, but CE left all replacement setup until the first generated Present.
- **Fix / invariant:** a fresh authoritative post-FSR Streamline handoff with a previously live overlay now preserves the warm adapter and prebuilds the replacement proxy's RTV heap plus allocator/list/fence state on the proxy's exact queue before DLSS is enabled. This preparation records/submits no overlay draw and does not touch a backbuffer state; the first PostSL callback only records the real overlay draw. The gate requires FSR history, runtime-owned DX12 proxy, DLSS still OFF, a genuinely live retiring overlay, and a fresh authoritative queue. Pure-DLSS cold startup, already-running DLSS, reused/non-authoritative queues, non-DX12 swapchains, and incomplete old overlays retain their prior guarded paths. Any prewarm failure leaves the ordinary first-PostSL bootstrap available.
- **Diagnostics:** expect `Fresh authoritative Streamline handoff ... preserving the warm device-scoped backend`, followed before `slDLSSGSetOptions(ON)` by `PostSL handoff prewarm READY before DLSS enable`. The first `PostSL WARMUP COMPLETE` should then report `overlayInit=1 syncInit=1` and should not log `PostSL bootstrap — rebuilding torn-down overlay state`.
- **Validation:** required clean x64/x86 build passed at `0.1.4499`; focused warm-reuse/prewarm policy tests passed; canonical no-build validation passed all `1315` native tests and three Python tool self-tests at metadata build `0.1.4500`. Interactive validation is intentionally left to the user's already-running switch tests to avoid process/log interference.
- **Source anchors:** `hook/apis/dx12_hook.cpp`, `hook/common/dx12_overlay_policy.h`, `tests/test_dxgi_shared.cpp`, `llm-wiki/frame-generation/guardrails.md`.
### 2026-07-11 - Strict true-10-bit DXGI/WGC capture and CFR packet-coverage enforcement

- **Observed root cause:** the short DXGI capture retained BGRA8 and paid the expensive BGRA8→P010 path while the encoder took roughly 28–89 ms per frame. Its MKV declared about 6.19 seconds at 120 fps but contained only 170 video packets instead of about 743, with a 48-tick maximum PTS gap. The comparison WGC capture delivered 746 contiguous packets and used FP16 source → retained R10 → P010.
- **DXGI precision contract:** explicit `capture_method=dxgi_dup` plus `bit_depth=10` offers R10 then FP16 for SDR and FP16 for HDR, disables legacy BGRA duplication, waits up to two seconds for the first acquired texture, and validates that texture rather than `ModeDesc.Format`. BGRA8/unknown first frames fail loudly. Explicit DXGI 10-bit failures cannot silently switch to WGC; auto and 8-bit policies retain compatibility fallback. R10 stays compact end-to-end until P010 conversion; FP16 SDR converts to retained R10 without an 8-bit intermediate.
- **WGC correction:** WinRT still rejects R10 pools, so explicit 10-bit WGC uses FP16 staging → retained R10 → P010. The compact BGRA staging option is now default-off and is gated out for explicit 10-bit/HDR even if configured true. Therefore the user's `wgc_prefer_compact_10bit_pool=false` log was a genuine 10-bit chain; the earlier contrary diagnosis was wrong.
- **CFR/A/V validation:** encoder shutdown logs expected/emitted/missing packet coverage. `analyze_capture_av.py` scans/sorts packet PTS and treats missing CFR ticks or >1.01-tick gaps as strict faults. The A/V matrix now covers DXGI duplication, WGC, and inject; the codec pass runs AAC/ALAC/FLAC/Opus/PCM for all three backends. Source policy/config regressions cover strict fallback and precision gating.
- **Validation:** the independent clean x64/x86 build passed at `0.1.4511`; after integration with the concurrent Streamline changes, the main-workspace clean build/install passed at `0.1.4512`, followed by all `1317` native tests and Python tool self-tests at metadata build `0.1.4513`. Packet scanning classifies the reference WGC capture as complete (`746/746`, max gap ≈1 tick) and the broken DXGI capture as strict failure (`170/743`, 573 missing, max gap 48 ticks).
- **Ancillary pre-existing test repairs:** the owner-queue suspension source test now accepts both LF and CRLF checkouts. The audio ring deferred-growth race test no longer compares two independent lock-free getters as if they formed one atomic snapshot; each getter must publish a complete old/new value, while a mixed pair across the growth boundary is valid.
- **Source anchors:** `captureengine/{dxgi_dup_capture,wgc_capture,media_main}.cpp`, `common/{capture_pipeline_policy,config}.{h,cpp}`, `mediaengine/video_encoder.cpp`, `tools/{analyze_capture_av,run_av_sync_matrix}.py`, `tests/{test_capture_pipeline_policy,test_capture_coordinator_source,test_config,test_dxgi_shared}.cpp`.

### 2026-07-11 - Startup-cached FFX routing fixes permanent suspension loss and reduces FSR-to-DLSS transition churn

- **Root cause (`logs/20260711_140926`):** the switch app resolved and cached the original `ffxCreateContext`, `ffxConfigure`, and `ffxDestroyContext` exports during a startup race. CE's one-shot protected-runtime breakpoint observed startup traffic and then retired, so the later `ffxConfigure(frameGenerationEnabled=0)` suspension never reached CE. Creation interception was also missed, leaving no exact proxy `gameQueue`; the owner-queue renderer correctly refused to guess. The overlay therefore remained on the active UI-resource route and disappeared permanently in FSR passthrough.
- **Fix:** `ffx_cached_pointer_router` enumerates eligible loaded client PE images and atomically routes only exact original-export pointers found in writable, non-executable, non-discardable, pointer-aligned slots. System, CE, overlay, Streamline, and FFX runtime images are excluded. Routed slots are tracked for guarded restoration. Captured create calls now bind the exact owner queue; cached configure calls expose every suspend/resume edge without modifying AMD executable code.
- **Durable transition handling:** routing a cached `ffxConfigure` slot immediately restores/retires the temporary protected-runtime breakpoint. Context destruction keeps it retired while the durable caller-owned route exists, avoiding the prior teardown rearm and repeated code-byte mutation. Per-context state serializes and deduplicates global enable/disable and callback-routing publication while every provider descriptor is still forwarded. Proxy prework logs target changes on the first Present (`active-ui-resource` versus `suspend-backbuffer`) plus submission proof.
- **Runtime evidence (`logs/20260711_142448`, intermediate build):** CE routed all three cached exports, captured the exact queue, submitted the active UI overlay, observed the manual FSR suspension, switched to owner-queue backbuffer submissions, and released bindings on destroy. The same run showed an approximately 25-second FSR-to-DLSS startup gap, but no dump, no device removal, and successful PostSL activation/overlay submission afterward. That intermediate build still rearmed the protected breakpoint and replayed full transition bookkeeping on repeated configure packets; the durable-retirement/dedupe follow-up directly removes those two observed sources of teardown churn. Final on-hardware rerun remains required; CE did not launch another interactive app while the user's tests could conflict.
- **Build validation:** required clean x64/x86 build completed at `0.1.4494`; the final no-build run passed all `1314` native tests plus Python tool self-tests at metadata build `0.1.4496`. No additional interactive FG test was launched to avoid conflicting with the user's running validation.
- **Source anchors:** `hook/apis/{ffx_cached_pointer_router,ffx_hook,dx12_hook}.{h,cpp}`, `tests/{test_ffx_api_parsing,test_dxgi_shared}.cpp`, `llm-wiki/frame-generation/guardrails.md`.

### 2026-07-11 - DX12 FFX owner-queue overlay: active FG + suspension, transactional UI generations

- **Root cause / queue ownership (refined by the 2026-07-12 GTA entry above):** FFX 3.1.6 FrameGenerationSwapChain DX12 create descriptors expose the logical `gameQueue` that AMD uses for the game-to-present handoff. The earlier suspension attempt wrote a proxy swapchain backbuffer from CE's independent queue (illegal cross-queue swapchain access), while the active UI path also used an independent queue plus a per-present CPU wait and lacked an incoming game-queue dependency. CE parses Wrap/New/ForHwnd creation descriptors, binds `{context, raw proxy identity, retained gameQueue}`, and records both active-UI and suspension-backbuffer overlay command lists immediately before proxy Present. The initial implementation required exact queue/resource device identity; the later GTA trace proved Streamline can wrap that logical queue with a different device identity, so the current rule is the target-validated exact/proven-wrapper owner route documented above. Queue order is game draw -> CE overlay -> AMD handoff; there is no new queue, cross-queue copy, guessed owner, or per-frame CPU wait.
- **Per-proxy renderer:** `dx12_ffx_suspend_overlay.{h,cpp}` owns device/queue/format-scoped overlay state with 16 allocator/list/RTV slots keyed to the proxy's current buffer index, a CE fence, and forced matching VB/IB upload slots. Reuse is nonblocking and requires real fence completion. Each slot retains its target resource until completion because D3D12 command lists do not retain resource references. Signal-unknown/in-flight generations are quarantined instead of freed or overwritten; context retirement is proxy-keyed so contexts may safely share a game queue.
- **Transition/lifecycle safety:** Present/Present1 nesting is deduplicated; a freshly patched proxy is not treated as the live driver until a successful composite is observed, so the real-present fallback remains active during handoff. Removal first quiesces prework, restores the vtable, and drains already-entered detours before queue/renderer/UI teardown. Weak `g_LastSwapChain` execution fallback was removed from PostSL startup activation; execution uses only the retained COM owner.
- **Transactional UI registration:** UI targets/substitutes are staged and published only after `ffxConfigure(RegisterUiResource)` succeeds; rejected/stale generations preserve the last known-good target. Substitute reuse now keys device identity, dimensions, format, and exact D3D12 initial state; COMMON/PRESENT numeric zero is preserved. Successful game-texture registration clears stale substitute re-registration, and re-registration failure no longer counts an unconsumed draw as overlay coverage.
- **Regression coverage / validation:** parser tests cover all three DX12 swapchain creation descriptors. Source invariants cover exact-owner suspension, target retention/nonblocking submission, configure commit/rollback, device/state generation keys, first-prework fallback, and detour quiesce/drain. Required full x64/x86 build completed successfully at build `0.1.4479`; all `1311` native tests and Python tool self-tests passed at metadata build `0.1.4480`. Hardware GTA/Talos/FG-switch validation remains required for visual/pacing confirmation.
- **Source anchors:** `hook/apis/{ffx_hook,dx12_hook,dx12_ffx_suspend_overlay}.{h,cpp}`, `hook/common/{ffx_api_parsing,custom_overlay_dx12,overlay_adapter}.{h,cpp}`, `tests/{test_ffx_api_parsing,test_dxgi_shared}.cpp`.

### 2026-07-11 - Capture reliability audit: lifetime-safe WGC/DXGI/inject and lossless audio stop

- **WGC/coordinator lifetime:** queued WinRT callbacks now use per-instance callback epochs and drain before teardown; active capture publication uses atomic shared ownership plus an exclusive lifecycle gate. Retarget is transactional with prior-source rollback. Producer-assigned source epochs and per-frame cursor metadata prevent stale source/cursor lineage after retarget. Auto inject fallback is first-frame-proven and keeps inject alive on failure/timeout; unresolved process targets never default to primary-monitor capture.
- **DXGI duplication:** reset/unusable state parks on a condition variable rather than polling; thread-creation failure, callback exceptions, MMCSS cleanup, format publication, and running-state teardown are explicit.
- **Inject transport correctness:** media queueing no longer acknowledges shared ring metadata early. Move-only leases hold each producer texture until successful synchronous media copy or deliberate discard, and `readIndex` advances only across a contiguous completed prefix. DX8/9/10/11/12, DDraw, OpenGL, Vulkan, and DX9 shmem producers all preflight outstanding texture references before overwriting. D3D11/OpenGL/Vulkan/D3D12 capture setup and submission paths gained transactional cleanup/error handling; real-time GPU retry sleeps/flushes were removed.
- **CFR failure handling:** fresh-frame metadata commits only after successful non-deferred encode. A failed scheduled fresh encode repeats the prior successful media cache at the same QPC when possible, avoiding a CFR hole without mislabeling failed pixels. Source transitions reset all repeat-cache layers. Cursor scaling/cropping now uses signed outward rounding and proportional source cropping rather than squashing partially clipped cursors. Post-mux probing is bounded and synchronous on its owner thread.
- **Audio:** endpoint WASAPI COM/client lifecycle is worker-owned; reactivation is serialized with stop. Endpoint and app loopback validate packet counts/byte sizes/pointers and contain allocation/queue failures. Stop drains already committed packets once without waiting/reactivation and within an endpoint-buffer bound. Capture sources drain while `AudioLoop` remains alive, including audio-only resampler/track tails; the audio worker exception boundary always releases drain waiters.
- **Injection manager:** WMI callback epochs drain before manager destruction; worker ownership is acyclic and every worker is joined before eject/COM teardown.
- **Regression coverage / validation:** callback epoch, atomic owner, handoff state, inject ring lease, cursor geometry, audio source/lifecycle, coordinator/source, encoder source, queue, policy, and ring-buffer tests. Required full x64/x86 build passed at build `0.1.4470`; all `1308` native tests and all Python tool self-tests passed at metadata build `0.1.4471`.
- **Source anchors:** `captureengine/{media_main,wgc_capture,dxgi_dup_capture,injection}.cpp`, `common/{callback_epoch,atomic_shared_owner,capture_handoff_state,inject_frame_ring_lease,frame_queue}.h`, `hook/apis/{ddraw,dx8,dx9,dx11,opengl}_hook.cpp`, `hook/capture/shared_capture.cpp`, `hook/vulkan_layer/*`, `mediaengine/{audio_capture,app_audio_capture,audio_ring_buffer,mediaengine,video_encoder}.cpp`, and the corresponding `tests/test_*` additions.

### 2026-07-18 - Make mip-filter overrides reliable across legacy D3D, Vulkan, and OpenGL

- **Unified contract:** `[Graphics] mip_mapping` is now case-normalized and accepts only `default`, `nearest`, `bilinear`, or `trilinear`; invalid input logs once and falls back to `default`. One shared policy maps those modes to point/linear MIN, MAG, and mip-filter triples and covers all four OpenGL mip MIN enums without enabling mipmapping on a non-mip object.
- **Mutable Direct3D coverage:** D3D6/7 hooks are installed on every actual returned device vtable instead of assuming the bootstrap HAL class, and DX8 sampler originals are also retained per vtable. DX6/7 refresh config at EndScene; DX8/9 retain their Present refresh. D3D7/8 ApplyStateBlock and D3D9 state-block Create/End/Apply are intercepted so a successful Apply refreshes physical state while retaining tracked logical state, then immediately reapplies the override. D3D9 config-disable transitions now pass through the state engine even when the new config is already `default`. Pure DirectDraw 2D has no sampler state; its hosted mip coverage is the D3D6/7 device path.
- **Vulkan/OpenGL coverage:** Vulkan mip eligibility is independent of the stricter safe-AF material heuristic, so ordinary point and clamp-to-edge samplers receive the requested mode while comparison, special-reduction, border, unnormalized, nonstandard, and no-mip-range descriptors remain protected; rejected modified descriptors retain the original transactional retry. OpenGL scalar/vector/float, bound, sampler-object, core/EXT DSA, allocation/storage/copy/view/mipmap, and cached bind paths now share the mip mapping. Bind caches are context/config/object-generation scoped, and texture/sampler deletion invalidates reused names across contexts.
- **Coverage / verification:** policy tests lock normalization, all OpenGL mip enums, discrete D3D triples, and Vulkan mip-vs-AF eligibility; config and source-wiring regressions cover invalid input, per-vtable legacy hooks, state blocks, bind/delete hooks, and transactional Vulkan fallback. Marker-allocation failure defers reactivation instead of escaping the capture thread or publishing a replacement epoch out of order.

### 2026-07-18 - Make first process-loopback epoch consumption transactional after the repeat automatic stop

- **Runtime proof / corrected diagnosis:** neither supplied session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260718_004211` nor `20260718_022031` was user-stopped (`hk=0`); both stopped automatically with process-loopback integrity code 1 and finalized their media cleanly. The first protocol-v2 trace could not distinguish producer rejection from consumer corruption, so the earlier producer-format attribution was not proven. The protocol-v3 Heroes of the Storm reproduction did distinguish it: `status=3 stage=6/ConsumerEpochValidation sequence=0 lastError=0xd`, `produced=1 consumed=0`, followed by an exact requested 48 kHz/stereo/float32 480-frame packet. Thus the first `EpochStart` descriptor was still at sequence 0 while shared consumer lifecycle state rejected it as already active or stale. The former multi-atomic protocol made that partial combination representable; the logs do not retain the exact interruption or corruption mechanism that produced it.
- **Root invariant / protocol 4:** consumer lifecycle state no longer lives in the cross-process header. Each worker owns a generation-bound producer state and the parent `WorkerInstance` owns its serialized consumer state; both track expected descriptor/byte cursors plus current/last epoch. Producer packet shape and lifecycle order are validated before commit. Consumer read materializes the output, publishes both shared read cursors, then advances only its private lifecycle state. `DiscardPackets` scans the complete snapshot into prospective locals and publishes nothing if any later descriptor or epoch is invalid. Endpoint state cannot be reused across a worker generation or a divergent cursor. The consumer still independently validates committed descriptors/epochs, so moving state private does not weaken corruption rejection.
- **Failure publication / diagnostics:** first failure ownership is now claimed by the fatal `PublishingFailure` transport status. The winner fills final status/stage names, failure descriptor sequence, read/write descriptor and byte cursors, current/last/packet epoch, record type, observed committed sequence, and error before publishing the final status. A publisher that exits halfway remains fatal instead of looking healthy. Worker and parent fatal/exit lines relay the complete evidence; producer packet, epoch, and endpoint-state failures are distinct from consumer/discard validation.
- **Coverage / verification:** focused `ProcessLoopbackProtocolTest.*` passed with new first-epoch coherence, producer/consumer epoch rejection, state-generation mismatch, evidence, incomplete-publication, transactional-discard rollback, and concurrent SPSC order coverage. One temporal coincidence is insufficient grounds to change wrapper retry behavior or any capture/pacing policy.

### 2026-07-17 - Make incremental and failed-build retry verification authoritative

- **Waste identified:** the canonical agent product command force-recompiled every object, including on a retry after an earlier clean attempt had already compiled unaffected x64/x86 hook/media units. The subsequent `--no-build --run-tests` command also minted a new `build_version.h` despite compiling no binary. Initial end-to-end measurement then exposed that `build_version.h` was included by high-fanout `shared_defs.h`/`config.h`, so even a validated incremental build recompiled most of the tree merely to change identity. Routine command/per-file console output duplicated the durable `build.log` and consumed agent context without adding verification coverage.
- **Safe workflow:** ordinary source changes now use `--incremental --skip-updates --concise` for the final product gate; link, packaging, shader, PE/import/PDB, and other product validation remain unconditional. Clean/default compilation remains mandatory for build-script, compiler/linker/hardening, dependency/toolchain/FFmpeg, generated-build, and shared ABI/layout changes, cache investigations, or explicit requests. Focused iteration uses incremental tests-only plus a GoogleTest filter. A clean attempt followed by a successful guarded resume is one complete clean transaction.
- **Hardening / retry identity:** incremental signatures now include the compiler executable's SHA-256 in addition to source, flags, dependency files, and project-header contents, and signature-evaluation errors fail closed to recompilation. Generated version macros now live behind stable `common/build_identity.*` accessors; only `build_identity.cpp` includes `build_version.h`, while discovery defaults/validation, logs, manifests, and Vulkan layer naming retain exact-build semantics. `--resume` implies incremental validation, requires `--skip-updates`, and reuses an identity only when `latest_manifest.json` proves the immediately preceding top-level run failed and matches both the current `build.py` SHA-256 and `build_version.h`; successful/no-build/sanitizer-child predecessors, build-script changes, and `--no-build`/`--force-rebuild` combinations are refused. `--no-build` and sanitizer children reuse the current identity.
- **Context efficiency / object correctness / coverage:** `--concise` hides routine command and compile-progress lines from the console but preserves them in `build.log`, preserves all errors/stage summaries, and propagates into the sanitizer child. The separately created x86 Vulkan environment now inherits `FORCE_REBUILD`, closing a clean-gate inconsistency revealed when three layer objects were cached during a nominal clean run. Measurement also exposed that product and unit-test phases shared x64 object paths despite differing flags: they invalidated each other's cache on every build, and the later CaptureEngine link could consume common objects most recently compiled by the test phase. Ordinary tests and sanitizer tests now have distinct namespaces separate from product objects. Build-policy tests cover compiler replacement with older mtime, fail-closed signature evaluation, generated-version and object-variant isolation, guarded resume identity, no-build version reuse, build-control propagation, and console-only log suppression.
- **Measured verification:** clean/default build `0.1.5047` passed in 213.2 seconds with zero cache hits in every x64/x86 product, ordinary-test, and Vulkan group. The immediately following validated incremental build `0.1.5048` passed in 96.0 seconds (54.97% less wall time): exactly five identity objects recompiled and all 365 ordinary objects were signature-proven cache hits, while every product link, all 30 test-app builds, six embedded Vulkan shaders, packaging, import closure, PE hardening, and PDB checks still ran. The final no-build gate reused `0.1.5048` and passed the complete native suite, all Python tool self-tests, seven FFmpeg patch tests, and all 23 build-policy tests.

- **Root fix:** inject CFR now selects the monotonic source frame nearest `scheduledOutputQpc - avContentDelayQpc`, with half-frame lead tolerance. Only the physical fence tail is unselectable, startup waits for `reserve + delay + 1`, pruning is relative to committed source lineage, and the input-rate EMA is telemetry only. Catch-up uses the same timestamp target and encoder-health gate. This preserves zero added repeats at matched cadence, honest evenly spaced repeats below target, timestamp decimation above target, and stable behavior through source-rate transitions. WGC/DXGI's shared nearest helper now advances to a successor only when it is actually at least as close, eliminating tolerance-induced raw-timestamp holds without changing its compositor tolerance or CFR/audio grid.

### 2026-07-17 - Remove the four-texture Vulkan recording deadlock and root integration summary

- **Runtime proof / root cause:** ordinary-account session `20260717_150205` loaded the build-specific Vulkan layer, initialized and rendered the overlay, but layer publication stopped permanently at four frames and media finished with `input=0 output=0`. At 120 fps, the measured 31.242 ms loopback A/V content delay retained four frames and the warmup fence reserve retained one more; the encoder requires a sixth buffered frame before releasing the oldest lease. The Vulkan producer's four hard-coded textures were therefore all outstanding, so it could never publish that sixth frame. This was independent of registry/elevation after startup repair succeeded.
- **Root fix:** both layer-owned Vulkan resources and DXVK encoder-owned zero-copy imports use `SHARED_TEXTURE_SLOT_COUNT`/`ENCODER_TEXTURE_SLOT_COUNT` across all 16 existing lease slots. No A/V delay, fence correctness, capture feature, per-frame copy, wait, sleep, or polling behavior is weakened. The shared layout/name advances to ABI 36 because `EncoderTextures` expands.
- **Harness/logging fix:** the integration runner now requires final encoder output statistics and uses that count for the recording threshold; overlay `perf_metrics` cannot make a zero-frame recording pass. Its default `integration_results.json` moves into the latest corresponding session directory, while an explicit caller path remains supported. The prior root summary was relocated into `20260717_150205`.
- **Coverage / validation:** regression units lock the 16-slot Vulkan/encoder pool invariant, forbid reintroduced four-slot layer arrays, parse final recording output, and require the default integration-summary path to be session-scoped. Required full build `0.1.5032` passed x64/x86 products, both Vulkan layers, packaging, PE/PDB/import checks, and compile-command generation. Metadata `0.1.5033` passed the complete native suite and every Python self-test. ### 2026-07-17 - Make stale Vulkan registration recovery prompt-free for ordinary launches

- **Runtime proof:** ordinary session `20260717_142845` wrote the current HKCU manifest registrations but had no Vulkan-layer startup log or overlay. Session `20260717_143113` worked when CE was already elevated. A controlled ordinary CE plus `vulkaninfo` run exposed the difference: stale HKCU values from `captureproject_overlay_repeat_validation` advertised the same `VK_LAYER_CE_overlay` identities, and the Vulkan loader explicitly discarded both current manifests as later duplicates. Elevated CE worked because its current HKLM values were found before the stale HKCU entries. Swapchain cleanup in the working session was normal layer lifecycle, not the cause.
- **Privilege policy:** default CE remains non-elevated and never requests UAC. Runtime repair enumerates CE-owned manifest basenames in both HKCU registry views on every controller startup. Only when the process is already elevated does it add both HKLM views; this covers unrestricted/UAC-off accounts and explicit elevated starts without making a prompt part of ordinary operation. `build.py` remains registry-side-effect-free, so build harnesses cannot mutate live Vulkan state. Machine registration stays ephemeral because leaving a user-writable build path active for elevated applications would be unsafe.
- **Stale-installation isolation:** x64/x86 manifests now carry build-specific layer names and implementation versions. Discovery ABI 36 publishes `BUILD_NUMBER`, and every current consumer validates it; a stale same-ABI Vulkan DLL therefore stays dormant if multiple CE layer DLLs load, while an inaccessible old manifest no longer has the duplicate identity needed to suppress the current build. Startup repair is basename-limited; normal teardown still deletes only the retained plan's exact paths once.
- **Coverage / validation:** focused tests cover split HKCU/HKLM architecture views, the elevation gate around HKLM repair, owned manifest matching, repair-before-registration ordering, exact teardown, build-specific manifest identities, and exact discovery build validation. Full build/test verification passed at `0.1.5032`/`0.1.5033`. Fresh session `20260717_152124` ran ordinary HKCU mode with `elevated=false`, loaded the build-specific layer, rendered and recorded successfully, then removed both exact HKCU values; the final four-view audit found no CE registration and no process remained.

### 2026-07-17 - Isolate the shared ABI that corrupted Vulkan logs, telemetry, and inject recording

- **Exact runtime evidence:** in supplied session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260717_133007`, media initialized the Vulkan frame-ring cursor to decimal `1819637339` = `0x6C75765B`, whose little-endian bytes are `[vul`. The pre-ABI-33 log buffer began exactly where the current frame-ring write index lives, so an old-layout `[vulkan-layer.log] ...` record overwrote capture metadata. The current logger then viewed that record 24 bytes late at the new log-buffer offset, lost the filename prefix, and wrote the tail as root `logs/hook_debug.log`. The screenshot's max-core value `3933208576` = `0xEA700000` exactly matches the low 32 bits of the host-published 11,943 MB VRAM capacity at the old reader's shifted max-core offset. The other visible values follow the same one-field shift introduced by `publicationSequence`: sequence as CPU, CPU as RAM, RAM as GPU, and GPU as VRAM. This proves mixed compiled layouts; available evidence does not distinguish a stale incremental object from an already-running/injected stale binary, so both recurrence paths are closed.
- **Root fix:** shared ABI 34 uses versioned main/discovery names, exclusive main ownership, placement construction, magic-last publication, exact struct size, and a fingerprint over major/nested sizes and offsets. Every controller/service/media/hook/Vulkan consumer validates before payload access. Stale retained discovery mappings are reused only when their advertised owner is dead; shutdown withdraws discovery first. Build object signatures now include compiler-reported project-header content, so an older-mtime checkout cannot retain layout-skewed objects.
- **Logging, telemetry, and recording behavior:** the logger snapshots `DiscoveryInfo.logsPath` per session instead of deriving root `logs`, owns and sanitizes the filename prefix, and closes mappings on shutdown. Vulkan shared-log writers reserve the MPSC ring with CAS. Media rejects corrupt frame windows with a recording-integrity code, while Vulkan emits early/periodic publication and rate-limited full-ring diagnostics. Hook telemetry rejects non-finite/out-of-range/incoherent host publications, host max-core calculation rejects counter regression/overflow/idle underflow, and sensor summaries expose the complete publication.
- **Coverage / verification:** new/updated tests cover exact ABI publication and fingerprint rejection, versioned names, wrap-safe/corrupt frame windows, session-log path selection and filename containment, CPU counter discontinuities, and dependency content signatures with a forced older mtime. Required build `0.1.5028` completed x64/x86 hooks, captureengine/mediaengine, both Vulkan layers, test apps, packaging/import/PE/PDB verification, and compile commands. Canonical no-build metadata `0.1.5029` passed the full native suite and every Python tool self-test. Fresh game-process restart plus live Vulkan overlay/inject-recording validation remains required.
- **Source anchors:** `common/{shared_defs,invariants}.h`, `captureengine/{inject_main,ipc,logger_service,media_main,sensor_service,host_metrics}.cpp`, `hook/common/{ipc_client,system_metrics}.cpp`, `hook/vulkan_layer/{layer_ipc,layer_main}.cpp`, `build.py`, `test_build_flags.py`, `tests/{test_shared_runtime_state,test_logger_service_policy,test_host_metrics_policy}.cpp`, and `llm-wiki/{process-ipc,overlay-rendering,build.py,current,log/recent}.md`.

### 2026-07-17 - Disable the dormant malformed AV1 NVENC timecode path without touching capture timing

- **Verified defect / reachability:** pinned FFmpeg 8.1.2 exposes `av1_nvenc`'s `s12m_tc` boolean with default true. Its shared NVENC path passes `ff_alloc_timecode_sei()` output—written with HEVC time-code syntax—as AV1 timecode metadata. NVIDIA's June 2026 public diagnosis confirms that FFmpeg payload error plus a separate driver byte-alignment limitation in AV1 metadata OBU injection. The bundled Matroska and NVENC CFR/B-frame patches do not touch this path. Repository-wide inspection found no CaptureEngine creation or forwarding of `AV_FRAME_DATA_S12M_TIMECODE`, so the supplied captures did not exercise the defect; this is a real but currently dormant future-input hazard, not an explanation invented for observed overload/cadence/audio behavior.
- **Minimal safety fix:** AV1 NVENC now adds required `s12m_tc=0` after custom options and logs that last-applied invariant. An attempted custom enable is overridden with a high-signal warning. H.264/HEVC NVENC and AV1 AMF/QSV/MF are unchanged. Generic SEI, A53 captions, HDR metadata, pixels, rate control, CFR scheduling, capture backends, mux timing, and every audio path remain untouched. The former post-`avcodec_open2` `repeat_pps=1` block was removed because it could not affect the opened codec, `av1_nvenc` exposes no such option, and AV1 has no PPS; the valid cached-texture re-encode diagnostic remains.
- **Coverage / verification:** focused encoder policy/source tests passed 39/39 and lock backend scoping, custom-versus-required precedence, application before `avcodec_open2`, and absence of the bogus PPS option. All seven custom-FFmpeg patch tests passed, including strict application to the exact pinned source. Required build `0.1.5026` passed x64/x86 compilation, packaging/import closure, Vulkan shader validation, PE hardening, and PDB verification. ### 2026-07-17 - Make inject CFR overload recovery converge without touching audio or screen capture

- **Runtime evidence:** Fortnite DX12/DirectFlip/VRR inject session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260717_005930` produced 14,693 contiguous 120-fps CFR video packets. All three AAC tracks fully decoded to 5,877,200 samples (`122.4416667 s`) with equal endpoints, one-microsecond container rounding only, and no capture loss, ring overflow, mixer/resampler fault, discontinuity, clipping, or decoder error. The brief subjective sound may therefore be game percussion; the old build has no worker-service-gap telemetry that can prove or disprove scheduling starvation at that instant. Video cadence was not optimal: after the overload, inject recovery remained active at about 35-37 ticks of debt, used 4,296 recovery repeats with no fresh catch-up, and sustained only roughly 60-76 unique frames/s despite 125-147 source FPS and roughly 2-5.5 ms encode time.
- **Root cause/fix:** a two-output catch-up cycle was treated as one service sample, so its raw duration falsely tripped the slow-service gate. The catch-up output also advanced the normal wake deadline, making a two-output cycle wait two ticks and mathematically unable to repay debt. Inject now divides cycle service by actual outputs, assigns every live output QPC from the immutable `liveStart + outputCount * interval` grid, and does not advance the normal wake for its one bounded recovery output. Pure encode and authoritative encoder/mux pressure still stop unsafe catch-up. Episode start/best/current debt, duration, fresh/repeat work, per-output service, and raw cycle time are logged; a recovery still active after five seconds is strict visual triage evidence. WGC/DXGI keep their prior scheduling path and wake advancement.
- **Audio boundary:** no capture, mix, resample, drift, codec, mux, timestamp, priority/MMCSS, or silence policy changed. The audio worker now records rate-limited >=25 ms service gaps after startup, including ring/fanout/epoch queue pressure, and emits a summary. The analyzer exposes this as diagnostic `audio_worker_scheduling_stall`; packet continuity counters and decoded audio remain authoritative, so a scheduling gap alone is not mislabeled an audio artifact.
- **Coverage/verification:** policy tests simulate debt convergence and lock immutable output QPC, per-output capacity accounting, and unchanged WGC/DXGI wake behavior. Source-contract tests cover inject-only integration, audio diagnostic non-interference, and analyzer classification. `python build.py --skip-updates` passed as build `0.1.5022`, including x64/x86 products, test apps, Vulkan layers, packaging, imports, PE hardening, and PDB checks. Final `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` at metadata `0.1.5023` passed all 1,649 native tests plus every Python tool self-test. Fresh equivalent real-game overload validation remains pending.

### 2026-07-16 - Restore truthful legacy-overlay GPU, VRAM, and RAM telemetry

- **Root cause:** old graphics APIs did not prevent out-of-process sensor polling. The host ignored the selected game PID and required a nonzero hook LUID before initializing/filtering GPU counters; DirectDraw's overlay-only D3D9Ex helper did not publish its adapter; the consumer conflated numeric zero with unavailable data; and RAM copying was incorrectly gated on CPU load being greater than zero.
- **Fix:** hook LUIDs now carry publisher-PID provenance. Exact same-process LUIDs win; otherwise the host parses the target PID's Windows `GPU Engine` instances, selects the highest non-video-load adapter, and retains stable process evidence across zero-load ties or temporary gaps. GPU usage, VRAM usage, and VRAM capacity have independent validity bits plus coherent publication sequencing/source metadata, so real zeros remain visible and stale values clear on process/adapter replacement. RAM updates independently of CPU. DirectDraw publishes its D3D9Ex helper LUID without requiring recording.
- **Runtime/performance boundary:** no-recording 4K/150% DirectDraw7 runs for both x64 and x86 visibly reported `RTX 5070`, numeric GPU load, about 1.76/11.66 GB VRAM, and about 13/31.93 GB RAM. Each sensor log transitioned from target-PID inference (`0xBAB1`) to the same-process hook LUID. Recording was deliberately off because legacy capture is not zero-copy. DirectDraw/DX6/DX7 still pay the existing full-surface lock/copy/helper-Present cost; replacing that architecture remains outside this targeted patch.
- **Verification:** 14 focused telemetry/provenance tests pass, including conservative multi-GPU zero/tie handling. Required build `0.1.4989` passed x64/x86 products, test apps, Vulkan layers, packaging/import closure, PE hardening, and PDB checks. The no-build run passed 1,644 native tests when excluding only the shared-system-cursor test; `IDC_ARROW` was temporarily transparent while the ChatGPT Windows-control session was active, consistent with cursor substitution, so that environment-dependent failure is unrelated to this change.
- **Source anchors:** `captureengine/{host_metrics,host_metrics_policy,sensor_service,ipc}.*`, `common/{capture_base,shared_defs}.h`, `hook/apis/ddraw_hook.cpp`, `hook/common/{hook_common,overlay_adapter,system_metrics}.*`, `hook/vulkan_layer/layer_ipc.cpp`, `tests/test_host_metrics_policy.cpp`, and `llm-wiki/overlay-rendering.md`.

### 2026-07-16 - Harden Vulkan presentation/Reflex behavior and remove the DLSS suspension stall

- **DLSS suspension root cause/fix:** repeated key `2` previously called `slDLSSGSetOptions(eOff)` without retaining plugin resources. The call synchronously flushed/destroyed DLSS-G worker state, causing a roughly 2.5-second one-off stall and apparently bad suspended performance. The Vulkan app now sets `eRetainResourcesWhenOff` for its retained-proxy/context contract, logs option-call duration, and warns above 50 ms. Focused active -> suspended -> resumed validation measured 0.001 ms for each option call; suspended real-frame throughput stabilized around 144 FPS and generated counts stopped/resumed correctly.
- **Present path:** VSync-off now prefers `IMMEDIATE` before mailbox, matching the DX12 tearing-capable game route and leaving forced driver VSync/VRR in control. Opt-in `[Vulkan] async_present=1` / `--vk-async-present` reserves a distinct graphics+compute+present queue index in the game family, routes Native/Streamline/FFX replacement Present through it, and supplies it as FidelityFX's game queue while leaving FFX's internal async/present/acquire queues distinct. Render-complete semaphores are swapchain-image-owned so a separate presentation queue cannot still own a binary wait when a frame slot is reused.
- **Reflex contract/diagnostics:** Reflex is explicitly configured even for initial OFF, `slReflexSleep` runs at frame start before fence/acquire waits whenever feature functions are loaded, and `slReflexGetState`, requirement flags, DLSS-G VSync support, sleep failures, CPU-stage timing, and final counts are logged. `frameLimitUs` remains zero and build policy rejects an explicit cap. A focused borderless application-VSync-off run with driver VSync forced showed Native at about 144 real FPS and DLSS FG at about 72 real + 72 generated, not the expected roughly 138.5 output headroom. Focus/DirectFlip/profile application/Reflex calls were proven; public Streamline 2.11.1 guidance and the plugin log still call VSync-with-FG Vulkan-unsupported even though `bIsVsyncSupportAvailable` returned true, so no game-side limiter was added to mask this plugin/driver boundary.
- **Runtime evidence:** an all-state PresentMon capture recorded 5,591/5,594 Presents as independent flip (three compositor startup Presents). A focused debug-utils separate-queue run exercised OFF, DLSS active/suspended/resumed, FSR active/suspended/resumed, and OFF on queue `0:4`; it exited `frames=29001 presented=29001 generated=3969 transitions=3 failures=0 validationErrors=0 deviceLost=0`, with zero Reflex sleep failures and no lingering test process. HDR needs a separate RGB10/BT.2100/PQ path and fresh vendor validation. Source anchors are `testapp/vulkan_fg_policy.h`, `testapp/vulkan_fg_switch_{common,device,fidelityfx,renderer,resources,streamline,test,wsi}.*`, `tests/test_vulkan_fg_{policy,build_policy}.cpp`, and `llm-wiki/vulkan-fg-switch-test.md`.

### 2026-07-16 - Remove registry repair from builds and exact-scope Vulkan registration lifetime

- **Build boundary:** `build.py` previously called a Python `winreg` cleanup after each x64/x86 layer link. - **Runtime boundary:** normal registration no longer enumerates, repairs, or basename-matches ambient registry values. `ApplyRegistrationPlan` writes only `plan.installTargets` on startup and deletes only those targets' exact `manifestPath` values on teardown. CaptureEngine retains the original startup plan instead of rebuilding ownership at shutdown, so deleted/moved artifacts cannot broaden or lose the teardown scope. The existing controller singleton is the concurrency boundary. Console-handler and normal exit use one blocking `call_once`; normal exit completes unregistration before clearing the handler's non-owning pointer, preventing duplicate work or plan lifetime races.
- **Repair boundary:** opposite hives/views, other CE installations, the legacy manifest name, and missing/stale entries are untouched by ordinary startup and shutdown. A same-path residue from a prior crash is naturally overwritten by the next same-mode registration and removed at its clean exit. Any broader legacy repair remains deliberately absent until it has an explicit user-facing repair/uninstall workflow and stronger ownership proof.

### 2026-07-16 - Treat an authoritative DLSS-off swapchain creation as a new lifetime even after pointer ABA reuse

- **Observed interruption / root cause:** supplied long-switch session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260716_125557` contains a real `[OVERLAY VISIBILITY] INTERRUPTED/UNPROVEN` span: 61 uncovered Presents over 453 ms, gated by `overlay-backend-uninitialized`. The exact sequence was `OFF -> FSR -> OFF -> DLSS -> OFF -> FSR -> OFF -> DLSS -> OFF`. Both authoritative DLSS-off native returns reused swapchain address `0000027B56C5FD30`; the first return differed from `g_LastSwapChain`, but the second new COM lifetime was ABA-equal. Creation had armed the exact one-Present native-return proof, yet `ProcessFrame` guarded all replacement handling with raw pointer inequality, so it missed the second lifetime and the late outer OFF observer tore down the backend into the 60-Present cooldown.
- **Root fix:** logical replacement is now `pointer changed || exact creation-time lifetime proof`. An ABA-equal authoritative return therefore runs the same guarded native ownership transaction, immediate first-Present rebuild, and late-observer preservation as an address-changing return. A high-signal `[OVERLAY VISIBILITY] ... reused the previous COM pointer address; processing it as a new lifetime` breadcrumb makes the exceptional branch explicit. A later `DLSS -> OFF -> FSR` run exposed a zero-duration telemetry double count: inline PostSL keep-alive and its enclosing ProcessFrame accounted the same Present separately. The inline callback now delegates draw accounting to the enclosing scope, while standalone PostSL callbacks remain separately accounted. These results did not cover the separate pre-SetOptions first-proxy-Present failure later caught in `20260716_132719`; see the newer entry above.
- **Performance / compatibility boundary:** the lifetime decision is one boolean on a replacement edge; it adds no copy, queue, allocation, wait, delay, polling, game branch, Reflex/manual-limiter mutation, FG-status rewrite, or steady-state GPU work. ### 2026-07-16 - Make fatal-exit interception recursion-free through normal shutdown

- **Dump proof / root cause:** supplied session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260716_025345` contained seven x64 `0xC00000FD` dumps from DX9, DX9Ex, DX10, DX11, DX12 FG switch, OpenGL, and Vulkan tests. A new inline-hook publication API atomically exposes each trampoline before its target patch becomes callable and rolls publication back if activation fails; forwarded KernelBase/kernel32 and Nt/Zw functions remain fallback pairs rather than sharing one original slot across two live hooks. These changes affect only hook installation and exit/failure paths, not capture or rendering hot paths.

# llm-wiki Log — Archive 2026-W29c

### 2026-07-15 - Eliminate D3D11 forced-AF submission starvation and close material coverage gaps

- **Evidence / root cause:** supplied 32-bit BioShock Infinite DX11 session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260715_223043` ran around 54 FPS with the limiter inactive and about five million draws. The wrapper performed about 1.67 million draw reconciliations, scanned 4.83 million sampler slots, rebound 863 thousand slots, and issued about 704 thousand effective sampler calls. Temporal SRV warm-up, global streaming-quiet transitions, sampler-role probation, resource mutation registries/negative caches, string-heavy configuration copies, private-data/resource queries, process-global locks, and periodic hot-path atomics/logging turned a state override into CPU submission starvation. The same conservative model skipped valid BC5 normal/mask data, array/cube views, clamp-addressed material samplers, and derivative-footprint bias/gradient sampling.
- **Root fix / invariants:** D3D11 shader metadata is now one immutable private COM interface with precomputed sampler/texture lookup masks; SRV structural suitability is cached once on each view; and 2x/4x/8x/16x forced variants plus negative/compliant markers live on the original sampler. Safe/aggressive eligibility precedes variant lookup so a live mode transition cannot reuse an unsafe aggressive variant. Contexts track O(1) masks and reconcile only dirty slots, coalescing only actual pointer changes into real `PSSetSamplers` calls. Clean wrapper draws have only the cached config-version/dirty checks—no global lock, descriptor/COM resource walk, history scan, allocation, diagnostic atomic, or driver state call. The raw fallback returns on one dirty-context atomic and clears stale tracking across `ExecuteCommandList(FALSE)`. `PSGetSamplers` remains logically transparent, and all reset/command-list/device-context-state boundaries clear tracking.
- **Coverage / Blackwell policy:** `sample`, `sample_b`, and `sample_d` are derivative-footprint safe; `sample_l`, comparison, and unknown explicit operations are protected. Typed, mipmapped, single-sample Texture2D/array/cube/cube-array views now cover BC1-BC7 (including BC4/5/6), common color/channel float/UNORM/SNORM formats, and legitimate RTV/UAV-capable material resources. Depth, typed integer, typeless/problematic, multisample, non-2D-family, and one-visible-mip views remain blocked. D3D10/11 safe mode requires linear min/mag but permits clamp/mirror-once; all modes reject border, comparison/reduction, and fixed mip ranges. DX12 remains creation-time-only and now rejects border in aggressive mode too. Vulkan remains creation-time/transactional and now rejects border, unnormalized coordinates, compare, special reduction, and nonstandard filters in every mode.
- **Performance / validation:** the intended steady state has no sampler override driver work and no lock/COM/descriptor work on clean draws; a cached version/dirty branch still exists, so “zero overhead” means no measurable submission starvation rather than literally zero CPU instructions. Required `python build.py --skip-updates` passed end to end as installed build `0.1.4878`, including x64/x86 hooks, both Vulkan layers, packaging, import closure, PE mitigation/architecture, and PDB checks. ### 2026-07-15 - Harden module discovery, ring-buffer overflow policies, and byte-safe case folding

- **Broad shipping review / root causes:** fixed-size PSAPI module arrays were iterated using the full required byte count, so a process with more loaded modules than local storage could drive out-of-bounds reads; the 256-entry post-injection verification could also miss a successfully loaded hook. `RingBufferPolicy::Overwrite` advanced only the write index, producing a logical size above capacity and unsigned `Available()` underflow, while zero-capacity and moved-from dynamic buffers could index empty storage. Several config, process/window matching, module-path, and hash comparisons passed signed `char` values directly to C locale case conversion, which is undefined for negative byte values.
- **Targeted fixes:** shared PSAPI enumeration now grows and retries a bounded number of times, returns only complete snapshots, and preserves the existing default-vs-architecture-specific filter choices at each caller. Fixed and dynamic overwrite modes both retire the oldest logical element; zero-capacity pushes fail safely; dynamic moves leave a valid empty source. Case conversion at the reviewed input boundaries now promotes bytes through `unsigned char`. No capture cadence, encoder, overlay rendering, FG state, or IPC ABI changed.
- **Coverage / validation:** focused module, ring-buffer, and config-fuzz validation passed 12/12 before the final move-assignment regression was added. Required `python build.py --skip-updates` passed end to end as build `0.1.4871`, including x64/x86 hooks, CaptureEngine/MediaEngine, Vulkan layers, packaging, import closure, PE mitigation, and PDB checks. Canonical `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` then passed all 1,537 native tests in 108 suites, four FFmpeg patch tests, three build-policy tests, and all Python tool self-tests at metadata `0.1.4872`.
- **Review boundary / stale-risk:** `common/sequence_lock.h` has no production users, and its current design is not a sound general C++ multi-writer primitive; making its non-atomic payload formally race-free would require a redesign outside this targeted shipping pass. Do not introduce it into production paths without revisiting that design.
- **Source anchors:** `common/{module_enumeration,ring_buffer}.h`, `captureengine/{injection,inject_main,media_main}.cpp`, `common/config.cpp`, `hook/{main.cpp,common/dxgi_shared.cpp,apis/ffx_hook.cpp,wrappers/{iat_hook,inline_hook}.cpp}`, and `tests/{test_module_enumeration,test_ring_buffer,test_config_fuzz}.cpp`.

### 2026-07-15 - Make DXGI cursor shader creation compile and fail safely

- **Dump/log proof:** DXGI Duplication session `installed/captureengine/logs/20260715_130953` reached live 3840x2160 R10 capture, opened the mux, and encoded video/audio until the desktop cursor changed from Windows-embedded to a separate hardware plane. Cursor shader/resource failure therefore retains the existing fail-open video behavior instead of crashing the media child. A source regression rejects the reserved identifier, requires module-before-blob lifetime ordering, and forbids manual compiler unloads in the resource builder.

Canonical `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` passed all 1,504 native tests in 105 suites, four FFmpeg patch tests, three build-flag tests, and all three Python A/V self-tests at metadata `0.1.4820`. ### 2026-07-15 - Harden screenshot/output/process boundaries and source-built runtime closure

- **Screenshot boundary:** shared-memory ABI 32 replaces request/ack booleans with a request ID, completed ID, explicit status/error/payload kind, and request-specific event. Every graphics backend copies mapped pixels before returning and hands filesystem work to one managed hook worker. The worker writes an exact `ScreenshotRawHeaderV2` plus pixels to a new `.part`, flushes/closes, publishes `.ready`, then completes only the matching request. The host rejects stale, truncated, corrupt, overflowed, unknown-format, and non-exact payloads. SDR uses WIC PNG; HDR uses strict-FP BT.2020/PQ conversion and source-built libaom `YUV444P10LE` AVIF with complete packet drain and checked mux/close operations. Detached writers, BMP parsing, size polling, sleeps, and publication-before-close are removed.
- **Output ownership:** video, audio-only, PNG, and AVIF use `ReservedCaptureOutput`. Empty paths resolve to the executable's `captures` directory, relative paths remain executable-relative, and mapped-drive resolution remains intact. UTC-millisecond/PID/sequence names are reserved with `CREATE_NEW`; identity-checked cleanup cannot remove a pre-existing or replaced file. Muxers retain the reservation through close; screenshots atomically replace only their owned placeholder with a closed staging file. Collision regressions force identical name seeds and prove sentinels remain byte-identical.
- **Process isolation and IPC:** `RestrictedChildProcess` uses `STARTUPINFOEX` and an exact inherited-handle list. Each controller/inject/media/limiter child gets a unique connected duplex pipe restricted to SYSTEM/current user, verifies the server PID, and completes a protocol-2 startup handshake containing its exact PID, mode, and per-channel 128-bit nonce. Exact message validation rejects malformed sizes, kinds, opcodes, modes, sequences, PIDs, nonces, and payloads with rate-limited diagnostics. Fixed public production endpoints and reconnect-by-name behavior are gone; a broken channel triggers clean respawn.
- **Process-loopback integrity:** protocol 2 replaces 256 fixed 256 KiB slots with 32,768 descriptors plus a variable byte ring sized for the validated format's 30-second retention and one legal two-second packet. Only data and stop events are inherited. Producer/consumer validation covers payload bounds/wrap, record type, `1..8` channels, rate/bit depth/alignment/divisibility, flags, epoch, and zero-payload lifecycle records. Descriptor/byte exhaustion and corrupt committed metadata latch fatal status, stop MediaEngine, and fail the recording instead of silently restarting across an audio gap. Helper arguments and inherited handles are strictly parsed before Media Foundation/MediaEngine loading.
- **Configuration and toolchain boundaries:** numeric config no longer relies on `atoi`/`atof`; malformed or non-finite text falls back to documented defaults with rate-limited diagnostics. Explicit ranges cover GPU priority, capture multiplier, backbuffers, B-frames, quality/sharpness, capture/limiter FPS, HDR paper white, WGC floor, process IDs, and format-derived allocation arithmetic. The source-built manifest adds signed/pinned libwinpthread 14.0.0.r179.g24aaa6147-1 and AOM 3.14.1-1, their licenses/runtime DLLs/import closure, and FFmpeg `libaom-av1` 10-bit 4:4:4 support while retaining SVT-AV1. First-party x64 is baseline `x86-64`, host/dependency fast-math is absent, and strict FP covers audio/color paths. Sanitizers include x64 hook/helper/media/capture/Vulkan; explicit x86 sanitizer requests fail while the runtime is unavailable. PE verification retains ASLR, NX, x64 high-entropy VA, W^X, architecture, import closure, and first-party PDB checks. Effective x64/source-runtime CFG remains enforced; the current linker's empty x86 CFG tables are explicitly deferred at the user's direction.
- **Validation:** regression coverage was added for screenshot generation/encoding/corruption/color/AVIF, collision ownership, private process IPC, process-loopback wrap/maximum packet/corruption/lifecycle/fatal behavior, strict parsing, dependencies, and PE hardening. Required `python build.py --skip-updates` passed end-to-end as build `0.1.4806`. `python build.py --no-build --run-tests --skip-updates` then passed all 1,501 native tests in 105 suites and all four Python tool self-tests. The focused hardening/dependency suite passed 19/19. The CRLF patch fixture now initializes its workspace-temp directory as an isolated Git repository, matching the disposable FFmpeg checkout and preventing parent-repository discovery from turning `git apply` into a false no-op.

WGC and inject retain their existing hotspot convention, DPI-aware cursor resources, GPU composition, and SDR/HDR transfer paths. The only synchronization added is the duplication source's coherent pointer-state snapshot, outside the game/render path; there is no wait, sleep, GPU readback, extra texture copy, or per-frame allocation.
- **Diagnostics / validation:** rate-limited timeline and rectangle logs now report `coord=hotspot|shape-top-left`, pointer observation QPC, and authoritative plane-state position validity. ### 2026-07-14 - Remove WGC finite-gate aliasing and qualify process-loopback startup

- **Independent evidence / root causes:** the supplied Fortnite WGC window session delivered roughly 132-136 fps
  before collapsing through 92/102/84 fps to about 72 fps while the game remained near 138 fps and all CE pool,
  encoder, mux, and queue-pressure counters stayed zero. A finite WGC `MinUpdateInterval` is a minimum accepted-update
  gap, not a resampler: a periodic source rate `S` gated at `P` is accepted near `S / ceil(S / P)`, so 138 gated at
  120 becomes about 69 fps. Phase and source jitter make the transition look random, and callback-derived feedback is
  already downstream of the gate, so it can self-lock in the aliased state. The same session selected Brave's correct
  process-tree root and activated process loopback successfully, but the event-driven client emitted no packet for the
  full recording while system loopback still contained Brave audio.
- **Root fixes / invariants:** WGC CFR now keeps `MinUpdateInterval=0` and local throttling disabled throughout the
  session; only the timestamp-nearest CFR scheduler resamples surplus input. The applied WinRT interval is read back,
  any nonzero runtime target is logged as a contract violation and immediately reset, and cached callback-rate windows
  age to zero during a stall instead of retaining stale healthy FPS. DXGI Duplication shares the zero-target screen-grab
  invariant without using the WinRT property; inject remains causal and GPU-native. Isolated process loopback now tries
  polling mode first, qualifies every activation on its first packet, and only uses event mode as an initialization
  fallback. An event activation that initializes but emits no packet is reactivated polling-only; epoch replacement
  causes the disposable helper to be reaped, which bounds abandoned AudioSes COM state. Silent-stall recovery is armed
  by the current activation rather than session-lifetime packet history, so a silent replacement cannot trigger
  indefinite helper recycling during a long pause or closed audio session.
- **Diagnostics / coverage:** rate-limited producer-contract, interval-readback, first-packet, mode-fallback,
  no-data-epoch, and final qualification records expose the causal state without hot-path noise. The completed-file
  analyzer reports `wgc_producer_rate_contract_fault` for nonzero/mismatched WGC producer policy and
  `app_audio_active_no_data` when an active selected process never supplies audio. Unit coverage models the 138->69,
  144->72, and 160->80 alias families, rate-window expiry, and event first-packet fallback. Analyzer syntax/self-tests
  pass, and re-analysis of the supplied session now distinguishes upstream WGC delivery starvation from CE pressure
  while identifying the active Brave no-data epoch. The final required x64/x86 product build passed at `0.1.4710`;
  14 focused cadence/rate/recovery regressions passed at test metadata `0.1.4711`; and the canonical no-build run passed
  all 1,425 native tests across 94 suites plus three Python self-tests at metadata `0.1.4712`. No synthetic capture
  harness, stimulus capture, matrix, or automated soak was run.

- **Root fix:** WGC/DXGI may now replace an already-required catch-up hold with one buffered historical frame only when its smoothed selection timestamp is within half a CFR interval and raw timestamp within one interval of that exact old content target, source/selection lineage remains monotonic, and the active-delay reservoir stays above its low-water reserve. Candidate submission uses `repeatScheduledQpc` and the existing contiguous CFR timeline; no selection clamp or live fast-forward is allowed.
- **Capacity gate:** recovery requires a measured end-to-end fresh-frame service EMA (including waits/copy overhead), no encoder-bottleneck or actively-too-slow state, and cost below 75% of the frame interval. Four submissions at that ceiling fit in three intervals, so the maximum four-tick burst can repay one wall-clock slot. Renewed pressure, exhausted surplus, an encode failure, or no grid-matched candidate immediately falls back to the prior held-repeat behavior.
- **A/V invariant and diagnostics:** this changes only the pixels of an existing output slot. PTS count/grid, audio target/cursor, compensation, mixing, resampling, and finalization are untouched. The legacy `[EncoderThread] CFR Catchup applied using fresh frame` string remains a strict failure; safe substitutions use `[EncoderThread] WGC CFR grid-matched recovery frame`, per-window `FreshSvcEma`/`CatchFresh`, and final `[WGC CFR RECOVERY] GridFresh=... Held=... PtsGrid=immutable AudioTimeline=unchanged`.
- **Coverage / boundary:** focused policy and source-integration tests pin headroom/reserve limits, exact threshold behavior, monotonic half-slot/raw-slot matching, rejection of live content relabeling, scheduled cursor/timeline use, and the absence of the legacy path. Required full verification build `0.1.5203` passed the clean product build, full native suite, all 12 Python tool self-tests, file-size/clang-tidy ratchets, and ASan/UBSan regression pass. Fresh faster-preset runtime overload validation is still required to measure the actual reduction in holds and confirm the conservative gates remain effective.
- **Source anchors:** `captureengine/media_main.cpp`, `common/capture_policy/{constants,cfr_repeat_metrics,cfr_scheduling}.h`, `tests/{test_capture_pipeline_policy_part4,test_capture_coordinator_source}.cpp`, and `llm-wiki/{cfr-capture-sync,wgc-capture,current,index,log/recent}.md`.
